The law requires the filing of this report and the payment of tax on or before July 1, 1937, and annually thereafter. 

1. Extension of time for filing this report may be granted in instances where the unusual and extraordinary circumstances justify such extension. Application for extension must be made in writing to the Commissioner at least fifteen days before the due date of the report. Such application must fully state the reasons for such request. 

When extension is granted, the tax due will be subject to interest at the rate of 6% per annum. 

2. This report must be complete in every detail. Unless all information requested in the report is properly shown, the report will not be considered as having been filed under the law. Penalties and interest will accrue upon all incompleted and delinquent reports. 

3. A statement of dividends and interest paid, accrued or credited to the account of residents of Tennessee during the period for which this report is made must be attached. 

This statement must show the name and address of the person, the amount of dividends or interest paid to, or due to, or credited to such person, and the dates of credits or payments as required by Chapter 20, Acts of 1931 Second 

Extra Session. 

If the above information is furnished by the taxpayer in its Franchise Tax report, such taxpayer may so state and not furnish the above information as a part of this report. 

4. The term Manufacturing Costs shall be taken to mean the total cost of all goods, materials, and supplies used in manufacturing, assembling or processing; the total wages 112

Ch. 3) 113 

EXCISE TAX 

and salaries paid or incurred during the year and the total overhead or manufacturing burden properly assignable according to good accounting practice to such manufacturing, assembling or processing activities. 

5. The term sales as used in Section D, page 2 lines 24 and 29 shall be taken to mean sales made to customers within Tennessee irrespective of the location of the residence of such customer. Sales made to customers outside of Tennessee must be supported by records maintained in such manner as will readily permit expeditious examinations by representatives of this Department. 

The term sales as used in Section D, page 2, line 28, shall be taken to mean sales made through or by offices and branches located in this State irrespective of where the purchaser may reside. The determination of sales ratios must be obtained by an analysis of gross sales. 

6. The Federal Income tax deductible at line 2, Section 

A, page 1, of this report means and includes the total accrued Federal Income tax liability payable to the United States Government March 15, 1937, based on net income for the fiscal or calendar year 1936. 

7. Any taxpayer feeling aggrieved after paying his determined tax liability may file with this Department a written statement setting forth in detail his contentions with respect to the tax, and such taxpayer will be promptly notified upon final determination by the Commissioner. 

8. Excise tax reports are confidential and information contained therein cannot be divulged. Therefore, legal representatives or other persons acting in behalf of corporations are required to present duly executed power of attorney before excise tax matters will be discussed with such representatives. 

9. No credits are allowed under the excise tax law except the tax paid by insurance companies upon gross receipts and sums paid by State Banks into the State Treasury as fees for the use and benefit of the State Banking Department.

EXCISE TAX CORPORATIONS LIABLE FOR EXCISE TAX— APPORTIONMENT OF NET EARNINGS TO TENNESSEE 

Law. Section 1316 as amended: 

All corporations, cooperatives conducted for profit, joint stock associations and business trusts, organized under the laws of the State of Tennessee, other than those organized for general welfare and not for profit, and all such entities organized under the laws of any other state or country for profit and doing business in Tennessee, shall, without exception, pay to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation annually an excise tax, in addition to all other taxes, equal to three and three quarters (3-4) per cent of the net earnings for their next preceding fiscal or calendar year, from business done within the State. 

In the case of corporations, cooperatives, joint stock associations and business trusts doing business in Tennessee and elsewhere, the net earnings shall be apportioned as hereinafter set forth and the net earnings thus apportioned to Tennessee shall be deemed to be the earnings arising from business done within the State and shall be the measure of this tax. 

Such method of apportionment shall be as follows: (1) If the principal business in this State is manufacturing or if it is any form of collecting, assembling or processing of goods or material, the entire net earnings shall be apportioned to Tennessee on the basis of the ratio obtained by taking the arithmetical average of the following three ratios: (a) The ratio of the value of its real estate and tangible personal property in this State on the date of the close of the fiscal year is to the value of its entire real estate and tangible personal property, with no deductions on account of encumbrances thereon. (b) The ratio of the total cost of manufacturing, collecting, assembling or processing within this State, to the total cost of manufacturing, collecting, assembling or processing within and without the State. (c) The ratio of the gross sales to customers within Tennessee is to the total gross sales from all sources. (2) If the principal business in this State is selling, distributing, dealing in or using tangible personal property, the entire net earnings shall be apportioned to Tennessee on the basis of the ratio obtained by taking the arithmetical average of the following three ratios: (a) The ratio of the value of its real estate and tangible personal property in this State on the day of the close of its fiscal year is to the value of its real estate and tangible personal property then owned by it, with no deductions on account of encumbrances thereon. (b) The ratio of the total sales made through or by offices, agencies, or branches located in Tennessee during the income year to the total sales made everywhere during said year. (c) The ratio of the gross sales to customers within Tennessee is to the total gross sales from all sources. (3) If the principal business is other than the manufacture or sale of tangible property, such proportion as its gross receipts in Tennessee during the income year is to its gross receipts for such year within and without the State.

If, because of peculiar or unusual circumstances inherent in a particular case, the application of the above formulas would work a hardship or injustice, the Commissioner, upon application of the taxpayer and upon

(Ch. 3 

such showing, is authorized, with the approval of the Attorney-General, to adopt such other method of apportionment as would be fair and just under the facts of the case. 

Tennessee insurance companies shall pay on net earnings proportioned to premiums on policies on persons and property in this State. 

Corporations Liable for Tax- 

The Excise tax is a privilege tax levied upon domestic and foreign corporations, cooperatives, joint stock associations and business trusts organized for profit and actually carrying on business in Tennessee. The privilege taxed appears to be the right of "doing business in Tennessee for a profit." In Bank of Commerce & Trust Company V 

Senter, 149, Tennessee 569, December Term 1923, the court states: 

"The tax is upon the privilege as actually used by all within the class-This statute is not violative of the Constitution-requiring equality and uniformity in taxation on property, for such excise tax is not a direct tax on property, but a privilege tax permitted by said Constitutional provision. This statute is not unconstitutional under the contention that it arbitrarily taxes corporations to the exclusion of partnerships and individuals.

Joint stock associations, building and savings loan associations are subject to the excise tax. It may be noted that the provisions of Section 1316 of the Code as amended are broader than the provisions of Section one of the original Act; Section 1316 as amended states "shall, without exception pay-annually an excise tax, in addition to all other taxes." The Court in the case of Home Building and 

Loan Association of Memphis V. Graham, 155 Tennessee 

524, decided at the December Term, 1926, held that Chapter 134, Acts of 1925 (the General Revenue Bill) did not repeal the excise tax law. Therefore, it appears safe to assume that the only exceptions from the provisions of the Act are: 

1. National Banks. 

2. Corporations created under acts of Congress for purely Governmental purposes. 

3. Corporations organized for welfare purposes and not conducted for profit. 

4. Municipal Corporations. 

Measure and Rate of Tax- 

This privilege tax is measured by "net earnings." The 

Act, prior to the amendments of 1937, provides: "Equal to 

3% of the net earnings-arising from business done wholly

Ch. 3) 117 

EXCISE TAX 

99 within the State, excluding earnings arising from interstate commerce. The Act as amended provides "equal to 

3.75% of the net earnings for their next preceding fiscal or calendar year, from business done within the State." The 

Act contains no definition of "net earnings." However, the 

Court has indicated that the term should be "given its usual and ordinary meaning of what is left of earnings after deducting necessary and legitimate items of expense incident to the corporate business." See Bank of Commerce & Trust Company V Senter, 149 Tennessee 569. In view of the absence of Court decisions and rules and regulations defining the term, it will be of interest to point out the trend of the Court in regard to this question: "The bills present an actual controversy between the complainants and the State as to what items of expense are deductible in finding the net earnings of corporations from intra-state business. The term "net earnings," not being defined by the Act, must be given its usual and ordinary meaning of what is left of the earnings after deducting necessary and legitimate items of expense incident to the corporate business. 

This question is not presented by the appeal, and must await answer and proof in the trial court." Bank of Commerce and Trust Company V 

Senter, supra.

Since the tax is to be measured by "net earnings," an adequate definition of the term is most essential. 

Determination of Net Earnings- 

Under date of June 24, 1936, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation issued a ruling with respect to the determination of taxable net earnings. This rule, as ap proved by the Attorney-General, follows: 

1. The excise tax is to be assessed upon net earnings arising from business done wholly within the State. The term "net earnings" is more or less a general term and to determine the amount of net earnings subject to the tax, it is necessary to first ascertain Gross Revenue or Gross Income. After Gross Revenue or Gross Income is determined this amount should be analyzed and classified as to source, such classification to be substantially as follows: (a) Gross Sales, or Gross Receipts arising from the conduct of the business in which the corporation is engaged. (b) Total interest received on Loans, Notes, Mortgages, Bonds, Bank 

Deposits, etc. (c) Total rents received. 

(d) Total Royalties Received. 

(e) Total Commissions Received. 

(f) Total Profit from the sale of Real Estate, Machinery and Equipment, Stocks, Bonds, and other capital assets. (g) Total interest received on non-taxable securities such as Federal, State, County and Municipal Bonds.

(Ch. 3  

(h) Total dividends received on stock held in other corporations. (i) Total recovery of bad accounts which have been previously allowed in the determination of excise tax under the law of this 

State. 

(j) Total income from any other source with description of source from which such income was received. 

2. After ascertaining Gross Revenue or Gross Income and classifying same in accordance with paragraph one, the next step is to determine "net earnings. Therefore, it is necessary to ascertain the aggregate deduction allowable in determining net earnings. Deductions should be analyzed and classified, the classification of allowable deductions to be substantially as follows and as far as possible shall be applied directly to the source of receipts or income from which the expense or deductions arose:

Salaries and Wages. 

(b) Compensation of Officers. 

Rent Paid. (d) Interest.

Taxes, (except such taxes as are allowed as a direct tax credit). 

(f) Insurance. 

(g) Repairs to business property. 

(h) Bad Debts, provided the debt has been previously reported as receipts or income. (i) Depreciation and Depletion allowed by the Federal Government in computing income tax liability. (j) Ordinary and necessary expenses connected with the conduct of the business in which taxpayer is engaged. (k) Cost of merchandise sold. 

After the determination of Gross Revenue or Gross Income as set forth in paragraph one, the total allowable deductions ascertained and set forth in paragraph two shall be deducted from Gross Revenue or Gross Income, which should reflect net earnings as shown by books of the taxpayer. 

3. Upon the determination of net earnings of the entire business of the taxpayer, the next step is the determination of "net earnings from business done wholly in the State." To equitably apportion net earnings it becomes necessary to use an allocation basis in cases where the taxpayer does not keep records which reflect net earnings arising from business done in the State. It also becomes necessary to determine net earnings wholly within the State where the taxpayer receives income from external sources, such as Rents, Dividends, Interest, etc. The Commissioner of 

Finance and Taxation is vested with power to determine "net earnings arising from business done wholly within the State."' Therefore, for the purpose of allocating an equitable proportion of net earnings of corporations transacting business within and without the State the ratio of sales or gross receipts shall be used. This ratio shall be determined by dividing the Gross Sales or Receipts arising from business transacted everywhere. This sales or receipts ratio shall be applied to total allowable deductions used in determining net earnings from the entire business of the corporation. External receipts or income shall be localized where possible, however, unless the taxpayer can satisfactorily show that such external receipts or income arose from business transacted outside of the State; the receipts or sales ratio shall be used in allocating such net earnings. 

4. The Statute provides for the exclusion of net earnings arising from interstate commerce. Correspondingly, the proportion of expenses or allowable deductions shall be eliminated from the total expenses or allowable deductions. 

All business originating or handled through an office in this State shall be deemed "business done wholly within this State" unless the tax-

Ch. 3) 119 

EXCISE TAX 

payer shall keep his records thereof in such shape as to enable the Department to readily and at once identify the interstate transactions from those taking place wholly within the State. 

5. The following tax credits shall be allowed as a direct credit against the excise tax assessed: (a) Filing fee paid to Secretary of State in the preceding twelve months prior to July 1. (b) Taxes paid by insurance companies under section six of the General Revenue Bill and under Section 5716, provided said tax is paid in preceding twelve months prior to July 1. (c) All privilege tax paid under any General Revenue Bill, including the total privilege tax of fifteen cents levied as item 57 of General Revenue Bill, provided said tax was paid in preceding twelve months prior to July 1.

Since the adoption of the above rule, the Excise Tax law was amended by Chapter 99, Acts of 1937, and while there does not appear to have been any direct cancellation of the above rule, the present excise tax report forms require the use of "net income for year ending December 31, 1936 (or the fiscal year) as reported to the United States Collector of Internal Revenue as the measure of the excise tax." It may be contended that since the new excise tax report form, issued pursuant to the law as amended in 1937, repeals by implication or cancels the former rule with respect to determination of taxable net earnings. The adoption of net income as reported to the United States may or may not constitute net earnings for excise taxation and would appear to be contrary with the view of the 

Supreme Court of Tennessee. 

"The term "net earnings" not being defined by the Act, must be given its usual and ordinary meaning of what is left of earnings after deducting necessary and legitimate items of expense incident to the corporate business.' (See Bank of Commerce & Trust Company V. 

Senter, supra.) 

Upon reference to the Federal Law, certain items of income such as (a) Interest from obligations of the United States, Territory, or any political subdivision thereof, (b) Interest from obligations of corporations organized under Acts of Congress, (c) amounts received under life insurance contracts, etc. are to be excluded from the computation of net income, moreover, there are certain items of expense not permitted as deductions under the Federal Act in computing net income, and certain limitations placed upon losses arising from the sale of capital assets which render the net income figure inaccurate for excise taxation when

(Ch. 3  

viewed in accordance with the expression of the Supreme 

Court of Tennessee. "Undoubtedly, the interest received by appellant on tax free bonds constituted a part of its net earnings. This is not denied. The contention is that the portion of appellant's net earnings arising from tax free bonds must be excluded in calculating the amount of excise tax due by it. The statute itself authorizes no such exclusion. The only earnings excluded by the terms of the statute are those arising from interstate commerce. The enumeration of exceptions to a general statute excludes by necessary implication all other exceptions. It sees also that the 

Legislature intended by the Act that all net earnings of a corporation, from whatsoever source derived, shall constitute the measure of the tax, except that earnings from interstate commerce shall be excluded.' Na tional Life and Accident Insurance Company V. Demptster, 168. Tennes see 446, December term 1934. 

As a general rule, net income, net earnings or net profits are commonly understood to mean the same thing, i.e., the amount of net profit, net income or net earnings remaining after all expenses and charges are paid or accrued for the period; that amount which may be credited to surplus or undivided profits. However, these terms as used in taxing statutes have different meanings. The amount of net income for Federal income taxation does not appear to be the measure of the tax intended by the Legislature for excise taxation. It is reasonable to assume that had the Legislature thus intended, it would have so stated in the Act; on the other hand, the Legislature did intend to levy a tax for the privilege of exercising corporate powers in producing a profit and to tax the entire net profits or net earnings, the source of the profit and the character of the business being immaterial, with the exception as to net earnings arising from interstate business. 

The adoption of net income as reported to the Collector of Internal Revenue as a measure for the excise tax presents the following questions: 

1. Does the adoption of statutory net income as the measure of the tax change the character of the tax to one "upon income''? 

2. Does the adoption of statutory net income as the measure of the tax preclude or estop the Commissioner from subsequently increasing or decreasing the 'net income" figure so reported to the Collector of Internal Revenue by restoring to such items as non-taxable income or unallowable deductions under the Federal law?

While no authoritative answer can be offered to these questions, attention is drawn to the following: "It is conceded by counsel for the Commissioner that Chapter 21, of the Acts of the Extra Session of 1931 (the general income tax act) is

Ch. 3) 121 

EXCISE TAX 

invalid if the tax thereby levied is a property tax. This concession, of course, is required, for the tax levied is not at a rate uniform with taxes levied on other property and the rate prescribed by the Act increases with the amount of the income. If the tax levied by Chapter 21 of the 

Acts of the Extra Session of 1931 be a privilege tax, it is likewise invalid, Sec. 28 of Article II of the Constitution conferred the legislative power to tax privileges generally "in such manner as they may, from time to time, direct."' That section of the Constitution however, only authorized the legislature to tax incomes insofar as they were "'derived from stocks and bonds that are not taxed ad valorem." tion of 1870 contemplated an income tax as a privilege tax it must have included the income tax clause as a limitation on the power to levy such a tax. From such a viewpoint this clause is an exception or a proviso. 

The clause was certainly not designed to confer an additional power of privilege taxation. The preceding clause, in terms as broad as possible, had countenanced the power of the legislature to tax every privilege. 

The intent, however, was that only the income mentioned should be taxed." Evans V. McCabe, 164 Tennessee 672. Dec. term 1931.

If the conven- "It is insisted that the construction placed upon the Act, as exempting tax free securities, by the several Commissioners, for nine years, is entitled to great weight and should not be disturbed unless clearly erroneous. This is a correct statement if the language of the taxing statute be ambiguous. In Price-Bass Co. V. McCabe, 161 Tennessee 67, this court construed a taxing statute as requiring the payment of greater sums than the Department of Finance and Taxation had, under its prior rulings, required from taxpayers. It was held that the fact that the 

Department had given an unambiguous statute other than the correct interpretation was not controlling. So, in the instant case, the statute is free of ambiguity, and the erroneous construction placed thereon by certain of the Commissioners is not controlling. Mengel Box Co. V. 

Stevens, 141 Tenn. 373. It is insisted that the ruling by the defendant 

Dempster, to the effect that interest collected on tax free bonds should be included as part of complainant's net earnings was such a change in the taxing policy of the State as to render such construction void and unenforceable. It is sufficient to say that the unauthorized and erroneous acts of former Commissioners in excluding interest on tax free bonds as a part of complainant's net earnings by which to measure the tax cannot be held to bind the State. The policy of the State is reflected in the Act, and that policy has not been changed. Appellant can have no advantage from the circumstances that several Commissioners, after the Act became effective, erroneously permitted it to withhold from its net earnings, reported as a measure of its tax, the interest on tax exempt bonds."" National Life and Accident Insurance 

Company V. Dempster, supra.

Since the Court has construed the Act to be unambiguous in regard to "net earnings," and held the erroneous construction of the Act not binding upon the State, it is essential that great care be exercised in the determination of "net earnings." For example: The books of the X.Y.Z.

(Ch. 3 

 Apportionment of Net Earnings- 

All corporations doing business exclusively in Tennessee with property and sales 100% within the State are liable for the tax on their total net earnings-without any apportionment.

Corporations doing business in Tennessee and elsewhere are subject to the tax on apportionment of net earnings as follows: 

1. Manufacturing Corporations- 

The net earnings of manufacturing corporations doing business in Tennessee and elsewhere are to be apportioned to Tennessee by use of the arithmetical average of the following three ratios: (a) Ratio of the value of real estate and tangible personal property in this State to value of real estate and tangible personal property everywhere. (b) Ratio of total cost of manufacturing, collecting, assembling or processing in this State to total cost of manufacturing, collecting, assembling, or processing everywhere. (c) Ratio of gross sales to customers within Tennessee to gross sales everywhere.

The "value" of real estate and tangible personal property as used in sub-section (a) of Section 1316, appears to mean "book value." Care should be used in the determination of the average ratio to avoid an erroneous apportionment of net earnings for the purpose of taxation. The "book value" to be used appears to be the net or depreciated value of real estate and tangible personal property within and without the State. 

Regulations covering "manufacturing costs" is as follows:

Regulation No. 4. 

The term manufacturing costs shall be taken to mean the total cost of all goods, materials, and supplies used in manufacturing, assembling or processing; the total wages and salaries paid or incurred during the year and the total overhead or manufacturing burden properly assignable according to good accounting practice to such manufacturing, assembling or processing activities. 

The determination of "Manufacturing Costs" ratio has been discussed in Chapter One dealing with the Franchise Tax.

Ch. 3) 129 

EXCISE TAX 

With regard to "sales" ratio used in the apportionment of manufacturing corporations, department regulation states: 

Regulation No. 5. 

The term sales as used in Section D, Page 2, Lines 24 and 29, shall be taken to mean sales made to customers within Tennessee irrespective of the location of the residence of such customer. Sales made to customers outside of Tennessee must be supported by records maintained in such manner as will readily permit expeditious examinations by representatives of this Department.

The main question in arriving at "sales" ratios iswhen is a sale consummated or completed? Ordinarily, a sale is complete only upon delivery of the article of commerce, delivery constituting the final step in the consummation of the sale.

Therefore, deliveries in Tennessee and all sales "over the counter," irrespective of the residence of the customer, would be classified as sales within the State. However, if delivery is effected in interstate commerce, the sale is classified as sales without the State. Undoubtedly, the best and simplest method in differentiating sales within and without Tennessee would be an accurate accounting record of sales made direct and shipped to customers residing outside the State. Such a record should be supported by invoices and bills of lading or other evidence of delivery for inspection and verification by State representatives. 

The example on pages 130 and 131 is submitted illustrative of the completed Foreign Excise tax report of a manufacturing corporation. Of course the question as to the deductibility or addition of certain items not included in the Federal taxable income, herein previously discussed, will also apply to such corporations. 

2. Selling Corporations- 

The net earnings of selling corporations doing business in Tennessee and elsewhere are to be apportioned to Tennessee by use of the arithmetical average of the following three ratios: (a) Ratio of the value of real estate and tangible personal property in this State to value of real estate and tangible personal property everywhere.

(Ch. 3 

(b) Ratio of sales through or by agencies or branches in Tennessee to total sales everywhere. (c) Ratio of gross sales to customers within Tennessee to gross sales everywhere.

In addition to "property" ratio and "sales to custom ers' ratio another factor is to be used, viz: "Sales through or by agencies or branches in Tennessee to total sales everywhere. 

The "property" and "customers" ratios have previously been discussed. As regards the additional ratio, De partment Regulation is as follows: 

Regulation No. 5 (Par. 2) 

The term sales as used in Section D, page 2, line 28, shall be taken to mean sales made through or by offices and branches located in this State irrespective of where the purchaser may reside. The determination of sales ratios must be obtained by an analysis of gross sales. 

The determination of gross sales made through or by offices, agencies or branches within and without this State, does not necessarily present a difficult problem. Usually corporations operating offices, agencies or branches maintain records from which this information may be readily obtained. However, the possibility of error in this regard is increased by reason of the two "sales" ratios and accurate accounting records are necessary. 

Corporations having their main office in Tennessee and in addition branch offices therein must include the total sales made by or through all offices, and corporations without branch offices must include the total sales made by or through their principal office, or a ratio of 100%.

(a) Ratio of gross receipts in Tennessee to gross receipts everywhere. 

This ratio appears to have been intended only to corporations dealing in intangible personal property and personal service corporations. Generally, few questions will arise in connection with the determination or application of this basis of apportionment.

4. Insurance Companies— 

Tennessee Insurance companies, i.e., insurance companies organized under the laws of this State, are to apportion net earnings upon ratio of: (a) Fire insurance premiums on property in this State to total fire insurance premiums. (b) Life insurance premiums on persons in this State to total life insurance premiums. 

The Excise Tax Report forms do not contain a space for this specific computation, however, the space provided at line 32, page 2, may be used by changing the term "Gross 

Receipts" to read "Gross Premiums." Attention is here directed to Section 1317, permitting a credit against the excise tax for the total tax paid upon premium receipts, such tax may be deducted at lines 7 and 8, block B, page 1, of the report.

(Ch. 3 

plication of the formulas provided in the Act would work an injustice, the Commissioner with approval of the Attorney-General, may adopt a different method of apportionment upon proper showing by the taxpayer. 

As already stated, the proper apportionment of "net earnings" depends upon the accurate determination of each ratio; upon their determination they are to be set forth, totaled and the average ratio taken. The average ratio is then to be applied to total net earnings thereby apportioning a part of such net earnings to this State for taxation. However, the procedure is not clear in instances where one or more of the ratios do not exist, viz: 

(a) Property Ratio 

50% 

(b) Manufacturing Cost Ratio (c) Sales Ratio 

25% 

Total 

75% 

Is the average of the first two or 37.5% to be used or should the sales ratio (which is zero) also be used, thereby reducing the average to 25% ?

There are no published rules or regulations relative to this question but it is understood that apportionment is being allowed by the Commissioner at the 25% average. 

The pertinent part of the Act is as follows: 

"... The net earnings shall be apportioned as hereinafter set forth and the net earnings thus apportioned to Tennessee shall be deemed to be the earnings arising from business done within the State and shall be the measure of this tax. Such method of apportionment shall be as follows:'' 

The question as to whether the rigid application of the ratios obtained by averaging three factors, even though one or more factors be absent, must await decision of the Court. The taxpayer having all three factors present in the computation of the average ratio would receive an apportionment of net earnings greater in amount than a taxpayer having only two factors present and using zero as the third factor, in computing the average ratio; thus

Ch. 3) 139

1. Property ratio 

50% 

2. Manufacturing cost ratio 50 

3. Sales ratio 00 

Total 

100% 

Average ratio 333%

In this connection it should be remembered that the excise tax is a privilege tax for doing business for a profit in Tennessee. The Court in Bank of Commerce and Trust 

Company V. Senter, supra, says: "The tax is upon the privilege as actually used by all within the class. . . This statute is not violative of the Constitution." The Legislature may have intended the use of all three ratios, inserting zero for such factors as may be absent, as a means of equalizing or to measure the tax in accordance with the use made of the taxable privilege. A corporation engaged in manufacturing and selling its products in Tennessee enjoys a greater privilege than the corporation engaged only in manufacturing.

It might also be contended that "selling" profits were included in the total net earnings of the corporation and that by the exclusion of that factor, in arriving at apportionment, would result in allocation of profits to Tennessee that did not arise from business done therein. 

Another very important question, especially as regards foreign corporations, is whether income, which in no way is related to the business conducted in Tennessee, is to be included in the "net earnings" subject to allocation for excise tax assessment.

(Ch. 3  Take the following Example: 

A corporation has its principal offices in New York, it maintains its bank accounts, securities and books of account there, all of its offices are directed therefrom, and the business in Tennessee is a "branch'' either in selling or in the manufacture of the company's products. 

Certain income, received by the company in New York and included in its Federal taxable income, is as follows: (a) Dividends from corporations in England, France and Germany. (b) Rents and royalties. (From investments not in Tennessee) 

(c) Interest on Liberty Bonds. 

(d) Profit from sale of capital assets. (Not in Tennessee)

It is assumed that this income would have been received by the Company if it had no business in Tennessee and in no way whatsoever has the income any relation to the business "done within the State.' 99 

Tax Credits-State Tax Only- Law. Section 1317 as amended: 

The tax imposed shall be in addition to all other taxes, and no other tax shall be a credit upon the tax hereby imposed except that insurance companies paying a privilege tax of two and one-half (22) per cent on gross premium receipts shall be entitled to a credit for such tax so paid, and except that all sums paid by State banks into the State Treasury as fees for the use and benefit of the State Banking Department shall be a credit upon the tax hereby levied. The tax herein imposed is a State tax for State purposes only and no county or municipality or taxing district shall have power to levy any like tax. 

The excise tax is a State tax only. A similar tax cannot be levied by a county or municipality. The excise tax is in addition to all other taxes levied for State purposes. 

Prior to the amendment of 1937, Section 1317 permitted the deduction, as a direct credit against the excise tax of the following taxes, provided, such taxes were paid in the twelve months preceding July 1st of the current year; 

1. Tax paid to Secretary of State under Section 4136 of the Code. 

2.

Tax paid by insurance companies under the General Revenue Bill and under Section 5716 of the Code. 

3. Merchants' privilege tax paid to the State. 

4. All specific privilege taxes paid to the State under the General Revenue 

Bill.

Ch. 3) 141 

EXCISE TAX 

The 1937 amendment permits the deduction as direct credit against the excise tax as follows: 

1. Tax of 22% levied upon gross premium receipts of insurance companies. 

2. Sums paid by Tennessee banks for the use and benefit of the State 

Banking Department. 

It appears that the Legislature permitted the credit for the various taxes prior to 1937 in an effort to avoid double taxation. However, in actual practice it appears that all taxes, other than Federal income tax, were allowed as a deduction in computing net earnings and again as a direct credit against the tax. To avoid this double credit and to eliminate many administrative difficulties, the Section was amended excluding all direct tax credits, except those relating to Insurance companies and State Banks. 

The tax credit allowed insurance companies is discussed in Chapter Two dealing with Franchise Tax. 

When Payable-Penalties for Delinquents- Law. Section 1318 as amended: 

The tax imposed shall be due and payable on July 1st of each succeeding year; and, if delinquent thirty days, shall be subject to a penalty of one per cent, per month, and in addition interest at the rate of six per cent per annum from July 1st until paid. 

The Excise Tax is payable on or before July 1st of each year. This section of the Act provides the following: 

1. If delinquent thirty days penalty 1% of tax due plus interest at rate of 6%. (Interest to be computed on tax only). 

2. If delinquent more than thirty days penalty of one per cent per month plus interest from July 1st.

It appears that no penalty may be imposed until the expiration of thirty days from July 1st, but to avoid controversy and possibility of penalty, corporations finding it impractical to file the report and pay the tax on or before July 1st may apply for extension of time in accordance with:

Regulation No. 1. 

Extension of time for filing this report may be granted in instances where the unusual and extraordinary circumstances justify such extension. Application for extension must be made in writing to the Commissioner at least fifteen days before the due date of the report. Such

application must fully state the reasons for such request. When extension is granted, the tax due will be subject to interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

New corporations would appear to be liable for excise tax in the amount of "net earnings" arising from business done in Tennessee for the broken period up to the date of their elected fiscal closing date immediately preceding the due date of the return, viz., July 1st.

Distress Warrant Issued after January First of Each Year- Law. Section 1319 as amended: 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is empowered, and it shall be his duty, after the first day of January of each year, to issue a distress warrant for the collection of the excise tax, interest and penalty due from each delinquent corporation. Said distress warrant may be addressed and delivered to the Sheriff of the county wherein such delinquent corporation has its principal office or place of business, or to the sheriff of any county in which the Commissioner has reason to believe property of such delinquent corporation may be found. 

It is mandatory upon the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation to issue distress warrant for the collection of the excise tax. The warrant may be delivered for service to the sheriff of any county in which the Commissioner has reason to believe property belonging to the corporation may be found.

Delinquent corporations may avoid additional costs, penalties, and interest by paying the tax prior to January 1st.

Levy on Personal Property— Law. Section 1320 as amended: 

The sheriff into whose hands such warrant may come, or his deputy, may execute same by distraint and sale of personal property belonging to such delinquent corporation, and the proceedings in respect thereto shall be the same as are provided by law for proceedings under an execution at law from a court of record; and the executing officer shall be entitled to the same fees, commissions, and necessary expense of removing and keeping property distrained as in case of an execution from a court of record.

This section authorizes the sheriff or his deputy to execute the distress warrant issued by the Commissioner by distraint and sale of personal property of the delinquent corporation, the proceeding being the same as that of execution at law from courts of record. Attention is called

Ch. 3) 143 

EXCISE TAX 

to the fact that the executing officer is given the same fees, commissions, and expenses as those allowed in similar cases from a court of record. 

Levy on Real Property- Law. Section 1321 as amended: 

If the officer cannot find personal property to satisfy said distress warrant he may levy same upon any real estate in his county belonging to such delinquent corporation; and if levied on land, said distress warrant, together with the officer's return thereon, shall be returned to the circuit court of the county wherein the land lies, and the land shall be condemned and sold under the orders of said circuit court in the same manner as in case of the levy on land of an execution issued by a justice of the peace.

This Section authorizes the sheriff or his deputy to levy upon land of delinquent corporations where there is insufficent personal property to satisfy the distress warrant issued by the Commissioner for the collection of the tax. 

The distress warrant and the officer's return thereon are returnable to the circuit court of the county in which the land of the delinquent corporation is situated. Upon the proper delivery of said warrant and officer's return to the circuit court, it is mandatory that the court condemn and sell the land under its orders as in case of levy on land of an execution issued by a justice of the peace. Such procedure is expensive and should be avoided if possible. 

Administration of the Act- Law. Section 1322 as amended: 

The supervision and collection of the tax imposed shall be under the direction of the Department of Finance and Taxation and such department shall have authority and power to prescribe forms upon which corporations and joint stock associations, liable for the tax imposed, shall make reports of such facts and information as will enable the Commissioner of said department to ascertain the correctness of the amount reported and paid by such corporations or joint stock associations. 

The supervision and collection of the excise tax is placed under the Department of Finance and Taxation, this Department being vested with power and authority to prescribe forms to be used by taxpayers liable for tax. 

The Department is given power to require report of all facts, deemed necessary by the Commissioner, to enable the Department to ascertain the correctness of the amount reported and paid by the taxpayer. In this connection it is

(Ch. 3  

obvious that any form prescribed by the Department must be in conformity with the Statute. However, should the 

Department prescribe a form not in accordance with the Act, resulting in the payment of tax less than the full legal liability, it would appear that the State is not barred from the collection of the full liability. See National Life and 

Accident Insurance Company V. Dempster, supra. It is not clear as to whether additional excise tax found to be due by the Commissioner is subject to penalty and interest. 

However, since the Act imposes penalties and interest upon all delinquents, it appears to logically follow that deficiencies in tax payment would also be subject to such penalties. 

The Act appears to place the primary burden upon the taxpayer to disclose the full legal liability and to make full settlement of the tax on or before July 1st of each year. 

Commissioners Determination of Net Earnings Final-Rules and Regulations- Law. Section 1323 as amended: 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is hereby authorized o make and promulgate rules and regulations, not inconsistent with this law, for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this law, which rules and regulations, when approved by the Attorney-General, and when promulgated and published, shall have the force and effect of law. 

In all matters requiring the exercise of judgment and discretion as to what may or may not be net earnings, the judgment and opinion of said Commissioner shall be final and conclusive and there shall be no review of his action except that the taxpayer shall have the right to pay any such tax under protest and to sue for the recovery thereof or for the recovery of a part thereof under section 1790, et seq. Code of Tennessee. 

This Section authorizes the Commissioner to make and promulgate rules and regulations. Such rules and regulations, before they become binding, must be: 

1. Issued in accordance with the Act and not inconsistent therewith. 

2. They must be designed for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this Act. 

3. The rules and regulations must be approved by the Attorney-General, and 4. When promulgated and published, shall have the force and effect of law.

It appears that the absence of any material requirement of the Act as regards rules and regulations would void such rule or regulation. It also appears that the rules and regulations promulgated must have general or universal appli-

Ch. 3) 

145 

EXCISE TAX 

cation, i.e., the Commissioner is not authorized to make specific rules and regulations to a particular case—other than methods of apportionment in certain cases. The Commissioner is given discretion in the matter of determining what may or may not be "net earnings" and his judgment is final, subject only to review by the courts in accordance with the provisions of Section 1790, et seq. of the Code. 

It may appear that the vesting of authority in the Commissioner to declare "net earnings" is an invalid delegation of legislative authority. However, since the taxpayer may appeal from the judgment of the Commissioner such a delegation of power appears to have received favorable decision by the court. See National Life and Accident Insurance Company V. Dempster, supra and cases there cited: 

In connection with this power vested in the Commissioner, attention is directed to: 

Regulation No. 7. 

Any taxpayer feeling aggrieved after paying his determined tax liability may file with this Department a written statement setting forth in detail his contentions with respect to the tax, and such taxpayer will be promptly notified upon final determination by the Commissioner. 

Commissioner May Sue for the Tax Due 

Law. Section 1324 as amended: 

Said Commissioner may, in the name of the State of Tennessee, institute suit or suits for the collection of said tax or any part thereof and for the penalty and interest imposed. 

In addition to the authority of the Commissioner to issue distress warrant for the collection of the excise tax, this section further authorizes him to institute suit in the name of the State for the collection of tax, penalty and interest or any part thereof. 

Examination of Books and Records- Law. Section 1325 as amended: 

Said Commissioner shall have access to all books and records of all such corporations and joint stock associations to enable him to ascertain the correctness of any fact or report made or herein required. 

This Section gives the Commissioner access to all books and records of those subject to the tax in order that he may

(Ch. 3  

ascertain the correctness of any fact or report made in connection with the excise tax. 

It is noted that this authority is confined to the "Commissioner" and is not given to the Commissioner or his duly authorized representative. However, the use of the word "Commissioner" as a practical matter, implies all duly authorized representatives of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. It is also noted that the Act prescribes no penalties for refusing the Commissioner or his representative access to such books and records. 

Appropriation for Administration— Law. 

Section 1326 as amended: 

Said Commissioner may expend so much of two and one-half per centum of the amount received hereunder each year as may be necessary to defray the expenses and cost of litigation arising in the administration of this Statute.

This Section deals entirely with appropriations for administration of the law, and is of no practical value, since the enactment of the 1937 General Appropriation Bill. 

Wilful Failure to File Report and Pay Tax-Mis demeanor 

Law. 

Section 1327 as amended: 

The wilful failure or refusal of any corporation or joint stock association to pay the tax or make reports as hereinabove required shall be a misdemeanor and subject to a fine of not less than ten dollars nor more than one thousand dollars.

Wilful failure or refusal to pay tax or make report required by the Act is a misdemeanor and, upon conviction, the taxpayer is subject to fine of from ten to one-thousand dollars.

Reports Confidential-Reciprocal Inspection-Power of Attorney 

Law. Section 1328 as amended: 

Except in accordance with proper judicial order or as otherwise required by law, it shall be unlawful for the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, and Deputy, Agent, Clerk, or other officer or employee to make known in any manner the amount of income or any particular set forth in any report or return required under this statute; provided, nothing herein shall be construed to prohibit the publication of statistics, so classified as to prevent the identification of particular reports or returns

Ch. 3) 147 

EXCISE TAX 

and the items thereof; or the use of such reports or returns by legal representatives of the state in any suit or suits for the collection of said tax or any part thereof, or for the penalty and interest imposed by this statute. A violation of any of the provisions of this section shall be a misdemeanor punishable by fine of not exceeding one thousand dollars, or by imprisonment not exceeding one year, or both, at the discretion of the court; provided, however, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may permit the Commissioner of Internal Revenue of the United States, or the proper officer of any state imposing a tax similar to that imposed by this statute, or the authorized representative of either such officer, to inspect the tax return of any corporation, or may furnish to such officer or his authorized representative an abstract of the return of any corporation or supply him with information concerning any item contained in any return or disclosed by the report of any investigation of any return; but such permission shall be granted or such information furnished to such officer or his representative, only if the statute or regulations of the United States or of such other state, as the case may be, grant substantially similar privileges to the Governor or the proper officer of this state charged with the administration of this statute. 

As a general rule, this Section is of little interest to taxpayers. The Section makes it unlawful for the Commissioner or any employee of the Department of Finance and Taxation to divulge any information contained in excise tax reports, however, your attention is directed to: 

Regulation No. 8. 

Excise tax reports are confidential and the information contained therein cannot be divulged. Therefore, legal representatives or other persons acting in behalf of corporations are required to present duly executed power of attorney before Excise Tax matters will be discussed with such representatives.
