INHERITANCE TAX RITANCE Section 1260, Subdivision 2; 

Kind of transfers taxable—

The transfers enumerated in subdivision 1 of above section shall be taxable if made- 

(a) By a will. 

(b) By statutes regulating descent and distribution of property upon the death of the owner. (c) If a resident, any property specified in paragraph (a) of subdivision 1 of above section; and, if a nonresident, any property specified in paragraph (b) of subdivision 1 of said section transferred by the decedent prior to and in contemplation of death and any transfer of any such property made by a person within two years prior to death, shall, unless the contrary be shown, be deemed to have been made in contemplation of death. Contemplation of death, as used in this statute, shall be taken to include that expectancy of death which actuates the mind of a person on the execution of his will, and in no wise shall said words be limited and restricted to that expectancy of death which actuates the mind of a person in making a gift causa mortis; and it is declared to be the intent and purpose of this statute to tax any and all transfers which are made in lieu of or to avoid the passing of the property transferred by testate or intestate laws. (d) If a resident, any property specified in paragraph (a) of subdivision 1 of above section; and if a nonresident, any property specified in paragraph (b) of subdivision 1 of above section transferred by the decedent prior to death by gift or grant intended to take effect in possession or enjoyment at or after death. (e) A transfer of property subject to any charge, estate or interest, determinable by the death of the decedent, or at any period ascertainable only by reference to the death of the decedent, shall be deemed to have been intended to take effect in possession or in enjoyment at or after death.

(Ch. 5 

(f) If any transfer of property specified in paragraphs (c), (d) or (e) of this subdivision was made for a valuable consideration, so much thereof as is the equivalent in money value of the money value of such present consideration received by the transferrer shall not be included, but the remaining portion shall be. (g) In case of any transfer of property specified in paragraph (e) of this subdivision, the increase accruing to any person or corporation upon the extinction or termination of such charge, estate or interest, shall be deemed a transfer of property taxable under the provisions of this statute. (h) Transfers under powers of appointment shall be taxable in like manner and to the same extent as if property of the testator or donor was transferred. 

Section 1261, Subdivision 3; 

Joint ownership; apportionment—

Whenever property was held jointly by the decedent and one or more persons as joint tenants or tenants by the entirety or otherwise or was deposited in banks or other depositories in the joint names of the decedent and one or more other persons and payable to one or more, or to the survivor or survivors, so that, upon the death of the decedent, the survivor or survivors became entitled to the immediate possession, ownership or enjoyment of such property, there shall be included for taxation such part as may be clearly shown to have belonged to decedent, and in the absence of such showing, then (a) A fractional part of the value of such property to be determined by dividing the value of the entire property by the number of persons in whose joint names it was held; provided, however, that if money or other evidences of indebtedness, so deposited was subject to the individual control, or to the appropriation or use by the decedent prior to death, such circumstances shall be deemed to be

Ch. 5) 323 

INHERITANCE TAX 

prima facie evidence of the individual ownership by the decedent of the entire amount and shall be taxable as such, unless the contrary be shown. 

If the decedent was a resident of this state, this subdivision shall apply only to the property specified in paragraph (a) of subdivision 1 of first section; or, if a nonresident, to the property specified in paragraph (b) of said subdivision 1.

Section 1261a, Subdivision 4: 

Life insurance taxable; when- 

If the decedent was a resident of this state, there shall be included in the gross estate the proceeds of insurance policies payable to named beneficiaries, or to his estate, or in such manner as to be subject to claims against his estate and to distribution as a part thereof; provided, however, that there shall be exempt from the provisions of this statute the proceeds of such policies as may be payable to Class A beneficiaries of the decedent, and/or to a trustee, contractual, appointive or by will for such, to the extent of forty thousand dollars; and, provided further, that there shall be exempt from the provisions of this law the proceeds of policies upon the life of a soldier, or former soldier, irrespective of the amount thereof, payable by the government of the United States known as "War Risk Insurance.”

This subdivision shall include the proceeds of insurance policies commonly known as "paid-up" contracts or “investment contracts" or "annuity contracts" or similar types or forms of policies, the surrender value of which was subject to the control of the decedent prior to death. 

Where life insurance, the proceeds of which are under the control of the decedent is left by him in such manner that the proceeds thereof cannot be subjected to the payment of his debts and where the proceeds of such insurance are received by beneficiaries thereof and are not subjected to the debts of the decedent, the fact that the decedent may have been insolvent and that a portion of his debts may re-

(Ch. 5 

main unpaid shall not affect the liability for inheritance tax upon such insurance. 

Section 1262, Subdivision 5; 

Revocable trusts The gross estate of a resident shall include property specified in paragraph (a) of subdivision 1 of first section, and the gross estate of a non-resident shall include property specified in paragraph (b) of such subdivision and section transferred by the decedent by deed of trust wherein he reserved to himself, or herself, alone or in conjunction with others, powers of revocation, alteration or amendment, upon the exercise of which such property would revert to the decedent, to the extent of the value of such property subject to such powers and with respect to which such powers remained unexercised. 

Section 1263, Subdivision 6; 

Property in lieu of commissions—

If property is transferred to executors or trustees in lieu of their commissions or allowances, the excess in value of the property so transferred above the amount of commissions or allowances which would be payable in the absence of such transfer, shall be taxable. 

Section 1264, Subdivision 7; 

Dower or Curtesy interest- The vesting in a wife of a dower interest upon the death of her husband, or in the husband of an interest as tenant by the curtesy upon the death of his wife or his right to succeed to the personal property of his wife dying intestate leaving no descendants surviving her, or any transfer of property in any other manner by operation of law upon the death of any person, shall be deemed a transfer taxable under this statute.

Ch. 5) 325 

INHERITANCE TAX Section 1265, Subdivision 1; 

Determination of net estate; methods- 

For the purpose of determining the net estate subject to tax, there shall be deducted from the value of the gross estate: 

(a) The value of all property taxable under this statute transferred to the United States, the State of Tennessee, or to any political subdivision thereof, any public institution therein for exclusively public purposes, or any corporation, society, association or trust formed for charitable, educational, or religious purposes; provided, however, that the property so transferred is to be used exclusively for one or more of such purposes; but no deduction shall be allowed on account of property transferred to any such beneficiary if any officer, member, shareholder or employee thereof shall receive, or be entitled to receive any benefit or pecuniary profit from the operation thereof, except reasonable compensation in effecting one or more of such purposes, or as beneficiaries of a strictly charitable purpose, or if the organization of any such corporation, society, association or trust for any of the foregoing avowed purposes be a mere guise or pretense for directly or indirectly making for it or any of its officers, members, shareholders or employees any other pecuniary profit, or if it be not in good faith organized or conducted for one or more of such purposes. 

(b) Taxes: 

(1) On real and tangible personal property within the State of Tennessee which were a lien at the date of death. (2) On intangible personal property of the decedent or on the income therefrom which constituted a personal obligation during his lifetime, or were a lien at date of death. (3) Federal income taxes accrued upon the income of the decedent at the date of death.

(Ch. 5 

(4) Death duties paid or payable to other jurisdictions on intangible personal property but no deduction shall be allowed for the payment of any Federal Estate taxes. (5) Special assessments which, at the time of decedent's death, were a lien on real property within the State of Tennessee. 

(c) Other Expenses. 

Actual funeral expenses; and all other amounts reasonably and actually expended, or contracted to be expended, for the purchase of a memorial, or monument to the decedent, if a resident of the State. (d) Expenses of administration, including compensation of executors, administrators, or trustees and their attorneys, actually allowed and paid, not in excess of lawful rates. When the claimed allowance is excessive, the Commissioner is authorized to reduce it to a reasonable amount for the purpose of computing the tax.

From the action of the Commissioner in reducing the claimed amount, an appeal may be taken to the Board provided for in Section 1277. (e) Debts of the decedent which constituted lawful claims against his, or her, estate at the date of death, provided that in the case of a resident decedent there shall not be allowed a debt secured by property outside of this state, except when the property by which the debt is secured is included in the measure of the tax hereby imposed, or except when such debt exceeds the value of the property securing it, in which case the excess may be deducted.

In the case of a transfer other than by will or intestate laws, the only deductions permitted shall be liens subject to which the transfer is made and transfer taxes paid or payable to other jurisdictions on intangible personal property. 

In the case of the estate of a non-resident, only such portion of the aforesaid deductions shall be allowed

Ch. 5) 327 

INHERITANCE TAX 

as is properly chargeable against the property the transfer of which is subject to taxation. 

Section 1266, Subdivision 2; 

Exemptions allowed- For the sole purpose of determining the net taxable estate under this law, there shall be allowed against the net estate a maximum single exemption of ten thousand dollars against that portion of the estate distributable to one or more beneficiaries of Class A and a maximum single exemption of one thousand dollars against that portion of the estate distributable to one or more beneficiaries of Class B; provided, that no exemption shall be allowed against the estate of a non-resident decedent and no exemption or deduction shall be made on account of dower or curtesy. 

The following named beneficiaries shall be included in: 

Class A; 

Husband, wife, son, daughter, lineal ancestor or lineal descendant, legally adopted child and lineal descendant of such adopted child. 

Class B; 

Any other relative, person, association or corporation not specifically designated in Class A. 

In the case of estates of non-residents, the exemptions in this sub-division 2 of this section shall be apportioned in the ratio that the value of the property included in the gross estate, to wit, property, the transfer of which is subject to the tax imposed hereby, bears to the value of all of the property that would have been included in the gross estate if the decedent had been a resident of this state; provided, that, in any event, such proportionate part of the exemption shall not be less than is permitted by the Constitution of the United States. 

Section 1267, Subdivision 3; 

Rates of tax- 

The tax imposed upon the value of the net taxable estate of a decedent, distributable in accordance with the classifi-

(Ch. 5 

cations, deductions, allowances and exemptions hereinbefore set out in this statute, shall be, respectively, at the following rates, to-wit:

Class A. 

1 per centum on amounts from $10,000.00 to $25,000.00. 

12 per centum on the next $25,000.00 or part thereof. 

3 per centum on the next $50,000.00 or part thereof. 

4 per centum on the next $200,000.00 or part thereof. 

5 per centum on the next $200,000.00 or part thereof. 

7 per centum of the excess over $500,000.00 or part thereof. 

Class B. 

5 per centum on amounts from $1,000.00 to $50,000.00. 

7 per centum on the next $50,000.00 or part thereof. 

9 per centum on the next $50,000.00 or part thereof. 

10 per centum on the next $50,000.00 or part thereof. 

12 per centum on the next $50,000.00 or part thereof. 

15 per centum on the excess over $250,000.00 or part thereof. 

Section 1268, Subdivision 4;

Conditional deductions; executory contracts— 

No deduction from the value of the property included in the gross estate shall be allowed on account of any claim against the estate arising from a contract made by the decedent and payable by its terms at or after death unless such claim is supported, in whole or in part, by a valuable consideration, in which event only so much thereof as is the equivalent in money value of the money value of the consideration received by the decedent shall be allowed as a deduction, but the remaining portion shall not be. 

Section 1269, Subdivision 5; 

Credits allowed; prior transfer tax—

If the gross estate include property upon the transfer of which to the decedent a tax was previously and within five years, imposed by this state, or property which can be definitely identified as having been received by the decedent

Ch. 5) 329 

INHERITANCE TAX 

in exchange for property upon which a tax was so imposed, a credit on account of such tax actually so previously paid shall be allowed against the tax imposed with respect to the particular property, but not to exceed the amount of tax imposed with respect to the property on the present transfer; provided, however, that the burden of identification shall be upon the person claiming such credit. 

The five year period shall be computed from the date of death of the prior decedent and not from the date of payment of such tax.

Section 1270, Subdivision 6; 

Life estate annuities; computation- 

The value of every future, contingent or limited estate, income, interest or annuity for any life or lives in being shall, so far as possible, be determined by the rule, method and standard of mortality and of value set forth in the actuaries combined experience tables of mortality with interest at six per centum per annum. The value of the interest remaining after any such temporary interest, shall be determined by deducting the computed value of the temporary estate from the value of the entire property in which such interest exists. Unless otherwise provided by the transferer, the tax on such temporary interests and remainders shall be payable out of the property in which such temporary interests and remainders exist. 

Section 1271, Subdivision 7;

Divested estates taxable— 

Where an estate or interest may be divested by the Act or omission of the transferee, it shall be taxed as if there were no possibility of divesting. 

Section 1272, Subdivision 8; 

Agreement as to values—

If it shall be impossible to compute the present value of any of the property transferred, or of any interest therein,

(Ch. 5 

or if the tax cannot be determined because of a contingency as to who will take it, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, with the written approval of the Attorney General, may enter into an agreement with the representatives of the estate or the transferees, or both, to compound the tax upon such terms as may be deemed equitable, and the payment of any amount agreed upon shall be in full satisfaction for the tax imposed by this statute and such amount shall be payable out of the property transferred. If such an agreement cannot be reached, the taxation of the property or interest shall be held in abeyance and the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall require the representatives of the estate or transferees, or both, to give bond for the prompt payment of the tax at such time as the value of the property or interest, of the transferees may be determined; and such tax shall bear interest as provided in subdivision 2 preceding. The amount of said bond shall be fixed and the sufficiency of the surety determined by the 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. 

Section 1273, Subdivision 1; 

Rules and regulations; administration— 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, hereinafter called the Commissioner, shall have full supervision of the administration and enforcement of this law and of the collection of all taxes imposed thereunder, and shall make such rules and regulations as may be necessary for its proper interpretation and enforcement, and he is empowered to call upon other departments of the state government for such information and assistance as he may deem necessary; provided, however, that the cost of administering this law shall not exceed three per centum of the total tax collection. 

The Commissioner shall have power to compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of evidence, by subpoena, to administer oaths and to take testimony in relation to any matter under this statute. 

Witnesses shall receive the same fees as are paid other witnesses in courts of record, such fees to be a part of the cost of administration.

Ch. 5) 331 

INHERITANCE TAX Section 1274, Subdivision 2; 

Employment of appraisers; duties- 

The Commissioner may designate such deputies, appraisers, agents and other assistants as may be necessary for carrying out the full purpose and intent of this law. 

Such deputies, appraisers, agents and assistants, so designated by the Commissioner, shall be empowered to represent the Commissioner in inventorying and appraising estates, examining the contents of safe deposit vaults and to perform such duties as are, by this statute, required of the Commissioner, including the power to issue subpoenas and administer oaths and shall make bonds for the faithful performance of their duties, such bonds to be in such amounts and with such surety or sureties as the Commissioner may prescribe. 

Section 1275, Subdivision 3; 

Duties of County Court Clerks— 

(a) It shall be the duty of the county court clerk of the county wherein an estate is administered by an executor, administrator or trustee, before letters of administration are issued by such court, to demand and require of such executor, administrator or trustee a bond, with good and sufficient security, in the penal sum of five hundred dollars, payable to the Commissioner, for the use and benefit of the state, and conditioned upon the payment within the time required by this statute of any tax assessed against the estate with which such fiduciary is chargeable; provided, however, that, if in the sound discretion of the county court clerk an estate distributable to beneficiaries of Class A is of less value than Ten Thousand Dollars, and an estate distributable to beneficiaries of Class B is of less value than One Thousand Dollars, such bond may be waived by the county court clerk; provided the reasons for such waiver be fully reported to the 

Commissioner.

(Ch. 5 

(b) The bond herein required of such fiduciary shall be demanded by the clerk, subject to the exceptions above named, notwithstanding the decedent may have directed that his, or her, executor, administrator or trustee serve without bond. (c) Upon the execution of such bond, the county court clerk shall forthwith deliver, or forward by mail, to the Commissioner a statement under his seal of office giving the name and date of death of the decedent and his address at time of death, the name and address of the executor, administrator or trustee qualified, together with his estimate of the gross value of the estate; provided; however, that the clerk shall be required to furnish such statement even though the bond may have been waived. (d) For this service, the county court clerk shall be allowed to demand and collect, in advance, five dollars, which fee shall be in addition to the usual and customary probate fees now allowed by law and shall be paid by the representative of the estate and may be deducted as a part of the costs of administration. (e) Any county court clerk who shall violate any of the provisions of subdivision 3 of this section shall be subject to a penalty of five hundred dollars, to be recovered by the Commissioner, for the benefit of the state, in any court of competent jurisdiction; provided, however, that the Commissioner may, in his discretion, waive or reduce the above-named penalty in any case to not less than one hundred dollars where there appears no manifest intent to evade the statute. 

Section 1276, Subdivision 4; 

Report forms; due date 

Upon receipt of the aforesaid bond and/or statement from the county court clerk, the Commissioner shall furnish the representative of the estate all necessary forms and information for the proper inventorying of the property of

Ch. 5) 333 

INHERITANCE TAX 

the estate and shall furnish such representative with a copy of this statute and all instructions and information promulgated for the guidance of such representative of the estate in the performance of the duties required of him by this statute.

Such executor, administrator or trustee shall within sixty days thereafter, prepare and file with the Commissioner a copy of the will, if will there be, and a sworn inventory of the gross estate and shall set forth therein each item of real and personal property separately, showing its full and actual cash value at the date of decedent's death, together with the names, addresses and relationships of the several beneficiaries, the allowable deductions in detail and the costs of administration, separately set forth; provided, however, that the Commissioner may, upon application of the executor, administrator or trustee showing good cause, grant sixty days' additional time within which the said sworn inventory may be filed. 

Section 1277, Subdivision 5; 

Appraisal and assessment; appeals—

Upon receipt of such sworn inventory from the executor, administrator or trustee, the Commissioner shall proceed to make an appraisal of the various items of the gross estate and to investigate deductions claimed by such representative of the estate, and shall, as soon thereafter as possible, notify the representative of the estate by mail of his appraisal and the assessment of the tax thereof. Such notice shall be sent by registered mail to the last known address of such representative and such mailing shall constitute good and sufficient notice; provided, however, the 

Commissioner shall give such other and further notice, if any, as may be necessary to comply with constitutional requirements.

In making said appraisal, the Commissioner shall direct his deputies, agents or assistants to investigate the valuation placed upon each item of the estate, with a view to determining its fullness and fairness, and, in the absence of written objection upon the part of the representative of the

(Ch. 5 

estate, his appraisal shall be final and binding upon the estate; provided, however, that such representative shall have the right to file with the Commissioner, within thirty days from the date of such appraisal, an appeal from his appraisal, addressed to a Board composed of the Governor, the Treasurer, and the Comptroller of the State, which said Board shall have authority to consider the exceptions filed, hear proof and determine the valuation in dispute, and the findings, by a majority vote, of said Board shall be conclusive as to all parties in interest, subject only to the constitutional right of review in the courts. 

When any executor, administrator or trustee shall neglect or refuse to file the sworn inventory required under Section 1276, the Commissioner is authorized to appraise the estate and to assess the tax upon the basis of any information available. Notice of such appraisal and tax assessment shall be given by the Commissioner in accordance with the previous provision of this section and the subsequent procedure thereafter with reference to an appeal from the appraisal and with reference to the collection of the tax shall be the same as in other cases. 

In the assessment of any tax when the sworn inventory has not been filed in accordance with Section 1276 there shall be added to the amount of tax found to be due, a penalty of five (5%) per cent. Notwithstanding that the assessment made by the Commissioner in the absence of the sworn inventory required, shall be altered or revised upon appeal or in litigation, a penalty of five (5%) per cent upon the Tax ultimately found to be due shall be added and collected in all cases when the sworn inventory is not filed. 

Section 1278, Subdivision 6; 

Date when property valued All property, real and personal, shall be appraised at its full and true value at the date of death of the decedent. 

Stocks and bonds listed on recognized exchanges shall be appraised by ascertaining their quoted value on the date of death of the decedent, or on the nearest business day of such exchange to such date.

Ch. 5) 335 

INHERITANCE TAX Section 1279, Subdivision 7; 

Tax liability; lien upon property- 

The tax imposed by this law shall be and remain a lien upon the property transferred, and upon all property acquired by the representative of the estate, or transferees, in exchange or substitution therefor, from the date of decedent's death, until the same is paid, but such lien shall not follow personal property after it has passed to a bona fide purchaser for value; provided, however, that the provisions of this subdivision shall not authorize any transfer without the consent of the Commissioner, if such consent be a prerequisite to the transfer thereof. 

The lien upon all real estate transferred, or any portion thereof, may be discharged by the payment of such amount of tax as the Commissioner may specify and require; provided, the lien shall expire and be void unless action is brought for its enforcement within two and one-half years from the date of administration, and within four years from the death of the decedent where no administration was granted.

Section 1280, Subdivision 8; 

Collection of tax The Commissioner shall collect the tax imposed by this law and deposit same in such depository, or depositories, as he may select, which shall have executed and filed with him a bond in an amount fixed by the Commissioner, signed by an approved surety company authorized to transact business in Tennessee, guaranteeing the safe keeping and delivery of such funds upon demand. 

In event it should become necessary to enforce the payment of any tax imposed by this statute by legal action in the courts, the Commissioner shall make use of the offices of the several district attorneys, such action to be taken under the supervision and direction of the attorney general. 

It shall be the duty of the Commissioner to keep detailed records of the tax collected and to make report thereof to the Comptroller of the Treasury not later than the fifteenth

(Ch. 5  

day of the months of January, April, July and October each year of such collections made during the preceding quarterly period, remitting with such reports the amount so reported, which shall be and become a part of the general fund of the State.

The Commissioner is empowered to make refund of any excess, erroneous or improper tax payment received by him out of the funds in his keeping to the estate from which it is received.

Section 1281, Subdivision 9; 

Inspection of tax returns- The Commissioner is empowered to prescribe such forms as may be necessary under the provisions of this law and shall keep such records as are indicated by good accounting practice.

The Commissioner may, by general regulations, prescribe how much and what portion of his records shall be open to the inspection of the public and how much and what portion shall be held as confidential, and may exchange information with the United States Government, or with other state jurisdictions under reciprocal arrangements made and approved by him.

Section 1282, Subdivision 1; 

Tax due and payable; when- 

The tax so imposed by this statute shall be due and payable six (6) months after the death of the transferee, but such tax may be paid sooner if assessment thereof has been completed and if the personal representative desires to make payment. The value of all property transferred to each class of beneficiary, or beneficiaries, shall be aggregated for the purpose of computing the tax and allowing the exemptions heretofore provided for in this Act. 

Section 1283, Subdivision 1; 

Delinquents; penalties and interest—

All taxes not paid on or before the due date (six (6) months after the death of the decedent) shall thereafter

Ch. 5) 337 

INHERITANCE TAX 

bear interest at the rate of six (6%) per cent per annum, which interest cannot be waived or excused. To all taxes not paid within one year after the death of the decedent there shall attach, in addition to interest, a penalty of onehalf of one per cent for each month of delinquency which penalty the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is authorized to waive for good cause shown when written application for such waiver is made prior to the attaching of penalty. 

Section 1284, Subdivision 3; 

Installment payments; when permissible—

When it is shown to the satisfaction of the Commissioner that payment at one time of the whole tax due from an estate would work a hardship upon the beneficiaries, or would necessitate the sale of any portion of the estate at a sacrifice, or at an inadequate price, the Commissioner is empowered to enter into an agreement with the representative of such estate for the payment of the tax due thereon in installments.

Should any installment payments extend beyond one year after the death of the decedent, interest thereon shall be charged at the rate of six (6%) per centum per annum from the date of death until paid.

Section 1285, Subdivision 4; 

Certificates and receipts; issuance of— 

Upon the payment of the whole tax imposed against an estate under this law, the Commissioner shall issue his receipt therefor in duplicate to the representative of the estate, one copy of which shall be filed in the office of the clerk of the court in which such estate was being administered, and no final accounting, or settlement, of such estate shall be made by said court prior to the filing of such receipt, or until the filing of a certificate by the Commissioner that no tax is due thereon; such receipt, or certificate, to be furnished by the Commissioner without cost to the estate or to the beneficiaries thereof.

(Ch. 5 

Upon the payment of a fee of one dollar to the Commissioner, which said fee shall accrue to the state, any person other than the representative of the estate shall be entitled to receive from the Commissioner a certificate to the effect that the tax upon any particular parcel, or tract, of real estate has been paid, and such certificate may be recorded in the office of the register of the county in which such real estate is situated, and it shall be conclusive proof that the tax applicable to such real estate has been paid and any lien thereon shall be thereby released. 

Section 1286, Subdivision 5; 

Non-resident lifetime transfers In the absence of administration in this state upon the estate of a non-resident decedent, the Commissioner may, at the request of any representative of such estate, duly appointed and qualified in the state of decedent's domicile, or at the request of any beneficiary of such estate, or at the request of a transferee or trustee under a transfer made during the lifetime of such non-resident decedent, determine whether or not any property within this state transferred by such non-resident, or forming a part of his estate, is subject to tax under this Statute, and the amount of same. 

The Commissioner's certificate as to the amount of such tax and his receipt therefor may be filed in the county court of the county in which such property is located, and shall be conclusive evidence of payment of the tax imposed by this law thereon. 

Section 1287, Subdivision 6;

Appointment of administrator; when- 

In order that the tax imposed herein may be expeditiously collected, if within six months after the death of any decedent, resident or non-resident, an executor does not qualify or an administrator is not appointed in Tennessee at the instance of other persons interested in the estate, then the Commissioner may apply to the proper county court for the appointment of an administrator of such

Ch. 5) 

339 

INHERITANCE TAX 

estate and it shall be the duty of such court to make such appointment forthwith.

Section 1288, Subdivision 1; 

Transfers prohibited unless reported— No person or persons, corporation or association, having in his, or its, possession or control, property of a decedent forming a part of his estate, or property transferred in any manner as to be subject to taxation under this statute, shall deliver or transfer the same to representatives of the estate of the decedent, or to any other person or persons, corporation or association, or upon their order or request, unless notice of the time and place of the intended transfer or delivery be served upon the Commissioner at least twenty days prior thereto; nor shall any person deliver or transfer any such property without retaining a sufficient portion or amount thereof to pay any tax and interest which such property may be subject to a lien under this statute, unless the Commissioner consents in writing to such transfer.

The prohibitions herein contained shall apply to the transfer by a corporation, association or joint stock company of the shares of its capital stock or other interest therein, including registered bonds or other registered securities. 

It shall be lawful for the Commissioner to examine the property at the time of delivery or transfer. 

Failure to serve such notice, or failure to allow such examination, or failure to retain a sufficient amount to pay the tax and interest, shall, unless the Commissioner consents to the transfer, render such person or persons, corporation or association, liable to the payment of the amount of the tax for which a lien is imposed upon such property by this statute, with interest thereon and the costs of any proceeding necessary for the enforcement of same in the courts of Tennessee; provided, that the penalty provided by this section shall not apply to any insurance company which pays the proceeds of any policy of insurance on the

(Ch. 5 

life of the decedent after notifying the Commissioner that such payment is to be made. 

Section 1289, Subdivision 2;

Safe deposit vaults; agreement pertaining to- 

No safe deposit company, trust company, bank, or other person engaged in the business of renting safe deposit vaults or other receptacles of similar character, shall rent any such vault or receptacle without first requiring all persons entitled to access thereto to agree in writing to notify the lessor of the death of any such person; and all persons having the right of access to any such safe deposit vault or receptacle upon the death of any other person having the right of access thereto before seeking access, shall notify the lessor of the death of such person. 

No lessor shall permit access to any safe deposit vault or receptacle by anyone after the death of any person who, at the time of his death, had the right of privilege of access thereto, either as principal, deputy, agent, co-tenant or otherwise, without notice to the Commissioner. 

At the time of opening any such vault or receptacle after the death of any person having the right of access thereto, the Commissioner shall have the right to be present, in person or by his representative, and to examine and inventory its contents.

Any violation of the provisions of this sub-division shall subject the violator to a penalty of five hundred dollars to be recovered by the Commissioner for the benefit of the state in any court of competent jurisdiction. 

Section 1290, Subdivision 3; 

Failure to file reports; fraud; penalties—

Failure or refusal to make any report or return provided for in this statute shall constitute a misdemeanor and shall subject the offender to a penalty of five hundred dollars to be recovered for the benefit of the state in an action brought by the Commissioner in any court of competent jurisdiction; provided, however, that upon the filing

Ch. 5) 341 

INHERITANCE TAX 

of such report or reports, the Commissioner may, in his discretion, waive or reduce the above named penalty to not less than one hundred dollars in any case where there appears no manifest intent to evade payment of the tax herein imposed, and the payment of any such penalty shall in no wise affect the liability for the tax, interest and any other penalties prescribed herein. 

The making of a false return or report or affidavit with intent to deceive, shall constitute the crime of perjury. 

Section 1291, Subdivision 4; 

Tax payment before distribution of estate- All taxes due by an estate under the provisions of this statute shall be paid by the executor, administrator or trustee out of the funds in his hands for distribution, and no part of the property of an estate subject to this tax shall be distributed until the tax thereon has been paid; provided, however, that such executor, administrator or trustee, may with the written consent of the Commissioner, be authorized to sell or transfer so much of the property of the estate as may be necessary to pay said tax. 

Section 1292, Subdivision 5; 

Executors, etc. liable for tax 

Executors, administrators and trustees shall be liable for all taxes payable on the estate, together with any interest or penalties herein provided for, until the same shall have been paid; provided, however, that in no case shall such executor, administrator or trustee be liable for a greater amount than was actually received by him. 

Section 1293, Subdivision 6;

Reports required from insurance companies- Every life insurance company or association doing business in this state, shall within ten days after the approval of proof of death of a person insured under a policy or policies, in such companies or association, give

(Ch. 5  

notice in writing to the Commissioner where the estate is being administered stating: (a) The date and amount of each policy. (b) The name and address of each beneficiary therein. (c) The time and manner of payment. 

Any insurance company doing business in the state, failing to comply with the provisions of this statute, shall thereby forfeit their charter in this state and their right to do business within the state. 

Upon certification from the insurance Commissioner, that any insurance company has failed or refused to comply with the provisions of this statute, the secretary of state shall forthwith cancel the charter of such company and shall immediately notify such insurance company that it is barred from doing further business in the state. 

Section 1294, Subdivision 1; 

Estate tax law not affected—

This statute shall in no wise be construed impliedly or expressly to repeal or modify the Tennessee estate tax law. 

Section 1295, Subdivision 1; 

Constitutionality of this Act- If any section, subdivision, clause or phrase of this statute is for any reason held to be unconstitutional such decision shall not affect the remaining portion of the statute. The legislature declares that it would have passed this statute and each section, subdivision, clause, phrase and sentence thereof, irrespective of the fact that any one or more of such section, subdivision, clauses, phrases or sentences be declared unconstitutional.

Nature of Tax- 

Law. Section 1259, Subdivision 1;

A tax is imposed for the general uses of the State, under the conditions and subject to the conditions and limitations hereinafter prescribed, upon transfers, in trust or otherwise, of the following property, or any interest therein or accrued income therefrom: (a) When the transfer is from a resident of this state: (1) Real property situated within this state. (2) Tangible personal property, except such as has an actual situs without this state. (3) All intangible personal property. (4) Proceeds of insurance policies, except as hereinafter provided. (b) When the transfer is from a non-resident of this state: (1) Real property situated within this state. (2) Tangible personal property which has an actual situs within this state.

The inheritance tax is a "privilege" tax imposed upon the privilege of acquiring property by succession. "It must be borne in mind that the tax is not upon the property, but the right or privilege of acquiring it by succession.' State v. Alston, 94 Tennessee 674. 

The tax is imposed, for State purposes only, upon the transfer of property in trust or otherwise, and upon the transfer of any interest therein or accrued income therefrom.

(Ch. 5 

The right to acquire property by succession is not a natural right and since such right or privilege to so acquire property is the creature of the State, it follows that the State may exact a reasonable tax for granting such privilege.

The taxable transfer of property is divided into two classes, as follows: 

(a) Residents: 

Transfer of the following property by residents of Tennessee is taxable: 

1. Real property (land and buildings) situated within Tennessee. 

2. Tangible personal property actually located within Tennessee. (Such as machinery, equipment, trucks, automobiles, merchandise, etc.). 

3. All intangible personal property. (Such as stocks, bonds, notes, mortgages, etc.). The situs of such property being the domicile of the owner. 

4. Proceeds of insurance policies. 

(b) Non-Residents: 

Transfer of the following property by non-residents of 

Tennessee is taxable. 

1. Real property (land and buildings) situated within Tennessee. 

2. Tangible personal property actually located within Tennessee. (Such as machinery, equipment, trucks, automobiles, merchandise, etc.). 

Intangible personal property transferred from a nonresident is not included in this group, and the transfer of such property is not subject to tax. 

Transfers Taxable 

Law. Section 1260, Subdivision 2; 

The transfers enumerated in subdivision 1 of above section shall be taxable if made (a) By will. (b) By statutes regulating descent and distribution of property upon the death of the owner. (c) If a resident, any property specified in paragraph (a) of subdivision 1 of above section; and, if a non-resident, any property specified in paragraph (b) of subdivision 1 of said section transferred by the decedent prior to and in contemplation of death and any transfer of any such property made by a person within two years prior to death, shall, unless the contrary be shown, be deemed to have been made in contemplation of death. Contemplation of death, as used in this statute, shall be taken to include that expectancy of death which actuates the mind of a person on the execution of his will, and in no wise shall said words be limited and restricted to that expectancy of death which

Ch. 5) 347 

INHERITANCE TAX 

actuates the mind of a person in making a gift causa mortis; and it is declared to be the intent and purpose of this statute to tax any and all transfers which are made in lieu of or to avoid the passing of the property transferred by testate or intestate laws. (d) If a resident, any property specified in paragraph (a) of subdivision 1 of above section; and if a non-resident, any property specified in paragraph (b) of subdivision 1 of above section transferred by the decedent prior to death by gift or grant intended to take effect in possession or enjoyment at or after death. (e) A transfer of property subject to any charge, estate or interest, determinable by the death of the decedent, or at any period ascertainable only by reference to the death of the decedent, shall be deemed to have been intended to take effect in possession or in enjoyment at or after death. (f) If any transfer of property specified in paragraphs (c), (d) or (e) of this subdivision was made for a valuable consideration, so much thereof as is the equivalent in money value of the money value of such present consideration received by the transferrer shall not be included, but the remaining portion shall be. (g) In case of any transfer of property specified in paragraph (e) of this subdivision, the increase accruing to any person or corporation upon the extinction or termination of such charge, estate or interest, shall be deemed a transfer of property taxable under the provisions of this statute. (h) Transfers under powers of appointment shall be taxable in like manner and to the same extent as if property of the testator or donor was transferred.

Property enumerated in subdivision 1 of Section 1259 is used as the measure of the privilege tax when transfer is made: 

(a) By Will (Testate) — 

The transfer of property by a valid will is liable for tax. 

There are several different kinds of wills and for this reason beneficiaries receiving property by will should determine whether the will devising such property is valid before paying inheritance tax. Under Section 8094, Williams 

Tennessee Code, a nuncupative will is invalid when the estate exceeds two hundred and fifty dollars unless certain statutory conditions are present, and the court holds that real estate cannot be devised by a nuncupative will; See 

Smith V. Thurman, 49 Tennessee 110. Executors and Administrators should use care to determine whether the property, passing to beneficiaries, passes by will or under the intestate statutes of Tennessee in order to correctly compute the tax to be paid.

(Ch. 5 

 (b) By Statute (Intestate)— 

The transfer of property belonging to persons dying intestate (without a will) is liable for the tax. The property of all persons dying intestate is subject to regulation by statute, Section 8380 et seq., Williams Tennessee Code. (c) In Contemplation of Death- The transfer of property made in contemplation of death is taxable. It is the purpose of this section of the Act to tax all transfers made in lieu of, or as a means of, avoiding the operation of the testate or intestate laws of Tennessee. 

Obviously, the unrestricted transfer of property by persons contemplating death would nullify the purpose of the law, therefore the Act deems the transfer, if made within two years prior to death, to be a transfer made in "contemplation of death" and subjects such transfer to tax. Attention is directed to the fact that this legal presumption is not conclusive and that the burden is placed upon the taxpayer to show that such transfer was in fact not made in contemplation of death. 

(d) To Take Effect in Possession or Enjoyment at or 

After Death The transfer of property made prior to death, possession and enjoyment of which is not effective until death of the owner, is liable for the tax, i. e., "A" transfers to his son "B,' "" a tract of land retaining possession until his death; upon the death of “A,” the value of the land would be taxable to "B." (e) In Remainder to Take Effect in Possession or Enjoyment at or After Death The transfer of property subject to an interest terminating upon the death of the owner, with remainder in fee to beneficiary, is liable for the tax, i. e., "A" transfers to "B" a certain interest in a tract of land so long as he ("A") lives, upon his death the land is to become the property, in fee, of ""'; in such a case "C" would be liable for the tax.

Ch. 5) 349 

INHERITANCE TAX (f) For Valuable Consideration Where the Property 

Has a Value in Excess of the Consideration- The transfer of property for a valuable consideration is not subject to the tax, provided, the consideration is adequate. However, should "A" makes a transfer of a farm to his son "B" for $500.00 and the farm was in fact worth $50,000.00, the difference or $49,500.00 would be taxable if such transfer was made in contemplation of death, or contingent upon the death of the transferer "A.' 

(g) Of Increase in Value After Termination of 

Charge, Estate or Interest The increase in the value of property passing to beneficiaries at the death of the owner after the termination of a charge, estate or interest, is taxable, i. e., the value of the property at the date of death is the measure of the tax. 

(h) Under Powers of Appointment— 

The transfer of property under powers of appointment are taxable just the same as if transfer was made by the testator or owner.

Property Held Jointly- Law. Section 1261, Subdivision 3; 

Whenever property was held jointly by the decedent and one or more persons as joint tenants by the entirety or otherwise or was deposited in banks or other depositories in the joint names of the decedent and one or more other persons and payable to one or more, or to the survivor, or survivors, so that, upon the death of the decedent, the survivor or survivors became entitled to the immediate possession, ownership or enjoyment of such property, there shall be included for taxation such part as may be clearly shown to have belonged to decedent, and in the absence of such showing, then (a) A fractional part of the value of such property to be determined by dividing the value of the entire property by the number of persons in whose joint names it was held; provided, however, that if money or other evidences of indebtedness so deposited was subject to the individual control, or to the appropriation or use by the decedent prior to death, such circumstances shall be deemed to be prima facie evidence of the individual ownership by the decedent of the entire amount and shall be taxable as such, unless the contrary be shown. 

If the decedent was a resident of this state, this subdivision shall apply only to the property specified in paragraph (a) of subdivision 1 of first section; or, if a nonresident, to the property specified in paragraph (b) of said subdivision 1.

(Ch. 5  

The transfer of property held jointly is liable for the tax upon the death of owner. 

Difficulty does not arise in connection with the taxability where the property transferred can be clearly shown to have belonged to the decedent, however, the determination of a particular interest in jointly owned property, in the absence of facts clearly indicating that portion of the property owned by the decedent, frequently presents a difficult problem. The Act provides that a decedent's interest is to be determined by dividing the value of the property by the number of joint owners; but, if the property consists of money or evidences of indebtedness and was subject to decedent's control, appropriation or use prior to death, the entire amount is subject to taxation unless the contrary can be established.

It occurs that considerable difficulty may be avoided and beneficiaries relieved of excessive taxation in this regard, through the proper drafting of stipulations in wills affecting jointly owned property. 

Life Insurance-- Law. Section 1261a, Subdivision 4; 

If the decedent was a resident of this state, there shall be included in the gross estate the proceeds of insurance policies payable to named beneficiaries, or to his estate, or in such manner as to be subject to claims against his estate and to distribution as a part thereof; provided, however, that there shall be exempt from the provisions of this statute the proceeds of such policies as may be payable to Class A beneficiaries of the decedent, and/or to a trustee, contractual, appointive or by will for such, to the extent of forty thousand dollars; and, provided further, that there shall be exempt from the provisions of this law the proceeds of policies upon the life of a soldier, or former soldier, irrespective of the amount thereof, payable by the government of the United States known as "War Risk Insurance.' 

This subdivision shall include the proceeds of insurance policies commonly known as "paid-up" contracts or "investment contracts' or 'annuity contracts" or similar types or forms of policies, the surrender value of which was subject to the control of the decedent prior to death. 

Where life insurance, the proceeds of which are under the control of the decedent is left by him in such manner that the proceeds thereof cannot be subjected to the payment of his debts and where the proceeds of such insurance are received by beneficiaries thereof and are not subjected to the debts of the decedent, the fact that the decedent may have been insolvent and that a portion of his debts may remain unpaid shall not affect the liability for inheritance tax upon such insurance. 

The proceeds of insurance policies of residents of Tennessee are to be included as a part of the gross estate of

Ch. 5) 351 

INHERITANCE TAX 

such resident decedent, however, the Act provides the following exemptions before tax computation: (a) $40,000.00 insurance payable to Class A beneficiaries of decedent or to a trustee, contractual, appointive or by will. (b) Proceeds of insurance upon the life of a soldier or former soldier, payable by the United States Government. 

This subdivision of the Act includes the proceeds of insurance payable as "paid up," "investment contracts," or "annuity contracts" and similar forms of insurance; provided, the surrender value of such policies was subject to the control of the decedent prior to death. 

In cases where insurance premiums have been paid by beneficiaries, in which policy the decedent had no control over, or interest therein, the proceeds from such policy does not constitute a taxable transfer of property upon the death of the decedent. See Werthan V. McCabe 164 Tennessee 611.

The transfer or inheritance tax applies to the proceeds of all insurance policies, in excess of $40,000.00 when such proceeds are devised to Class A beneficiaries, even though such policies were in force prior to the passage of the Act. 

See State, ex rel V. Cain, 162 Tennessee 213.

The last paragraph of this subdivision was inserted by amendment, Chapter 129, Acts of 1937, and applies to certain insolvent estates, where proceeds from insurance exceeds the statutory exemption. 

Revocable Trusts— Law.

Section 1262, Subdivision 5; 

The gross estate of a resident shall include property specified in paragraph (a) of subdivision 1 of first section, and the gross estate of a nonresident shall include property specified in paragraph (b) of such subdivision and section transferred by the decedent by deed of trust wherein he reserved to himself, or herself, alone or in conjunction with others, powers of revocation, alteration or amendment, upon the exercise of which such property would revert to the decedent, to the extent of the value of such property subject to such powers and with respect to which such powers remained unexercised. 

In addition to property set forth in paragraphs (a) and (b) subdivision 1, of Section 1259, the gross estate is to include all property of the decedent transferred by deed of trust in which the decedent reserves the right to alter,

amend, or revoke such transfer. It should be noticed that only the value remaining after such transfer is revoked, is subject to the tax. 

Transfers in Lieu of Commissions- 

Law. Section 1263, Subdivision 6. 

If property is transferred to executors or trustees in lieu of their commissions or allowances, the excess in value of the property so transferred above the amount of commissions or allowances which would be payable in the absence of such transfer, shall be taxable. If A transfers property, prior to death, to the X Bank as compensation or in lieu of commissions or allowances, (the bank having been named in the will of A to act as executor or trustee of his estate) the value of such property being in excess of the amount of commissions or allowances payable, such excess is a taxable transfer of property. Section 1264, Subdivision 7; $5,000.00 2,000.00 $3,000.00

The vesting in a wife of a dower interest upon the death of her husband, or in the husband of an interest as tenant by the curtesy upon the death of his wife or his right to succeed to the personal property of his wife dying intestate leaving no descendants surviving her, or any transfer of property in any other manner by operation of law upon the death of any person, shall be deemed a transfer taxable under this statute.

Under this section of the Act, the dower interest of the wife upon death of the husband, and the interest of the husband as tenant by the curtesy upon the death of the wife, is a taxable transfer of property. 

The Supreme Court construing this Act of 1893, Shannon's Code, Section 724, as amended by Chapter 479, Acts of 1909, held that neither the year's support nor dower is subject to the tax; "As stated heretofore, she does not inherit from her husband, but derives her right by virtue of her marriage, which is consummated upon her husband's death, and becomes an incumbrance upon the inheritance of the heirs at law, and is, to that extent, an interest adverse to the inheritance from the husband.' Crenshaw, et al. V. Moore, 124 Tennessee 528.

Ch. 5) 353 

INHERITANCE TAX 

The Court construing Chapter 46, Acts of 1919, held in accordance with the rule laid down in Crenshaw, et al V. 

Moore, supra; "In 37 A. L. R. page 541, will be found a note citing numerous cases holding that dower or the widow's statutory right is not subject to a succession tax. Tennessee is classified with the States so holding, citing 

Crenshaw V. Moore, supra. Opinions in this and other States recognize that the homestead right is a creature of the Constitution and that this and the dower right pass to the wife, not by transfer from the deceased husband, but by right of marriage and by statutes declaratory of the common law." State ex rel McCabe V. Clayton, 162 Tennessee 368.

Attention is especially drawn to the provisions of Section 1264 of the present Act. Under this Act, it is mandatory "Dower interests-interest as tenant by the curtesy-or any transfer of property in any other manner by operation of law upon the death of any person, shall be deemed a transfer taxable under this statute.'' 

In the absence of court decision to the contrary, it appears that dower and the interest as a tenant by the curtesy is taxable.

Deductions— Law. Section 1265, Subdivision 1; 

For the purpose of determining the net estate subject to tax, there shall be deducted from the value of the gross estate: (a) The value of all property taxable under this statute transferred to the United States, the State of Tennessee, or to any political subdivision thereof, any public institution therein for exclusively public purposes, or any corporation, society, association or trust formed for charitable, educational, or religious purposes; provided, however, that the property so transferred is to be used exclusively for one or more of such purposes; but no deduction shall be allowed on account of property transferred to any such beneficiary if any officer, member, shareholder or employee thereof shall receive, or be entitled to receive any benefit or pecuniary profit from the operation thereof, except reasonable compensation in effecting one or more of such purposes, or as beneficiaries of a strictly charitable purpose, or if the organization of any such corporation, society, association or trust for any of the foregoing avowed purposes be a mere guise or pretense for directly or indirectly making for it or any of its officers, members, shareholders or employees any other pecuniary profit, or if it be not in good faith organized or conducted for one or more of such purposes. (b) Taxes: (1) On real and tangible personal property within the State of Tennessee which were a lien at the date of death. (2) On intangible personal property of the decedent or on the income therefrom which constituted a personal obligation during his lifetime, or were a lien at date of death. (3) Federal income taxes accrued upon the income of the decedent at the date of death.

(Ch. 5  

(4) Death duties paid or payable to other jurisdictions on intangible personal property but no deduction shall be allowed for the payment of any Federal Estate taxes. (5) Special assessments which, at the time of decedent's death, were a lien on real property within the State of Tennessee. 

(c) Other Expenses: 

Actual funeral expenses; and all other amounts reasonably and actually expended, or contracted to be expended, for the purchase of a memorial, or monument to the decedent, if a resident of the State. (d) Expenses of administration, including compensation of executors, administrators, or trustees and their attorneys, actually allowed and paid, not in excess of lawful rates. When the claimed allowance is excessive, the Commissioner is authorized to reduce it to a reasonable amount for the purpose of computing the tax. 

From the action of the Commissioner in reducing the claimed amount, an appeal may be taken to the Board provided for in Section 1277. (e) Debts of the decedent which constituted lawful claims against his, or her, estate at the date of death, provided that in the case of a resident decedent there shall not be allowed a debt secured by property outside of this state, except when the property by which the debt is secured is included in the measure of the tax hereby imposed, or except when such debt exceeds the value of the property securing it, in which case the excess may be deducted. 

In the case of a transfer other than by will or intestate laws, the only deductions permitted shall be liens subject to which the transfer is made and transfer taxes paid or payable to other jurisdictions on intangible personal property.

In the case of the estate of a non-resident, only such portion of the aforesaid deductions shall be allowed as is properly chargeable against the property the transfer of which is subject to taxation. 

From the "gross estate" of the decedent, the following deductions are allowed in computing the "net estate." 

1. The value of property transferred to the United States. 

2. The value of property transferred to the State of Tennessee. 

3. The value of property transferred to political sub divisions of Tennessee. 

4. The value of property transferred to public institutions for exclusively public purposes. 

5. The value of property transferred to any corporation, society, association or trust organized for charitable, educational, or religious purposes, but no part or benefit, except reasonable compensation, can enure to any person or employee thereof. 

6. All taxes due or which were a lien at date of death, except Federal Estate taxes. 

7. Actual funeral expenses of decedent. 

8. If a resident, actual cost or contracted cost of a monument or memorial for the decedent.

Ch. 5) 355 

INHERITANCE TAX 

9. Reasonable administration expense, and the Commissioner is authorized to reduce this deduction should it be unreasonable. Administrative expenses must be actually paid or allowed by the court before deduction can be sustained. 

10. Debts constituting lawful claims against the estate of the decedent. Debts of residents secured by property located outside of Tennessee are not deductible unless the property is listed as a part of the gross estate. If the debt exceeds the value of the property the excess is deductible.

Debts of non-residents are deductible in the same proportion as the property securing such debt is taxable. 

Exemptions- Law. Section 1266, Subdivision 2; 

For the sole purpose of determining the net taxable estate under this law, there shall be allowed against the net estate a maximum single exemption of ten thousand dollars against that portion of the estate distributable to one or more beneficiaries of Class A and a maximum single exemption of one thousand dollars against that portion of the estate distributable to one or more beneficiaries of Class B; provided, that no exemption shall be allowed against the estate of a non-resident decedent and no exemption or deduction shall be made on account of dower or curtesy.

The following named beneficiaries shall be included in: 

Class A; 

Husband, wife, son, daughter, lineal ancestor or lineal descendant, legally adopted child and lineal descendant of such adopted child. 

Class B; 

Any other relative, person, association or corporation not specifically designated in Class A. 

In the case of estates of non-residents, the exemptions in this subdivision 2 of this section shall be apportioned in the ratio that the value of the property included in the gross estate, to-wit, property, the transfer of which is subject to the tax imposed hereby, bears to the value of all the property that would have been included in the gross estate if the decedent had been a resident of this state; provided, that, in any event, such proportionate part of the exemption shall not be less than is permitted by the Constitution of the United States. 

Beneficiaries are divided into two classes:

Class A. Beneficiaries include: 

1. Husband. 

2. Wife. 

3. Son.

(Ch. 5 

 4. Daughter 5. Lineal Ancestor 

6. Lineal Descendant 

7. Legally adopted child 

8. Lineal descendant of legally adopted child.

Class B. Beneficiaries include: 

All other relations, persons, corporations, or associations not designated in Class A. 

Before the exemption is applied to the net estate the following facts must be ascertained. (a) Correct amount of the "gross estate.' (b) Correct amount of "deductions'' allowed by law. (c) Beneficiaries under the will or intestate laws must be classified in groups A or B. (d) Determination of that portion of the "net estate' passing to Class 

A beneficiaries. (e) Determination of that portion of the "net estate" passing to Class 

B beneficiaries.

From the aggregate amount of the "net estate" passing to Class A beneficiaries, an exemption of $10,000.00 is allowed; and from the aggregate amount of the "net estate" passing to Class B beneficiaries, an exemption of $1,000.00 is allowed. In this regard, it should be noted that the exemptions authorized do not apply to each beneficiary but to all beneficiaries within the class. See State, ex rel 

Thomason V. Branham, et al, 143 Tennessee 292.

The last paragraph of this section of the Act provides for the apportionment of exemption in case of estates of non-residents. Such apportionment is to be made upon the ratio of total property everywhere (which would be taxable if such nonresident was a resident of Tennessee) to the transfer of property located in this State. 

To illustrate: 

A resident of Kentucky dies testate owning property in Kentucky and Tennessee. The gross estate discloses property valued at $100,000.00 of which $50,000.00 is in Tennessee. The entire property is left to 

Class A beneficiaries.

The first paragraph states: 

"Provided, that no exemption shall be allowed against the estate of a non-resident decedent and no exemption or deduction shall be made on account of dower or curtesy." 

The last paragraph states: 

In the case of estates of non-residents, the exemptions in this subdivision shall be apportioned in the ratio that the value of the property in the gross estate etc. etc."'

It would be decidedly unfair to not allow exemptions to non-residents and it is understood that the practice of the department is to allow exemptions in the apportioned ratio as stated in the last paragraph of Section 1266. 

Tax Rates- 

Law. 

Section 1267, Subdivision 3;

The tax imposed upon the value of the net taxable estate of a decedent, distributable in accordance with the classifications, deductions, allowances and exemptions hereinbefore set out in this statute, shall be, respectively, at the following rates, to-wit:

Class A. 

1 per centum on amounts from $10,000.00 to $25,000.00. 

12 per centum on the next $25,000.00 or part thereof. 

3 per centum on the next $50,000.00 or part thereof. 

4 per centum on the next $200,000.00 or part thereof. 

5 per centum on the next $200,000.00 or part thereof. 

7 per centum of the excess over $500,000.00 or part thereof. 

Class B. 

5 per centum on amounts from $1,000.00 to $50,000.00. 

7 per centum on the next $50,000.00 or part thereof. 

9 per centum on the next $50,000.00 or part thereof. 

10 per centum on the next $50,000.00 or part thereof. 

12 per centum on the next $50,000.00 or part thereof. 

15 per centum on the excess over $250,000.00 or part thereof. 

The above rates apply to the value of the "net estate" transferable in accordance with the will of the decedent or

(Ch. 5 

under the intestate laws of the State. The tax is to be paid or withheld before transfer or distribution is made.

Unallowable Deductions- Law. Section 1268, Subdivision 4; 

No deduction from the value of the property included in the gross estate shall be allowed on account of any claim against the estate arising from a contract made by the decedent and payable by its terms at or after death unless such claim is supported, in whole or in part, by a valuable consideration, in which event only so much thereof as is the equivalent in money value of the money value of the consideration received by the decedent shall be allowed as a deduction, but the remaining portion shall not be.

Claims against the estate arising from contracts made by the decedent payable at death are not deductible, however, if under the terms of such a contract a valuable consideration passes to the decedent, prior to death, for the transfer of property at or after death, the value of such consideration may be deducted.

It appears that transfer made by contracts, contingent upon death, are conclusively deemed to be transfers in ❝contemplation of death" and that only the money value of the consideration passing to decedent may be deducted in computing the net estate. 

Tax Credits— 

Law. 

Section 1269, Subdivision 5;

If the gross estate include property upon the transfer of which to the decedent a tax was previously and within five years, imposed by this state, or property which can be definitely identified as having been received by the decedent in exchange for property upon which a tax was so imposed, a credit on account of such tax actually so previously paid shall be allowed against the tax imposed with respect to the particular property, but not to exceed the amount of tax imposed with respect to the property on the present transfer; provided, however, that the burden of identification shall be upon the person claiming such credit. 

The five year period shall be computed from the date of death of the prior decedent and not from the date of payment of such tax. 

This section permits a deduction from the inheritance tax shown to be due by Class A or Class B beneficiaries under certain conditions; viz: 

1. The gross estate of the decedent must include property the transfer of which has been previously taxed. 

2. The tax upon such property must have been imposed by Tennessee during a preceding period of five years; computed from the date of death of a prior decedent.

Ch. 5) 359 

INHERITANCE TAX 

3. The property used as a measure of the tax previously paid must be definitely identified; the burden of identification is upon the person claiming such credit. 

4. The tax credit cannot exceed the amount of tax imposed upon the same property under the present law. 

Usually, little difficulty arises in connection with the determination of inheritance tax credits. See Bank of Commerce & Trust Company V. McLemore, 162 Tennessee 137.

Computation Life Estates, Annuities, etc.- Law. Section 1270, Subdivision 6; 

The value of every future, contingent or limited estate, income, interest or annuity for any life or lives in being shall, so far as possible, be determined by the rule, method and standard of mortality and of value set forth in the actuaries combined experience tables of mortality with interest at six per centum per annum. The value of the interest remaining after any such temporary interest, shall be determined by deducting the computed value of the temporary estate from the value of the entire property in which such interest exists. Unless otherwise provided by the transferer, the tax on such temporary interests and remainders shall be payable out of the property in which such temporary interests and remainders exist. 

In computing the value of future estates, etc. the rule, method and standard of mortality set forth in the actuaries combined experience tables are to be used as far as possible. 

The table referred to may be found at page 590, volume 7, Williams Tennessee Code. 

To more clearly illustrate the method of computation, the following example is given: "A" dies testate January 15, 1935. At the time of his death "B"his son age 40, inherits property worth $200,000.00 for life, with remainder to "C," the only son of "B" (whose age is 15 yrs at the time of death of "A") in fee.

The computation of the life estate would be as follows: 

1. Value of property at death of "A" (principal).. 

$200,000.00 

2. 72.360% of $200,000.00 equals value of life estate of "B" $144,720.00 

3. Value of property at death of "A". 

4. Value of life estate of “B”.... 

5. Value of remainder estate to "C", .$200,000.00 144,720.00 .$ 55,280.00
