Definitions- Law. Section 1296. 

As used in this statute, the terms shall be construed as follows: (a) This statute shall be known and may be cited as the "Tennessee Estate Tax Law." (b) The term "federal estate tax" means the tax imposed by the federal revenue act of 1926, as amended by the federal revenue act of 1928 (which acts are hereinafter referred to as the revenue act of 1926''). 66 (c) The term "decedent'' means any person who at the time of his death is a resident of the State of Tennessee. (d) The term "executor' includes administrator, and any other person liable for the payment of the "federal estate tax." (e) The term "estate means the entire estate, and/or interest therein, of said decedent, which is subject to or liable for the payment of the "federal estate tax" before deducting any losses or exemptions in accordance with said revenue act of 1926. (f) The term "Tennessee estate tax” means the tax imposed by this statute. (g) The term "" "Tennessee estate" means such part of said estate, or interest therein, the transfer whereof is within the power of the State of Tennessee to subject to the Tennessee estate tax. (h) The term "non-taxable property' "" means all parts of said estate or interest therein other than the Tennessee estate. (i) The term "credit" means the maximum credit for any estate, inheritance, legacy, or succession taxes paid to any State or Territory or the District of Columbia, allowable with respect to the gross federal estate tax by section 301 (b) of said revenue act of 1926; said maximum credit, however, to be reduced in the proportion which the amount of the non-taxable property bears to the amount of the entire estate of the decedent. (j) The term "state taxes" means the aggregate estate, inheritance, succession, collateral inheritance and/or legacy taxes paid to any state, territory or the District of Columbia including also such taxes of any of the above kinds as are imposed by the state of Tennessee other than the Tennessee estate tax imposed by this statute, allowable in computing the maximum credit under said section 301 (b) of said revenue act of 1926, except such taxes of any of the above kinds or with respect to nontaxable property of the decedent.

Subsections (a) through (h) are deemed sufficiently clear and comment is unnecessary.

(Ch. 6 

Subsection (i)

Credit is given for all estate and inheritance tax liability allowable as a deduction in computing the Federal 

"Estate Tax" under Section 301 (b), Revenue Act of 1926, excluding Tennessee Estate tax; however, such credit must be reduced in the proportion which the amount of the nontaxable property in Tennessee bears to the entire estate. 

Section 301 (b) of the Federal Revenue Act of 1926 is as follows: 

(b) The tax imposed by this section shall be credited with the amount of any estate, inheritance, legacy, or succession taxes actually paid to any State or Territory or the District of Columbia, in respect of any property included in the gross estate. The credit allowed by this subdivision shall not exceed 80 per centum of the tax imposed by this section, and shall include only such taxes as were actually paid and credit therefor claimed within three years after the filing of the return required by Section 304."' 

Subsection (j)

The term "State taxes" includes only those items allowable as a deduction in computing the Federal "Estate Tax" liability but does not include the Tennessee "Estate tax."

Imposition and Computation of Tax- Law. Section 1297. 

In addition to any inheritance, succession and/or estate tax or taxes imposed by the State of Tennessee under the authority of any other statute or statutes, a Tennessee estate tax is imposed for the exclusive use of the state upon the transfer of the Tennessee estate of every decedent, the amount of which Tennessee estate tax shall be equal to the extent, if any, of the excess of the credit over the aggregate of state taxes, payable by or out of the Tennessee estate of the decedent, or any part thereof; provided, however, that such Tennessee estate tax imposed shall in no case exceed the extent to which its payment will affect a saving or diminution in the amount of the Federal estate tax, payable by or out of the estate of the decedent had this statute not been enacted. 

The Tennessee "estate tax" is imposed, in addition to the inheritance tax, for the exclusive use of the State. 

Counties and Cities are prohibited from levying a similar tax.

The amount upon which this tax is imposed is 80% of the Federal "estate tax" liability less inheritance taxes paid the State of Tennessee and estate and inheritance taxes paid to other states. To more clearly illustrate the computation, the following example is given:

Ch. 6) 477 

ESTATE TAX 1. Federal "Estate Tax" liability 

$150,000.00 

2. 80% of $150,000.00 120,000.00 

3. Tax Credits: 

(a) Tennessee inheritance tax $25,000.00 (b) Inheritance and estate taxes paid other states 35,000.00 60,000.00 

4. Tennessee "Estate Tax” liability $ 60,000.00

There cannot be any Tennessee "Estate Tax," unless a Federal Estate tax liability exists and the Tennessee tax cannot exceed 80% of the Federal tax. 

When Tax Payable and Interest Charged- Law. Section 1298. 

The Tennessee estate tax shall be payable at the same time or times at which the Federal Estate tax is payable and shall bear interest, if any, at the same rate and for the same period as such federal estate tax. 

The Tennessee tax is payable at the same time the tax is paid or becomes payable to the Federal Government. 

Subsection (a) of Section 305, Revenue Act of 1926 is as follows: 

"(a) The tax imposed by this title shall be due and payable fifteen months after the decedent's death, and shall be paid by the executor to the Collector."

Attention is drawn to the fact that if the tax is not paid within the time prescribed, the tax due shall bear interest at the rate of 6%. (See subsection (c) of Section 305, Revenue Act of 1926) Tax Payable to Commissioner- Law. Section 1299. 

The Tennessee estate tax shall be charged upon the entire Tennessee estate of the decedent; and the executor shall pay same to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and shall file with such Commissioner an affidavit showing: (1) The amount of the federal estate tax before allowing the maximum credit for taxes of any of the kinds as provided in section 301 (b) of said revenue act of 1926; (2) The proportion of nontaxable property to the entire estate, referred to in section 1296; (3) The amount of State taxes; (4) The amount of any additional taxes allowable in computing the federal estate tax of the decedent;

(Ch. 6 

(5) The amount of the Tennessee estate tax; (6) The amount of interest, if any, paid on such federal estate tax and the period covered by such interest, together with the amounts, if any, of any of said items theretofore paid and a duplicate of the federal estate tax return filed or being filed by him. 

The tax is payable to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and it is mandatory that an affidavit, containing the information set forth in this section, be filed at the time the tax is paid.

Commissioner to Account for Taxes Collected- 

Law. Section 1300. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall account to the Comptroller for all moneys so collected monthly (less not more than two and one half per cent thereof for expenses of administration) who shall receipt therefor and forthwith pay over to the State Treasurer all moneys thus received, who shall place same to the credit of the general fund; provided; however, that the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall retain in his hands at all times such a sum, as in his judgment, shall be sufficient to enable him to pay promptly all claims for refunds as provided for in section 1301 and 1306. 

This section of the law is not applicable. Sections 28 and 29 of Chapter 33, Public Acts of 1937, as amended, relates to the handling and accounting for taxes collected. 

All taxes collected by, or paid to the Commissioner, are deposited daily to the credit of the State Treasurer in 

State depositories.

Additional Taxes-Refund of Excess- Law. Section 1301. 

If the amount of federal estate tax shall, upon final determination of same, be increased or decreased as affecting an estate, the transfer of any part whereof is taxable hereunder subsequent to the payment of the Tennessee estate tax, the said Tennessee estate tax imposed shall be changed accordingly. Any additional estate tax shall be payable at the same time or times at which the additional federal estate tax is payable. 

In the event that there shall be a decrease in said federal estate tax, said executor shall file with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation an affidavit in such form as is prescribed by the said Commissioner, setting forth: (a) The amount of federal estate tax as originally computed; (b) The amount of said federal estate tax as revised and decreased; (c) The amount of Tennessee estate tax theretofore paid and date of payment; (d) The amount of Tennessee estate tax properly payable in view of such revision and decrease of federal estate tax. 

With said affidavit there shall also be filed: (a) A certificate or other evidence from the Bureau of Internal Revenue showing the amount of federal estate tax as so revised and decreased; (b) A certified copy of the affidavit filed with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation as provided in section 1299;

Ch. 6) 

479 

ESTATE TAX 

(c) A duplicate receipt by said Commissioner of Finance and Taxation for the Tennessee estate tax theretofore paid, showing date of payment. (d) Such other evidence as said Commissioner may require in order to enable him to determine the Tennessee estate tax, properly payable, and the amount, if any, of any refund due. 

Said Commissioner shall thereupon cause to be paid to said executor from the fund retained by him, as provided in section 1299, the amount of refund found to be due, together with interest thereon at the rate of six per cent, from the date of payment of the Tennessee estate tax; and if the fund retained by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall be insufficient, he shall retain from the next subsequent receipts of the Tennessee estate tax and pay to the executor such amount as will be necessary to make the said refund, or if the executor shall demand, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall direct the Comptroller to draw his warrant in the amount of such refund or unpaid balance thereof. 

Upon the final determination of the Federal "Estate Tax" liability by the Bureau of Internal Revenue, the executor is required to pay the Tennessee "estate tax" based upon the final assessment made by the Federal authorities. 

If such change reflects an excessive payment to Tennessee, claim for refund should be immediately filed with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, supported by the statement and affidavit required by this section. 

As regards refunds, attention is drawn to Chapter 167, Public Acts of 1935, which provides: "Any claim for refund by the State of taxes or revenues alleged to have been erroneously or illegally paid shall be filed with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation supported by proper proof within one year from the date of payment, otherwise the taxpayer shall not be entitled to refund and said claim for refund shall be barred." 

Distribution and Reimbursement of Tax- 

Law. Section 1302. 

If the Tennessee estate tax or any part thereof is paid by, or collected out of that part of the Tennessee estate passing to or in possession of, any person other than the executor or administrator in his capacity as such, such person shall be entitled to reimbursement out of any part of the Tennessee estate, still undistributed or paid, a just and equitable contribution by the person whose interest in the estate of the decedent would have been reduced if the tax had been paid before the distribution of the Tennessee estate, or whose interest is subject to equal or prior liability for the payment of taxes, debts, or other charges against the 

Tennessee estate.

The estate tax is payable by the executor from the estate and is to be apportioned equitably among the beneficiaries; if, however, the entire tax is paid from the portion of the estate of one beneficiary, reimbursement is

(Ch. 6  

authorized and is a prior liability against the interest of other beneficiaries.

Repeal of Title III. Revenue Act of 1926 Voids Tennessee Estate Tax- Law. Section 1303. 

Except as hereinafter provided, the statute shall become of no effect in respect to the Tennessee estate of persons who die subsequent to the effective date of the repeal of title III. of the Revenue Act of 1926 or of the provisions thereof allowing the credit. 

Should Title III. of the Federal Revenue Act of 1926, or any section thereof, be repealed, this statute becomes void as to persons dying after such repeal. 

Amendments to Federal Revenue Act of 1926Law. Section 1304. 

If said Title III. of said Revenue Act of 1926 shall be amended or if said title be repealed and an Act (hereinafter referred to as "substituted act') enacted by Congress imposing an estate, inheritance, succession and/or legacy tax in lieu of the tax imposed by said title III. then as to the Tennessee estate of decedents affected by such amendment or by such substituted act, the terms as defined by section 1296 shall relate to the provisions of said Title III. as amended, or of said substi tuted act, as the case may be, and the Tennessee estate tax as to such Tennessee estates shall be computed, imposed and paid accordingly. 

If said Title III. of said revenue act of 1926 is repealed and a substituted act, as above defined, is enacted, then section 1303 shall relate to the repeal of such substituted act. Said section 1303 shall also relate to the enactment of any amendment either to said Title III. or such substituted act, whereby the allowance of the maximum credit to the extent provided in said Title III. or to any other extent, shall be finally repealed. 

The amendment or repeal of Title III. of the Federal 

Revenue Act of 1926 automatically amends or repeals the provisions of this Act. 

Effective Date of Act- Law. Section 1305. 

(a) The provisions of this statute shall apply to the Tennessee estate of all decedents dying after December 14, 1929. (b) The provisions of this statute shall also apply to any Tennessee estate with respect to which the Federal estate tax has not been paid at that time.

The Act applies to the Tennessee estate of all decedents dying after December 14, 1929. It also applies to estates upon which the Federal tax was not paid prior to that date.

Ch. 6) 481 

ESTATE TAX Refund of Tax on Credit Disallowed by Federal Gov ernment- 

Law. Section 1306. 

If the Federal Government should refuse to allow a credit, or should collect the amount of a credit previously allowed by it for the Tennessee estate tax, with respect to the Tennessee estate of any person dying before the said effective date, then any Tennessee estate tax actually paid hereunder to the State of Tennessee, in any such case, shall be refunded by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation as herein before provided in sections 1301 and 1299 et seq.

In the event the Federal Government refused to allow a tax credit resulting in the excessive collection of Tennessee estate tax, such excess is to be refunded by the State. 

Provisions of Federal Revenue Act of 1926 Adopted— Law. Section 1307. 

In the application of this statute, the provisions of Title III. of the 

Revenue Act of 1926, or any amendment thereto, or of any substituted act, insofar as may be necessary, shall be applied to the same extent as if the said provisions were set forth at length herein. 

Under this section of the Act the provisions of Title III. 

of the Federal Revenue Act of 1926, and amendments, are to be given the same force and effect as if such provisions were enacted by the Tennessee Legislature so far as may be necessary for the administration of this statute. 

Rules and Regulations— Law. Section 1308. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is empowered to make all necessary rules and regulations not inconsistent with the terms of this statute, which shall have the force and effect of law, for the purpose of fully carrying out and giving effect to the provisions of this statute. 

Misdemeanor to Fail to File Reports or Make Affidavits-Fines- 

Law.

Section 1309. 

It shall be a misdemeanor for any executor to fail to file any affidavit or duplicate federal tax return or other instrument required by this statute to be filed or to pay the tax herein imposed when payable hereunder or to comply with and obey any rule or regulation promulgated by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation for the enforcement of this law, or to make and file a false return or report or other instrument required to be made and filed hereunder; and any such executor shall be fined in a sum of not less than fifty dollars nor more than one thousand dollars for cach offense.

(Ch. 6  Estate Tax-Lien- Law. Section 1310. 

The tax imposed, until paid, or until six years shall have elapsed after the death of decedent, shall be a lien upon all of the Tennessee estate of the decedent; provided, the lien shall expire at the close of one and one-half years from date of administration of the estate unless action be brought before that time for its enforcement. 

Commissioner to Issue Tax Receipts- Law. Section 1311. 

Upon the payment of said tax, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall issue receipt therefor in duplicate to the executor. 

Upon the payment of a fee of one dollar to the Commissioner, which fee shall accrue to the State, the executor or any other person shall be entitled to receive from the Commissioner a certificate to the effect that the tax upon any particular parcel, or tract, of real estate has been paid, and such certificate may be recorded in the office of the register of the county in which such real estate is situated, and shall be conclusive proof that the tax applicable to such real estate has been paid. 

Penalty of 25% upon Delinquents- 

Law. Section 1312. 

If any tax originally payable under the provisions of section 1298, or thereafter under the provisions of section 1301, be not paid at or before the time same shall be due, then there shall be added, and there is imposed for such failure, a penalty of twenty-five per cent of the amount of said tax exclusive of interest.

Suit to Collect Tax- 

Law.

Section 1313. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may, in his discretion, institute suit in the name of the State of Tennessee, in any court of competent jurisdiction for the collection of the tax imposed hereunder in the event same is not paid when due. Such suit shall be for the amount of the tax due, with penalty and interest herein provided. 

Commissioner to Employ Assistants, Agents, etc.—

Law. Section 1314. 

The Commissioner may employ necessary agents, representatives and assistants for the enforcement of this law, and the expense of their employment and all incidental expenses shall be defrayed out of the two and one-half per cent of the moneys collected as provided in Section 1299, and, in case of suit, out of the penalty herein provided, or so much thereof as may be necessary.

Counties and Cities Prohibited to Levy Estate Tax- Law. Section 1315. 

The tax herein imposed is a tax exclusively for the use of the state, and no county, municipality or taxing district shall have power to levy any like tax.

Sections 1308 through section 1315 are deemed sufficiently clear and comment is unnecessary.

HISTORY OF GASOLINE TAX 

Prior to 1923 Tennessee did not levy a tax upon the sale or storage of gasoline. The gasoline tax was recommended by Governor Peay; in his message to the 63rd 

General Assembly, under date January 17, 1923, he states: ... it is necessary for you to determine the disposition of the automobile fees from registration, which are now amounting to about $1,500,000.00 annually. The counties receive fifty per cent of these fees. The part retained by the State and the half mill levy on general property now yielding about $800,000.00 annually, and the aid derived from the federal government .compose the funds which are being used for highway purposes. It is not feasible in my judgment to economically maintain and conduct an adequate organization without annual funds to the amount of $3,500,000.00 or more. We cannot obtain federal aid without a Highway Department. I am opposed to federal aid in State activities. The policy is fundamentally unsound, though an exception can be justly taken in the matter of road building. 

We will never

An realize a general and connected system of modern roads of acceptable quality and permanency until the State builds and maintains the system without aid from the counties. The policy being pursued is most unsatisfactory. It has loaded the counties with bond issues, without satisfactory results. Some counties are unwilling and others are unable to sell bonds, and it is sound wisdom to discourage all bonds. If the counties are relieved of contribution to the State system, they should be willing to forego their share of the automobile funds now being received. The 

State should retain the entire revenue from this source. It should levy a tax of two cents on gasoline, which will produce a million dollars. It would then have with the aid expected from federal funds approximately $3,500,000.00 to annually spend on highways. In my judgment this is as much as our department for some time can profitably and economically expend. Perhaps your ingenuity will conceive a better plan. energetic propaganda is being conducted to issue seventy-five million dollars in bonds to be expended through a period of ten years. I am unable to appreciate the good business of this proposition. It is said that the gasoline tax and automobile fees will retire these bonds without substantial contribution from general taxes. I have no faith in that assur- 

It is absolutely certain that the bonds would not be salable, if only dependent for retirement on those receipts, and unless drawn to be an encumbrance on all property and resources of the State. It is highly probable that human wit will devise other fuel for motors before the bonds were matured. Thereupon, the gasoline tax would disappear. 

Many contingencies are possible in such a period of time, to render this huge debt inexpedient and unwise. It would be necessary to substantially increase the charges on automobiles, and to levy a gasoline tax of two cents or more to create a sufficient fund to pay the interest on the bonds, and retire them. It would be better if a large program was contemplated to use the same receipts for an annual budget, and not incur the bonded debt.

I recommend that you omit the direct levy for highways. This will relieve general property of $800,000.00 in taxes. 

Land cannot bear the taxes which the counties are imposing, and support the State government. We should begin framing our tax system to relieve real estate from all contribution to the State. To pursue the course I recommended it will become necessary to enact the gasoline tax in lieu of the direct levy for roads. ance. 

485

(Ch. 7  

Pursuant to the recommendation of Governor Peay,

Hon. F. S. Hall, representative from Dickson County, introduced under date March 5, 1923, a bill imposing a tax on the sale of gasoline (H. B. 525, Chapter 58, Public Acts of 1923) The act imposed a tax of two cents upon each gallon of gasoline sold in Tennessee and is the first "gasoline tax" law. 

Under date January 6, 1925, Governor Peay submitted his message to the 64th General Assembly, and as regards gasoline tax he stated: "" . a considerable sum is being annually covered into the treasury from the inspection of kerosene and gasoline. These receipts are now threatened in the courts. It is alleged that the present law is no longer an exercise of the State's police power, but has become a revenue measure. We cannot permit our present system to be overturned and we have prepared a bill relieving all questions in this matter and saving the receipts. It should be quickly enacted to forestall impending litigation. • • The Commission of Highways and Public works has submitted to you a comprehensive report. It should be analyzed with care and interest. You will obtain from it authoritative information on the State and progress of our highway system. This department has made remarkable strides since taking control in February of 1923. Order has been substituted for disorder. The department is now functioning with splendid efficiency. The people throughout the State are gratified and well pleased. What our department has accomplished in two years is little short of a marvel. The way is clear for the completion of this system in a few years. The gasoline tax should be raised to 3 cents. 

All revenues from gasoline and automobile registrations should go to the State Highway system for construction or maintenance until the State system is completed. There is no doubt in my mind that the counties would fare better to let their share of automobile funds which they are now receiving be used by the State in building or maintaining that mileage of the State system within the counties than for it to be used miscellaneously over the counties as is now being done. It will be a great mistake to enact any local bill laying additional taxes on gasoline or automobiles for county purposes. That field of taxation should be reserved for the State exclusively. It is highly desirable to abandon the present system of county aid as soon as possible. 

In accordance with the recommendation of Governor Peay the Legislature increased the gasoline tax from 2 cents to 3 cents per gallon. 

(See Chapter 4, Public Acts of 1925.) 

It appears that the road program was progressing satisfactorily and in the message of Governor Peay to the 

65th General Assembly under date January 6, 1927 we find:

I oppose any increase in the gasoline tax and recommend against it for the following reasons: Because three cents a gallon is enough tax to pay on gasoline. Because we can build and complete our

Ch. 7) 487 

GASOLINE TAX 

State system of highways on the present tax. The states about us, with the exception of Missouri, levy a gasoline tax of four, four and one half, and five cents on the gallon. It is a fine thing for us to maintain a lower tax. It is good advertising. It is of much benefit to gasoline dealers doing business in our border Cities of Memphis, Fulton, Bristol, Chattanooga, and smaller points. Our road revenues are greatly augmented through increased sales at all border stations. The State derives valuable advertisement from those who travel our roads as good or better than they find in surrounding States, while they pay a lower tax. Two years hence, it may be desirable to increase this tax in order to provide additional funds for discharging the county highway bonds, but I am thoroughly convinced that it would be well to leave the gasoline tax at three cents a gallon for the next two years at least. Nor, do I believe that it will ever be necessary to increase it. We are succeeding with our road system on a policy which is distinctively our own, and I take pride in the administration of our State government through constructive policies of our own creation. 

Governor Peay not only recommended that the gasoline tax rate remain at 3 cents per gallon, but expressed the opinion that it would "ever be necessary to increase it,' however, in the message of Governor Horton, submitted 

January 14, 1929 to the 66th General Assembly he stated: 

The The our highway construction has made remarkable progress during the past few years but the system is yet uncompleted. mileage in our primary highway system should be increased further in order to meet the growing demands of the traveling public. There should be at least seven thousand five hundred miles included. 

The secondary road system should provide for the construction and maintenance of rural roads that are not included in the State system. improvement of rural roads is imperative. The pay-as-you-go plan of financing the highways has been a marked success. It has been a triumph of financing which has given to this State a tremendous advantage over other Southern States. 

We have not been burdened with a huge bond issue for the construction of our highways and if the present plan is adhered to the primary system can be completed within the next three years. To consummate our program in the next three years it will be necessary in the future, as it has been in the past, to supplement highway revenues with anticipation revenue notes. I will approve the enactment of legislation permitting the Funding Board upon the recommendation of the Commissioner of Highways to borrow money to supplement the existing highway revenues, provided that provision shall be made to set apart a certain proportion of highway funds to pay all these anticipation-revenue notes that may be authorized by this Legislature or that have been authorized by previous Legislatures and issued by the Funding Board. Existing annual revenues should be supplemented by increasing the gasoline tax from three to five cents. 

One cent of this increased tax should be segregated for the construction and maintenance of rural roads; provided, however, that the expenditure of this money shall be closely supervised by the Highway Department in co-operation with county officials. One cent of the gasoline tax has already been set apart for the reimbursement of counties which have issued bonds for State highway purposes. With one cent set apart for rural roads there will be left three cents for general highway purposes. 

When the primary system is completed one cent may easily be allotted

(Ch. 7  

to the payment of all anticipation-revenue notes and our entire system will have been completed and paid for without the imposition of any property tax and without burdening the State with a bonded debt. . . ." 

The regular session of the 66th General Assembly enacted four amendments to the gasoline Tax Law, Viz. 

Chapters 11, 12, 124 and 27, Chapter 27, increased the rate of the tax from 3 to 5 cents per gallon in accordance with the recommendation of Governor Horton. 

An Extraordinary Session of the 66th General As sembly convened, Monday December 2, 1929 and in his message.

Governor Horton states: 

(( I have included in the program of this session the consideration of legislation that will enable the Highway Department to speed up its construction work during the year 1930, and in addition to provide for necessary public buildings for schools, health and administrative purposes. The enactment of legislation of this character will result in great benefit to the people, it will enable us to maintain present sound business conditions, to afford employment for both skilled and unskilled labor and to give additional markets for our materials. With this object in view, I most earnestly recommend that the Legislature authorize an increase in the issue of short time notes for Highway purposes to the amount of Ten Million Dollars ($10,000,000.00), and renewing the notes issued in 1925 that mature in 1930. This additional authorization will give the Highway Department funds adequate for the most extensive program of construction in the history of our State. . . 

For the purpose of liquidating the notes already authorized and to be authorized for highway construction, I recommend for your consideration a tax of five cents ($0.05) a quart on lubricating and motor oils, and a law setting aside in 1935, and for each year thereafter, one cent ($0.01) of the gasoline tax. It is estimated that the tax on lubricating and motor oils will be more than adequate to meet the interest charges on the highway notes already authorized and the Ten Million Dollars ($10,000,000.00) additional, which I recommend until 1935, when the additional revenue of one cent ($0.01) from gasoline will enable us to amortize and retire this whole indebtedness within a period of less than eighteen (18) years. ...

The extra session enacted chapters 19 and 30 for the purpose of creating a sinking fund, designated as "State 

Highway Bond and Note Retirement Fund No. 2" and from and after January 1931, the revenue divided from 1¢ of the gasoline tax was appropriated and set aside for this fund; from and after January 1, 1935, the revenue derived from 1¢ of the gasoline tax was appropriated and set aside as a sinking fund designated "State Highway 

Bond Retirement Fund." 

The tax recommended by the Governor upon lubricating and motor oils was not enacted and there is no such State tax in Tennessee at this time.

GASOLINE TAX 

The rate of gasoline tax remained at five cents; however, in Governor Horton's message to the 67th General 

Assembly he recommended an increase; "" of the five-cent gasoline tax levied, we are now using the proceeds of one cent in returning to the counties the money they furnished the Highway Department to be used by it in the State road system. One cent is being used on lateral roads in their maintenance and development. With the use of this money on lateral roads, great improvement has been made during the current biennium. But the money derived from the one cent gasoline tax is not sufficient for the development and maintenance of this class of roads. The total road mileage of the State is 68,000, and at present only about 20,000 miles are receiving aid from the State. This leaves 48,000 miles of roads not being aided by the State. The people living on these roads are demanding aid and should have it. They pay gasoline and automobile taxes and feel that they are entitled to more recognition. Another one cent of gasoline tax used on these lateral roads would result in the development of more than 12,000 miles of this class of roads, and would bring within reach of a great majority of the rural population an all-year road. I therefore recommend the use of another cent of gasoline tax money for these roads to be administered by the State Highway Department which is equipped with engineers and machinery and is the proper agency to have the Supervision of the roads and the expenditure of the money provided for them, because it can do it more economically and efficiently. ... I think it wise to add another cent of gasoline tax and provide that it be used on the secondary roads under the supervision of the State Highway Department. I therefore make this recommendation for your consideration. 

Chapter 40, Acts of 1931, passed June 24, 1931 and approved June 29, 1931, increased the gasoline tax to six cents per gallon. The Act became effective on and after passage and appears to be the result of Governor Horton's recommendation.

The Legislature also allocated the revenue derived from two cents of the gasoline tax to "County Aid Funds," to be divided and distributed by the State Highway Department to the several counties of the State. 

Several amendments were enacted at the Extra Session of the 67th General Assembly; however, the amendments were designed to strengthen the law and are considered of minor importance.

The regular Session of the General Assembly of 1931, as previously stated, increased the tax to six cents, and at the first extra session of the 67th General Assembly, Senate Bill Number 169, Chapter 11, Acts of extra session of 1931, was enacted which levies an additional one cent. 

This additional cent was imposed to provide a sinking fund

(Ch. 7 

for the retirement of $5,000,000.00 in bonds to be sold for the purpose of enabling the State to meet appropriations made by law. This Act provides that when the principal and interest of the bonds issued are fully paid and retired, this additional one cent tax shall cease. 

Governor McAlister delivered his message to the 68th 

General Assembly under date, February 28, 1933. His message contains no recommendations as regards gasoline tax; however, in view of the fact that the tax had reached the rather high rate of 7¢ per gallon, attention is directed to the following remarks by the Governor: ". . . To provide for expenditures that were authorized by the 

Legislature for the biennium ending June 30, 1931, the State borrowed at short term $5,000,000.00, and to provide for the expenditures authorized by the Legislature for the biennium which is to end June 30, 1933. 

We have already likewise borrowed the additional sum of $5,000,000.00, pledging one cent (the seventh cent) of the gasoline tax for the payment of said debt, principal and interest. By reason of the reduced amount that is accruing to the treasury from the gasoline tax, it will in all likelihood be near the end of 1934 before the last named debt will be fully discharged Under this budget it is not contemplated that a single dollar of new road construction will be undertaken by the Highway Department during the next biennium, unless it can be done with funds furnished by the Federal Government, or unless the State's receipts from present available gasoline tax are very much larger than we have any right at the present time to expect will be the case. Indeed, collections from this source are constantly showing an alarming shrinkage. In his message to the 69th General Assembly Governor 

McAlister states: "... Our gasoline tax is now 7 cents. Three cents of it is immediately returned to the counties of the State, and 3.1 cents of the remainder have heretofore been pledged by legislative acts which constitute contracts as a sinking fund for the payment of outstanding bonds heretofore issued by the State of Tennessee. Of the 7 cents gasoline tax, therefore, only .9 of one cent is thereafter available for highway purposes. The amount in dollars that this tax will yield for the benefit of the Highway Department has been estimated by that department for the year 1935 at $1,626,000. 

Governor Browning in his message to the 70th General 

Assembly states: "... The special tax levies on gasoline and tobacco are already higher than I wish to see them and cannot be raised without inviting wholesale law violation and discouraging the use of the products carrying the burden of the tax. . .

Ch. 7) 495 

GASOLINE TAX Section 1126: 

Definitions- 

As used in this statute the term "person" means and includes every individual, firm, association, joint-stock company, syndicate, and corporation. 

The term "distributor" means and includes every person who engages in the business in the State of refining, manufacturing, producing, or compounding gasoline or distillate, and selling or storing the same in this State; and also every person who engages in the business in this State of transporting, importing, or causing to be imported, gasoline or distillate into this State, and distributing, storing or making original sales of the same in this State, for any purpose whatsoever.

The term "original sales" as used in the definition of "distributor" shall mean the first sale made in this State after gasoline shall have been produced, refined and/or shipped or imported into this State, whether such sale shall be wholesale or retail, and/or to one for resale or use. 

The term "dealer" means and includes every person, other than a distributor, who engages in the business in this State, of distributing or selling gasoline or distillate within this State, and also every person who uses or consumes gasoline (except use or consumption in interstate commerce) when such gasoline has not previously been the measure of a privilege tax under this Statute. 

The term "gasoline" means and includes (a) the volatile substance produced from petroleum, natural gas, oil shales, or coal heretofore sold under the name of gasoline- (b) any volatile substance or product less than 112 Fahrenheit flash test when tested in a manner approved by U. S. Bureau of Mines derived wholly or in part from petroleum, natural gas, oil shales, or coal, and- (c) benzol and/or any other volatile substance used wholly or in combination with gasoline as a liquid fuel. 

The term "gallon" shall mean the amount of gasoline, at a temperature of sixty degrees (60) fahrenheit, necessary to completely fill a standard U.S. gallon liquid measure.

(Ch. 7  Section 1127: 

Rate and measure of tax-Distributor Every distributor when engaged in such business in this State, shall pay to the State Comptroller through the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, for the exclusive use of the State, a special privilege tax, in addition to all other taxes, for engaging in and carrying on such business in this State, in an amount equal to six cents for each gallon of gasoline, and six cents for each gallon of distillate refined, manufactured, produced, or compounded by such distributor and sold, stored, or distributed by him in this State, or shipped, transported, or imported by such distributor into, and distributed, stored, or sold by him within this State, during such year; provided, that no gasoline or distillate shall be included in the measure of the tax liability of a distributor unless said gasoline or distillate shall have previously come to rest within the meaning of the Interstate Commerce clause of the Federal Constitution; provided, further, that all gasoline and distillate distributed by any distributor, to any of its service stations in this State shall be deemed to have been sold, and shall be treated in the same manner as though the same had been sold to dealers or other persons.

Section 1128: 

Rate and measure of tax-Dealer Every dealer each year, when engaged in such business in this State, shall pay to the State Comptroller, through the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, for the exclusive use of the State, a special privilege tax, in addition to all other taxes, for engaging in such business in this State, equal to six cents for each gallon of gasoline and six cents for each gallon of distillate sold, or distributed, or stored, or used, or consumed by such dealer in this State during such year; provided, that gasoline or distillate previously identified as a measure of tax liability of a registered distributor shall not be included in the measure of said dealer's tax liability; provided, further, that no gasoline or distillate shall be included in the measure of any dealer's

Ch. 7)

tax liability unless said gasoline or distillate shall have previously come to rest within the meaning of the Interstate Commerce clause of the Federal Constitution; provided, further, that no gasoline or distillate shall be included in the measure of any dealer's tax liability when such gasoline or distillate was delivered within another state into the tank of the motor vehicle using it. 

Chapter 118; Public Acts of 1933-Section 3; 

Imposes additional One cent tax per gallon—

That for the purpose of providing a sinking fund for the payment of the interest and principal of said bonds, there is hereby levied and continued in full force and effect the tax of one cent (1¢) per gallon upon the sale or storage of gasoline and/or distilled and/or other volatile substances of the same character and nature as gasoline, which tax is levied by Chapter 11, Public Acts of the Second Extra Session of the General Assembly of 1931. Upon the receipt by the Comptroller of sufficient funds from the tax levied by Chapter 11, Public Acts of the Second Extra Ses sion of 1931, to pay the principal and interest on the bonds issued under authority of said Act, the said tax shall not cease but shall continue to be collected under the terms and conditions provided for in said Act until sufficient funds shall have been received therefrom to pay the principal and interest on the interest-bearing bonds issued under the provisions of this Act. The Comptroller shall place from the gasoline tax an amount equal to one (1¢) cent per gallon of gasoline and such other volatile substances so sold and/ or distributed and/or stored in a separate fund which shall begin to accumulate immediately after a sufficient amount has already accumulated to pay the bonds issued under 

Chapter 11, Acts of the Second Extra Session of 1931, which fund shall then be used solely and alone for the payment of the principal and interest on the bonds issued under authority of this Act, provided that when such principal and interest shall have been fully paid and retired, then the additional tax levied by Chapter 11, Acts of the Second Ex tra Session of 1931 and continued thereby shall immediately

General Assembly authorizing the issuance of not to exceed Ten million ($10,000,000.00) Dollars of State warrants, the purpose of said Act so authorizing the issuance of warrants and of this Act being to fund and pay the State's unfunded obligations as of July 2, 1933, and not to have outstanding at any time either in bonds or warrants obligations in excess of Ten million ($10,000,000.00) Dollars. 

Section 1128.1: 

Gasoline used for industrial purposes conditionally exempt- The tax on all gasoline, other than on gasoline as defined in Section 1126, subsection (a) of the fifth paragraph, shall be refunded when used for industrial purposes and not used in internal combustion engines, subject to such general limitations and regulations as the Commissioner may prescribe. The users of gasoline claiming the benefit of this section must obtain annually from the Department of Finance and Taxation an 'Industrial User's Permit' 

and the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is empowered to prescribe rules and regulations covering refunds; but a refund shall not be allowed until such rules and regulations are fully complied with. 

Section 1129: 

Payable monthly-penalty for delinquency- Such tax shall be paid in monthly installments. If the tax shall not be paid on or before the 20th day of said succeeding month, it shall become delinquent, and subject to a penalty of one per cent per day for not exceeding ten days, and it shall be the duty of the Comptroller to proceed to

Ch. 7) 499 

GASOLINE TAX 

collect same, with the penalty and interest by a distress warrant against the delinquent and his surety, and/or suit. 

Section 1130: 

Allowances for certain losses Allowance under general rule, covering loss of gallonage resulting from evaporation, handling, and unloading, must be uniform for all distributors, and other persons required to pay the tax; and must be based on true invoice receipts. 

Allowance under special rule, covering loss of gallonage due to fire, flood, storm, theft, or other causes over which the distributor has no control, (exclusive of loss resulting from causes listed under general rule) will be made; provided that such loss is immediately reported to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation; and further provided that an affidavit is made before a notary public setting out a complete description of the loss sustained, together with the further facts as to the nature of the casualty and date and time it occurred; provided, that such proof of loss shall be satisfactory to the Commissioner. 

Section 1131: 

Records to be kept-failure punishable by fine- Each person refining, storing, selling, distributing, or handling gasoline or distillate in this State, shall keep a record showing from whom the same was received, the date of its receipt, and the number of gallons received, together with such other and different information as the Commissioner may require. 

Persons transporting gasoline or distillate not previously identified as a measure of the tax liability of a registered distributor, shall have at all times with them, subject to scrutiny of representatives of the Department of Finance and Taxation and all peace officers, a true record showing where and from whom the gasoline or distillate was received, day and time of receipt, number of gallons, destination, and such other and different information as the Commissioner may require. 

Persons transporting gasoline and distillate previously identified as a measure of the tax liability of a registered

(Ch. 7  

distributor, shall, if the quantity transported exceeds forty gallons, be subject to the provisions of the foregoing paragraph.

Violation of any of the provisions of this section is hereby declared to be a misdemeanor and shall be punishable by a fine of not less than twenty-five ($25.00) dollars nor more than fifty ($50.00) dollars for each offense. 

Section 1132: 

Distributors must report monthly Each distributor must, within twenty days after the end of each month, make out in duplicate, on forms prescribed by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, and deliver to the said Commissioner, a true statement showing the total number of gallons of gasoline or distillate compounded, refined, manufactured, or produced by him in this State, and/or the number of gallons of gasoline or distillate transported, imported, or caused by him to be imported into this State; also a true statement showing the number of gallons stored, sold, or distributed by such distributor during the month, the total amount due the State as privilege taxes for such month, together with such other further and different information as the Commissioner shall require. 

Section 1133: 

Dealers must report monthly Each person other than a distributor who may be required under the foregoing sections to pay the privilege tax on gasoline or distillate, shall file a statement with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation as required by section 1132 and shall conform in all other respects to the provisions of said section. 

Section 1134: 

Commissioner's action-reports The Commissioner shall file one of such statements in his office and shall deliver the duplicate copy thereof to the Comptroller.

Ch. 7) 501 

GASOLINE TAX Section 1135: 

Due date of tax Each distributor and each dealer must, within twenty days after the end of each such month, and at the same time the statement required by Sections 1132-1134, is delivered to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, pay the Comptroller through the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, the amount of privilege tax shown by such statement to be due for the month for which the statement is made and filed.

Section 1136: 

Failure to file or make false report—misdemeanor—

It shall be unlawful for any distributor or dealer to fail, neglect, or refuse to make and file any statement required by the provisions of said sections, in the manner, or within the time therein provided, or to make any such statement false in any particular.

Any person violating the provisions of this section shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be fined not less than twenty-five dollars nor more than fifty dollars for each offense.

Section 1137: 

Assessment by Commissioner revocation of per mit- Upon the failure of any person engaged as distributor or dealer to make and deliver to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation the statement above provided for, or to pay the taxes due, it shall be the duty of the Commissioner to revoke his permit, and immediately to proceed to inform himself as best he may regarding the matters and things to be set forth in such statement, and, from such information as he may be able to obtain, to make a statement, showing such matters and things, and determine and fix the amount of the privilege tax due the State from such delinquent person, and proceed to collect said amount, including a penalty of one per cent per day, for not exceeding ten days, and interest, by the issuance of a distress warrant

(Ch. 7 

against the delinquent and the surety on his bond, and, if necessary, by suit on the bond. 

Upon the request of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, it shall be the duty of the Attorney General to institute, and prosecute to conclusion all proper and necessary suits for the collection of the taxes. 

Section 1138: 

Commissioner's assessment prima facie correct- Said statement, as prepared by the Commissioner, shall be deemed prima facie correct, and the burden of proof shall be upon the distributor or dealer to prove its incorrectness in any action growing out of matters and things contained therein.

Section 15-Art. 3; Chapter 108, Acts of 1937 (General Revenue Bill) 

Refunds of tax erroneously or illegally collected; limitation; adjustments 

That whenever it shall satisfactorily appear to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation that a license tax, privilege tax, inheritance tax or other tax has been erroneously or illegally collected for the use and benefit of the State, by any County or State official, department, or department head, agent, or attorney, the said Commissioner, with the approval of the Attorney-General, is hereby authorized and empowered to adjust, settle and order the refunding of the taxes so collected and to direct the Comptroller to draw his warrant in settlement of the same. 

The Commissioner shall have no power to order any refund unless claim for the same, supported by proper proof, shall have been made within one year from the date of payment. 

Section 1139: 

Invoices to be prepared by distributor- Every distributor selling any gasoline or distillate in this State, in the original packages in which shipped, transported, or imported into this State by such distributor, shall at the time of making such sale, make out and deliver

Ch. 7) 503 

GASOLINE TAX 

to the purchaser thereof, an invoice, in which invoice shall be stated the number of gallons of gasoline or distillate covered by such invoice, and that the same has been sold in the original packages in which the same was shipped, transported or imported into this State. 

Section 1140: 

Export shipments-conditional exemption—

Gasoline or distillate not previously the subject of an original sale in this State, stored in this State for export to points outside the State, shall not be included in the measure of the tax liability of any distributor or dealer; provided that such gasoline or distillate is stored in a separate tank marked "Export tank";

Provided, that a bond is executed by the distributor or dealer that in the opinion of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation adequately protects the state against loss of tax in case said gasoline or distillate is not subsequently exported outside the state; 

Provided, that gasoline or distillate stored for export longer than a period of sixty days must be included in the measure of the tax liability of the distributor or dealer so storing such gasoline or distillate.

Section 1141: 

Collection and expense thereof disposition of revenue- It shall be the duty of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation to collect all taxes accruing under this law, and to issue proper receipts therefor, and to pay over all taxes so collected to the Comptroller, who shall place them to the credit of a fund to be used solely in the construction and maintenance of the highway system of the State, and not exceeding one per centum of said fund shall be used for expenses of administration, and no part of said fund shall be used in any other department or for any other purpose whatsoever.

(Ch. 7  Section 1142: 

Issuance of distress warrants-penalty-fee— The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, in the name of the State, may issue a distress warrant for the collection of such tax when past due, and for the penalties and costs; and a penalty of one per centum per day is imposed for the failure to pay such tax, and a fee of two dollars for the issuance of a distress warrant, and the usual commissions allowed officers collecting money by virtue of an execution issuing from a court of record; provided, however, when the penalty reaches ten per cent no further penalty shall be collected.

Section 1143: 

Unlawful to engage in business without permit- It shall be unlawful for any distributor or other person to engage in the business of selling, storing or distributing, in intrastate commerce, gasoline or distillate without first having obtained a permit to carry on such business from the 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. 

Section 1144: 

Form of application for permit- Every person desiring a permit to engage in said business of distributor, dealer, or distributing and storing gasoline, shall make application in writing therefor to the Commissioner, on forms to be by him provided, which applica tion shall show: 

(a) The name and address of applicant; (b) Whether individual, partnership, association, or corporation, and, if partnership or association, the names and addresses of each member; (c) Whether it is the purpose of applicant to engage as distributor, dealer, or storer, and, (d) Whether wholesale, retail, or both. 

Section 1145: 

Bond required with application The application shall be accompanied by a bond, payable to the State of Tennessee, in such penalty as may be required by the Commissioner, such penalty, however, not to be less than one thousand dollars, nor more than ten

Ch. 7) 505 

GASOLINE TAX 

thousand dollars, signed by the applicant as principal, and by an authorized surety or bonding company, as surety, conditioned to be void if the applicant shall pay to the Comptroller all gasoline taxes that accrue against the applicant under and in accord with the provisions of this Statute. Upon the filing of the application and bond, it shall be the duty of the Commissioner to issue the permit. 

Section 1146: 

Revocation of permit; penalties—

The permit of every distributor, dealer or storer who fails to keep the records, or fails to make and deliver the statements and reports required, or who fails to pay the taxes accrued before they become delinquent, or fails to make and maintain bond as required by law, shall be revoked, and the carrying on of such business thereafter shall be unlawful.

If any distributor or other person operates without a permit, a business for which a permit is required under the provisions of the preceding sections, he shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be fined for each separate exercise of the functions of such business the sum of twenty-five to fifty dollars.

Provided; further, that the Commissioner may in his discretion and in the alternative, proceed under the provisions of Sections 9316 and 9317 of the Code of Tennessee, 1932, to abate and enjoin the further carrying on of said business as a public nuisance. 

Section 1147: 

Report forms and stationery- It shall be the duty of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation to provide all necessary and appropriate blank forms and stationery for carrying the provisions of this law into effect, the same to be provided and paid for as other supplies for his department are provided; to cancel permits of delinquents and promptly report them to the Comptroller for such proceedings as by law and this statute authorized.

(Ch. 7 

 Section 1147.1: 

Certificates of registration- 

All persons now or hereafter required by the provisions of Chapter 58 of the Public Acts of 1923 as amended to pay the tax on gasoline or substitutes therefor and all persons delivering such gasoline or substitutes in quantities exceeding nine (9) gallons liquid measure to any such person required to pay said tax by the laws aforesaid shall be required to first register their names and addresses, by mail or in person, at the office of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and to receive and keep posted at their usual place of business, a certificate of registration bearing a serial number, which serial number shall be assigned to such person by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. 

Section 1147.2: 

Invoices to be issued and kept— Whenever gasoline or substitutes therefor, subject to the tax aforesaid, shall hereafter be delivered or distributed in the State of Tennessee by any person in quantities exceeding nine (9) gallons liquid measure to a person required to pay the tax aforesaid, such person making said delivery or distribution shall be required, at the time of said delivery, to give to the person receiving said gasoline or substitutes a written or printed invoice or sales ticket showing thereon the serial registration number of the person so delivering or distributing said gasoline and the number of gallons thereof and time of delivery, which invoice or sales ticket shall be kept on file by the person receiving the same, subject to inspection during reasonable business hours by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, or his duly authorized deputies, agents, inspectors or employees, for a period of six (6) months from the date of the receipt of such gasoline or substitutes.

Ch. 7) 507 

GASOLINE TAX Section 1147.3: 

Bond required of persons liable for tax; notice to surety upon delinquency All persons required to pay said gasoline tax as aforesaid shall execute a bond securing the payment of all such taxes thereafter accruing, said bond to be payable to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, and to be signed by some solvent corporate surety residing in or having an office and agent in the State of Tennessee, and to be approved by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. The penalty of said bond shall be in a sum equal to twice the amount of the tax required to be paid by such person per month and shall be determined by averaging such tax over the period of six (6) months immediately preceding the execution of said bond, and if such person shall not have been in business for a period of six (6) months the penalty of said bond shall be determined on the average tax per month during the actual time such person has been engaged in business. In the event such person shall not have previously engaged in said business, the penalty of said bond shall be fixed at Five thousand ($5,000.00) dollars during the first month and thereafter said penalty shall be governed by the previous provisions of this Act; provided, however, that in no event shall the penalty of the bond herein provided for be less than the sum of Twenty-five hundred ($2,500.00) dollars irrespective of the volume of business carried on by the taxpayer. If at any time after the execution of said bond the surety thereon shall become insolvent the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may require the execution of a new bond with good and solvent surety in the same manner and with the same penalty as aforesaid, and subject to the approval of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, and any person executing a bond under the provisions of this law, may, at any time prior to default under any existing bond, apply to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation for cancellation of the existing bond and for leave to file a new bond with new surety thereon in accordance with the provisions aforesaid, and shall have the right to file such new bond, at such time, by

(Ch. 7  

and with the approval of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation.

In case the taxpayer fails to pay the taxes due for any month as and when the same becomes due, the surety on the taxpayer's bond shall be notified by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation within fifteen days from the date such taxes become delinquent, and in the absence of such notice the surety will not be liable for additional taxes which may accrue for succeeding months after the taxes become delinquent. Such notice shall be given to the surety by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation in writing sent either to the authorized representative of the surety in the State of Tennessee or to the home office of the surety. 

Section 1147.4: 

Delinquents; Commissioner's action; prosecution 

If any such person shall at any time make default in the payment of said taxes required by the laws aforesaid, the 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall send by registered mail, with return receipt requested, written notice and demand for payment of such delinquent tax, showing the amount thereof due and unpaid, to the surety or sureties on said bond, at the address shown thereon or to the last known address, and if said delinquent tax and all interest and penalties legally due thereon shall not be paid within ten (10) days after the mailing of such notice and demand such fact shall be certified to the State Comptroller by the 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and Attorney General for State of Tennessee shall upon request of State Comptroller institute and prosecute suit in a court of proper jurisdiction for the amount of said delinquent tax with all legal interest and penalties thereon against the principal and surety or sureties on said bond, or said Attorney General may, within his discretion, institute said suit solely against the surety or sureties on said bond without the necessity of joining the principal in said suit. 

The Commissioner is hereby directed and empowered to cancel and revoke the certificate of registration provided in Section 1147.1 of this Act if and when the holder of such certificate of registration is delinquent in the payment of the

tax for a period of thirty days, and when such certificate of registration is thus revoked, and cancelled by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, it shall be a misdemeanor for the person to whom such certificate shall have been issued to continue in business and punishable as provided in Section 1147.7 hereof. 

Section 1147.5: 

Unlawful to receive gasoline from non-registered person- It shall hereafter be unlawful for any person required by law to pay the tax on gasoline or substitutes as aforesaid to accept or receive gasoline or substitutes thereof in quantities exceeding nine (9) gallons from any person who has not been duly registered and issued a serial number as required by the provisions of this Act, or whose certificate of registration has been revoked or cancelled by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation as heretofore provided. 

Section 1147.6: 

Definition of “person”- The word "person" as herein used shall mean and include persons, firms, partnerships, companies, corporations, associations, receivers, common law trusts, statutory trusts and other concerns, by whatever name known or howsoever organized, formed or created. The rights and remedies herein provided with reference to the enforcement and collection of the tax herein mentioned shall be cumulative and shall be in addition to the rights, remedies and procedure now provided by existing laws. 

Section 1147.7: 

Violation of Act: penalties- 

Any person violating any provision of this Act shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction shall be fined not less than One Hundred ($100.00) dollars nor more than 

One Thousand ($1,000.00) dollars and in case such person is an individual he may be imprisoned in the county jail not exceeding six (6) months in addition to the fine, within the discretion of the court.

(Ch. 7 

 Section 1147.8: 

Disposition of fines collected- All fines collected under the provisions of the Act shall go to the State of Tennessee, to be transmitted when collected, to the State Comptroller, and shall constitute a part of the receipts of the tax levied under Chapter 58, Public Acts of 1923 as amended. 

Section 1147.9: 

; rules and regulations- 

The administration of the provisions of this Act shall be conducted by the Department of Finance and Taxation, and said Department shall have the power to make all reasonable rules and regulations necessary to carry out the provisions of this Act, and in all matters, connected with the administration of the provisions of this Act, requiring the exercise of judgment and discretion, the judgment and opinion of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall be final and conclusive, and there shall be no review thereof; except the constitutional right of redress in the courts under existing or future laws. 

Section 1147.10: 

Common carriers; reports from- 

That every public and/or common carrier delivering gasoline, benzol, kerosene and/or any other liquid petroleum substance or substitutes therefor in this State shall make out and send in to the Department of Finance and Taxation at the end of each calendar month a true report showing the date of delivery, location and consignee, car number and initial, contents, and, in case of delivery by tank-wagon, or other motor vehicle, the truck license of said vehicle and the number of gallons delivered during the month for which the report shall be made. These reports shall be made and sent in on forms provided by the Department of Finance and Taxation, and must be made out and sent in by the delivering carrier, or his or its agent nearest to the point of delivery within ten (10) days after the end of the month in which the deliveries were made, provided

Ch. 7) 511 

GASOLINE TAX 

that any public and/or common carrier and/or any agent or servant of such carrier which or who shall wilfully fail or refuse to comply with the provisions of this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction shall be fined not less than One ($1.00) dollar nor more than Five hundred ($500.00) dollars, or imprisoned in the county jail for thirty (30) days, or both.

Section 1147.11: 

Notification of deliveries to non-registered persons- Any public and/or common carrier delivering gasoline, benzol, and/or substitutes therefor to any consignee or person to whom delivery is made who does not have a permit to sell, store, use or distribute gasoline or whose permit has been revoked, shall immediately notify the Department of Finance and Taxation at the expense of such Department, by telegraph of such deliveries if telegraphic service is reasonably available, but, if not, by the next quickest medium reasonably available. The Department of Finance and Taxation shall furnish to said carrier a list of all persons holding permits and shall supplement and amend said list from time to time as permits are issued or revoked, provided that any public and/or common carrier and/or agent or servant of such carrier who, after receiving said list or lists, shall wilfully fail or refuse to comply with the provisions of this section, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction shall be fined not less than One ($1.00) dollar nor more than Five hundred ($500.00) dollars, or imprisoned in the county jail for thirty (30) days, or both.

Section 1147.12: 

When "delivery" takes place The placing of any shipment for unloading shall constitute delivery.

Section 1148: 

Rights in certain areas; Federal exemptions- 

Under the terms of the cession of jurisdiction to the United States of America by this State, the right is reserved to this State to tax sales of, and privileges of deal-

(Ch. 7  

ing in, gasoline and other fuels, and oils, used in the operation of motor vehicles, within the limits of the Great Smoky Mountain Park in the boundaries of the State. 

Provided, further, the right is reserved to this State to tax sales of and privileges of dealing in, gasoline and other fuels and oils used in operation of motor vehicles, within limits of any reservation or preserve in the boundaries of this State.

Section 1148.1: 

Conditional special tax of one-half of one cent per gallon- All inhabitants, persons, firms, corporations, syndicates, joint-stock associations, or agents thereof engaged in the activity in this State of dealing in and/or storing for any purpose whatsoever coal oil, kerosene, benzol, benzine, gas oil, processed fuel oil, gasoline as defined in Chapter 20, Acts of 1925, carried into the Code as Article 6, and/or any other volatile substance identified in Chapter 12, Acts of 1929, Article 14, Code of Tennessee, shall pay to the State of Tennessee, as a special privilege tax in addition to all other privilege taxes required to be paid in this State, an amount equal to one-half of one cent for each gallon of coal oil, kerosene, benzol, benzine, gas oil, processed fuel oil, gasoline and/or any other volatile substance identified in Chapter 12, Acts of 1929, sold, delivered or distributed in this State, after such commodities have come to rest in this State.

Provided, however, that when such substances subject to inspection under present or future inspection laws, have been inspected and the inspection fees thereon paid to the State of Tennessee as now required by law, they shall not be subject to or required to pay this one-half of one cent special privilege tax.

Provided, further, that this is a special privilege tax for the State, and no county or municipality in this State is authorized to levy and collect said special privilege tax as provided herein.

GASOLINE TAX 

Section 1148.2: 

Monthly reports and payment of special tax- Each inhabitant, person, firm, corporation, syndicate, joint-stock associations or agent thereof, subject to the payment of the special privilege tax provided for herein, and subject to pay the special privilege tax herein provided, shall make a monthly report to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation on or by the tenth of the succeeding month, showing the amount in gallons of each said commodity sold, delivered or distributed for the preceding month and subject to be estimated in calculating the amount of privilege tax as herein provided, and shall also make monthly remittance to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation for the amount of the special tax based upon and equal to said one-half cent per gallon for each gallon of said commodities so sold, delivered or distributed during the preceding month. Said report to be made under oath. 

Provided, that in making said report and remittance to cover to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, any of the commodities named and defined in this Act, and which have been inspected and the inspection fees thereon paid shall not be included in said report, nor in estimating the amount of privilege tax to be paid under the provisions of this Act.

Section 1148.3: 

"Export" products exempt from special tax- None of the provisions of this Act shall apply to any of the above mentioned substances and commodities coming to rest or stored in this State for the purpose of sale, exportation and shipment out of the State and not to be sold, distributed and used or consumed within this State.

Every distributor or other person engaged in selling, storing, handling or distributing gasoline, or substitutes therefor, not previously identified as a measure of the gasoline tax must register with Commissioner of Finance and

Where new partners are taken into a firm, the new firm so constituted shall file full information with Commissioner of Finance and Taxation.

All changes of location must be registered with Commissioner.

[A-5] Revocation of Gasoline Dealer's Permit- Certificate- 

The Code of Tennessee, Section 1146 as amended, directs and authorizes the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation to revoke the permits or certificates of gasoline dealers when guilty of certain violations of the statute and to prevent such gasoline dealers, whether individuals, partnerships or corporations, from further engaging in the gasoline business in Tennessee. In order to effectually carry out the provisions of said statute the following regulations are promulgated, which shall govern the procedure in revoking gasoline dealer's permit or certificate: 

1. Upon the filing of any complaint in writing with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation by any inspector or official of the Gasoline Tax Unit, alleging any violation of the statutes or regulations governing gasoline or its taxation, the Commissioner will issue a citation against the party or parties so charged to appear before him and show cause why their permit or certificate should not be revoked. Such citations may also be issued by the Commissioner in his discretion without the filing of written charges. 

2. Notice of such proceedings for the revocation of permit or certificate will be transmitted by registered mail to the last known address of the holder of such permit or certificate and he will be advised of the general nature of the charges against him and will be permitted a reasonable time within which to appear before the Commissioner and show cause why his permit or certificate should not be revoked. 

3. The holder of any such permit or certificate, after notice, may appear before the Commissioner in person or by counsel and present such evidence as the Commissioner deems material. These proceedings shall be held before the Commissioner in his office in the city of Nash-

Ch. 7) 519 

GASOLINE TAX 

ville, or at such other place as he may designate for the convenience of all interested parties. 

4. Upon a hearing of such citations for the revocation of permit or certificate the action of the Commissioner will be entered in a well-bound docket, showing the material facts of each case, together with the order either revoking the permit or certificate or dismissing the citation. Any such hearing may be continued within the discretion of the Commissioner for the introduction of further evidence, or any other valid reason which the Commissioner deems expedient. 

5. Upon the revocation of any permit or certificate the previous holder shall not be permitted to further engage in the gasoline business in the State of Tennessee and the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation will invoke the penal and injunctive relief provided for by the statute and prevent any continuation of business by the individuals, partnerships or firms affected.
