[B-1]—Regulation Issued August 13, 1936In view of the opinion of the Attorney-General of the State of Tennessee, dated August 13, 1936, in which he construes the Gasoline Tax Statutes and the Oil Inspection Statutes of this State, and in view of the further fact that the Attorney-General recommends the withdrawal of Rules heretofore promulgated under the head, "Supplement Q, (and); Supplement A; and Circular G," it is therefore 

ORDERED, That from and after August 13, 1936, the above mentioned Rules and Regulations are hereby cancelled and withdrawn, and that any other Regulation heretofore issued by this Department in conflict with the opinion of the Attorney-General, dated August 13, 1936, is hereby cancelled and withdrawn.

Copy of the Attorney-General's opinion, dated August 13, 1936 is attached hereto. 

[B-2]-Attorney General's Opinion Dated August 

13, 1936This will respond to your letter of August 3, in which you ask certain questions regarding the gasoline taxing statutes (sec. 1126 et seq. of the Code of Tennessee) and the oil inspection statutes (sec. 6809 et seq. of the Code of Tennessee). (1) The first question which you ask is: "When does the privilege tax liability accrue for the handling of gasoline or distillate as enumerated in section 1127 of the Code as amended?"

Section 1127 of the Code as amended provided for the imposition of a tax of seven cents per gallon for each gallon

(Ch. 7  

of gasoline or distillate "Refined, manufactured, produced or compounded by such distributor and sold, stored, or distributed by him in this State, or shipped, transported or imported by such distributor into, and distributed, stored or sold by him within this State." The section further provides that no gasoline or distillate shall be included in the measure of the tax liability of a distributor unless said gasoline or distillate shall have previously come to rest within the meaning of the Interstate Commerce Clause of the 

Federal Constitution.

While your inquiry asks when the tax liability accrues, it is evident from conferences that the real inquiry is when such tax liability accrues with reference to gasoline imported and stored in Tennessee. The question is whether or not tax liability attaches at the time when gasoline is stored, or only attaches at such time as the gasoline is withdrawn from storage and distributed. 

You are advised that tax liability accrues when gasoline is imported into Tennessee and placed in storage here. 

Such tax liability begins at such time as interstate commerce ends and at such time as the gasoline comes to rest within the State of Tennessee. There can be no postponement of tax liability until such time as gasoline stored in Tennessee shall be withdrawn from storage. There is an exemption in the case of gasoline or distillate stored in this State for export to points outside the State, provided section 1140 of the Code as amended is complied with. This exemption is more fully dealt with hereafter. 

In order to understand the proposition that the gasoline taxing statutes of Tennessee now impose a privilege tax upon the storage of gasoline without reference to withdrawal and without the necessity of withdrawal, use or distribution, a brief reference to the prior statutes is necessary.

The original gasoline taxing statute of Tennessee was Chapter 58 of the Public Acts of 1923. This Act imposed a privilege tax upon the sale of gasoline. Under the provisions of this statute it was only the sale of gasoline which was taxed as a privilege. A person who purchased gasoline without the State of Tennessee and brought it within the

Ch. 7) 527 

GASOLINE TAX 

State, storing it for use, was not liable for the privilege tax imposed by the Act of 1923.

By Chapter 67 of the Public Acts of 1925, the original gasoline taxing statute of 1923 was amended and broadened. 

Under the Act of 1925 a privilege tax was required to be paid in all cases where gasoline was stored in Tennessee and withdrawn for sale or other use. In other words, the amendatory Act of 1925 required that there be storage of gasoline and withdrawal of it from storage before the tax became due. 

Foster & Creighton Co. v. Graham, 154 Tenn., 412 

Quick Service Tire Company v. Smith, 156 Tenn., 96 

Nashville, C. & St. L. R. Co. v. Wallace, 288 U. S. 249, 77 L. ed., 730.

The time when liability for gasoline tax attaches was changed by Chapter 130 of the Public Acts of 1933. This amendatory Act provided for the collection of a gasoline tax measured by quantity placed in storage and not measured by quantity withdrawn from storage. This statute made an important and drastic change in the gasoline tax laws of Tennessee. Prior to the enactment of Chapter 130 

of the Public Acts of 1933 the State had never claimed a tax upon storing of gasoline in the absence of withdrawal, no matter how long gasoline was stored. The amount at any time received or held in storage under the prior law was immaterial. The tax depended solely upon the amount withdrawn from storage. 

The gasoline taxing statutes as amended in 1933 provide for a tax upon gasoline received or held in storage. The older statutes permitted of fraud and tax evasions. The amended statutes were designed to prevent such evasions. 

The quantity of gasoline placed in storage can readily be ascertained and the taxpayer is now required to pay the tax upon the quantity of gasoline stored without reference to withdrawals, and receive refund where there is a loss due to fire, flood, storm, theft or other cause over which the dealer has no control.

Some of the gasoline distributors were not satisfied with

(Ch. 7  

Chapter 130 of the Public Acts of 1933 as construed by the Department of Finance and Taxation and the Attorney- General. The constitutionality of this Act was attacked, with the result that the statute was held constitutional by the Supreme Court of Tennessee in the case of The Texas Company v. Fort, 168 Tenn., 678. The contention of the 

State that tax liability attaches to all gasoline stored in Tennessee after the effective date of the statute was sustained.

The fact that tax liability accrues when gasoline or distillate is placed in storage in Tennessee does not mean that there is tax liability where gasoline moving in interstate commerce is temporarily halted in Tennessee awaiting a continuation of its movement to a destination. Gasoline or distillate which is halted in Tennessee without having reached its destination and without having come to rest in Tennessee is not stored here because of its temporary stoppage. This situation is not to be confused with the shipment of gasoline into Tennessee and its storage here with the intention subsequently to remove the gasoline into other states. The fact that gasoline stored in Tennessee will later be shipped into other states does not prevent tax liability from attaching except when section 1140 of the Code, exempting certain gasoline stored for export, is complied with. (2) You also ask an opinion regarding "the correct interpretation of section 1140 of the Code as amended with respect to the special 'export tank' provision." 

You are advised that, as previously outlined, tax liability attaches to all gasoline or distillate stored in this State subject to the exemption provided for by section 1140. 

This section provides that gasoline or distillate not previously the subject of an original sale in Tennessee, which is stored in this State for export to points outside the State, shall not be included in the measure of the tax liability of any distributor or dealer if certain provisions of the section are complied with. These provisions require (a) that such gasoline or distillate shall be stored in a separate tank marked "export tank," (b) that a bond be executed by the distributor or dealer, satisfactory to the Commissioner of

Ch. 7) 529 

GASOLINE TAX 

Finance and Taxation, to protect the State against loss of tax in case such gasoline or distillate is not subsequently exported outside the State; and (c) that such gasoline or distillate, if stored for export longer than a period of 60 days, must be included in the measure of the tax liability. 

In order to claim exemption from the privilege tax imposed by the statutes upon the storage of gasoline in Tennessee, it is necessary that a dealer or distributor shall strictly observe the provisions of section 1140, and especially shall comply with the requirement that all gasoline stored for export and claimed as exempt from the gasoline tax shall be kept in a separate tank marked "export tank.” 

No dealer or distributor is entitled to tax exemption on gasoline stored in Tennessee merely because the books or records of such dealer or distributor show that the gasoline stored was intended for export from Tennessee. No dealer or distributor is exempt from gasoline tax upon gasoline stored in Tennessee for export if such gasoline is commingled with the quantity of gasoline stored in this state for domestic use. In other words, there can be no commingling of gasoline intended for export and of gasoline intended for domestic use without tax liability attaching to the entire amount kept in storage. If, and only if, gasoline stored in this State for export is kept in a separate tank marked "export tank, can exemption from the gasoline tax be claimed. 

In this connection it should be kept in mind that sec. 1140 of the Code as amended gives an exemption from taxation which the State was not required by the Commerce Clause of the Federal Constitution to give. The fact that gasoline stored in Tennessee is intended for use in other states and will subsequently be withdrawn from storage for transportation to other states furnishes no reason under the Federal Constitution why such storage should not be taxed. This was decided in the case of Nashville, Chattanooga & St. 

Louis R. Co. v. Wallace, 288 U. S. 249, 77 L. ed., 730. The exemption by section 1140 is a statutory exemption, to which the general rule of law that exemptions from taxation are strictly construed is applicable. It necessarily follows that all gasoline stored in Tennessee is subject to the gaso-

(Ch. 7  

line tax, excepting such gasoline as can be shown to be exempt by a compliance with section 1140 of the Code as amended, which requires that such gasoline for export be stored in a separate tank marked "export tank.” 

Certain rules and regulations of the Department of Finance and Taxation, including Supplement "Q (2nd) 

Supplement "A" and "Circular G," are apparently in conflict with this opinion. At least the construction which has been given these circulars by certain oil dealers is in conflict with this opinion. For this reason it is suggested that these rules and regulations ought to be withdrawn and new rules and regulations promulgated in their place which are not in conflict with this opinion.

[C-2]-Attorney General's Opinion Dated Septem ber 28, 1936In your letter of September 19, 1936 you request an opinion as to whether or not the regulation copied into 

Regulations No. 8, at Pages 105, 106 and 107, is in conflict with the opinion rendered you on August 13, 1936. The regulation in question purports to exempt from the gaso-

(Ch. 7  

line tax such volatile substances as are "manufactured, sold, stored and used for solvents and driers in the arts and sciences, or in manufacturing or cleaning processes." You are advised that this regulation is in conflict with the opinion rendered on August 13, 1936.

The gasoline tax statutes of Tennessee contain their own definition with reference to the substance which is taxable under the statute. According to this definition, any one of three things constitutes a substance as gasoline taxable under the law. First, the volatile substance heretofore sold under the name of gasoline is declared to be taxable. 

Secondly, any volatile substance or product less than 112 Fahrenheit flash test when tested in a manner approved by the United States bureau of mines derived wholly or in part from petroleum, natural gas, oil shales, or coal, is declared to be taxable. Thirdly, benzol or any other volatile substance used wholly or in combination with gasoline as a liquid fuel, is made subject to the tax. 

Under the definitions of gasoline contained in the gasoline tax laws it is not necessary that a volatile substance shall be used as a fuel for motor vehicles in order to be taxable. The statute itself contains a definition of gasoline and such statutory definition is not subject to change by rule or regulation.

In view of the fact that there is a statutory definition of gasoline which is explicit and which cannot be added to nor subtracted from by rule or regulation, I see no reason for the promulgation of a new regulation in this regard to replace that printed on pages 105, 106 and 107 of Regulation No. 8. However, it should be pointed out that there was a regulation printed on page 101 of Regulation No. 8 which was issued on September 13, 1933. This regulation embodies the law as I understand it and is in conflict with that copied on pages 106, et seq. In my opinion, the regulation on page 101 represents the obvious interpretation of the law and the one on page 105, et seq., is in conflict with the law.

This inquiry will, of course, dispose of the inquiry of the Company addressed to you, copy of which was sent to the Attorney-General. The administrative officers are power-

less to grant exemptions from taxation which are not contained in the taxing statute and when the provisions of the taxing statute are express they can not be abrogated by rule or regulation.

[D] Regulation Issued November 14, 1936In the reorganization of this Department the methods used in assessing the various forms of taxes are being given close scrutiny. It was found that certain regulations promulgated by the Department relative to the assessment and collection of the Privilege tax measured by gallonage of gasoline and the Inspection fees due on all volatile petroleum substances were in direct conflict with the laws relating thereto.

Under date of August 13, 1936, after several conferences, the Department issued a regulation, copy of which was mailed to all gasoline distributors and others dealing in or handling volatile petroleum products in this State. This regulation cancelled and withdrew all prior rules and regulations promulgated with respect to Privilege tax on gasoline and Inspection fees on volatile petroleum products in

(Ch. 7  

conflict with the laws and the opinion of the Attorney General, copy of same having been sent to all taxpayers affected thereby.

The ruling of August 13, 1936, is not ambiguous neither is the opinion of the Attorney General, however, there seems to be some misunderstanding relative to this matter and, therefore, for the benefit of the taxpayers and others the administrative procedures of the assessment and collection of the Privilege tax on gasoline brought to rest in this State and the Inspection fees due on all volatile petroleum substances are summarized as follows:

PRIVILEGE TAX MEASURED BY QUANTITY OF GASOLINE 

1. Privilege tax liability accrues upon all engaged in importing and storage of gasoline in this State and will be assessed and collected from such importers rather than the distributor as has been the practice heretofore. 

2. The Privilege tax liability is measured by the number of gallons of gasoline received or held in storage in this State. Please note that the tax is measured by the receipt of gasoline, and not by sales in this State. 

3. All volatile petroleum substances, including cleaning fluid and solvents having a flash point of less than 112 degrees F. (U. S. Bureau of Mines approved test) are defined to be gasoline by the law and will be used as a part of the measure of the Privilege tax liability. 

The only exemptions from the measure of the Privilege Tax liability contained in the gasoline statutes are as follows: 

1. Gasoline imported and stored in the State for export to points outside the State in strict accord with the provisions of Section 1140 of the Code will not be used as a measure of the tax, provided; all gasoline stored for export is stored in separate tanks marked "Export Tanks" and all shipments from such "Export Tanks" must be made to point outside this State.

Ch. 7) 535 

GASOLINE TAX 

Commingling of gasoline intended for export with gasoline intended for domestic consumption will render the entire gallonage subject to the tax. Gasoline stored for export and stored in tanks marked export gasoline cannot remain in said "Export Tanks" for a period exceeding sixty days without tax liability accruing. 

2. Gasoline sold to the United States Government and instrumentalities thereof may be deducted on the regular monthly report, however, before credit will be allowed for such deduction by the Department, supporting evidence on Federal form No. 1094 must be attached to the monthly report.

In view of the fact that dealers and distributors had in good faith operated under the old regulations of the Department, it is the opinion of the Attorney General, the 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and the Auditors engaged in the reorganization of this Department, that the new regulation issued August 13, 1936, should be effective as follows: 

1. The Privilege tax liability must be paid on gasoline inventories in all tanks exclusive of gasoline in tanks marked "Export Tanks" as of September 30, 1936. The tax must be paid on all receipts and imports at the time of the receipt in this State. 

2. The gasoline Privilege tax will be assessed and collected from the first importer rather than from the distributor after October 31, 1936. The importer must pay the 

Privilege tax direct. 

3. Gasoline tax will not be assessed on cleaning fluids or solvents imported prior to and in storage as of September 30, 1936. All volatile substances having a flash point of less than 112 degrees F. (U. S. Bureau of Mines approved test) received or imported after September 30, 1936, will be taxed.

Dealers and distributors will facilitate matters by furnishing information requested in the Department's letter dated October 26, 1936 as to inventories on hand and export shipments since August 13, 1936.

Definitions- Law. Section 1126. 

As used in this statute the term "". 

person means and includes every individual, firm, association, joint-stock company, syndicate, and corporation.

571

(Ch. 7 

The term 'distributor'' means and includes every person who engages in the business in the State of refining, manufacturing, producing, or compounding gasoline or distillate, and selling or storing same in this State; and also every person who engages in the business in this State of transporting, importing, or causing to be imported, gasoline or distillate into this State, and distributing, storing or making original sales of the same in this State, for any purpose whatsoever. 

The term "original sales" as used in the definition of "distributor'' shall mean the first sale made in this State after gasoline shall have been produced, refined and/or shipped or imported into this State, whether such sale shall be wholesale or retail, and/or to one for resale or use. 

The term "dealer'' means and includes every person, other than a distributor, who engages in the business in this State, of distributing or selling gasoline or distillate within this State and also every person who uses or consumes gasoline (except use or consumption in interstate commerce) when such gasoline has not previously been the measure of a privilege tax under this Statute. 

The term "gasoline" means and includes: (a) The volatile substance produced from petroleum, natural gas, oil shales, or coal heretofore sold under the name of gasoline- (b) Any volatile substance or product less than 112° Fahrenheit flash test when tested in a manner approved by U. S. Bureau of Mines derived wholly or in part from petroleum, natural gas, oil shales, or coal, and- (c) Benzol and/or any other volatile substance used wholly or in combination with gasoline as a liquid fuel. 

The term "gallon" shall mean the amount of gasoline, at a temperature of sixty degrees (60) fahrenheit, necessary to completely fill a standard U. S. gallon liquid measure.

The definitions or meanings of the terms used in the law are summarized as follows: 

1. "PERSON"-Every individual, firm, association, joint-stock company, syndicate and corporation. 

2. "DISTRIBUTOR"-Every person engaged in the business of- (a) Refining, manufacturing, producing or compounding gasoline or distillate; and (b) Selling or storing gasoline or distillate. (c) Transporting or importing, or causing to be imported, gasoline or distillate into the State; or (d) Distributing, storing or making original sales of gasoline or distillate in the State for any purpose whatsoever. 

3. "ORIGINAL SALES"-The first sale made in the

State after gasoline shall have been produced, refined, shipped or imported into the State, whether wholesale or retail, and for resale or use. 

4. "DEALER"-Every person other than a distributor engaged in the business of distributing or selling gasoline or distillate in the State.

Ch. 7) 541 

GASOLINE TAX 

Also every person who uses or consumes gasoline not previously taxed. 5. "GASOLINE"- (a) Volatile substances produced from petroleum, natural gas, oil shales, or coal, sold as gasoline. (b) Volatile substances or products, less than 112 degrees fahrenheit flash test, derived from petroleum, natural gas, oil shales, or coal, and (c) Benzol or any other volatile substance used with gasoline as a liquid fuel. 

6. "GALLON"-Amount of gasoline at a temperature of sixty (60) degrees fahrenheit necessary to completely fill a standard U. S. gallon liquid measure. 

Rate and Measure of Tax: Distributor_ Law. Section 1127. 

Every distributor when engaged in such business in this State, shall pay to the State Comptroller through the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, for the exclusive use of the State, a special privilege tax, in addition to all other taxes, for engaging in and carrying on such business in this State, in an amount equal to six cents for each gallon of gasoline, and six cents for each gallon of distillate refined, manufactured, produced, or compounded by such distributor and sold, stored, or distributed by him in this State, or shipped, transported, or imported by such distributor into, and distributed, stored, or sold by him within the State, during such year; provided, that no gasoline or distillate shall be included in the measure of the tax liability of a distributor unless said gasoline or distillate shall have previously come to rest within the meaning of the Interstate Commerce clause of the Federal Constitution; provided, further, that all gasoline and distillate distributed by any distributor, to any of its service stations in this State shall be deemed to have been sold, and shall be treated in the same manner as though the same had been sold to dealers or other persons.

Every distributor engaged in business in Tennessee is liable for the tax. The tax levied under Chapter 40, Public 

Acts of 1931, is six (6) cents per gallon and an additional tax of one (1) cent per gallon was levied under Chapter 118, Public Acts of 1933, making a total tax at the present time of seven (7) cents per gallon.

The "measure" of the tax liability is the number of gallons of gasoline or distillate- "Refined, manufactured, produced, or compounded, by such distributor and sold, stored or distributed by him within this State."' 

This section further provides that-

(Ch. 7  

"No gasoline or distillate shall be included unless said gasoline or distillate shall have previously COME TO REST within the meaning of the 

Federal Constitution."

Very little, if any, refining, manufacturing, producing or compounding is done in the State and inasmuch as all taxable substances under the Act are imported into the State, tax liability accrues when gasoline or distillate is placed in storage in Tennessee. 

There has been in the past some misunderstanding as to when the gasoline tax should be paid and in some instances payment of the tax was being made upon "withdrawals" from storage.

The gasoline tax law was amended in 1933, changing the tax liability or measure from a "sales" basis to a "receipts" basis and in Texas Company V. Fort, Commissioner, 168 Tennessee 679, the opinion of the Court was that: "Gasoline tax should be paid by dealers and distributors according to the amount held in storage in this state, instead of according to the number of gallons withdrawn from storage-and that it also applied to gasoline in storage on April 22, 1933, the effective date of the Act." 

Under the statutes there is a conditional exemption in the case of gasoline and distillate stored in the State for subsequent export to points outside the State-discussed more fully herein under Section 1140. "The gasoline tax is a privilege or excise tax-it is not a property tax'-(Foster and Creighton Co., V. Graham, 154 Tennessee 412.) "The 'privilege' tax is imposed upon storing, withdrawing, or distributing gasoline it is not a tax on gasoline."" (American Airways, Inc. V. Wallace, 57 Federal (2nd) 877).

Gasoline moving in Interstate Commerce, or temporarily halted in Tennessee awaiting a continuation of its journey to another state, is not taxable because such gasoline could not be construed as having "come to rest" or stored in this State. In Nashville, Chattanooga and St. 

Louis R. R. Co., V. Wallace 288 U. S. 249, the opinion of the U. S. Supreme Court was- (a) All gasoline stored in Tennessee is subject to the privilege tax. ceased upon unloading and storage in this State.

Ch. 7) 543 

GASOLINE TAX 

(c) The tax is not a forbidden burden upon Interstate Commerce and it does not violate the Fourteenth Amendment-the levy is a taxnot a toll or charge for the use of the highway. 

It would appear from the U. S. Supreme Court case above quoted that the State was not required under the Interstate Commerce clause of the Federal Constitution to give the conditional "export" exemption under section 1140 and further discussion in this connection will be found under that section. 

This section (1127) further provides that all gasoline and distillate distributed by any distributor to any of its service stations shall be treated as sold. This provision would appear to be useless inasmuch as tax liability accrues upon the "receipt" of all gasoline in the State. 

Gasoline purchased in Tennessee from distributors outside the State, and whether subsequently stored, sold or used, is subject to the tax. Section 1128.1, enacted in 1937, permits exemption in certain industrial usage. In Foster and Creighton Company V. Graham, Comptroller, 154

Tennessee 412, the opinion of the court was: 

1. Gasoline used in operation of motor trucks used in construction of state highways is taxable. 

2. Statute applies to consumers who purchase gasoline in interstate commerce and store it, thereafter withdrawing the same, whether for sale or other use.

Rate and Measure of Tax: Dealer- Law. Section 1128. 

Every dealer each year, when engaged in such business in this State, shall pay to the State Comptroller, through the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, for the exclusive use of the State, a special privilege tax, in addition to all other taxes, for engaging in such business in this State, equal to six (6) cents for each gallon of gasoline and six (6) cents for each gallon of distillate sold, or distributed, or stored, or used, or consumed by such dealer in this State during such year; provided, that gasoline or distillate previously identified as a measure of tax liability of a registered distributor shall not be included in the measure of said dealer's tax liability; provided, further, that no gasoline or distillate shall be included in the measure of any dealer's tax liability unless said gasoline or distillate shall have previously come to rest within the meaning of the Interstate Commerce clause of the Federal Constitution; provided, further, that no gasoline or distillate shall be included in the measure of any dealer's tax liability when such gasoline or distillate was delivered within another state into the tank of the motor vehicle using it. 

The rate and measure of the tax on a dealer is the same as on a distributor and is discussed under section 1127 herein above.

(Ch. 7  

This section (1128) also provides that gasoline and distillate previously taxed to a registered distributor shall not be included in the measure of the dealer's tax liability. 

It further provides that when gasoline or distillate was delivered in another State into the tank of a motor vehicle using it, tax liability does not accrue on such gasoline.

Tax Payable Monthly: Penalty for Delinquency- Law. Section 1129. 

Such tax shall be paid in monthly installments. If the tax shall not be paid on or before the 20th day of said succeeding month, it shall become delinquent, and subject to a penalty of one (1) per cent per day for not exceeding ten days, and it shall be the duty of the Commissioner to proceed to collect same, with the penalty and interest, by a distress warrant against the delinquent and his surety, and/or suit. 

The gasoline tax is payable in monthly installments on or before the 20th day of each succeeding month. If the tax is not paid promptly a penalty of one (1) per cent per day, but not exceeding ten days, is imposed and it is the duty of the Commissioner to proceed to collect the delinquent tax, with the penalty and interest added, by a distress warrant against the delinquent and his surety or by suit if necessary. 

In the case of George R. Dempster, Commissioner, V. 

Roy C. Wallace, Comptroller, 165 Tennessee 141, the question of authority resting with these respective officials was decided, the opinion of the court being as follows:

Ch. 7) 547 

GASOLINE TAX 

(a) The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation administers the gasoline tax laws and ascertains liability. (b) The Comptroller is the recipient of the tax. 

Allowances for Certain Losses 

Law. Section 1130. 

Allowance under general rule, covering loss of gallonage resulting from evaporation, handling, and unloading, must be uniform for all distributors, and other persons required to pay the tax; and must be based on true invoice receipts. 

Allowance under special rule, covering loss of gallonage due to fire, flood, storm, theft, or other causes over which the distributor has no control, (exclusive of loss resulting from causes listed under general rule) will be made; provided that such loss is immediately reported to the 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation; and further provided that an affidavit is made before a notary public setting out a complete description of the loss sustained, together with the further facts as to the nature of the casualty and date and time it occurred; provided, that such proof of loss shall be satisfactory to the Commissioner. 

Upon the total gallonage received or stored, or in other words, the tax "measure, an allowance of one per cent is permitted to cover losses resulting from evaporation, handling and unloading; or; expressed in another way, no tax is imposed on that portion of the product that was lost. 

The allowance under the law must be uniform and the deduction of the one per cent is permitted upon the monthly report forms made by distributors or other persons liable for the tax.

Allowances are also permitted covering loss of gallonage due to fire, flood, storm, theft, or other causes over which the distributor has no control. Such losses under the law should be reported immediately to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, supported by a sworn affidavit giving a complete description of the loss sustained, its nature and date and time it occurred. Allowance will not be made unless proof of loss is completely satisfactory to the Commissioner.

It is customary for these adjustment claims to be submitted by distributors with their monthly reports and to deduct the same from the gallonage received or the tax "measure"; but where a loss of considerable size is involved it probably would be advisable for distributors to report such losses immediately to the Commissioner, thereby allowing him or his deputies to inspect and prove such losses to their entire satisfaction.

(Ch. 7  Records to Be Kept: Failure Punishable by Fine- Law. Section 1131. 

Each person refining, storing, selling, distributing, or handling gasoline or distillate in this State, shall keep a record showing from whom the same was received, the date of its receipt, and the number of gallons received, together with such other and different information as the Commissioner may require. 

Persons transporting gasoline or distillate not previously identified as a measure of the tax liability of a registered distributor, shall have at all times with them, subject to scrutiny of representatives of the Department of Finance and Taxation and all peace officers, a true record showing where and from whom the gasoline or distillate was received, day and time of receipt, number of gallons, destination, and such other and different information as the Commissioner may require. 

Persons transporting gasoline and distillate previously identified as a measure of the tax liability of a registered distributor, shall, if the quantity transported exceeds forty gallons, be subject to the provisions of the foregoing paragraph. 

Violation of any of the provisions of this section is hereby declared to be a misdemeanor and shall be punishable by a fine of not less than twenty-five ($25.00) dollars nor more than fifty ($50.00) dollars for each offense.

Every person liable for the tax must keep records showing- (a) From whom the product was received.

(b) Date of its receipt. 

(e) Such other and different information as the Commissioner may require. 

Persons transporting gasoline or distillate upon which the tax has not been paid, and persons transporting more than forty (40) gallons upon which the tax has been paid, must have with them at all times a true record showing- (a) Where and from whom the product was received. (b) Day and time of receipt. (c) Number of gallons received. 

(d) Destination. 

(e) Such other and different information as the Commissioner may require.

Failure to keep and carry records as outlined in this section is punishable by a fine of from twenty-five ($25.00) to fifty ($50.00) dollars for each offense.

Assessment by Commissioner; When; Revocation of

Permit- Law. Section 1137. 

Upon the failure of any person engaged as distributor or dealer to make and deliver to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation the statement above provided for, or to pay the taxes due, it shall be the duty

Ch. 7) 555 

GASOLINE TAX 

of the Commissioner to revoke his permit, and immediately to proceed to inform himself as best he may regarding the matters and things to be set forth in such statement, and, from such information as he may be able to obtain, to make a statement, showing such matters and things, and determine and fix the amount of the privilege tax due the State from such delinquent person, and proceed to collect said amount, including a penalty of one per cent per day, for not exceeding ten days, and interest, by the issuance of a distress warrant against the delinquent and the surety on his bond, and, if necessary, by suit on the bond. 

Upon the request of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, it shall be the duty of the Attorney General to institute, and prosecute to conclusion all proper and necessary suits for the collection of the taxes.

Upon any distributor or dealer failing to make and deliver the monthly report or pay the taxes when due, the Commissioner must immediately revoke the permit or certificate of such distributor or dealer.

The Commissioner must then proceed to determine and fix the amount of the privilege tax due, and effect collection, including penalty of one (1) per cent per day for a period not exceeding ten (10) days, together with interest thereon. 

Distress warrants may be issued against the delinquent and the surety on his bond, and if necessary suit on the bond instigated. The Attorney General of the State, upon request of the Commissioner, must prosecute to conclusion all proper and necessary suits for the collection of gasoline taxes.

Commissioner's Assessment Prima Facie Correct- Law. Section 1138. 

Said statement, as prepared by the Commissioner, shall be deemed prima facie correct, and the burden of proof shall be upon the distributor or dealer to prove its incorrectness in any action growing out of matters and things contained therein. 

When it becomes necessary for the Commissioner to determine, fix and assess the tax, the statement so prepared by him is deemed to be correct and the burden of proof as to its incorrectness is upon the distributor or dealer in any court action. "The Commissioner is empowered to determine the amount of gasoline tax due from any delinquent dealer or distributor and is authorized to enforce collection by distraint-adequate remedies by statutory provision permits taxpayers to recover taxes illegally collected.'' (Fort, Commissioner, V. Dixie Oil Co. 170 Tennessee 183.)

(Ch. 7  Refunds of Tax Erroneously or Illegally Collected: 

Limitation: Adjustments- Law. Section 15, Art. 3, Chapter 108 Acts 1937. (General Revenue Bill) 

That whenever it shall satisfactorily appear to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation that a license tax, privilege tax, inheritance tax or other tax has been erroneously or illegally collected for the use and benefit of the State, by any county or state official, department, or department head, agent, or attorney, the said Commissioner, with the approval of the Attorney-General, is hereby authorized and empowered to adjust, settle and order the refunding of the taxes so collected and to direct the Comptroller to draw his warrant in settlement of the same. 

The Commissioner shall have no power to order any refund unless claim for the same, supported by proper proof, shall have been made within one year from the date of payment. 

Whenever it appears to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation that tax has been erroneously or illegally collected he may, with the approval of the Attorney General of the State, adjust, settle and order the refund of such tax and direct the Comptroller to draw warrant in settlement. It should be noted, however, that all claims for refund must be supported by proper proof and that under no circumstances whatsoever will a claim for refund be entertained unless submitted within one year from the date of tax payment.

Invoices to Be Prepared by Distributor- 

Law. Section 1139. 

Every distributor selling any gasoline or distillate in this State, in the original packages in which shipped, transported, or imported into this State by such distributor, shall at the time of making such sale, make out and deliver to the purchaser thereof, an invoice, in which invoice shall be stated the number of gallons of gasoline or distillate covered by such invoice, and that the same has been sold in the original packages in which the same was shipped, transported or imported into this State. 

Distributors selling gasoline or distillate in the original packages in which shipped, transported or imported into this State shall make out and deliver to the purchaser an invoice showing the number of gallons sold, and that same has been sold in the original packages. 

"Export" Shipments: Conditional Exemption- Law. Section 1140. 

Gasoline or distillate not previously the subject of an original sale in this State stored in this State for export to points outside the State, shall not be included in the measure of the tax liability of any distributor

Ch. 7) 557 

GASOLINE TAX 

or dealer; provided, that such gasoline or distillate is stored in a separate tank marked "Export Tank";

Provided, that a bond is executed by the distributor or dealer that in the opinion of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation adequately protects the State against loss of tax in case said gasoline or distillate is not subsequently exported outside the State; 

Provided, that gasoline or distillate stored for export longer than a period of sixty days must be included in the measure of the tax liability of the distributor or dealer so storing such gasoline or distillate. 

This section provides that gasoline or distillate not previously taxed and stored in Tennessee for export to other States shall be exempt from tax liability. 

In order to claim exemption under this section, distributors or dealers must. strictly comply with the following requirements: 

(a) Gasoline or distillate must be stored in separate tank or tanks marked "Export." (b) Products so stored cannot remain for a period longer than sixty (60) days; otherwise tax liability accrues. (c) Gasoline intended for "export" and that maintained for "domestic'' use cannot be commingled in the "export" tanks-otherwise tax liability accrues on the total gallonage stored in such tanks. (d) Bond-satisfactory to the Commissioner-must be executed adequately protecting the State against loss in tax in the event that such products should not be exported. 

For some time it was the general opinion that, if distributor's or dealer's books or records reflected the export of certain products, it was sufficient evidence to claim exemption under this section and in many instances gasoline intended for "export" and that intended for "domestic" use was commingled in the same tanks. 

The Interstate Commerce clause of the Federal Constitution does not require the State to give the exemption allowed under this section. The fact that gasoline stored in this State will be subsequently withdrawn and transported to, and for use in, other States, does not violate the Federal Constitution.

This was decided in Nashville, Chattanooga, and St. 

Louis R. R. Company V. Wallace 288, U. S. 249, the court opinion being: (a) All gasoline stored in Tennessee is taxable. (b) Immunity, as subject of transportation in Interstate Commerce, ceased upon unloading and storage in the State. (c) Subsequent withdrawals for use, some within and some without the State, part of it thus becoming again the subject of interstate transportation, does not affect tax liability.

(Ch. 7  

(d) The tax is not a forbidden burden on Interstate Commerce-and it does not violate the Fourteenth Amendment. 

In American Airways V. Wallace, Comptroller, 57 Federal (2nd) 877, the Court said:

Plaintiff's gasoline is brought into the State where it may remain indefinitely-Interstate transportation ceased and tax liability was created when it came to rest in the State. 

It therefore resolves itself to this: That the Legislature did not, under the Federal Constitution, have to give ex-

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is empowered to assess and collect the taxes accruing under this law. He shall issue receipts therefor if required and transmit all revenues collected to the Comptroller. Remittances of gasoline taxes are made daily as received.

Issuance of Distress Warrants: Penalties: Fee- Law. Section 1142. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, in the name of the State, may issue a distress warrant for the collection of such tax when pastdue, and for the penalties and costs; and a penalty of one per centum per day is imposed for the failure to pay such tax, and a fee of Two Dollars for the issuance of a distress warrant, and the usual commissions allowed officers collecting money by virtue of an execution issuing from a court of record; provided, however, when the penalty reaches ten per cent. no further penalty shall be collected. 

To enforce collection of taxes past due, and penalties and interest thereon, the Commissioner may, in the name of the State, issue distress warrants. Penalty of one per cent per day, with a limitation of ten per cent, is imposed for the failure to pay the tax when due. A fee of Two ($2.00) Dollars for issuance of a distress warrant, and the usual commissions allowed court officers collecting money by execution, are chargeable and collectible from the delinquent taxpayer.

Petition to stay levy of distress warrant, issued by Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and granted by Chancery Court, is dismissed. (Fort, Commissioner, V. Dixie Oil Co., 170 Tennessee 183.) 

Unlawful to Engage in Business without Permit 

Law. Section 1143. 

It shall be unlawful for any distributor or other person to engage in the business of selling, storing or distributing, in intrastate commerce, gasoline or distillate without first having obtained a permit to carry on such business from the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation.

Ch. 7) 563 

GASOLINE TAX 

Before any distributor or other person can engage in selling, storing, or distributing in instrastate commerce gasoline or distillate, a permit to carry on such business must first be obtained from the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. This section applies to all persons, including those handling gasoline upon which tax has been paid by other dealers or distributors.

Form of Application for Permit- Law. Section 1144. 

Every person desiring a permit to engage in said business of distributor, dealer, or distributing and storing gasoline, shall make application in writing therefor to the Commissioner, on forms to be by him provided, which application shall show: (a) The name and address of applicant; (b) Whether individual, partnership, association, or corporation, and, if partnership or association, the names and addresses of each member; (c) Whether it is the purpose of applicant to engage as distributor, dealer, or storer, and, (d) Whether wholesale, retail, or both. 

Bond Required-with Application for Permit 

Law. Section 1145. 

The application shall be accompanied by a bond, payable to the State of Tennessee, in such penalty as may be required by the Commissioner, such penalty, however, not to be less than one thousand dollars nor more than ten thousand dollars, signed by the applicant as principal, and by an authorized surety or bonding company, as surety, conditioned to be void if the applicant shall pay to the Comptroller all gasoline taxes that accrue against the applicant under and in accord with the provisions of this Statute. Upon the filing of the application and bond, it shall be the duty of the Commissioner to issue the permit. 

These sections apply to all persons handling gasoline upon which tax has been paid by other dealers or distributors.

All applications for permit must be accompanied by a bond, payable to the State, in an amount required by the 

Commissioner but not less than One Thousand ($1,000.00) 

Dollars nor more than Ten Thousand ($10,000.00) Dollars, signed by the applicant as principal and by an authorized surety or bonding company, conditioned to be void if applicant pays all taxes due under the statute. 

It should be noted that all persons required to pay the tax must furnish bond as required under section 1147.3.

The permit of every distributor, dealer or storer who fails to keep the records, or fails to make and deliver the statements and reports required, or who fails to pay the taxes accrued before they become delinquent, or fails to make and maintain bond as required by law, shall be revoked, and the carrying on of such business thereafter shall be unlawful. 

If any distributor or other person operates without a permit, a business for which a permit is required under the provisions of the preceding sections, he shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be fined for each separate exercise of the functions of such business the sum of Twenty-five to Fifty dollars.

Certificates of Registration- Law. Section 1147.1 

All persons now or hereafter required by the provisions of Chapter 58 of the Public Acts of 1923 as amended to pay the tax on gasoline or substitutes therefor and all persons delivering such gasoline or substitutes in quantities exceeding nine (9) gallons liquid measure to any such person required to pay said tax by the laws aforesaid shall be required to first register their names and addresses, by mail or in person, at the office of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and to receive and keep posted at their usual place of business, a certificate of registration bearing a serial number, which serial number shall be assigned to such person by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. 

All distributors or persons handling gasoline and liable for the tax and all persons delivering gasoline or substitutes exceeding nine (9) gallons liquid measure to persons liable for the tax, must first register with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, and the registration certificate issued by the Commissioner must be posted at the usual place of business of the holder. 

The certificate of registration used for dealers and distributors under this section is in lieu of the permit required under Section 1143; however, the same form of permit is issued.

Invoices to Be Issued and Kept- 

Law. Section 1147.2 

Whenever gasoline or substitutes therefor subject to the tax aforesaid, shall hereafter be delivered or distributed in the State of Tennessee by any person in quantities exceeding nine (9) gallons liquid measure to a person required to pay the tax aforesaid, such person making said delivery or distribution shall be required, at the time of said delivery, to give to the person receiving said gasoline or substitutes a written or printed invoice of sales ticket showing thereon the serial registration number of the person so delivering or distributing said gasoline and the number of gallons thereof and time of delivery, which invoice or sales ticket shall be kept on file by the person receiving the same, subject to

(Ch. 7  

inspection during reasonable business hours by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, or his duly authorized deputies, agents, inspectors or employees, for a period of six (6) months from the date of the receipt of such gasoline or substitutes. 

All persons making delivery of gasoline or substitutes to any person required to pay the tax must at the time of delivery give an invoice or sales ticket showing: (a) Registration number. (b) Amount of gasoline. (c) Date and time of delivery.

Such invoice or sales ticket must be kept on file by the recipient and be made readily available for inspection by the Commissioner or his deputies for a minimum period of six (6) months from the date of the receipt of such gasoline or substitutes. 

It would appear advisable for all persons dealing in, handling, or transporting gasoline or substitutes to use extreme care and diligence in the preparation and maintenance of all records pertaining to the products taxable under this Act. 

Bond Required of Persons Liable for the Tax; Notice to Surety Upon Delinquency- 

Law.

Section 1147.3 

The All persons required to pay said gasoline tax as aforesaid shall execute a bond securing the payment of all such taxes thereafter accruing, said bond to be payable to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, and to be signed by some solvent corporate surety residing in or having an office and agent in the State of Tennessee, and to be approved by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. penalty of said bond shall be in a sum equal to twice the amount of the tax required to be paid by such person per month and shall be determined by averaging such tax over the period of six (6) months immediately preceding the execution of said bond, and if such person shall not have been in business for a period of six (6) months the penalty of said bond shall be determined on the average tax per month during the actual time such person has been engaged in business. 

In the event such person shall not have previously engaged in said business, the penalty of said bond shall be fixed at Five Thousand ($5,000.00) 

Dollars during the first month and thereafter said penalty shall be governed by the previous provisions of this Act; provided, however, that in no event shall the penalty of the bond herein provided for be less than the sum of Twenty-Five Hundred ($2,500.00) Dollars irrespective of the volume of business carried on by the taxpayer. If at any time after the execution of said bond the surety thereon shall become insolvent the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may require the execution of a new bond with good and solvent surety in the same manner and with the same penalty as aforesaid, and subject to the approval of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, and any person

Ch. 7) 569 

GASOLINE TAX 

executing a bond under the provisions of this law, may, at any time prior to default under any existing bond, apply to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation for cancellation of the existing bond and for leave to file a new bond with new surety thereon in accordance with the provisions aforesaid, and shall have the right to file such new bond, at such time, by and with the approval of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation.

In case the taxpayer fails to pay the taxes due for any month as and when the same becomes due, the surety on the taxpayer's bond shall be notified by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation within fifteen days from the date such taxes become delinquent, and in the absence of such notice the surety will not be liable for additional taxes which may accrue for succeeding months after the taxes become delinquent. 

Such notice shall be given to the surety by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation in writing sent either to the authorized representative of the surety in the State of Tennessee or to the home office of the surety. 

This section requires all persons liable for the gasoline tax to furnish bond signed by solvent surety, payable to the Commissioner and approved by him. The amount of the bond is regulated by the tax liability. It is determined by taking the average monthly tax over a period of six months and multiplying by two, and in the event that the applicant for bond has not previously engaged in the gasoline business, then such bond is fixed at $5,000.00 and adjusted later upon the average monthly tax basis. 

In no event, can the amount of the bond be less than $2,500.00.

Should the surety on any bond become insolvent, the Commissioner may require the execution of a new bond in the same manner as heretofore stated. Application for cancellation of an existing bond may be made by the execution thereof at any time prior to default, provided at that time a new bond be filed and approved by the Commissioner. 

Under Chapter 134, Acts of 1937, a new provision was enacted to the effect that when a taxpayer fails to pay gasoline taxes when due, the surety on the bond shall be notified by the Commissioner within fifteen (15) days from the date of delinquency, and should the Commissioner fail to notify the surety within the time provided, then the surety is relieved from any liability for additional unpaid taxes accruing after the date of delinquency. Such notices to sureties must be made in writing by the Commissioner.

 Commissioner's Action Against Delinquents: Prose cution 

Law. Section 1147.4 

If any such person shall at any time make default in the payment of said taxes required by the laws aforesaid, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall send by registered mail, with return receipt requested, written notice and demand for payment of such delinquent tax, showing the amount thereof due and unpaid, to the surety or sureties on said bond, at the address shown thereon or to the last known address, and if said delinquent tax and all interest and penalties legally due thereon shall not be paid within ten (10) days after the mailing of such notice and demand such fact shall be certified to the State Comptroller by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and Attorney

General for State of Tennessee shall upon request of State Comptroller institute and prosecute suit in a court of proper jurisdiction for the amount of said delinquent tax with all legal interest and penalties thereon against the principal and surety or sureties on said bond, or said Attorney General may, within his discretion, institute said suit solely against the surety or sureties on said bond without the necessity of joining the principal in said suit.

The Commissioner is hereby directed and empowered to cancel and revoke the certificate of registration provided in Section 1147.1 of this 

Act if and when the holder of such certificate of registration is delinquent in the payment of the tax for a period of thirty days, and when such certificate of registration is thus revoked, and cancelled by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, it shall be a misdemeanor for the person to whom such certificate shall have been issued to continue in business and punishable as provided in Section 1147.7 hereof. 

Upon delinquency of any taxpayer the Commissioner must send by registered mail written notice and demand for payment of the tax to the surety or sureties and if said delinquent tax, penalties and interest shall not be paid within ten (10) days after mailing of the notice, certification of such fact shall be made by the Commissioner to the State Comptroller and the Attorney General, upon request, must institute and prosecute suit for the full amount against the principal or the bond surety, or both. 

If the holder of a certificate of registration is delinquent in payment of tax for a period of thirty days, the Commissioner is empowered to cancel and revoke such certificate and continuance in business of any person after such revocation is punishable by fines as provided in sec tion 1147.7.

These

That every public and/or common carrier delivering gasoline, benzol, kerosene and/or any other liquid petroleum substance or substitutes therefor in this State shall make out and send in to the Department of Finance and Taxation at the end of each calendar month a true report showing the date of delivery, location and consignee, car number and initial, contents, and, in the case of delivery by tank-wagon, or other motor vehicle, the truck license of said vehicle and the number of gallons delivered during the month for which the report shall be made. reports shall be made and sent in on forms provided by the Department of Finance and Taxation, and must be made out and sent in by the delivering carrier, or his or its agent nearest to the point of delivery within ten (10) days after the end of the month in which the deliveries were made, provided that any public and/or common carrier and/or any agent or servant of such carrier which or who shall wilfully fail or refuse to comply with the provisions of this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction shall be fined not less than One ($1.00) Dollar nor more than Five Hundred ($500.00) Dollars, or imprisoned in the county jail for thirty (30) days, or both.

Rights in Certain Areas- Law. Section 1148 

Under the terms of the cession of jurisdiction to the United States of America by this State, the right is reserved to this State to tax sales of, and privileges of dealing in, gasoline and other fuels, and oils, used in the operation of motor vehicles, within the limits of the Great Smoky Mountain Park in the boundaries of the State. 

Provided, further, the right is reserved to this State to tax sales of and privileges of dealing in, gasoline and other fuels and oils used in operation of motor vehicles, within limits of any reservation or preserve in the boundaries of this State. 

The State of Tennessee has the right to tax sales of, and privileges of dealing in, gasoline and other fuels, and

(Ch. 7  

oils, used in operating motor vehicles in the Great Smoky Mountain Park and within the limits of any reservation or preserve in the boundaries of the State. 

Federal Exemptions- 

On the monthly report form, distributors and others. are permitted to deduct from "receipts" or "measure" of the tax the amount of gasoline sold to agencies of the United States and used in government-owned vehicles. 

However, the following remarks are made in connection with this "exemption".

The gasoline tax law does not contain or make reference to any exemption other than by products intended for "export" under Section 1140. 

In Foster and Creighton Company V. Graham, Comptroller, 154 Tennessee 412, the court said: "Gasoline tax is a Privilege or Excise tax-it is not a Property tax." 

In American Airways V. Wallace, Comptroller, 57 

Federal (2nd) 877, the court said: "Statute imposes tax upon the privilege of storing, withdrawing or distributing gasoline-it is not a tax on gasoline.' 

The statute does not impose a tax on the Federal Government, nor an instrumentality, or agency thereof. It is a privilege tax upon engaging in business within this state and applies to all persons, firms or corporations doing a like business.

The tax is on the distributor for storing the gasoline and it matters little what he does with it after such storage takes place. Of course if the Federal Government stored the gasoline itself, then the tax would be a direct tax; on the other hand, it might be argued that the present taxing statute, if applied in its strict terms, would constitute an indirect tax and burden upon a governmental function. 

If the tax was assessed to the distributor storing the gasoline it probably would be impossible for him to pass the tax on to the Federal Government and in addition, he could not afford to absorb the tax burden himself: and, therefore, the Federal Government would undoubtedly

Ch. 7) 575 

GASOLINE TAX 

store the gasoline itself and then of course no tax liability could exist. Undoubtedly the practical solution is to allow the exemptions in their present form. 

Conditional Special Tax of One-Half of One Cent Per Gallon- Law. Section 1148.1 

All inhabitants, persons, firms, corporations, syndicates, joint-stock associations, or agents thereof engaged in the activity in this State of dealing in and/or storing for any purpose whatsoever coal oil, kerosene, benzol, benzine, gas oil, processed fuel oil, gasoline as defined in Chapter 20, Acts of 1925, carried into the Code as Article 6, and/or any other volatile substance identified in Chapter 12, Acts of 1929, Article 14, Code of Tennessee, shall pay to the State of Tennessee, as a special privilege tax in addition to all other privilege taxes required to be paid in this State, an amount equal to one-half of one cent for each gallon of coal oil, kerosene, benzol, benzine, gas oil, processed fuel oil, gasoline and/or any other volatile substance identified in Chapter 12, Acts of 1929, sold, delivered or distributed in this State, after such commodities have come to rest in this State. 

Provided, however, that when such substances subject to inspection under present or future inspection laws, have been inspected and the inspection fees thereon paid to the State of Tennessee as now required by law, they shall not be subject to or required to pay this one-half of one cent special privilege tax.

Provided, further, that this is a special privilege tax for the State, and no county or municipality in this State is authorized to levy and collect said special privilege tax as provided herein. 

Monthly Reports and Payment of Special Tax- Law. Section 1148.2 

Each inhabitant, person, firm, corporation, syndicate, joint-stock associations or agent thereof, subject to the payment of the special privilege tax provided for herein, and subject to pay the special privilege tax herein provided, shall make a monthly report to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation on or by the tenth of the succeeding month, showing the amount in gallons of each said commodity sold, delivered or distributed for the preceding month and subject to be estimated in calculating the amount of privilege tax as herein provided, and shall also make monthly remittance to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation for the amount of the special tax based upon and equal to said one-half cent per gallon for each gallon of said commodities so sold, delivered or distributed during the preceding month, Said report to be made under oath. Provided, that in making said report and remittance to cover to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, any of the commodities named and defined in this Act, and which have been inspected and the inspection fees thereon paid shall not be included in said report, nor in estimating the amount of privilege tax to be paid under the provisions of this Act. 

"Export" Products Exempt from Special Tax- Law. Section 1148.3 

None of the provisions of this Act shall apply to any of the above mentioned substances and commodities coming to rest or stored in this State for the purpose of sale, exportation and shipment out of the State and not to be sold, distributed and used or consumed within this State.

(Ch. 7  

Chapter 77 of Public Acts of 1933 levies an additional privilege tax equal to one-half of one cent for each gallon of petroleum products or other volatile substances taxable under the gasoline taxing statutes. Provided, however, that such substances have not been inspected and the inspection fees thereon paid. 

This additional tax cannot be levied where distributors or other persons have paid the fees under the inspection statutes.

Foster and Creighton Company

EDGAR J. GRAHAM, COMPTROLLER, ET AL 154 TENNESSEE 412 December Term, 1925 (From Davidson County) 

1. Gasoline used in operation of motor trucks used in the construction of state highways is taxable. 

2. Statute applies to consumers who purchase gasoline in interstate commerce and store it, thereafter withdrawing the same, whether for sale or other use. 

3. Gasoline tax is a privilege or excise tax-it is not a property tax. 

Opinion by Justice Hall. 

The bill in this cause was filed by Foster & Creighton Company, a Tennessee corporation, with its principal office at Nashville, against Edgar J. Graham, State comptroller, and Frank S. Hall, commissioner of finance and taxation, both individually and in their official capacities, to recover two payments made by complainant, under protest, of gasoline tax, amounting to $510.45, which complainant had been compelled to pay the State under chap- 577

(Ch. 7 

ter 58 of the Public Acts of 1923, as amended by chapter 67, of the Public Acts of 1925, on two tank cars of gasoline, one car containing eight thousand ninety-five gallons and the other eight thousand thirty-six gallons. 

The bill alleges that the complainant is engaged in the contracting business, erecting buildings, building roads, etc., and while engaged in constructing a road in Maury 

County, Tenn., it purchased in interstate commerce, and had shipped to it, the two cars of gasoline in question, not for sale, but to be used by it in the operation of its motor trucks used in the construction of said highway under a contract with the State.

The bill further alleged that complainant has never been a distributor or dealer in gasoline, nor engaged in the business of refining, manufacturing, producing, or compounding gasoline or selling it in this State, nor has it ever been engaged in the business of storing the same in this State for any other purpose than its own use; that, when the gasoline in question was received in the tank cars above mentioned, it was placed in a tank in Maury County, to be used by complainant for its own purposes, and was so used as a necessary incident to the proper carrying on of its business as a road contractor, for the carrying on of which business it had paid a privilege tax to the State; that there was no filling station convenient to the work in which complainant was engaged in performing; and that said gasoline was purchased by complainant, and stored by it in its own tank, for convenience, and withdrawn as it was needed for use in its business. 

The bill alleged that, under a proper construction of chapter 58 of the Public Acts of 1923, as amended by chapter 67 of the Public Acts of 1925, the act does not impose the three cent gasoline tax upon one who is not a dealer or distributor, but only stores gasoline in his own tank, and withdraws the same for his own use; but that, if said act, as amended, when properly construed, does apply in such case, then, to that extent, it contravenes article 1, section 8, article 11,. section 8, article 2, section 17 and article 2 section 28, of the State Constitution and is invalid.

Ch. 7) 579 

GASOLINE TAX 

That article 2, section 28, is violated because: (a) A tax on the use or consumption of a particular commodity is a property tax, and all taxes on property must be uniform, and according to its value. (b) That it is not a privilege tax, and is not included in the power delegated to the legislature by our Constitution to levy privilege taxes. (c) That the selection of the use of gasoline alone for taxation, to the exclusion of all other petroleum products, is reasonable and arbitrary, and violates article 1, section 8, and article 11, section 8 of our Constitution. (d) That the act, as amended, violates article 2, section 17, of our Constitution, because the caption is expressly limited to a tax on the business of selling, storing, or distributing gasoline, while the body of the act applies to those who may purchase and store gasoline, and thereafter withdraw it for their own use, and therefore contains a subject not expressed in the caption. 

A demurrer was filed to the bill by the defendants, which was sustained by the chancellor, and the bill dismissed, from which decree complainant has appealed and assigned errors, raising substantially the questions above indicated.

The caption of chapter 58 of the Acts of 1923 reads as follows. "An act requiring all persons, firms, associations, joint-stockcompanies, syndicates and corporations engaged in or carrying on the business of this State, of selling gasoline and distillate in this State, to pay to the State comptroller a privilege tax, for engaging in and carrying on such business in this State, equal to two cents per gallon of such gasoline and distillate, to be in addition to all other taxes, such fund to be used solely in the construction and maintenance of a highway system in the State."'

Section 1 of said act reads: 

"Be it enacted by the general assembly of the State of Tennessee, that as used in this act the term 'person' means and includes every individual, firm, association, joint-stock company, syndicate and corporation. "The term 'distributor' means and includes every person who engages in the business in the State of refining, manufacturing, producing or compounding gasoline or distillate, and selling the same in this State; and also every person who engages in the business in this State

(Ch. 7  

of shipping, transporting or importing any gasoline or distillate into, and making original sales of the same, in this State. 

"The term 'dealer' means and includes every person, other than a distributor, who engages in the business in this State, of distributing or selling gasoline or distillate with in this State."' 

By subsequent sections a privilege tax of two cents a gallon was imposed on dealers, "for each gallon of gasoline sold or distributed by such dealer in this State." This tax, by the express terms of the act, was denominated a special privilege tax in addition to all other taxes."' 

The tax was subsequently increased to three cents by chapter 4 of the Public Acts of 1925. 

The caption of the amendatory act (chapter 67, Acts of 1925) reads as follows: 

"An act to amend an act entitled: 'An act requiring all persons, firms, associations, joint-stock companies, syndicates and corporations engaged in or carrying on such business in this State of selling gasoline and distillate in this State, to pay to the State comptroller a privilege tax for engaging in and carrying on such business in this State, equal to two cents per gallon of such gasoline and distillate, to be in addition to all other taxes, such fund to be used solely in the construction and maintenance of a highway system in the State,' being chapter 58 of the Public Acts of 1923, so as to amend the caption by including the words, 'or storing or distributing' after the word 'selling' in the third line of the caption of the printed act as published, and by amending the body of the act by imposing the tax upon persons, firms, associations, joint-stock companies, syndicates and corporations storing or distributing any of the products mentioned in said act." 

Section 1 of this amendatory act reads: 

"Be it enacted by the general assembly of the State of Tennessee, that the caption of chapter 58, of the Public Acts of 1923, being entitled 'An act requiring all persons, firms, associations, joint-stock companies, syndicates, and corporations engaged in or carrying on the business in this State of selling gasoline and distillate in this State, to pay to the State comptroller a privilege tax for engaging in and carrying on such business in this State, equal to two cents per gallon of such gasoline and distillate, to be in addition to all other taxes, such fund to be used solely in the construction and maintenance of the highway system in the State, 'be amended so as to add after the word 'selling' and before the word 'gasoline,' the words, 'or storing or distributing. 

Section 2 reads: 

" "" " that section 3 thereof be amended by adding at the end thereof the following: 'The tax imposed by this act shall apply to persons, firms, or corporations, dealers or distributors, storing any of the products mentioned in this act, and distributing the same, or allowing the same to be withdrawn from storage, whether such withdrawal be for sale or other use; provided that "sellers" of gasoline and such substitutes thereof and distillates paying the tax herein provided

Ch. 7) 581 

GASOLINE TAX 

may continue to pay the same computed and paid on the basis of their sales as hereinbefore required and stores and distributors shall compute and pay this tax on the basis of their withdrawals or distributions.'" 

It will be seen that the act of 1923 imposed a tax on "dealers," and measured it by the quantity of gasoline "sold or distributed" by them, and the term "dealer" was defined as one engaged in the business of "distributing or selling gasoline.”

The act of 1925 extended the scope of the act of 1923 so as to include, not only those engaged in selling gasoline, but also those engaged in storing it, and then withdrawing it for sale or other use.

The original act expressly excluded from its operation gasoline while it was in interstate commerce (section 2). 

All other gasoline, when sold or distributed, was included in the calculation of the tax.

We think the effect of the amendatory act of 1925, when properly interpreted, is to reach gasoline that is stored and thereafter withdrawn and used without being sold by any person, etc.

Under the act of 1923, a large consumer of gasoline, desiring to escape the tax levied by the act, could do so by buying his gasoline in quantities, say in tank lots, storing it, thereafter withdrawing it, and using it as needed. 

In such case there would be no intrastate sale or distribution within the meaning of said act, and such consumer would not, therefore, be subject to the tax. 

It was manifestly the purpose of the legislature in passing the amendatory act to cut off this avenue through which large consumers might evade the tax. 

We think the act, when properly interpreted, not only applies to distributors and dealers in gasoline, but applies to consumers who purchase gasoline in interstate commerce and store it, and thereafter distribute the same, or allow the same to be withdrawn from storage, whether such withdrawal be for sale or other use. It therefore necessarily follows that complainant, and all other persons, etc, in like situations, come within the provisions of said act. 

We now come to a consideration of the constitutional question urged against the validity of the act. It is first

(Ch. 7  

said that this tax is not a privilege tax, but is a tax on property, because a tax levied upon the use of, or by reason of the ownership of, property, such as its withdrawal from storage, etc., is a tax upon the property itself, and therefore the act, as amended, violates article 2, section 28, of our Constitution.

All taxes, other than polls, are either direct or indirect. 

A direct tax is one that is imposed directly on property according to its value. It is generally spoken of as a property tax, or an ad valorem tax. An indirect tax is a tax upon some right or privilege, and it is also called an excise or occupation tax. 

In 26 R. C. L., section 16, p. 35, it is said: "The phraseology of the various Constitutions is not invariably the same, and different words are used in the different States to describe the two classes of taxes; but it is believed that there is no substantial difference in actual practice. An excise and a property tax, when the two approach each other, ordinarily may be distinguished by the respective methods adopted of laying them and fixing their amounts. If a tax is imposed directly by the legislature without assessment, and its sum is measured by the amount of business done or the extent to which the conferred privileges have been enjoyed or exercised by the taxpayer irrespective of the nature or value of the taxpayer's assets, it is regarded as an excise; but, if the tax is computed upon a valuation of property, and assessed by assessors either where it is situated or at the owner's domicile, although privileges may be included in the valuation, it is considered a property tax." 

In 26 R. C. L., section 209, p. 236, it is also said; "Every form of tax not imposed directly upon polls or property must constitute an excise, if it is a valid tax of any description." 

Again, in the same section, it is said: "On the other hand, the use of property of certain classes, especially luxuries, has always been considered a proper subject of excise. 

Thus a tax on the use of carriages was imposed in some of the colonies even prior to the Revolution, and a similar tax imposed by the United States in 1794 was sustained after much discussion as a valid excise. 

So also taxes on the use of billiard tables even by the owner for his own amusement have not been uncommon, and have been everywhere sustained. The license taxes on automobiles, from which almost every 

State derives a substantial revenue, are a modern example of the same sort of tax." 

In Bank of Commerce & Trust Co. v. Senter, 149 Tenn., 569, 260 S. W., 144, this court expressly held that the term "excise tax" was synonymous with the term "privilege tax," and that the two are often used interchange-

Ch. 7) 583 

GASOLINE TAX 

ably. It was also held in that case that the term "excise tax" is never applied to direct taxation. 

In Ogilvie v. Hailey, 141 Tenn., 392, 210 S. W., 645, this court upheld the validity of an act levying a privilege tax on automobiles used for pleasure. In that case, among other things, the court said: "It is next insisted that the use of automobiles for pleasure cannot be declared a privilege, inasmuch as such use is not the pursuit of any business or occupation, and it is sought to limit a privilege to such pursuits. "While some of our older cases apparently justify these arguments, later decisions of this court declare that the doing of a single act may be declared a privilege.'
