HISTORY OF TOBACCO TAX 

Governor Peay appears to be the first Governor to recommend the Tobacco Tax, in his message to the 64th 

General Assembly he states: 

"" Recent history is briefly repeated. January 1st, 1923, before this administration assumed control, the correct deficit as hereinbefore shown was a little less than $3,000,000. During 1923, an extra million dollars was paid on the State debt and this deficit was reduced to $418,276.16. This amount was the deficit on January 1st, 1924. By

January 1st, 1925, we had liquidated the deficit in its entirety and had on hand a surplus of $761,570.89. Therefore, we should be able by a strict business and rigid economy to produce a further surplus during 1925 of $1,000,000. We have prepared a bill approved by the Attorney- 

General as to its validity, imposing a moderate sales tax on all manufactured tobacco sold in this State which we estimate will produce a new revenue of $750,000 per year. The present surplus combined with this revenue will provide the necessary funds for the first year of the biennium. We are hoping to accumulate such surplus during this year which combined with the increased revenues from the biennial assessments to be made in 1925, which undoubtedly will show much new property and from suggested amendments to the revenue bill recommended for your enactment to cover the disbursements in the second year of the biennium in spite of the tax reduction. We believe from mature consideration that these plans can be executed and that these splendid improvements and additions to our institutional and school plants and the supplemental aid to our rural schools can thus be provided and accomplished without issuance of any interest bearing debt. All depends on our ability to compel absolute and rigid economy in the next two years and on your action in refusing other appropriations. Working together in the execution of these plans, we can realize this program and establish a new record for constructive progress in our State. The goal is worth our while. This sales tax should not be continued as a permanent feature in our revenue system. The ordinary revenue will be sufficient after these capital investments have been executed. • • 

Pursuant to the recommendation of Governor Peay, the Legislature of 1925 enacted the first Tobacco Tax Law (Chapter 2, Acts of 1925). A tax of 10% of the intended retail sales price of all manufactured tobacco products was imposed. The act expired by limitation on Feb'y 28, 1927, and appears to have been passed to raise revenue for a specific purpose.

It is interesting to note that Governor Peay in recommending the Tobacco Tax states "This tax should not be continued as a permanent feature in our revenue system," however, it appears that this tax was an issue in the campaign of 1926 and in his message to the 65th General Assembly under date January 6, 1927, Governor Peay states: 717

(Ch. 9 

The tax on manufactured tobacco imposed in Chapter 2 of the Public Acts of 1925, expiring by limitation February 28 next, should be reenacted without any delay. Hesitation on your part would be misunderstood and misconstrued. This tax was a prominent issue in the campaigns of last year. The present Governor advocated its reenactment. 

The people sustained him. They expect you to continue this tax. Failure to do so would be a breach of good faith. All appeals to the contrary should be ignored with contempt. I urge you to reenact this tax as soon as possible. It is not subject to any sound objections. Some objections can be found to any tax. This tax is profitable to the merchants who sell tobacco. There is no substance in their complaints. It would be suicidal to not reenact this tax. It would be a blow to education in this State which could not be cured in another generation. All revenues from this tax are needed for schools. Not less than $800,000 from the proceeds must be used to extend the eight month school to all the counties. Disposition of the balance should be provided in later bills, as will be recommended hereinafter in order to avoid multiplicity of subjects and detail in the reenacting bill. 

Other amendments will be introduced for the better administration and enforcement of the tax and to protect honest dealers from evading and dishonest dealers. . . ."

Under date, January 20, 1927, the Legislature passed Chapter 2, Acts of 1927, The Act was approved by Governor Peay on January 28, 1927 and became effective Feby. 27, 1927 thus continuing the Act of 1925 and imposing a tax of 10% on the intended retail sales price of all manufactured Tobacco products.

In accordance with the recommendations of Governor Peay the Legislature enacted Chapter 41 and 77 designed to strengthen the Tobacco Tax Law. 

Under date January 18, 1929, Governor Horton sent his message to the 66th General Assembly and as regards 

Tobacco Tax he states: "... they are convinced as troublesome as certain privilege and luxury taxes may be they are far more desirable than the general property tax, the abolition of which their adoption will make possible. 

Our first experience with a luxury tax was the result of Chapter 2, of the Public Acts of 1925, known as the Tobacco Tax. This tax has made possible the marked improvement in our educational system. It has provided $800,000.00 per annum for rural elementary schools, $200,000.00 each year for the high schools, $82,500.00 per annum for the amortization of the Rural Schoolhouse Bonds, and $148,927.58 for the amortization of the University of Tennessee Building Bonds. But notwithstanding the accomplishments which have been made possible by this legislation the administration of the Act has been made difficult because the tax insignia has generally remained to be affixed by the retailer and it has required more field men than the statutory administrative expense could supply to assure the State that income to which it is by law entitled. An amendment to the Tobacco Tax Act has been submitted and has my approval. This amendment does not raise the rate of taxation and has to do merely with the administrative features of the Act. This tax should be collected from the person, firm or corporation which makes the original sale of Tobacco in Tennessee. The loop-holes for evasion

Ch. 9)

TOBACCO TAX 

12 20 will thereby be avoided. It is my belief that this amendment will greatly increase receipts from the tobacco tax by decreasing the opportunities for evasion. As soon as the amendment is enacted I recommend a change in Chapter 88, Acts of 1927, whereby the sum of $206,250.00 per annum be set apart as the fourth lien upon tobacco tax receipts for the retirement of the University of Tennessee Building Bonds, with a provision that the residue revert annually to the General School Fund. Under this plan considerable revenue will revert to the school fund each year.' 

On March 29, 1929, Governor Horton approved House

Bill No. 468, Chapter 50, Acts of 1929, which amends Chap ter 2, Acts of 1927 in accordance with his recommendation, however, despite his recommendation that the tax rate remain the same, it was increased from "10% of the intended retail sales price" on cigarettes to one-tenth of one cent for each cigarette. . . ."

The Proclamation of Governor Horton convening the 

General Assembly in extraordinary Session on December 

2, 1929, contains the following: • • • 66 the more effective enforcement of the Tobacco Tax Law, Chapter 2, of the Public Acts of 1927, as amended, the express limitation thereon of noninterference with interstate or foreign commerce and the increase of the tax on the sale of cigarettes therein imposed.'' 

In his message to the Extra Session, under date of Dec. 

2, 1929 he states: "" it is, of course, imperative that the State should have additional revenue. It is out of the question for a rich and prosperous State like Tennessee not to have a balanced budget. 

The tobacco tax has become one of the fixed features of our fiscal system. It is an admirable revenue producer and is a voluntary luxury tax, greatly to be preferred to a compulsory property tax. An increase from two to four cents per package on cigarettes is recommended in this tax."

Upon the recommendation of the Governor, Chapter 17 and 22 were enacted amending the Tobacco Tax Law, from an administrative point of view and increasing the tax on cigarettes to 4 cents per package.

Governor Horton convened the General Assembly into the second Extraordinary Session under date Nov. 30, 1931. The Proclamation issued Nov. 27, 1931, as regard tobacco tax states: 66 6. Legislation amending the acts levying tax on tobacco and/or its manufactured products, so as to require the tobacco tax to be paid and the stamps applied by the manufacturers and/or jobbers and/or wholesalers.’

Under date of February 28, 1933 Governor McAlister delivered his message to the 68th General Assembly, and while he made no specific reference to Tobacco Tax he did state: there will, therefore, be submitted to you for your consideration, in addition to the budgeted requirements of the department, other special statutes revising and modifying existing laws, all with a view of enhancing the certainty of the collection of such revenues and preventing their being dodged and evaded by those who should pay it." 

Accordingly the Legislature enacted two amendments to the Tobacco Tax Law of 1925 as amended (Chapter 57 and 58) seeking greater efficiency in tobacco tax collections. 

Governor Browning states in his message to the 70th

Chapter 133 Public Acts of 1937 as Amended by Chapters 201, 295 and 311 Public Acts of 1937. 

"An Act to impose a special privilege tax upon the selling, distributing, by gift or sale, storing, using or consuming of cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco and snuff; to provide means for its enforcement; to provide penalties for its violation; to appropriate revenue derived from this tax, and to repeal conflicting laws and parts of laws.'

(Ch. 9  Section 1. 

Definitions- 

Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of 

Tennessee. 

That the following terms, wherever used or referred to in this Act, shall have the following meaning: (a) The term "person" means and includes every individual, firm, association, joint stock company, syndicate and corporation. (b) The term "distributor" means and includes every person engaged in the business of receiving, manufacturing, importing or handling tobacco products and making the first sale, gift or distribution of such products; or making the first use or consumption of such products in this 

State. 

(c) The term "'dealer' means and includes every person, other than a distributor, engaged in the distribution, sale, gifts or otherwise handling tobacco products in this State. (d) The term "tobacco products" means and includes cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco and snuff. (e) The term "retail sales price" means the established price for which each cigar, cigarette, piece of manufactured tobacco or snuff is sold at retail, exclusive of the special privilege tax hereinafter imposed. (f) The term "stamp" shall mean the impression, device, stamp, label or print manufactured, printed or made as prescribed by the Commissioner. 

(g) The term "Commissioner'' means the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation of the State of Tennessee. (h) The term "Department" means the Department of Finance and Taxation of the State of Tennessee. 

Section 2. 

Persons liable; application for license; fee- 

Be it further enacted:

That every person engaged in the business of selling, distributing or handling tobacco products in this State shall on or before the first day of May, 1937, and annually thereafter, file with the Commissioner an application for license authorizing said person to engage in such business. 

The application for license shall be made on blanks furnished by the Commissioner. Said application blanks shall show the following: 

(a) Name of Applicant. 

(b) Street address of Applicant. (c) City or Town in which Applicant's place of business is to be located. (d) Kind or nature of business to be conducted. (e) Such other and further information as the Commissioner may require.

Ch. 9) 725 

TOBACCO TAX 

The application for license shall be accompanied with a fee of Five ($5.00) Dollars for "distributor's" license, and a fee of Two ($2.00) Dollars for a "dealer's' license. 

Upon receipt of application, together with the fee imposed in this section, the Commissioner, upon approval of the application, shall issue within a reasonable time to said applicant the necessary license to engage in the business named therein, the license to expire on the thirtieth day of April.

No license so issued shall be transferable and a separate license shall be required for each separate place of business and shall be prominently displayed in the place of business operated by the person to whom such license is issued. 

The Commissioner, in his discretion, is empowered to require applicants for license to execute bond with a surety company qualified to do business in this State as surety thereon, payable to the State of Tennessee and conditioned upon licensee paying the tax and affixing tax stamps to all packages or parcels of tobacco products used, sold, distributed or handled by such licensee. 

Section 3. 

Revocation of license; hearings; appeals 

 That the Commissioner may revoke any license issued under this Act upon the failure of the licensee to pay the tax or taxes herein imposed or for the violation of this statute or any rule or regulation promulgated by the Commissioner under the authority vested in him. 

The Commissioner shall, before revoking any license, notify said licensee by letter addressed and mailed to the last known address of said licensee, notifying him, and shall afford said licensee an opportunity to be heard in person or by counsel in reference thereto. The notice shall be mailed at least ten (10) days prior to a date set for hearing. 

Any licensee aggrieved by a ruling of the Commissioner with respect to the revocation of a license may have the ruling reviewed by the court in the manner now provided by law for review of actions of boards and commissions. 

Licensee shall refrain from the selling, distributing or

(Ch. 9 

handling of tobacco products pending final determination. 

The Commissioner shall have the power to issue subpoenas as provided in Code Section 1234; and this Act in no way repeals or limits Code Section 1234 through 1238, inclusive. 

(SEE SECTIONS 1234 THROUGH 1238, CODE OF TENNESSEE FOLLOWING THIS ACT.) Section 4. 

Rates of tax; conditional upon amount collected;

exemptions- 

That every dealer or distributor of tobacco products as herein defined shall pay to the Department of Finance and Taxation for exclusive state purposes, a special privilege tax in addition to all other taxes as follows: 

1. (a) When the retail sales price is one (14) cent per cigarette or less, the rate shall be one and one-half (12) mills on each such cigarette. (b) When the retail sales price is more than one (14) cent per cigarette, the rate shall be fifteen (15%) per cent of the sales price on each such cigarette. 

2. Manufactured Tobacco and Snuff.

The rate shall be five (5%) per cent of the retail sales price. 

3. (1) Little Cigars. 

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of tobacco or any substitute therefor, and weighing not more than three (3) pounds per thousand, one cent ($0.01) for each ten (10) cigars, or fraction thereof. (2) Cheroots, Stogies, etc.

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of tobacco or any substitutes therefor, retailing for three and one-third ($0.03%) cents each or less, one ($1.00) dollar per thousand. (3) Cigars.

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of tobacco, or any substitute therefor, retailing for more than three and one-third ($0.03%) cents each and not more than five ($0.05) cents each, two ($2.00) dollars per thousand. (4) Cigars.

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of Tobacco, or any substitute therefor, retailing for more than five ($0.05) cents each and not exceeding nine ($0.09) cents, three ($3.00) dollars per thousand. (5) Cigars.

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of tobacco, or any substitute therefor, retailing for more than nine ($0.09) cents each and not exceeding ten ($0.10) cents each ($5.00) dollars per thousand. (6) Cigars.

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of tobacco, or any sub-

stitute therefor, retailing for more than ten ($0.10) cents each and not exceeding twenty ($0.20) cents each, ten dollars and fifty cents ($10.50) per thousand. (7) Cigars.

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of Tobacco, or any substitute therefor, retailing for more than twenty ($0.20) cents each, thirteen dollars and fifty cents ($13.50) per thousand.

In the event the total revenues collected from the special privilege tax hereinabove levied shall, from July 1, 1937, to December 31, 1937, inclusive, amount to the sum of one million three hundred and fifty thousand ($1,350,000.00)

Dollars, then the rate hereinabove levied shall continue, be and remain in effect for the six (6) calendar months following December 31, 1937; namely, from January 1, 1938, to and including June 30, 1938; and in the event the total revenue collected from the special privilege tax hereinabove levied shall, from January 1, 1938 to June 30, 1938, inclusive, amount to the sum of one million three hundred and fifty thousand ($1,350,000.00) Dollars, then the rate hereinabove levied shall continue to be and remain in effect for the nine (9) calendar months following June 30, 1938; namely, from July 1, 1938 to March 31, 1939. In the event the total revenue in any semi-annual period herein enumerated shall not amount to the sum of one million three hundred and fifty thousand ($1,350,000.00) Dollars; then the special privilege taxes upon tobacco and tobacco products shall be as provided by Section 4 of the Chapter 133, of the 

Public Acts of the General Assembly for 1937. 

To effectuate this Act, the collecting officer shall, at the conclusion of each semi-annual period hereinabove provided, certify to the Governor the total amount of revenue collected under this Act. If such total amount is less than the sum of one million three hundred and fifty thousand ($1,350,000.00) Dollars, the Governor shall proclaim such fact and thereupon the rates provided for in Section 4 of Chapter 133, Public Acts of 1937, shall be restored and this Act shall become inoperative. It is hereby declared to be the legislative intent that this provision for a restoration of former tax rates shall be a material and vital part of this Act, without which the Act would not have been enacted. 

If, for any reason, the provision of this Act which provides for the contingent increase in the tobacco tax to the rates,

(Ch. 9

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall not be required to make any refunds on tobacco tax stamps sold prior to the date of the taking effect of this Act, or nothing herein contained shall preclude the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation from exchanging damaged stamps or stamps affixed to damaged merchandise, which stamps were sold prior to the taking effect of this Act. 

Provided, that the words "Manufactured tobacco" included in and made use of in this section of said Act, and any and all other parts of said Act, shall not include handmade twist tobacco; and that the tax provided for and imposed by said Act shall not apply to hand-made twist tobacco. 

(SEE ORIGINAL SECTION 4, CHAPTER 133 ACTS OF 1937 FOLLOWING THIS ACT.) Section 5. 

Payment of tax; stamps- 

That (a) the tax shall be paid by purchase from the Commissioner of stamps of such design and denomination as may be prescribed by the Commissioner, (b) the Commissioner is empowered to employ agents to sell the stamps herein required. Such agents shall execute bond with a solvent surety company, qualified to do business in the state, as surety thereon, payable to the State of Tennessee and conditioned to faithfully perform the duties imposed upon him, and to faithfully account for and promptly pay to the State any and all sums due the State by virtue of his employment, and shall contain such other reasonable conditions as the Commissioner may require.

Ch. 9) 729 

TOBACCO TAX Section 6. 

Discount allowed- 

That it shall be the duty of each distributor or dealer to affix to each package or parcel of tobacco products a stamp or stamps purchased from the Commissioner. Said stamps shall be affixed upon receipt of such products in this State in the manner prescribed by the Commissioner. It is not the intention of this Act to tax products in violation of the Interstate Commerce clause of the Constitution of the United States.

The Commissioner is empowered to allow any dealer, distributor or agent a discount of an amount not to exceed seven and one-half (72%) per cent of the value of the stamps as compensation for selling and affixing the stamps to tobacco products. 

Section 7. 

Contraband goods; seizure; disposition of property- 

Be it further enacted,

That all manufactured tobacco products which are or shall be owned or possessed by any person in avoidance, evasion or violation of any of the provisions of this Act, are hereby declared to be contraband goods and the same may be seized by the Commissioner, or any duly authorized representative, agent or employee of the Department, without a warrant and the said goods shall be delivered to the Department for sale at public auction to the highest bidder after due advertisement. The Department, before delivering any of said goods so seized, shall require the purchaser to affix proper amount of stamps to goods so seized. Proceeds of all such seizures shall be paid by the Commissioner into the State Treasury, and Ten (10%) per cent of such proceeds shall be set aside as expenses for the administration of this section. 

Any vehicle, not a common carrier, which may be used for transporting for the purpose of distribution, gift or sale of unstamped tobacco products shall likewise be subject to confiscation and sale in the same manner as above provided.

(Ch. 9 

Provided further, should any unstamped tobacco be found in any vehicle the same shall be prima facie evidence that it was there for gift, sale or distribution. 

In all cases of seizure of any tobacco products or other property, subject to forfeiture under the provisions of this Act, the officer or other person making the seizure shall proceed as follows:

First, he shall prepare a list containing a description of the tobacco products or other property seized, shall appraise the value of same according to his best judgment as to usual and ordinary retail prices of the articles seized, and shall deliver to the person, if any, found in possession of same, a receipt showing the fact of seizure, from whom seized, the place of seizure, a description of goods and the appraised value. A copy of said receipt shall be posted at the place of seizure and a copy shall be filed in the office of the Department and shall be open to public inspection.

Second, the Commissioner or any representative of the Department shall within five (5) days advertise the said tobacco products for sale for cash to the highest bidder, by written or printed poster, at as many as two public places in the county where the property is to be sold, one at the courthouse door in the county and one at any public place in the county, said notices to be posted at least five (5) days prior to date of sale, and shall contain a description of the property to be sold. 

Third, any person claiming any property so seized as contraband may, at any time before the sale, file with the Commissioner at Nashville a claim in writing requesting a hearing and stating his interest in the articles seized. The Commissioner shall set a date for hearing within ten days from the day the claim is filed. Any decision of the Commissioner adverse to any claimant may be reviewed in the manner now provided by law for the review of actions of boards or commissions as prescribed by Section 9008, et seq. of the Code of Tennessee. 

In the event the ruling of the Commissioner is favorable to the claimant, the Commissioner shall deliver to the claimant the tobacco products or other property so seized.

If the ruling of the Commissioner is adverse to the claimant, the Commissioner shall proceed to sell such contraband goods in accordance with the foregoing provisions of this Act unless the claimant shall secure a supersedes under Section 9017 of the Code or unless the claimant give a bond under the provisions of the following paragraph. 

When the ruling of the Commissioner is adverse to the claimant, the Commissioner shall deliver to the claimant the tobacco products or property so seized, provided the tobacco products have proper tobacco stamps affixed to each article before delivery and, provided_further, that such claimant shall give a bond payable to the State of Tennessee in a sum double the value of the property seized, with sureties approved by the Commissioner. The condition of the bond shall be that the obligors will pay to the State, through the Department, the full value of the goods or property seized unless upon certiorari the decision of the Commissioner shall be reversed and the right of the claimant to such property judicially determined.

If no claim is interposed, such tobacco products or other property shall be forfeited without further proceedings and the same shall be sold as herein provided. The above procedure is the sole remedy of any claimant and no court shall have jurisdiction to interfere therewith by replevin injunction or in any other manner.

Ch. 9) 731 

TOBACCO TAX Section 8. 

Drop shipment plan; reports required— 

That the Drop Shipment plan or system means any device whereunder a manufacturer or sales agency or drop shipment depot ships tobacco products to points in the State to be billed or collected for by some person other than the manufacturer, or sales agency, or drop shipment depot, or person shipping said products. 

Every person engaged in the activity within this State of billing, collecting for, distributing or selling tobacco products through the device, plan, scheme or artifice, commonly known as the drop shipment plan or system, shall make a complete and itemized report, giving name and address of purchaser within Twenty-four (24) hours of the receipt of taking of the order, and shall pay the tax and affix the stamps on the tobacco products before delivery. 

Section 9. 

Supervision; rules and regulations— 

Be it further enacted,

That the supervision and collection of the tax imposed herein shall be under the direction of the Department. 

The Commissioner is hereby granted full power and authority to adopt such reasonable rules and regulations not in conflict with this Act, or other statute, as he may deem necessary to enforce the collection of the tax herein levied. 

Such rules and regulations, before being effective, shall be approved by the Attorney-General. 

The Commissioner is further authorized and empowered to prescribe the methods to be used by dealers and distributors in recording purchases and sales of tobacco products and purchases and consumption of tobacco tax stamps. The 

Commissioner is further authorized and empowered to require persons selling, distributing, or dealing in tobacco products to file such reports with the Department in the manner and at such times as he may deem necessary in carrying out the provisions of this law. 

Every distributor or dealer shall permit the Commis-

(Ch. 9 

sioner, or his authorized agent or representative, to inspect at any time all tobacco products, invoices, books, papers and memoranda including the general books, both operating and proprietary ledgers, etc. as may be deemed necessary by the Commissioner in ascertaining whether or not the tax levied under the provisions of this Act has been paid, or in determining amount of such tax due. No licensed distributor or dealer shall be permitted to claim any part of the premises whereon he is engaged in business, to be exempt from inspection; as his dwelling or home, his application for license under this Act being declared an express waiver of such claim. All persons failing to permit the examination of tobacco products, invoices, books and other memoranda including the general books, both operating and proprietary ledgers, etc. or interfering with the orderly inspection or examination thereof, or failing to file such reports as may be required by the Commissioner, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

Section 10. 

Common carriers; records to be kept- 

That every common carrier in this state, transporting cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco or snuff, in this state, shall keep a complete record of all tobacco products handled in each transaction, separately, and shall show the transportation of such tobacco products, both interstate and intrastate. Every common carrier in this state shall give and permit the Commissioner free access to such books and records, and furnish such information and reports as the Commissioner may require, and any person violating this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. 

Section 11. 

Selling without license; fines- 

Be it further enacted, That it shall be unlawful for any distributor, dealer or other person to engage in the business of selling, distributing or handling tobacco products without the license as

Ch. 9) 733 

TOBACCO TAX 

herein required, or after the license herein required has been revoked; or for any distributor, dealer and their agents, representatives and employees or other person to sell, or offer for sale, or display for sale, or to possess for the purpose of sale or gift any package or parcel of tobacco products to which the tax stamp or stamps are not affixed, which, under the provisions of this Act, are required to be affixed; or for any distributor, dealer or other person to possess for the purpose of use or consumption any package or parcel of tobacco products to which, or on which, the stamp or stamps are not affixed, which, under the provisions of this Act, are required to be affixed; or for any person to violate any rule or regulation promulgated or prescribed by the Commissioner under the authority hereir vested in him; and any such distributor, dealer and their agents, representatives and employees or any other person shall be fined in a sum not less than Twenty-Five ($25.00) Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00) Dollars; and for each subsequent violation shall be punished by a fine of not less than 

One Hundred ($100.00) Dollars nor more than One Thousand ($1000.00) Dollars and be imprisoned for a period of not less than ten (10) days nor more than eleven (11) months and twenty-nine (29) days.

Section 12. 

Counterfeiting stamps; penalties— 

That any person who shall falsely and fraudulently make, forge, alter or counterfeit a stamp or stamps so prescribed by the Commissioner, or who shall cause or procure to be falsely or fraudulently made, forged, altered, or counterfeited, such stamps, or who shall knowingly and wilfully utter, publish, 'pass or tender as true, any false, altered, forged, or counterfeited stamps prescribed by this Act, or who shall re-use any stamp previously affixed, shall be guilty of a felony and be punished by imprisonment in the State Penitentiary for not less than one (1) year nor more than ten (10) years.

SECTIONS 1234 THROUGH 1238 CODE OF TENNESSEE-NOT REPEALED OR MODIFIED BY CHAPTER 133, ACTS OF 1937 AS AMENDED Section 1234. 

Witnesses may be subpoenaed—

The Commissioner shall have power to issue subpoenas in the name of the State of Tennessee requiring the attendance of such witnesses as may be designated therein at the place or places, at either the office of the Commissioner at Nashville, or at any place in the county in which the licensee has his place of business, and at such time or times as may be designated in such subpoena. The licensee shall have the right to require the Commissioner to issue any such subpoena requiring the attendance of any such witnesses as may be desired by the licensee. All such subpoenas shall be served by the sheriff, or any deputy, of the county where same is directed, and such sheriff or deputy shall be entitled to the same fees for serving such subpoenas as in the case of serving subpoenas in civil cases from any court of records. The Commissioner or any authorized agent, representative or employee, is empowered to administer oaths to

(Ch. 9  

any person so summoned or to any person giving evidence at the hearing.

Section 1235. 

Evidence required; by whom 

Any person so summoned shall give all such evidence relevant to the matter under investigation as may be required by the Commissioner or his authorized agent, representative or employee, or as may be required by the licensee.

Section 1236. 

Fees and costs allowed witnesses- The usual fees and mileage expenses allowed witnesses in cases in a court of record shall be allowed any witnesses so summoned. At such time and place of the hearing so designated, or at any time and/or place to which the Commissioner, or his duly authorized agent, representative or employee, may adjourn such hearing, the matters under consideration shall be gone into, and, after a full hearing, the Commissioner, or his duly authorized agent, representative and/or employee, shall make such finding as, in his opinion, the facts may warrant, and if he shall determine that the licensee has failed to pay the tax or taxes imposed by the terms of this law when due, or has violated any rule or regulation promulgated by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation under the authority vested in him by the terms of this statute, or has been guilty of a violation of any of the provisions of this law, as charged, the license of said licensee shall be revoked; otherwise, the charges shall be dismissed, and the license shall continue in force unimpaired; provided, however, that even though the Commissioner shall find that the licensee is guilty of the delinquency charged, but further finds that such violation by the licensee was unintentional or inadvertent, the Commissioner, or his duly authorized agent, representative or employee, may suspend the license of said licensee for a period of not exceeding thirty days; or may, if the licensee shall not there-

Ch. 9) 737 

TOBACCO TAX 

tofore have been found guilty of any delinquency by the Commissioner under this law, or the dereliction charged be remedied by the licensee at or prior to the time of the hearing, dismiss the proceeding and charges against the licensee upon the payment by the licensee of all costs and fees incurred in holding and having said hearing. 

Section 1237. 

Costs to be advanced All witness fees, mileage expenses and all fees of sheriffs for serving any notices of subpoenas shall be taxed as costs by the Commissioner, his authorized agent, representative or employee. All costs and fees for witnesses and/or sheriffs shall be advanced or collected as provided in the case of witnesses attending upon cases in courts of record, and the service of subpoenas requiring their attendance and testimony.

Section 1238. 

Costs of hearing; paid by whom- 

If, upon the hearing, the licensee shall be found by the Commissioner, or his authorized agent, representative or employee, to be guilty of the delinquency charged, all of the aforesaid costs shall be taxed and charged against the said licensee, but if the charge against such licensee shall be dismissed, then such costs shall be paid by the Commissioner out of the funds in his hands collected under the provisions of this law, after approval by him, and shall be and constitute lawful expenditures hereunder. The judgment and findings of the Commissioner, or his duly authorized agent, representative or employee, on all questions of fact in the trial of the charges preferred against any licensee under the provisions of this law shall be final, and there shall be no review thereof, except for fraud or illegality or want of jurisdiction, or, when there appears to be a lack of preponderance of evidence against any holder of the license.

SECTION 4, CHAPTER 133, ACTS OF 1937, PRIOR TO AMENDMENT BY CHAPTER 295, ACTS OF 1937 Rates of Tax- 

That every dealer or distributor of tobacco products as herein defined shall pay to the Department of Finance and Taxation for exclusive State purposes a special privilege tax in addition to all other taxes as follows: 

1. (a) When retail sales price is less than one (1) cent per cigarette, the rate shall be one-fifth (%) of one (14) cent for each cigarette. (b) When retail sales price is more than one (1) cent per cigarette, the rate shall be Twenty (20%) per cent of the sale price. 

2. Cigars, manufactured tobacco and snuff-The rate shall be ten (10%) per cent of the retail sales price.

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation (approved by

These rules and regulations supersede and rescind all rules and regulations heretofore promulgated by this Department.

Sale of Tobacco Stamps- 

1. Distributors may purchase tobacco tax stamps at a discount of 72% in lots of $100.00 or more, provided such distributor is complying with the tobacco tax law and rules and regulations promulgated in accordance therewith. 

2. Distributors who become delinquent in the payment of the tobacco tax or who violate the law or any rule or 739

(Ch. 9 

regulation, will not be permitted to purchase tobacco tax stamps at a discount for a period of six months. 

3. Dealers will not be permitted to purchase tobacco tax stamps at a discount. 

4. Dealers or Distributors must not buy, sell, or barter tobacco tax stamps, except from the Department or its authorized agent.

Affixing and Cancellation of Tobacco Tax Stamps- 

1. Tennessee Tobacco Tax Stamps must be applied to all tobacco products within twenty-four hours after the same shall have come to rest in this State. 

2. Tobacco Tax Stamps shall be applied to packages of tobacco products as follows: (a) Cigarettes. Cigarette tax stamps may be applied at any place upon cigarette packages. (b) Cigars. Cigar tax stamps must be applied to package or boxes of cigars in a manner similar to the application of Federal stamps, with stamp overlapping front and 'top of box. At the time packages or boxes of cigars are sold such stamps must be cancelled by marking date thereon. (c) Manufactured Tobacco Products and Snuff. Tobacco tax stamps must be affixed to packages or containers of manufactured tobacco products on the front of each box. In case of smoking tobacco in cloth or other bags the tax stamp may be placed on the label appearing on the package or container. (See Regulation dated November 23, 1937.) 

3. Cancellation. Tobacco tax stamps must be cancelled by placing the number of the distributor's license upon the face of the tobacco tax stamp with indelible and waterproof ink. Cancellation may be effected by the use of a rubber stamp or such other means as the distributor may choose, provided indelible and waterproof ink is used. 

Monthly Report Required- 

Distributors Shall Make Monthly Reports on blank forms prescribed by the Department and furnished to the distributors. The distributor's monthly report must be filed with this Department on or before 5th day of each month, said report to contain the total tax value of all products on hand at the beginning of the preceding month, the total tax value of tobacco products purchased or received during the month, the total tax value of all tobacco products sold or given away during the month, and the

Ch. 9) 741 

TOBACCO TAX 

total tax value of all tobacco products on hand at the end of the month. The monthly report must also show the total value of stamps on hand at the beginning of the preceding month, the total value of stamps purchased during the month, the total value of stamps affixed to tobacco products during the month and the total value of stamps on hand unaffixed at the end of the month. The report must show name and address of person and quantity of tobacco products exported before credit will be allowed for such out-of-State shipments. Incompleted, delinquent, false or fraudulent monthly report shall be justification for revocation of distributor's license.

Export Tobacco Products- 

Distributors will be permitted to keep unstamped to bacco products for EXCLUSIVE EXPORT PURPOSES 

in such quantity to cover the distributor's ordinary EXPORT requirements. The term "quantity" means a specified number of cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco products or snuff, and the quantity allowed each distributor for export purposes can in no instance exceed the quantity of such product specifically specified and shown in the distributor's license issued by this Department. Such quantity of tobacco products for export purposes must be kept in separate part of building from other tobacco products, and if not so separated the same shall be stamped.

Books and Records- 

Distributors and Dealers of tobacco products shall keep books, invoices, records and other memoranda pertaining to the handling of tobacco products until such time as the Department grants permission for such records to be destroyed. Distributors must maintain book records in such manner as will permit representatives of this Department to readily verify monthly reports with their books. 

Drop Shipments—

Distributors engaged directly or indirectly in making DROP SHIPMENTS of tobacco products must affix and

(Ch. 9  When tobacco cancel tobacco stamps before delivery. products are shipped to or in care of a licensed distributor the Drop Shipment report will not be required within twenty-four hours.

Vending Machines— 

The sale of manufactured tobacco products through vending machines will not be permitted unless such vending machine is so constructed as to permit representatives of this Department to readily determine whether tobacco products being sold through such machine have the necessary tax stamps properly affixed to such products and are properly cancelled. No dealer or distributor shall dispense tobacco products through vending machines which are not so constructed as to permit inspection of all tobacco products contained therein. Any machine used in violation of this regulation will be presumed to be used for the sale of unstamped tobacco products.

License Required for Each Separate Place of Busi ness

Dealer's license must be secured for each automobile. truck or other vehicle from which tobacco products are sold, bartered or given away. This does not include trucks used by distributors solely for delivery purposes. A dealer's license is required for each machine vending tobacco products and such license must be prominently displayed and securely attached to each vending machine. 

Confiscated Tobacco Products and Other Property— 

Confiscated tobacco products and other goods must be sent to the Department of Finance and Taxation, Nashville, Tennessee, for sale in accordance with Section 7, Chapter 133, Acts of 1937. The right to reject any or all bids to purchase confiscated tobacco products or other property is hereby reserved.

Interstate Shipments- 

Sale of tobacco products "over the counter" are not interstate sales, regardless of where the purchaser might

Ch. 9) 743 

TOBACCO TAX 

reside. All tobacco products so sold must have the proper tax stamps affixed thereto. Interstate shipments must be invoiced and copies of invoice must accompany shipment and be available to inspection of representatives of this Department at any time or place. 

Inspection- 

Every distributor, dealer or other person shall permit any authorized representative of the Department to inspect at any time all tobacco products, invoices, books, papers and memoranda including the general books, both operating and proprietary ledger. This provision includes tobacco products and invoices placed on delivery trucks or located elsewhere. Refunds Distributors having unusable stamps or stamps on unsalable products must have such stamps voided by a representative of the Department before a claim for refund will be allowed. 

Assisting Violators—

Direct or indirect assistance in the evasion of the payment of the tobacco tax or in the violation of the tobacco tax law or any rule and regulation contained herein, will be grounds for revocation or suspension of license. 

Regulation of May 1, 1937-Monthly Reports— 

The monthly report must show the total tax value of cigarettes and cigars on hand at the beginning of May 1st, and the first of each month thereafter, the total tax value of cigarettes and cigars purchased or received during the month, total tax value of cigarettes and cigars sold or given away during the month, and the total tax value of cigarettes and cigars on hand at the end of the month. 

The monthly report must, also, show the total value of four-cent cigarette stamps and cigar stamps on hand May 1st, and the first of each month thereafter, the total value

(Ch. 9  

of such stamps purchased during the month, the total value of such stamps affixed to cigarettes and cigars during the month and the total value of such stamps on hand unaffixed at the end of the month. 

The report must show name and address of the person and quantity of cigarettes and cigars exported before credit will be allowed for such out-of-state shipments. Incomplete, delinquent, false or fraudulent monthly reports shall be justification for revocation of distributor's license. 

Provided, "four-cent" cigarette stamps are affixed only to cigarettes and only "cigar" stamps are affixed to cigars. 

Regulation of August 19, 1937 Distributors of tobacco products, licensed in Tennessee, and having distribution points in other States, from which tobacco products are shipped into Tennessee, will be required to give to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, or his authorized representatives, access to books and records of all kind with reference to the handling of tobacco products kept at or for such distribution points. 

For the purpose of this Regulation, corporations, associations, and partnerships in which there is a common ownership of a majority interest, an interlocking ownership or a common management shall be deemed a single Distributor.

Regulation of November 23, 1937Tobacco tax stamps may be affixed on the front of each carton of not more than twenty-four packages of smoking tobacco or snuff when such smoking tobacco or snuff is sold by the Distributor in carton lots. 

When such tobacco or snuff is sold by the Distributor in less than carton lots, tobacco tax stamps shall be affixed' to each individual package, sack or can. 

Tax stamps, when affixed to a carton, shall be cancelled with the Distributor's cancellation number, and shall, in addition, be further cancelled by the marking of the date when such carton is sold.

This Rule and Regulation shall take effect the 1st day of December, 1937, and supersedes Rule and Regulation promulgated the 6th day of August, 1937, and all parts of Rule and Regulation promulgated the 22nd day of March, 1937, which are in conflict herewith.

May be subpoenaed 752 Definitions- 

Law. Section 1. 

That the following terms, wherever used or referred to in this Act, shall have the following meaning: 

(a) The term "person" means and includes every individual, firm, association, joint stock company, syndicate and corporation. (b) The term "distributor" means and includes every person engaged in the business of receiving, manufacturing, importing or handling tobacco products and making the first sale, gift or distribution of such products; or making the first use or consumption of such products in this State.

(Ch. 9 

(c) The term "" "'dealer'' means and includes every person, other than a distributor, engaged in the distribution, sale, gifts or otherwise handling tobacco products in this State. (d) The term "tobacco" means and includes cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco and snuff. (e) The term "retail sales price" means the established price for which each cigar, cigarette, piece of manufactured tobacco or snuff is sold at retail, exclusive of the special privilege tax hereinafter imposed. (f) The term "stamp" shall mean the impression, device, stamp, label or print manufactured, printed or made as prescribed by the Commissioner. (g) The term "Commissioner'' means the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation of the State of Tennessee. (h) The term "Department" means the Department of Finance and Taxation of the State of Tennessee. 

Person, includes individuals, firms, associations, joint stock companies, syndicates, and corporations. 

Distributor, includes: (a) All persons making the first sale, gift or distribution of tobacco products in Tennessee. (b) All who are engaged in the business of receiving, manufacturing, importing or handling tobacco products. (c) A resident of Tennessee receiving a shipment of tobacco products from a manufacturer or dealer outside of Tennessee for his personal use or consumption is defined to be a 'distributor" and as such is liable for tax and license fee imposed. 66 

Dealer, includes all persons other than a "distributor" when engaged in handling tobacco products. 

Tobacco Products, includes all manufactured tobacco products and snuff; however, handmade twist tobacco is excepted and is not to be included in this definition. 

Retail Sales Price is the established price for which each article of manufactured tobacco and snuff is sold retail, and the tax imposed upon tobacco products is not to be included in such price.

Stamp, includes all devices, impressions, prints, labels, etc. prescribed by the Commissioner.

Commissioner-Commissioner of Finance and Taxation of the State of Tennessee. 

Department-Department of Finance and Taxation of the State of Tennessee. 

Persons Liable; Application for License; Fees- 

Law. Section 2. 

That every person engaged in the business of selling, distributing or handling tobacco products in this State shall on or before the first day

of May, 1937, and annually thereafter, file with the Commissioner an application for license authorizing said person to engage in such business. 

The application for license shall be made on blanks furnished by the 

Commissioner. Said application blanks shall show the following: 

(a) Name of Applicant. 

(b) Street Address of Applicant. 

(c) City or Town in which Applicant's place of business is to be located. (d) Kind or nature of business to be conducted. (e) Such other and further information as the Commissioner may require.

The application for license shall be accompanied with a fee of Five ($5.00) Dollars for "distributor's' license, and a fee of Two ($2.00) 

Dollars for a "dealer's" license. Upon receipt of application, together with the fee imposed in this section, the Commissioner, upon approval of the application, shall issue within a reasonable time to said applicant the necessary license to engage in the business named therein, the license to expire on the thirtieth day of April.

No license so issued shall be transferable and a separate license shall be required for each separate place of business and shall be prominently displayed in the place of business operated by the person to whom such license is issued. 

The Commissioner, in his discretion, is empowered to require applicants for license to execute bond with a surety company qualified to do business in this State as surety thereon, payable to the State of Tennessee and conditioned upon licensee paying the tax and affixing tax stamps to all packages or parcels of tobacco products used, sold, distributed or handled by such licensee. "Distributors" and "Dealers' in tobacco products are required to make application to the Commissioner, on or before May 1, 1937 and annually thereafter, for a license to engage in the business of selling, distributing or handling tobacco products in Tennessee. The application is to be made upon forms prescribed and furnished by the Commissioner. A fee of $5.00 must accompany the application for "distributor" license, and a fee of $2.00 must accompany the application for "dealer" license. The license issued by the Commissioner is not transferable; and, in instances of change in ownership or location, a new license must be secured.. Licenses must be prominently displayed in the place of business and in this connection, the following rules should be noted: 

Regulation. License Required for Each Separate Place of Business. 

Dealer's license must be secured for each automobile, truck or other vehicle from which tobacco products are sold, bartered or given away. 

This does not include trucks used by distributors solely for delivery purposes. A dealer's license is required for each machine vending tobacco products and such license must be prominently displayed and securely attached to each vending machine. 

Vending Machines. 

The sale of manufactured tobacco products through vending machines will not be permitted unless such vending machine is so constructed as to permit representatives of this Department to readily determine whether tobacco products being sold through such machine have the necessary tax stamps properly affixed to such products and are properly cancelled. 

No dealer or distributor shall dispense tobacco products through vending machines which are not so constructed as to permit inspection of all tobacco products contained therein. Any machine used in violation of this regulation will be presumed to be used for the sale of unstamped tobacco products. 

Revocation of License; Hearings; Appeals—

Law. Section 3. 

That the Commissioner may revoke any license issued under this Act upon the failure of the licensee to pay the tax or taxes herein imposed or for the violation of this statute or any rule or regulation promulgated by the Commissioner under the authority vested in him. 

The Commissioner shall, before revoking any license, notify said licensee by letter addressed and mailed to the last known address of said licensee, notifying him, and shall afford said licensee an opportunity to be heard in person or by counsel in reference thereto. The notice shall be mailed at least ten (10) days prior to a date set for hearing. Any licensee aggrieved by a ruling of the Commissioner with respect to the revocation of a license may have the ruling reviewed by the court in the manner now provided by law for review of actions of boards and commissions. Licensee shall refrain from the selling, distributing or handling of tobacco products pending final determination. 

The Commissioner shall have the power to issue subpoenas as provided in Code Section 1234; and this Act in no way repeals or limits 

Code Section 1234 through 1238, inclusive. 

The Commissioner may revoke any license issued upon: (a) Failure of licensee to pay the tobacco tax, or (b) Violation of the law or any rule or regulation. 

Before revoking any license the Commissioner must give the licensee opportunity to be heard. Notice of hearing is to be given by mail at least ten days prior to the date set

(Ch. 9  

for such hearing. The licensee may be represented by counsel and if the decision of the Commissioner is adverse, appeal may be taken to any court of competent jurisdiction; however, it is unlawful for any licensee to deal in or handle tobacco products from the date of the appeal until final determination of the issue.

Commissioner May Issue Subpoenas- Law. Section 1234, Code of Tennessee. 

The Commissioner shall have power to issue subpoenas in the name of the State of Tennessee requiring the attendance of such witnesses as may be designated therein at the place or places, at either the office of the Commissioner at Nashville, or at any place in the county in which the licensee has his place of business, and at such time or times as may be designated in such subpoena. The licensee shall have the right to require the Commissioner to issue any such subpoena requiring the attendance of any such witnesses as may be desired by the licensee. All such subpoenas shall be served by the sheriff, or any deputy, of the county where same is directed, and such sheriff or deputy shall be entitled to the same fees for serving such subpoenas as in the case of serving subpoenas in civil cases from any court of records. The Commissioner or any authorized agent, representative or employee, is empowered to administer oaths to any person so summoned or to any person giving evidence at the hearing.

The Commissioner is authorized to issue subpoenas requiring the attendance of witnesses. Such subpoenas are to be served by any sheriff or his deputy and the same fee is allowed as in case of service of any subpoena in civil cases from any court of record. 

The last paragraph of Section 3, Chapter 133, Acts of 

1937, does not modify or repeal this section of the Code of Tennessee and the Commissioner is required to subpoena witnesses for the licensee as well as for the State. 

Evidence Required- Law. Section 1235 Code of Tennessee. 

Any person so summoned shall give all such evidence relevant to the matter under investigation as may be required by the Commissioner or his authorized agent, representative or employee, or as may be required by the licensee.

Persons summoned must give evidence, under oath, of all facts relevant to the case as may be required by the licensee or the Commissioner.

Ch. 9) 753 

TOBACCO TAX Fees and Costs-Allowed Witnesses- Law. Section 1236, Code of Tennessee. 

The usual fees and mileage expenses allowed witnesses in cases in a court of record shall be allowed any witnesses so summoned. At such time and place of the hearing so designated, or at any time and/or place to which the Commissioner, or his duly authorized agent, representative or employee, may adjourn such hearing, the matters under consideration shall be gone into, and, after a full hearing, the Commissioner, or his duly authorized agent, representative and/or employee, shall make such finding as, in his opinion, the facts may warrant, and if he shall determine that the licensee has failed to pay the tax or taxes imposed by the terms of this law when due, or has violated any rule or regulation promulgated by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation under the authority vested in him by the terms of this statute, or has been guilty of a violation of any of the provisions of this law, as charged, the license of said licensee shall be revoked; otherwise, the charges shall be dismissed, and the license shall continue in force unimpaired; provided, however, that even though the Commissioner shall find that the licensee is guilty of the delinquency charged, but further finds that such violation by the licensee was unintentional or inadvertent, the Commissioner, or his duly authorized agent, representative or employee, may suspend the license of said licensee for a period of not exceeding thirty days; or may, if the licensee shall not theretofore have been found guilty of any delinquency by the Commissioner under this law, or the dereliction charged be remedied by the licensee at or prior to the time of the hearing, dismiss the proceeding and charges against the licensee upon the payment by the licensee of all costs and fees incurred in holding and having said hearing.

After full and complete hearing the Commissioner shall make such findings as the facts warrant and if he finds that the licensee has failed to pay the taxes imposed or has violated any rule or regulation, the license shall be revoked; however, if the licensee is able to show that such violation was unintentional or inadvertent, the Commissioner may suspend the license for a period of thirty days; provided, the licensee has not theretofore been found guilty of violation of the law or rules and regulations. All fees, cost and expenses are to be paid by the licensee in case of revocation or suspension of license. 

Costs to be Advanced 

Law. Section 1237, Code of Tennessee. 

All witness fees, mileage expenses and all fees of sheriffs for serving any notices of subpoenas shall be taxed as costs by the Commissioner, his authorized agent, representative or employee. All costs and fees for witnesses and/or sheriffs shall be advanced or collected as provided in the case of witnesses attending upon cases in courts of record, and the service of subpoenas requiring their attendance and testimony. 

Costs and witness fees are to be advanced in the same manner as is provided for witnesses attending upon cases in

(Ch. 9  

courts of record and are to be taxed by the Commissioner upon the licensee if his findings result in the revocation or suspension of the license.

Costs of Hearing; Payable by- Law. Section 1238, Code of Tennessee. 

If, upon the hearing, the licensee shall be found by the Commissioner, or his authorized agent, representative or employee, to be guilty of the delinquency charged, all of the aforesaid costs shall be taxed and charged against the said licensee, but if the charge against such licensee shall be dismissed, then such costs shall be paid by the Commissioner out of the funds in his hands collected under the provisions of this law, after approval by him, and shall be and constitute lawful expenditures hereunder. The judgment and findings of the Commissioner, or his duly authorized agent, representative or employee, on all questions of fact in the trial of the charges preferred against any licensee under the provisions of this law shall be final, and there shall be no review thereof, except for fraud or illegality or want of jurisdiction, or, when there appears to be a lack of preponderance of evidence against any holder of the license.

Except in case of fraud, illegality or want of jurisdiction, the judgment of the Commissioner is final and there is no appeal to any court of record provided in this section; however, it appears that appeal may be taken under the provisions of Section 3, Chapter 133, Acts of 1937. 

If judgment is in favor of the State, all costs, fees and expenses are to be paid by the licensee; if judgment is for the licensee the costs, fees and expenses are to be paid by the State.

Tax Rates; Conditional Upon Amount Collected; 

Exemptions- Law. Section 4. 

That every dealer or distributor of tobacco products as herein defined shall pay to the Department of Finance and Taxation for exclusive state purposes, a special privilege tax in addition to all other taxes as follows: 

1. (a) When the retail sales price is one (14) cent per cigarette or less, the rate shall be one and one-half (12) mills on each such cigarette. (b) When the retail sales price is more than one (14) cent per cigarette, the rate shall be fifteen (15%) per cent of the sales price on each such cigarette. 

2. Manufactured Tobacco and Snuff— 

The rate shall be five (5%) per cent of the retail sales price.

3. (1) Little Cigars. 

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of tobacco or any substitute therefor, and weighing not more than three (3) pounds per thousand, one cent ($0.01) for each ten (10) cigars, or fraction thereof.

Ch. 9) 755 

TOBACCO TAX 

(2) Cheroots, Stogies, eto.

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of tobacco or any substitutes therefor, retailing for three and one-third ($0.03%) cents each or less, one ($1.00) Dollar per thousand. (3) Cigars.

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of tobacco, or any substitute therefor, retailing for more than three and one-third ($0.03%) cents each and not more than five ($0.05) cents each, two ($2.00) dollars per thousand. (4) Cigars.

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of tobacco, or any substitute therefor, retailing for more than five ($0.05) cents each and not exceeding nine ($0.09) cents each, three ($3.00) Dollars per thousand. (5) Cigars..

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of tobacco, or any substitute therefor, retailing for more than nine ($0.09) cents each and not exceeding ten ($0.10) cents each, five ($5.00) Dollars per thousand. (6) Cigars.

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of tobacco, or any substitute therefor, retailing for more than ten ($0.10) cents each and not exceeding twenty ($0.20) cents each, ten dollars and fifty cents ($10.50) per thousand. (7) Cigars.

Upon cigars of all descriptions made of tobacco, or any substitute therefor, retailing for more than twenty ($0.20) cents each, thirteen dollars and fifty ($13.50) per thousand.

In the event the total revenues collected from the special privilege tax hereinabove levied shall, from July 1, 1937, to December 31, 1937, inclusive, amount to the sum of one million three hundred and fifty thousand ($1,350,000.00) Dollars, then the rate hereinabove levied shall continue, be and remain in effect for the six (6) calendar months following 

December 31, 1937; namely, from January 1, 1938 to and including June 

30, 1938; and in the event the total revenue collected from the special privilege tax hereinabove levied shall, from January 1, 1938 to June 30, 1938, inclusive, amount to the sum of one million three hundred and fifty thousand ($1,350,000.00) Dollars, then the rate hereinabove levied shall continue, be and remain in effect for the nine (9) calendar months following June 30, 1938; namely, from July 1, 1938 to March 31, 1939. In the event the total revenue in any semi-annual period herein enumerated shall not amount to the sum of one million three hundred and fifty thousand ($1,350,000.00) Dollars; then the special privilege taxes upon tobacco and tobacco products shall be as provided by Section 4 of the Chapter 

133, of the Public Acts of the General Assembly for 1937. 

To effectuate this Act, the collecting officer shall, at the conclusion of each semi-annual period hereinabove provided, certify to the Governor the total amount of revenue collected under this Act. If such total amount is less than the sum of one million three hundred and fifty thousand ($1,350,000.00) Dollars, the Governor shall proclaim such fact and thereupon the rates provided for in Section 4 of Chapter 133, Public Acts of 1937, shall be restored and this Act shall become inoperative. 

It is hereby declared to be the legislative intent that this provision for a restoration of former tax rates shall be a material and vital part of this Act, without which the Act would not have been enacted. If, for any reason, the provision of this Act which provides for the contingent increase in the tobacco tax to the rates, as stated in Section 4, Chapter

(Ch. 9 

133, of the acts of the General Assembly for 1937, should be held invalid, then the Legislature hereby declares that it would not have enacted this amendatory Act, or any portion thereof, it being the Legislative intent that this entire amendatory Act shall, in that event, be null and void, thereby restoring the rates as fixed by Section 4 of Chapter 133, Acts of 1937. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall not be required to make any refunds on tobacco tax stamps sold prior to the date of the taking effect of this Act, or nothing herein contained shall preclude the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation from exchanging damaged stamps or stamps affixed to damaged merchandise, which stamps were sold prior to the taking effect of this Act. 

Provided, that the words "manufactured tobacco" included in and made use of in this section of said Act, and any and all other parts of said Act, shall not include handmade twist tobacco; and that the tax provided for and imposed by said Act shall not apply to handmade twist tobacco. 

The tobacco tax is a "Special Privilege" tax imposed upon dealers and distributors as defined in Section 1 and is in addition to all other taxes imposed by the State. The tax is exclusively for State purposes and a city, town, or county cannot impose a similar tax. 

The tax is measured by the "retail sale" price of manufactured tobacco products (except handmade twist tobacco) and snuff.
