The tobacco tax rates set forth above are contingent upon the total revenue aggregating $1,350,000.00 for the six months period beginning July 1, 1937 and ending December 31, 1937. If the total revenue amounts to that figure, these rates are to be continued for an additional six months period, from January 1, 1938 to June 30, 1938 and if the revenue for this period amounts to the same figure, the rates are to be continued for an additional period of

(Ch. 9 

nine months, from July 1, 1938 to March 31, 1939. It appears however, that these special rates expire by limitation on March 31, 1939 and the rates to be charged after that date are not stated.

If the revenue collected during either of the six months periods above stated is less than $1,350,000.00, the special rates provided in Chapter 295, Acts of 1937, become null and void.

This section of the Act requires the Commissioner to certify tobacco tax collections for each of the six months periods to the Governor, and if the certificate of the Commissioner indicates total revenue less than $1,350,000.00, it is mandatory-upon the Governor-for him to proclaim such fact and the tax rates provided in section 4, Chapter 133, Acts of 1937 become effective immediately. 

Payment of Tax-Sale of Stamps-Agents— Law. Section 5. 

That (a) the tax shall be paid by purchase from the Commissioner of stamps of such design and denomination as may be prescribed by the Commissioner, (b) the Commissioner is empowered to employ agents to sell the stamps herein required. Such agents shall execute bond with a solvent surety company, qualified to do business in the state, as surety thereon, payable to the State of Tennessee and conditioned to faithfully perform the duties imposed upon him, and to faithfully account for and promptly pay to the State any and all sums due the State by virtue of his employment, and shall contain such other reasonable conditions as the Commissioner may require. 

The tax is to be paid through the purchase of tobacco tax stamps of such design and in such denominations as the Commissioner may prescribe. 

The Commissioner is authorized to collect the tax through the sale of tobacco stamps by agents, and before such agent is appointed the Commissioner must secure a corporate surety bond in such amount as he deems sufficient guaranteeing the faithful performance of the agent and prompt payment of money to the State. 

However, Agents are not employed by the State and Tobacco Tax Stamps can only be purchased from the Department of Finance and Taxation, Nashville, or from branch offices of the Department located in Knoxville, Memphis and Chattanooga.

Ch. 9) 759 

TOBACCO TAX Affixing Tobacco Tax Stamps-Compensation There for- 

Law. Section 6. 

That it shall be the duty of each distributor or dealer to affix to each package or parcel of tobacco products a stamp or stamps purchased from the Commissioner. Said stamps shall be affixed upon receipt of such products in this State in the manner prescribed by the Commissioner. It is not the intention of this Act to tax products in violation of the Interstate Commerce clause of the Constitution of the United States.

The Commissioner is empowered to allow any dealer, distributor or agent a discount of an amount not to exceed seven and one-half (72) per cent of the value of the stamps as compensation for selling and affixing the stamps to tobacco products. 

Dealers and distributors are required to affix tobacco tax stamps to each package or parcel of tobacco products upon receipt thereof: Regulation.

Tennessee Tobacco Tax Stamps must be applied to all tobacco products within twenty-four hours after same shall have come to rest in this State.

Tobacco Tax Stamps shall be applied to packages of tobacco products as follows: (a) Cigarettes. Cigarette tax stamps may be applied at any place upon cigarette package. (b) Cigars.

Cigar tax stamps must be applied to package or boxes of cigars in a manner similar to the application of Federal stamps, with stamp overlapping front and top of box. At the time packages or boxes of cigars are sold such stamp must be cancelled by marking date thereon. (c) Manufactured Tobacco Products and Snuff.

Tobacco tax stamps must be affixed to package or containers of manufactured tobacco products on the front of each box. 

In case of smoking tobacco in cloth or other bags, the tax stamp may be placed on the label appearing on the package or container. (See 

Regulation dated November 23, 1937.) Cancellation.

Tobacco tax stamps must be cancelled by placing the number of the distributor's license upon the face of the tobacco tax stamp with indelible and waterproof ink. Cancellation may be effected by the use of a rubber stamp or such other means as the distributor may choose, provided indelible and waterproof ink is used. 

As compensation for affixing stamps to packages and containers of tobacco products, this section authorizes the Commissioner to sell tobacco stamps at a discount not to exceed 72 per cent; but, it should be noted that this provision is not mandatory upon the Commissioner. Attention is directed to the following;

(Ch. 9  Regulation. 

Distributors may purchase tobacco tax stamps at a discount of 72% in lots of $100.00 or more, provided such distributor is complying with the tobacco tax law and rules and regulations promulgated in accordance therewith.

Distributors who become delinquent in the payment of the tobacco tax or who violate the law or any rule or regulation, will not be permitted to purchase tobacco tax stamps at a discount for a period of six months.

Dealers will not be permitted to purchase tobacco tax stamps at a discount.

Dealers or Distributors must not buy, sell, or barter tobacco tax stamps, except from the Department or its authorized agent. 

It will be observed that, under this regulation, "dealers" are not allowed the discount of 72%, and the discount may be suspended against any distributor who becomes delinquent in tax payment, or violates the law or any rule or regulation.

Contraband Goods: Seizure; Disposition of Prop erty- 

Law. Section 7. 

That all manufactured tobacco products which are or shall be owned or possessed by any person in avoidance, evasion or violation of any of the provisions of this Act, are hereby declared to be contraband goods and the same may be seized by the Commissioner, or any duly authorized representative, agent or employee of the Department, without a warrant and the said goods shall be delivered to the Department for sale at public auction to the highest bidder after due advertisement. The Department, before delivering any of said goods so seized, shall require the purchaser to affix proper amount of stamps to goods so seized. Proceeds of all such seizures shall be paid by the Commissioner into the State Treasury, and ten (10) per cent of such proceeds shall be set aside as expenses for the administration of this section.

Any vehicle, not a common carrier, which may be used for transporting for the purpose of distribution, gift or sale of unstamped tobacco products shall likewise be subject to confiscation and sale in the same manner as above provided. Provided further, should any unstamped tobacco be found in any vehicle the same shall be prima facie evidence that it was there for gift, sale or distribution. 

In all cases of seizure of any tobacco products or other property, subject to forfeiture under the provisions of this Act, the officer or other person making the seizure shall proceed as follows: 

First, he shall prepare a list containing a description of the tobacco products or other property seized, shall appraise the value of same according to his best judgment as to usual and ordinary retail prices of the articles seized, and shall deliver to the person, if any, found in possession of same, a receipt showing the fact of seizure, from whom seized, the place of seizure, a description of goods and the appraised value. A copy of said receipt shall be posted at the place of seizure and a copy shall be filed in the office of the Department and shall be open to public inspection.

Ch. 9) 761 

TOBACCO TAX 

Second, the Commissioner or any representative of the Department shall within (5) days advertise the said tobacco products for sale for cash to the highest bidder, by written or printed poster, at as many as two public places in the county where the property is to be sold, one at the courthouse door in the county and one at any public place in the county, said notices to be posted at least five (5) days prior to date of sale, and shall contain a description of the property to be sold.

Third, any person claiming any property so seized as contraband may, at any time before the sale, file with the Commissioner at Nashville, a claim in writing requesting a hearing and stating his interest in the articles seized. The Commissioner shall set a date for hearing within ten days from the day the claim is filed. 

Any decision of the Commissioner adverse to any claimant may be reviewed in the manner now provided by law for the review of actions of boards or commissions as prescribed by Section 9008, et seq. of the Code of Tennessee. 

In the event the ruling of the Commissioner is favorable to the claimant, the Commissioner shall deliver to the claimant the tobacco products or other property so seized. If the ruling of the Commissioner is adverse to the claimant, the Commissioner shall proceed to sell such contraband goods in accordance with the foregoing provisions of this Act unless the claimant shall secure a supersedes under Section 9017 of the Code or unless the claimant give a bond under the provisions of the following paragraph. 

When the ruling of the Commissioner is adverse to the claimant, the Commissioner shall deliver to the claimant the tobacco products or property so seized, provided the tobacco products have proper tobacco stamps affixed to each article before delivery and, provided further, that such claimant shall give a bond payable to the State of Tennessee in a sum double the value of the property seized, with sureties approved by the Commissioner. The condition of the bond shall be that the obligors will pay to the State, through the Department, the full value of the goods or property seized unless upon certiorari the decision of the Commissioner shall be reversed and the right of the claimant to such property judicially determined. 

If no claim is interposed, such tobacco products or other property shall be forfeited without further proceedings and the same shall be sold as herein provided. The above procedure is the sole remedy of any claimant and no court shall have jurisdiction to interfere therewith by replevin injunction or in any other manner. 

Tobacco products owned or possessed by any person in avoidance or evasion or in violation of this Act are contraband goods and are subject to seizure; such goods may be seized by the Commissioner or his representatives without a warrant. 

Under the rules and regulations, tax stamps must be affixed to all tobacco products within twenty-four hours after the same shall have come to rest, unless such tobacco products are for "export" and have been segregated and are being handled in accordance with:

(Ch. 9 

 Regulation. 

Distributors will be permitted to keep unstamped tobacco products for Exclusive Export Purposes in such quantity to cover the distributor's ordinary Export requirements. The term "quantity" means a specified number of cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco products or snuff, and the quantity allowed each distributor for export purposes can in no instance exceed the quantity of such product specifically specified and shown in the distributor's license issued by this Department. Such quantity of tobacco products for export purposes must be kept in separate part of building from other tobacco products, and if not so separated the same shall be stamped. 

Tobacco products intended for domestic sale or consumption are subject to seizure in all cases where such products are not properly stamped within twenty-four hours after receipt of same. As a precaution, distributors should use care to have the correct date shown upon all invoices and the hour of delivery and date upon the delivery receipts.

Tobacco products "for export purposes must be kept in a separate part of building from other tobacco products, and if not so separated, the same shall be stamped," therefore, if such products are commingled with products intended for domestic sale or consumption, and are not properly stamped within twenty-four hours after receipt, such products are subject to seizure. 

Automobiles, trucks and other vehicles (not operated as a common carrier) are subject to confiscation when used to transport or distribute unstamped tobacco products. 

Unstamped tobacco products found in such vehicles is prima facie evidence of the intent to evade the statute. Tobacco manufacturing companies operating vehicles in Tennessee and advertising or selling its products should use care to see that all products are properly stamped. 

Confiscated tobacco products and other property is to be sold at public auction to the highest bidder and all tobacco purchases are to be stamped by the purchaser before delivery is made by the Commissioner. Attention is direct to: 

Regulation. 

Confiscated tobacco products and other goods must be sent to the Department of Finance and Taxation, Nashville, Tennessee, for sale in accordance with Section 7, Chapter 133, Acts of 1937. The right to reject any or all bids to purchase confiscated tobacco products or other property is hereby reserved.

Ch. 9) 763 

TOBACCO TAX 

Upon seizure of tobacco products or other property, the officer or person making such seizure shall: 

1. Make a list containing: 

(a) Description of property seized. (b) The appraised value of such property. 

2. Issue and deliver receipt to person from whom property was seized. 

3. Post copy of receipt at the place of seizure. 

4. File copy of receipt with the Department. 

The Commissioner or representative of the Department shall: 

1. Within five days advertise the contraband property for sale at public auction to the highest bidder. 

2. The advertisement must contain description of the property to be sold, and 3. Notices of such sale must be posted in two public places in the county where the property is to be sold. 

Any person claiming property seized as contraband may, at any time prior to sale thereof, file claim in writing with the Commissioner and request a hearing. The claim must state the interest of the claimant in the articles seized and the Commissioner must set a date for hearing within ten days.

Upon favorable decision the Commissioner shall deliver the seized property to such claimant. 

Attention is directed to the fact that in the event of adverse decision of the Commissioner appeal may be taken under section 9008 et seq. of the Code. However, the Commissioner shall proceed to sell the property unless supersedes is obtained under Section 9017 of the Code or unless bond is given. The writ of supersedes or the making of bond are conditions precedent to appeal. 

The Commissioner is authorized, in case of decision adverse to the claimant, to accept bond, with sureties approved by him, for an amount double the value of the property. Upon posting of acceptable bond the Commissioner will deliver the property to claimant; however, tobacco products must be properly stamped by the claimant before delivery.

The courts of the State do not have jurisdiction to grant writs of replevin or injunction in such cases, and if

(Ch. 9 

no claim is filed with the Commissioner, the property is sold and any subsequent claim barred. 

Drop Shipments- Law. Section 8. 

That the Drop Shipment plan or system means any device whereunder a manufacturer or sales agency or drop shipment depot ships tobacco products to points in the State to be billed or collected for by some person other than the manufacturer, or sales agency, or drop shipment depot, or person shipping said products. 

Every person engaged in the activity within this State of billing, collecting for, distributing or selling tobacco products through the device, plan, scheme or artifice, commonly known as the drop shipment plan or system, shall make a complete and itemized report, giving name and address of purchaser within twenty-four (24) hours of the receipt of taking of the order, and shall pay the tax and affix the stamps on the tobacco products before delivery. 

Under this section of the law the practice commonly referred to as "drop shipping" is restricted in Tennessee. 

A broker receiving an order from a customer and directing a distributor in Tennessee to "drop ship" the tobacco products to the customer must have the necessary tax stamps applied to the tobacco products before delivery and must report the taking of such order, giving the name and address of the purchaser, to the Commissioner within twenty-four hours. It is the practice of the Department to investigate "drop shipments" of tobacco products and "drop shipment" reports. Regulation. 66 'Distributors engaged directly or indirectly in making Drop Shipments of tobacco products must affix and cancel tobacco stamps before delivery. When tobacco products are shipped to or in care of a licensed distributor the drop shipment report will not be required within twentyfour hours."'

Supervision and Collection- 

Law. Section 9. 

That the supervision and collection of the tax imposed herein shall be under the direction of the Department. 

The Commissioner is hereby granted full power and authority to adopt such reasonable rules and regulations not in conflict with this Act, or other statute, as he may deem necessary to enforce the collection of the tax herein levied. Such rules and regulations, before being effective, shall be approved by the Attorney-General. 

The Commissioner is further authorized and empowered to prescribe the methods to be used by dealers and distributors in recording purchases and sales of tobacco products and purchases and consumption

Ch. 9) 765 

TOBACCO TAX 

of tobacco tax stamps. The Commissioner is further authorized and empowered to require persons selling, distributing, or dealing in tobacco products to file such reports with the Department in the manner and at such times as he may deem necessary in carrying out the provisions of this law.

Every distributor or dealer shall permit the Commissioner, or his authorized agent or representative, to inspect at any time all tobacco products, invoices, books, papers and memoranda including the general books, both operating and proprietary ledgers, etc. as may be deemed necessary by the Commissioner in ascertaining whether or not the tax levied under the provisions of this Act has been paid, or in determining amount of such tax due. No license distributor or dealer shall be permitted to claim any part of the premises whereon he is engaged in business, to be exempt from inspection; as his dwelling or home, his application for license under this Act being declared an express waiver of such claim. All persons failing to permit the examination of tobacco products, invoices, books and other memoranda including the general books, both operating and proprietary ledgers, etc. or interfering with the orderly inspection or examination thereof, or failing to file such reports as may be required by the Commissioner, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

The supervision and collection of the tax is placed under the direction of the Department of Finance and Taxation. The Commissioner is authorized to adopt rules and regulations which must be: 

1. Reasonable, and not in conflict with this Act. 

2. Necessary to enforce the collection of the tax. 

3. Approved by the Attorney-General before becoming effective. 

Rules and Regulations must be in accordance with the requirements of this section and should have general application to all taxpayers. 

The Commissioner is further authorized to: (1) Prescribe accounting methods to be used in recording purchases and sales of products and tobacco tax stamps. (2) Require dealers and distributors to file reports, in such form and at such time as may be deemed necessary. 

In this connection, attention is directed to: 

Regulation. 

The monthly report must show the total tax value of cigarettes and cigars on hand at the beginning of May 1st. and the first of each month thereafter, the total tax value of cigarettes and cigars purchased or received during the month, total tax value of cigarettes and cigars sold or given away during the month and the total tax value of cigarettes and cigars on hand at the end of the month.

The monthly report must, also, show the total value of four (now 3) cent cigarette stamps and cigar stamps on hand May 1st. and the first of each month thereafter, the total value of such stamps purchased during the month, the total value of such stamps affixed to cigarettes and cigars during the month and the total value of such stamps on hand unaffixed at the end of the month.

(Ch. 9  

The report must show name and address of the person and quantity of cigarettes and cigars exported before credit will be allowed for such out-of-state shipments. Incomplete, delinquent, false or fraudulent monthly reports shall be justification for revocation of distributor's license. Provided, "four cent" (now 3 cent) stamps are affixed to cigarettes and only "cigar" stamps are affixed to cigars.

As regards "interstate" or "out-of-state" shipments, attention is called to:

Regulation. 

Sales of tobacco products over the counter are not interstate sales, regardless of where the purchaser might reside. All tobacco products so sold must have the proper tax stamps affixed thereto. Interstate shipments must be invoiced and copies of invoices must accompany shipment and be available to inspection of representatives of this Department at any time or place.

The Commissioner and his authorized agent or representative are authorized to inspect, at any time; (a) All tobacco products. (b) All invoices, books, papers and memoranda. 

Licensed distributors are not permitted to claim any part of the premises to be exempt from inspection, and any person failing to permit, or interfering with such inspection, or failing to permit examination of books and records, is guilty of a misdemeanor. Regulation. 

Every distributor, dealer or other person shall permit any authorized representative of the Department to inspect at any time all tobacco products, invoices, books, papers and memoranda including the general books, both operating and proprietary ledger. This provision includes tobacco products and invoices placed on delivery trucks or located elsewhere. 

Books and records are to be maintained in such a manner as will permit representatives to readily verify monthly reports and permission to destroy tobacco records must be secured from the Commissioner:

(Ch. 9

Regulation.

Dealers and distributors of tobacco products shall keep books, invoices, records and other memoranda pertaining to the handling of tobacco products until such time as the Department grants permission for such records to be destroyed. Distributors must maintain book records in such manner as will permit representatives of this Department to readily verify monthly reports with their books. 

The above regulation, as regards destroying records, applies to both "dealer" and "distributor." Care should be used to obtain permission of the Commissioner or the Department before destroying records pertaining to the handling or sale of tobacco products. Failure to secure such permission subjects such person to fine under the provisions of the Act. 

Common Carriers 

Law. Section 10. 

That every common carrier in this state, transporting cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco or snuff, in this State, shall keep a complete record of all tobacco products handled in each transaction, separately, and shall show the transportation of such tobacco products, both interstate and intrastate. Every common carrier in this state shall give and permit the Commissioner free access to such books and records, and furnish such information and reports as the Commissioner may require, and any person violating this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

The rules and regulations adopted by the Commissioner do not require "common carriers" to report the transportation of tobacco products, however, the above section of the law makes it mandatory upon all common carriers to "keep a complete record of all tobacco products handled in each transaction, separately, and shall show the transportation of such tobacco products, both interstate and intrastate." The Commissioner is to be given free access to such records. It should be noted that failure to maintain records pertaining to the transportation of tobacco products constitutes a misdemeanor. 

Violation of Act-Penalties- Law. Section 11. 

That it shall be unlawful for any distributor, dealer or other person to engage in the business of selling, distributing or handling tobacco products without the license as herein required, or after the license herein

Ch. 9) 769 

TOBACCO TAX 

required has been revoked; or for any distributor, dealer and their agents, representatives and employees or other person to sell, or offer for sale, or display for sale, or to possess for the purpose of sale or gift any package or parcel of tobacco products to which the tax stamp or stamps are not affixed, which, under the provisions of this Act, are required to be affixed; or for any distributor, dealer or other person to possess for the purpose of use or consumption any package or parcel of tobacco products to which, or on which, the stamp or stamps are not affixed, which, under the provisions of this Act are required to be affixed; or for any person to violate any rule or regulation promulgated or prescribed by the Commissioner under the authority herein vested in him; and any such distributor, dealer and their agents, representatives and employees or any other person shall be fined in a sum not less than 

Twenty-Five ($25.00) Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00) Dollars; and for each subsequent violation shall be punished by a fine of not less than One Hundred ($100.00) Dollars nor more than One Thousand ($1,000.00) Dollars and be imprisoned for a period of not less than ten (10) days nor more than eleven (11) months and twenty-nine (29) days.

Under this Section of the Law it is unlawful to: (1) Engage in the business of selling, distributing or handling tobacco products without first securing the license or licenses required under Section 2 of the Act, or to engage in such business after revocation of license. (2) Sell, offer or display, or possess for the purpose of gift or sale, tobacco products without the proper tax stamps being affixed thereto. This section applies to all "dealers, "distributors" and their "agents, representatives and employees." (3) Violate rules and regulations promulgated by the Commissioner and approved by the Attorney General. 

Attention is drawn to the fact that, not only the dealer or distributor is punishable for violation of this Act, but their employees, agents and representatives are also punishable.

Persons violating the provisions of this Act or the rules and regulations promulgated and approved in accordance with the Act are guilty of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction are punishable as follows: 

1. First offense-Fine $25 to $50 Dollars. 

2. Second and subsequent offenses-Fine $100.00 to $1,000.00 and in addition to the fine-imprisonment for not less than ten days nor more than eleven months and twenty-nine days.

The court is not allowed any discretion; therefore, upon conviction, the punishment becomes mandatory.

(Ch. 9

 Counterfeiting Tobacco Tax Stamps- 

Law. Section 12. 

That any person who shall falsely and fraudulently make, forge, alter or counterfeit a stamp or stamps so prescribed by the Commissioner, or who shall cause or procure to be falsely or fraudulently made, forged, altered, or counterfeited, such stamps or who shall knowingly and wilfully utter, publish, pass or tender as true, any false, altered, forged, or counterfeited stamps prescribed by this Act, or who shall re-use any stamp previously affixed, shall be guilty of a felony and be punished by imprisonment in the State penitentiary for not less than one (1) year nor more than ten (10) years. 

Counterfeiting tobacco tax stamps or the re-use of stamps, previously affixed to tobacco products, as evidence of tax payment, is a felony punishable by imprisonment in the State penitentiary from one to ten years. 

Distribution of Taxes Collected- 

Law. Section 13. 

That all of the taxes collected under this law shall be applied in the following manner: 

1. Four (4%) per cent of the amount so collected shall be allowed as the expense for carrying out the provisions of this Act. 

2. The amount of Eight Hundred Thousand ($800,000.00) Dollars thereof annually as an equalized fund to provide an eight (8) months school term in the rural elementary schools of the State as provided in 

Section 2405, et seq., Code of Tennessee. 

3. The amount of Two Hundred Thousand ($200,000.00) Dollars annually to the high schools of the State to supplement high school fund and to be distributed as said fund is distributed. 

4. The amount of Eighty-Two Thousand Five Hundred ($82,500.00)

Dollars shall be used annually to provide the special sinking fund to pay the principal and interest on the """ "Tennessee Rural Public

School Building and Repair Bonds." 

5. The amount of Two Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand ($225,000.00)

Dollars shall be used annually to provide the special sinking fund for the payment of the principal and interest of the "University of 

Tennessee Building Bonds."' 

6. The remainder shall be applied to and become a part of the General 

State School Fund created by Section 2405, et seq. of Code of Tennessee.

This section has no practical application to taxpayers and comment is considered unnecessary.

April Term 1926 From Gibson County 

Page 780 784 1. The plaintiff in error, hereinafter referred to as defendant, was convicted below of violating what is known as the Tobacco Sales Tax Law, being Chapter 2, of Public Acts passed by the Legislature of 1925. 

The defendant is a blind merchant, engaged in business at Trenton, Gibson County. 

2. There are but three questions in the lawsuit: 

(a) Is Chapter 2, Public Acts of 1925 constitutional? 

(b) If constitutional, then is Chapter 87, Public Acts of 1901 constitutional, and if constitutional, does it exempt the blind merchant from the payment of the tax imposed by said 

Chapter 2, Acts of 1925? 

(c) Was it error to refuse to permit proof to go to the jury that the defendant had been exempted from the payment of special privilege taxes? 

3. We have therefore reached the conclusion that this Act is not unconstitutional on the grounds set out by the defendant. 

4. We are of the opinion that this contention is not good, because no action of the county court under said statute of 1901 could release the defendant of the obligation to stamp his tobacco which he offered for sale and sold.

Opinion by Justice Kinney, Special Justice. 

The plaintiff in error, hereinafter referred to as defendant, was convicted below of violating what is known as 772

Ch. 9) 773 

TOBACCO TAX 

the Tobacco Sales Tax Law, being chapter 2, of the Public Acts passed by the legislature of 1925. 

The defendant is a blind merchant, engaged in business at Trenton, Gibson County. 

His able attorney assigns six errors to the action of the trial judge, but says in his brief that it will readily appear, when the case is considered by this court, that there are but three questions in the lawsuit, and that these three ques tions are as follows: 

"First. Is the act of the General Assembly of the State of Tennessee for the year 1925, the same being chapter 2 of the Public Acts, valid and binding, and therefore constitutional, or is the same unconstitutional? "" 'Second. If the Act above referred to is constitutional, then is the act of 1901, the same being chapter 87 of the Public Acts of the General Assembly for the State of Tennessee for the year 1901, constitutional or unconstitutional! And, if constitutional, does it not exempt the blind merchants in Tennessee from the payment of the taxes referred to in chapter 2 of said Acts of 1925% "Third. Was it not error on the part of the court below to refuse to permit proof to go to the jury that the defendant had been exempted from the payment of special privilege taxes, as contemplated in both of the acts above referred to?" 

We also are of the opinion that these are the controlling questions in the case. 

The defendant then insists that said act is unconstitutional for two reasons: "First. Because the body of the act is broader than its caption. "Second. Because the bill embraces more than one subject, one of which subjects is not expressed in the title.'' 

The most serious attack made as to the constitutionality of the act is directed at section 7, but there are also objections to sections 4, 5, and 6. 

It is said that section 4 creates a separate criminal offense from any now on the statutes, and provides penalties for the violation thereof, and that section 5 also creates a separate criminal offense, and that section 6 enlarges the jurisdiction of the grand juries, and enlarges the duties of the circuit and criminal judges, sheriffs and peace officers. 

Most all tax statutes provide means for their enforcement, and penalties and punishments for their violation, and would be of little consequence without such provisions. 

These are germane to the principal purpose of the statute

(Ch. 9  

as expressed in the caption, and no reference in the caption to such provisions need be made; but in fact it was made in the caption of this act as follows: 

"And to provide methods and penalties for its enforcement." 

We are of the opinion, therefore, that the attacks made on sections 4, 5, and 6 are not good. 

As to section 7, the defendant contends as follows: "Of yet more serious objection, however, is section 7 of said act, which provides that the administration of the provisions of said act shall be conducted by the excise tax division of the department of finance and taxation, and then goes further and says: 'Provided, that, in addition to one-third of the revenue derived from this tax that under the present law will accrue to the general school fund that the further sum of $250,000.00 from the revenue from this tax shall be used as a special fund to create an eight-months school term in the rural schools of the State to be expended under any State law which may be enacted for securing such school term in the rural schools in the absence of such future legislation under the direction of the commissioner of education and the governor.' "" "That section of said act above quoted creates a special sinking fund, or a special fund out of the revenues provided for said act, and the caption of the act in no place mentions that such fund is to be created therein, or refers to the same, and it is our insistence that the creation of this special fund, or sinking fund, in the body of the act, makes the act broader than its caption, and that the caption only refers to one subject, namely, imposing a special privilege tax upon sales, etc., while the body of said act embraces two subjects in that it creates this special sales tax, and in addition to creating the separate criminal offense herein mentioned, and enlargement of the duties of the circuit judges, grand juries, sheriffs, and peace officers, it goes still further, and creates a special fund out of the moneys coming to the treasury of the State." The proviso of the act, above quoted, contemplated that the legislature would enact other and additional legislation to effect the purpose therein expressed; that is, that $250,- 

000.00 of the revenue realized from the tobacco tax should go in aid of rural school education, but provided that, "in the absence of such future legislation," said $250,000.00 should be used "under the direction of the commissioner of education and the Governor." 

This was simply a direction in the act as to what disposition should be made of this tax, or, at least, of so much as $250,000.00 of same, when collected. The defendant insists that this was another subject, and made the act obnoxious to that provision of the Constitution which inhibits embracing more than one subject in a bill.

Ch. 9) 775 

TOBACCO TAX 

It was never intended that the title should express fully everything contained in an act. 

In the case of State v. Lasater, Baxter, 586, this court, in passing upon this provision of the constitution, said: "Legislation upon different subjects, and upon subjects not indicated in the title of the act, are forbidden; but it was not intended that every provision or feature of the law should constitute a different subject, so as to make it necessary to pass separate acts in regard to each, nor was it intended that the title should express fully everything contained in the act. "Here the subject is the rights, duties, and liabilities of innkeepers, common carriers, and proprietors of places of public amusement, etc. 

Now a provision that no turbulent or riotous conduct shall be allowed in such places, and providing for the punishment of the offenders, we think, is not legislation on a different subject. Looking to the evil to be remedied, and bearing in mind that there must be a clear violation of the Constitution before we can declare an act void, we hold that this act is not void on this ground." 

In Garvin v. State, 13 Lea, 162 it is said: "The object and purpose of the constitution, in providing that an act shall embrace but one subject, which shall be expressed in the title, is to give notice to the legislator of the subject of legislation, and it is sufficient so long as the subject-matter of the act is germane to that expressed in the title, whether the body enlarges or restricts the title. 

If a statute admits two constructions, one of which would render it constitutional, and the other unconstitutional, the former should be adopted; and a doubt in relation to its constitutionality should be resolved in favor of the act." 

In Truss v. State, 13 Lea, 312, the court said: "Whatever is of sufficient import to direct the mind to the subject of proposed legislation meets the object of the constitution. Cannon v. 

Mathes, 8 Heisk. 519; State v. Lasater, 9 Baxt., 584; Gowan v. State, MS. "The use in the caption, to 'prevent sales of cotton,' necessarily calls the attention to sales of every character and the steps ordinarily taken to effect them. The term 'receive on deposit' is used in the act in connection with sale, barter, and exchange, and as a step to their accomplishment."

In State v. McMinnville, 106 Tenn. (22 Pickle), 384, 61 

S. W. 785, the court held as follows: 

"1. Constitutional Law-Title and Subject of Statutes.-A statute with one general subject may embrace subdivisions, provisos, and exceptions pertinent to that subject to any extent that they can be grouped without incongruity."

The late decisions of this court on this provision of the constitution quote approvingly from the leading case of Cannon v. Mathes, 8 Heisk., 504. In House v. Creveling, 147 Tenn. 589, 598, 250 S. W. 357, this court said:

(Ch. 9  

"It has been held in Tennessee since Cannon v. Mathes, 55 Tenn. (8 Heisk.), 504, that the generality of a title is not objectionable, if not made a cover for legislation incongruous in itself, and that the legislature must determine for itself how broad and comprehensive the object of the statute shall be. Our cases are very numerous. The last review of them is contained in State v. Cumberland Club, 136 Tenn., 84, 188 S. W. 583. We would hesitate to say what is the limit, if any, to the scope of an act of the legislature suitably entitled. We have many acts covering very wide fields.' House v. Creveling, 147 Tenn. 

598, 250 S. W. 359.

The title of the act, the constitutionality as to which was construed by the court in Cannon v. Mathes, was as follows: "An act to fix the State tax on property." Laws 1870, chapter 74. The body of this act, however, contained provisions increasing the property tax, and also increasing the privilege taxes of the State. The body of said act also repealed a former act, and further amended a former act "as to the manner and order in which the comptroller and treasurer were directed to pay out the money in the treasury." It was contended in that case that this was a violation of that provision of the constitution involved in this case. In that case, the court, in construing that act, said: "The general subject of the act is revenue, and each and every section has direct reference to the subject of revenue in its different phases. It cannot be said that there is the least incongruity among the provisions of the four sections. They have a natural, if not a necessary, connection with and dependence upon each other. Revenue is the general subject of the act; its amount and its disbursement from the treasury are the special objects provided for. It is clear that the act is not obnoxious to the objection that it embraces more subjects than one. (State v. Bowers), 14 Ind., 195; (Harriman v. State), 2 

Iowa, 280; Brewster et al v. City of Syracuse), 19 N. Y. 119; Cooley's 

Const. Lim. 145."' Cannon v. Mathes, 8 Heisk. 519, 520.

Considering the statute involved in this case in the light of the above holding, it is apparent that the general subject of the statute, expressed in the caption, is the raising of revenue by a tax on tobacco. Provisions for the application of the revenue so raised, or expressions of the legislative purpose in raising such revenue and the disposition thereof, are clearly germane to and directly connected with the general subject of the statute. 

Cannon v. Mathes also contains a statement which has been quoted and applied by this court in numerous cases, as follows:

Ch. 9) 777 

TOBACCO TAX 

"It is obvious, therefore, that the true rule of construction, as fully established by the authorities, is that any provision of the act, directly or indirectly relating to the subject expressed in the title, and having a natural connection thereto, and not foreign thereto, should be held to be embraced in it.'' Cannon v. Mathes, 8 Heisk., 523. 

In State v. Cumberland Club, 136 Tenn., 97, 188 S. W., 586, after quoting the language just set out above, this court said: "It may be said generally that things naturally and usually connected in thought are germane to each other, as for example, where they appear as incidents to the main subject, or the means of its execution. The same is true of exceptions and provisos.' 

We are of the opinion that the raising of revenue by taxes on tobacco and the disposition of that revenue when so raised are things naturally and usually connected in thought and germane to the main thought in the caption. 

The imposition of a tax on tobacco was certainly made for some purpose, to support some department of the State government, and this thought would naturally and usually occur in connection with an act to raise revenue. 

We have therefore reached the conclusion that this act is not unconstitutional on the grounds set out by the defendant.

We have examined the cases cited in his brief on these points, namely: Acklen v. Thompson, 122 Tenn. 49, 50, 126 S. W., 730, 135 Am. St. Rep. 851; Ledgerwood v. Pitts, 122 Tenn. 608, 609, 125 S. W. 1036; Gossett v. State, 2 Shan. 

Cas. 546; Malone v. Williams, 118 Tenn., 466, 103 S. W. 798, 121 Am. St. Rep. 1002-but we find nothing in any of these cases in conflict with this holding. 

It is next contended that the defendant is exempt under the act of 1901, chapter 87 of the Public Acts of the General Assembly of this State, and the release from payment of privilege and license taxes by the county court of Gibson County.

We are of the opinion that this contention is not good, because no action of the county court under said statute of 1901 could release the defendant of the obligation to stamp his tobacco which he offered for sale and sold. 

Chapter 87 of the Acts of 1901 is a statute for the relief of blind persons from the payment of certain privileges and license taxes, and provides as follows:

(Ch. 9  "Section 1. Be it Enacted by the General Assembly of the State of Tennessee, that all persons living within the State of Tennessee who are totally blind and who are exempted from paying county privilege and license taxes by the county courts of the counties in which such persons reside and do business, be and the same are hereby relieved from all license and privilege taxes due the State of Tennessee for such business as said persons shall be engaged in, except liquor dealers' tax, for and during the time for which said persons shall have been relieved of such taxes by the county courts of said counties." 

The resolution of the county court which the defendant offered in evidence is as follows: 

'Special Releasements.-District 7. Mr. Forrester. From paying license in business. ""

The language of the above release by the said county court is "from paying license." 

The act of 1925 as to the stamp tax on tobacco does not require any license at all. The dealer is not required to procure a license at all, but is required under this act simply to buy stamps from the commissioner of finance and taxation of the State of Tennessee, and affix to each package of cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco, and snuff a stamp of the required value, and which shall evidence the payment of the tax imposed by this act. 

No license at all being required by the act of 1925, the above release by said county court "from paying license" could in no wise release the defendant from procuring and affixing the stamps required by the act to the manufactured tobacco sold or offered for sale. 

The tobacco stamp tax imposed by chapter 2, Acts of 1925, is a species or kind of privilege tax, entirely distinct from any which was contemplated by chapter 87, Acts of 1901. It is not a tax paid on the privilege of doing a general business, for which a license must be obtained, but it is a tax on each separate sale of manufactured tobacco. 

The county is not authorized to levy a tax similar to the State stamp tax on sales of tobacco, and hence the said statute of 1901 could not apply to it, as under that statute it was expressly made a condition precedent to the release of the State tax as to blind merchants that the county should first grant such release from the payment of similar county taxes, and, as the county is not authorized to make such levy, it cannot, of course, make such release.

Ch. 9) 779 

TOBACCO TAX 

To ascertain the intention of the legislature is said to be the cardinal rule in the construction of statutes. Did the legislature, then, by the act of 1901 intend to release blind merchants from the payment of such a tax as this on manufactured tobacco?

The act of 1925 defines the word "person" as used therein, to mean and include every individual, with no exceptions whatever. It defines the term "dealer," as used therein, to mean and include every person, other than a distributor, who engages in the business in this State of distributing, etc., with no other exception. This broad, allinclusive definition in the statute necessarily included all persons selling tobacco whether blind or otherwise. 

It follows, from the conclusions we have reached as to the first and second contentions of the defendant, that his third contention, that the trial judge was in error in refusing to permit evidence to go to the jury to the effect that the defendant had been exempted from the payment of this tobacco stamp tax, is also untenable.

The uncontradicted evidence in this case shows the sale by the defendant of unstamped cigarettes, and the possession in stock for the purpose of sale of a quantity of manufactured tobacco, which was not stamped as required by the Tobacco Stamp Tax Law of 1925, and we are therefore constrained to affirm the judgment of the Court below.

Opinion by Justice Timberlake, Special Justice. 

There

From the judgment of the Circuit Court for Gibson County sustaining a motion to quash the presentment in this case, the State of Tennessee has appealed in error to this Court and assigned errors. There is no error in the judgment of the lower Court and it is affirmed. 

The quashed presentment charged, that James Bryant and R. L. Bryant, retailers of manufactured tobacco, cigars and cigarettes doing business within the jurisdiction of the court on the day of October, A. D. 1927, in the County of Gibson in the State of Tennessee then and there unlawfully "did fail to affix stamps as required by law upon sundry quantities of manufactured tobacco, cigars and cigarettes, the same having come to rest in this State and within the jurisdiction of this Court the said James Bryant and 780

Ch. 9) 781 

TOBACCO TAX 

R. L. Bryant having said tobacco, cigars and cigarettes in their possession and place of business and for the purpose of sale and having as aforesaid unlawfully failed to affix the stamps as required by law thereto and thereon said packages against the peace and dignity of the State." 

The grounds of the motion to quash (three in number) need not be here stated at length. It is sufficient to say that the legal effect of said motion was to challenge the presentment because it failed to charge any criminal offense. 

The State relies on Chapter 2, Public Acts of 1927, as amended by Chapters 41 and 77 of the same Session of the General Assembly of the State of Tennessee, as furnishing the base upon which said presentment rests. The cap tion of said Chapter 2 is as follows, towit: 

"An Act to impose a special privilege tax upon sales and/or distribution by gift or sale, in this State of cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco and snuff sold and/or distributed by any person, firm, association, joint stock company, syndicate or corporation in this State, and to provide methods and penalties for its enforcement, and to appropriate the revenues derived from this tax to educational purposes. 

It will be observed that the prime purpose of said Act as expressed in its caption is "to impose a special privilege tax upon sales and/or distribution by gift or sale," within the State of Tennessee, of the articles mentioned; and that the "methods and penalties for its enforcement" are but incidents to such prime purpose. 

While sections 2 and 3 of said Act deal with the amount of said special privilege tax and the method of its payment, there is by said sections no penalty imposed and no offense of a criminal nature therein created for a failure to comply with the method of tax payment as therein provided, which is as follows, viz: "Such tax to be paid and the stamps hereinafter provided for affixed by the person having possession and ownership of such cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco and/or snuff, after the same shall have come to rest in this State, and intended to be sold or given away in this State.' ""

It is by sections 4, 5 and 6 of said Act that criminal offenses are created and penalties fixed. If the presentment in this case can be sustained, it must be by virtue of the legislative enactment set forth in section 4 of said Chapter 2, as amended by Chapter 41 of the Public Acts of 1927.

(Ch. 9  

Without copying the whole of said section 4, as amended, we deem it only necessary to quote so much thereof as creates the criminal offense therein and thereby defined, as is shown by the following language, towit: "Sec. 4.  that it shall be a misdemeanor for any person, distributor or dealer, as hereinabove defined, to sell or offer for sale, or display for sale, in this State, any package or parcel of cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco and snuff without having affixed thereto or thereon the stamps or stamps required to be affixed thereto or thereon under the provisions of this Act; 

There is no averment in the presentment in this case that the defendants therein named did unlawfully "sell or offer for sale, or display for sale, in this State, any package or parcel of cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco and snuff without having affixed thereto or thereon the stamp or stamps required to be affixed thereto or thereon" as provided by said Act; but the charge made in the presentment is, that the defendants therein named unlawfully "did fail to affix stamps as required by law," etc. In other words, the gravamen of the offense charged in the presentment was a failure to affix stamps as required by law; while the misdemeanor created by the section 4 of said Act, as amended, was, the selling or offering for sale, or displaying for sale, in this State, the articles therein mentioned, without having affixed thereto or thereon stamp or stamps as provided by said Act.

In the case of Jordan v. State, Vol. 3 (2nd), S. W., 159, recently decided by this Court, opinion by Mr. Justice 

McKinney, it was said viz: "The description of a statutory offense in the words of the statute is sufficient, and renders the indictment sufficiently certain, if it gives to the defendant notice of the nature of the charge against him." 

But in the instant case the description of the offense charged is not in the words of the statute creating the misdemeanor, and the language of the presentment gives to the defendants, therein named, no notice of their being called upon to meet any charge, which the statute has declared to be a criminal offense. State v. Willis, 130 Tenn., 412; Wilson v. State, 103 Tenn. 87.

The suggestion made by counsel for the State, that a failure to affix stamps, as required by the second section of

Ch. 9) 783 

TOBACCO TAX 

said Act, should be by construction held to be a misdemeanor, else the purpose of the Act might be easily defeated, in the mode and manner pointed out by counsel in argument, is one which might influence the legislature, but should have no weight with a court. Affirmed.

THE STATE 161 TENNESSEE 341

From Washington County. 

1. Plaintiff in error was convicted of violating Chapter 2, Acts of 

1927, known as the Tobacco Tax Law, and fined $10.00.-It was charged that in the indictment-that on June 10th the defendant "unlawfully did sell, offer to sell and display for sale packages of cigars, cigarettes and manufactured tobacco without having affixed the stamps." 

2. The defendant testified in part that this tobacco and cigarettes were stored in the cabinet for purpose of sale when needed in the regular course of his business, but that it was not offered for sale, and that his supply of stamps was exhausted, for which reason the packages were not stamped. He says it was his purpose to affix the stamps before selling the articles. 

3. The Act imposes no penalty for intending to sell cigarettes and tobacco without stamping them, nor was it a violation of the Act, prior to the amendment of the Extra Session of 1929, to be in possession of unstamped cigars, cigarettes, tobacco and snuff. The penalty imposed by the original act was for failure to stamp such articles when sold, offered for sale, or displayed for sale. 

For the error indicated, the judgment is reversed and the cause remanded.

Opinion by Justice Cook. 

Plaintiff in error was convicted of violating chapter 2, Acts of 1927, known as the Tobacco Tax Law, and fined $10.00. He appealed and insists that the judgment should be reversed for error in the charge and because the evidence does not sustain the indictment. 

It was charged in the indictment, which was found at the September term, 1929, that on June 10th the defendant "unlawfully did sell, offer to sell and display for sale packages of cigars, cigarettes and manufactured tobacco without having affixed the stamps." The indictment charged the terms of section 4 of the Act of 1927, which reads: "It shall be a misdemeanor for any person, distributor, or dealer to sell or offer for sale, or display for sale, any package or parcel of cigars, cigarettes, manufactured tobacco and snuff without having affixed the stamps.' 784

Ch. 9) 785 

TOBACCO TAX 

Sections 2 and 3 of the Act levy the tax and determine the method of collecting it by the use of stamps supplied by the State and affixed to the article in the manner therein provided. These sections do not impose a penalty. Section 

4 does that, declaring it a misdemeanor to sell, offer for sale or display for sale the unstamped articles. The Act was so construed in State v. Bryant, 157 Tenn. 350. 

Chapter 50, Acts of 1929, did not amend section 4 beyond increasing the fine from ten to fifty dollars. It purports to amend section 2 without materially broadening its scope. 

By this amendment no penalty was imposed for the omission to stamp cigarettes and tobacco after it came to rest in the State. But that was done by chapter 17, Acts Extra Session 

1929, passed December, 13. As thus amended section 4 reads. ... "It shall be a misdemeanor for any person, distributor or dealer to sell or offer for sale or display for sale in this State, or to possess for the purpose of sale or gift in this State, after the same has come to rest, cigars, cigarettes or manufactured tobacco to which or on which the stamps are not affixed.''

The tobacco tax inspector testified that on previous occasions the defendant refused to permit examination of drawers and cabinets in his place of business, claiming that they contained post office supplies, a post office substation being located there. After removal of the substation, the inspector procured a search warrant and demanded the keys to the cabinets and drawers. He says defendant delayed the investigation, pretending that the key was at his home, saying he would go after it, but in fact loitering in concealment for about two hours when he produced the keys which opened the cabinet. There was found locked in the cabinet forty-five packages of cigarettes and eleven packages of smoking tobacco. None of the packages bore stamps. They were not displayed or exposed to view, but easily accessible for purpose of sale by the clerk at the soda fountain. 

The defendant testified in part that this tobacco and cigarettes were stored in the cabinet for purpose of sale when needed in the regular course of his business. But that it was not offered for sale, and that his supply of stamps was exhausted, for which reason the packages were not

(Ch. 9  

stamped. He says it was his purpose to affix the stamps before selling the articles. 

The defendant's testimony, together with the facts and circumstances disclosed by Charles M. Wagner, the inspector, and D. L. Smith, deputy sheriff, made an issue of fact, to be determined by the jury, as to whether or not defendant was in fact selling the undisplayed cigarettes and tobacco. 

The trial judge correctly charged that if defendant offered for sale, displayed for sale or sold any of the articles without affixing the stamps he would be guilty. But erroneously instructed the jury that if defendant did not have the stamps as required by law affixed thereon, and thus had the articles in his possession and ownership intending to sell them without affixing the stamps, he would be guilty. 

The Act imposes no penalty for intending to sell cigarettes and tobacco without stamping them, nor was it a violation of the Act, prior to the amendment of the Extra 

Session of 1929, to be in possession of unstamped cigars, cigarettes, tobacco and snuff. The penalty imposed by the original Act was for failure to stamp such articles when sold, offered for sale, or displayed for sale. The amendatory Act passed at the Extra Session of 1929 was not in force when the indictment charging the offense was found, hence defendant could not be penalized under it. 

For the error indicated, the judgment is reversed and the cause remanded.

Rate of tax; exported products exempt;

state tax only- 

That every person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association in this State storing, selling, distributing or manufacturing such beer or such other beverages as are described above, shall pay a special privilege tax, in addition to all other taxes, in an amount equal to one and 70/100 (1.70) Dollars per barrel of thirty-one (31) liquid gallons stored, sold, distributed by gift or sale, or manufactured in this State. The tax upon barrels containing more or less than thirty-one (31) gallons shall be at a proportionate rate.

Beer or other such beverage manufactured in Tennessee and thereafter exported for sale, distribution or gift shall not be included in the measure of the tax liability hereby provided for. The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is authorized to promulgate rules and regulations for the purpose of securing the exemption hereby given and for the purpose of preventing such exemption from being claimed in the case of beer sold, distributed or given away in Tennessee. The burden shall be on the manufacturer claiming exemption to establish to the satisfaction of the collecting officers that the beverage manufactured in Tennessee is exempt under this paragraph. 

The tax above levied shall be a State tax and no county, municipality or taxing district shall have power to levy any like tax. This tax shall not apply to beverages previously used as a measure of tax under the provisions of this Act.

No employee of the Commissioner of Finance and Tax ation shall, while so employed, be interested, directly or indirectly in the vending, storing, distributing and/or manufacturing of such beer, and/or any other beverage under the penalty of dismissal from office and of Five Hundred ($500.00) Dollars fine, to be recovered by indictment or presentment.

RULES AND REGULATIONS No. 11 Beer and Other Alcoholic Beverage Tax Issued by Department of Finance and Taxation Approved by Dancey Fort, Commissioner, and Roy Beeler, Attorney-General, Under date 

October 1, 1933 These regulations, for convenience designated Regulations Number 11, are issued pursuant to Section 8 of the Beer Tax Act, same being Chapter 69, Public Acts of 1933, which Section provides: 

"The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is hereby authorized and it shall be his duty to make rules and regulations necessary, in his opinion, to effectuate the purposes and carry out the provisions of this Act, which rules and regulations shall have the force and effect of law if not in conflict with express statutory provision."

Violations of any of the rules and regulations issued by 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation carry the same penalties as are provided for violation of any of the provisions of the Act itself. 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation will, from time to time, make and issue such additional rules, regulations or rulings with reference to the administration and enforcement of the Act as necessity or expediency may require. 

Regulations Number 11 supersede Preliminary Rules and Regulations issued on April 22, 1933.

Definitions- 

In adopting the Act the General Assembly could have included statutory definitions for words and phrases con- 804

Ch. 10) 805 

BEER TAX 

tained therein, but since that was not done, all words and phrases must be given the usual and ordinary meaning without any forced or subtle construction. 

Certificate of Registration is to all intents and purposes a Permit. Cancellation thereof constitutes the conduct or carrying on a business or occupation without a license. Section 9316, Code of Tennessee, 1932. 

The movement of beer or any other beverage of like alcoholic content over the highways, bridges and streets of the State for sale or storage or re-sale or re-storage constitutes distribution.

Nature of Act— 

The Act imposes two types of regulation. 

1. It is material that the Department of Finance and 

Taxation and all local authorities understand that this law has a dual aspect, or that its operation is distinctly divided into two phases. 

The Department of Finance and Taxation, as the State's tax collecting agency, is charged with the issuance of licenses and the collection of the tax. Beyond this it is only the duty of the Department to secure good and solvent bonds for the payment of said tax and to strictly enforce the collection of all taxes arising from this law and due the State and to revoke any license where the tax is not paid as provided. 

The second phase of the law contemplates that the cities and counties shall exercise the police power in the regulation of the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of such beer, and/or other beverages of like alcoholic content. 

Bearing in mind that the Department of Finance and Taxation is only interested in the collection of the tax and that the cities and counties are interested in the police regulation of the sale of the beer and/or other beverages of like alcoholic content, Department would have no right to refuse to register any citizen or citizens of the United States applying for registration certificates as manufacturers, wholesalers or retailers, after receiving a satisfactory bond from them to guarantee payment of the tax levied and the stipulated registration fee.

(Ch. 10  

Treating of the second phase of the law, viz., the police power of the cities and counties, it will first be observed that the cities and counties are separate and distinct with respect to the authority that each may exercise. The city authorities are empowered to promulgate regulations applying within the corporate limits, while the county authorities are empowered to promulgate regulations applying within the limits of the county. Any manufacturer, wholesaler or retailer shall comply with both the regulations of the city and the county when operating or doing business in both. 

The authority of the cities and the counties is the same in reference to the scope of the regulations which they may promulgate, with the exception that the law grants to the cities additional restrictions which permit the fixing of zones or territories within which beer may be sold, and also providing for the hours of opening and closing of places where sold and other regulations looking to the morals and safety of the community. It is not contemplated by the law that either the city or county authorities shall have the right to arbitrarily refuse a license to a bona fide applicant who complies with the provisions of the law and the regulations made by the cities and counties. The power of these governing bodies is limited to an exercise of reasonable discretion, looking particularly to the safety, morals and public health of the community. 

The character of regulation and supervision to be exercised by the cities and counties is set forth in somewhat general terms in the law, but it is anticipated that these governing bodies will prevent the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale by persons not citizens of the United States, or by persons who have been guilty of violating the prohibition laws of the State. Further, that they will prevent the sale of beer to any minor, and that they will also regulate the sale so as not to interfere with schools, churches or other public gatherings. 

2. The first section of the bill legalizes the transportation, storage, sale and manufacture of beer and/or other beverages containing not more than 3.2 per cent. alcohol by weight. This provision repeals by implication all State

Ch. 10) 807 

BEER TAX 

statutes or municipal ordinances prohibiting the sale of beer of this alcoholic content anywhere in the State of Tennessee. It is therefore not necessary for any municipality or county to pass any ordinance or repeal any ordinance, or take any other action on this question, since the general law has specifically authorized the sale of such commodity. (The alcoholic content is now 5% by weight) 3. The second section of the bill provides for a special privilege tax of $1.20 per barrel of thirty-one liquid gallons upon the storing, selling, distributing or manufacturing of such beer. This tax is paid exclusively and directly to the State and the cities and counties are directly prohibited from levying any like tax. The State in turn then makes a distribution to the cities and counties as provided by the terms of the Act. (The tax rate is now $1.70 per barrel) 

Retailer's Certificates- 

All persons selling, keeping, storing or offering for sale or gift at retail beer or any other beverage of like alcoholic content as described in the Act, either within or outside of the corporate limits of any city or town, must secure a State Certificate of Registration. This will include not only persons operating stores, hotels, restaurants and other businesses where the retail sale of merchandise, food and beverages is the principal and continuing business, but also road houses, tourist camps, country and city clubs, lodges, barbecue stands, picnic grounds, summer resorts, railroad cars, dining rooms of boats and vessels, ferry boats, aeroplanes, and manufacturers, importing distributors and wholesalers who make any sale or gift at retail. 

All State Retailers' Certificates of Registration au thorize the sale of beer or any other beverage of like alcoholic content as described in the Act, for consumption either on the premises of the retailer or for consumption at a place other than the premises of the retailer. EXCEPT it is not permissible under the Act for a person holding a State Certificate of Registration to sell at retail at a special location to sell such beverages by peddling them from house to house by means of a truck or otherwise, sales being

(Ch. 10  

consummated and deliveries made concurrently at the residences or places of business of consumers. Nor may any person be granted a State Certificate of Registration to so peddle beer or any other beverage of like alcoholic content to consumers.

This does not in any way prohibit the delivery by a retailer of such beverages to consumers. 

Separate Certificate Required for Each Premise- 

A separate State Certificate of Registration is required for and with respect to each location, premise, premises, railroad dining car, dining room of any boat or vessel, or aeroplane, upon which beverages described in the Act are sold, given away or offered for sale at retail. Any person (for example, a corporation operating chain stores) may operate any number of such premises or places of business, but such retailer is required to secure a separate Certificate of Registration for each such place of business. Where a brewer operates several breweries in the State, or an importing distributor operates several warehouses, at each of which such beverages are sold or given away at retail, such brewer or distributor must obtain separate State Retail Certificates of Registration for each premise upon which retail sales or gifts are made, irrespective of the fact sales other than at retail may be made from all the several warehouses or breweries.

Where a hotel has several dining rooms, at each of which such beverages are sold, given away or kept or offered for sale at retail, but which are operated under a common ownership and management and are situated within the same building, the entire hotel building is considered to constitute one location or premise for the purposes of the Act, and one State Retail Certificate of Registration will satisfy the requirements of the law. But separate Certificates of Registration will be required where the ownership or management of the several dining rooms is separate and distinct, or where such dining rooms are situated in different buildings even though such buildings may be owned and operated by the same person.

Ch. 10) 809 

BEER TAX Registration Certificates for Railroad Dining Cars- 

State Retail Certificates of Registration to sell and/or give away such beverages at retail on the dining, club or buffet cars of a train need not be issued for and with respect to any particular car, or any particular train. The operator of any railway or of any dining cars may, upon written request to Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, be granted permission to secure such a number of Retail Certificates of Registration as is equal to the maximum number of cars upon which such beverages are sold, offered for sale or given away in Tennessee at one time. Such Certificate must be conspicuously displayed on each and every car upon which sales or gifts of such beverages are made. 

When State Certificate May be Issued— 

A State Certificate of Registration authorizing the sale, transportation, storage, receiving, distribution and manufacture of beer or beverages of like alcoholic content may be issued only after application to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and no such beverage may be transported, stored, sold, distributed, received or manufactured in this State unless a State Certificate of Registration has been obtained from the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and prominently displayed on the premise or premises where such beverages are sold, stored, distributed, received or manufactured and/or on vehicle transporting such beverages over the highways, bridges and streets of this State. 

Term of Certificate of Registration- 

All State Certificates of Registration to transport, store, sell, distribute, possess, receive and/or manufacture beer or any other beverage of like alcoholic content as described in the Act, are issued to expire April 30th in each year.

In no case will the registration fee be prorated or State Certificate of Registration be issued to expire at any date other than April 30th.

(Ch. 10 

Penalty and costs will attach on all State Certificates of Registration as of May 1st in each year. 

Transfer of State Certificate of Registration- 

No refunds will be made, regardless of subsequent action of cities and counties and no transfers will be made from one person to another or from one location to another. 

Certificates Must be Conspicuously Displayed— 

Each State Certificate of Registration issued in accordance with the provisions of the Act must be displayed conspicuously on the premises on which it authorizes the sale, storage or distribution of beer or other beverages of like alcoholic content, in such a manner as to be readily visible by patrons of the place of business and employees of Department of Finance and Taxation.

Retailers Transporting or Delivering by Truck- 

Each motor truck or other delivery vehicle owned or employed by holder of a State Certificate of Registration to retail beer or other beverages of like alcoholic content for the purpose of transporting or delivering such beverages must display conspicuously and in such a manner as to be readily visible at a distance of 50 (fifty) feet the State Certificate number of such retailer, in a form substantially as follows: 

Tennessee Department Finance and Taxation

Certificate No.- 

This legend must be painted upon both sides of the vehicle.

Monthly Reports and Payment of Gallonage Tax- Each manufacturer of beer and/or other beverages of like alcoholic content must make a report between the First and the Tenth of each calendar month, covering manufacture during the preceding calendar month, such report to be sworn to and each item thereon completed by the person making the report. Each wholesaler and importing distributor must make a report between the First and the Tenth of each calendar month, covering receipts during the preceding calendar month. Motor carriers and contract haulers as defined by Chapter 119, Public Acts of 1933, must make a report between the First and the Tenth of each calendar month covering beer and other beverages of like alcoholic content transported during the preceding calendar month, such report to be sworn to and each and every item thereon completed by the person making the return. In addition to the above Trip Delivery Report, each and every person or transportation line herein above mentioned, shall make and furnish the Department of Finance and Taxation between the first and tenth of each calendar month a monthly report on Form BT 7 showing the amount of beer and/or other beverage of like alcoholic content delivered within the State during the preceding calendar month and to whom each delivery was made. 

Regulation dated Oct. 25, 1935In the event a barge operator, or truck operator or other transportation facility holds his tonnage not exceeding seventy-two hours in making truck distributions on orders from final destination points, no report will be required by Department of Finance and Taxation. 

In the event a barge operator or truck operator or other transportation facility holds his tonnage for a period exceeding seventy-two hours in making truck distribution on orders from final destination points, there is an indication that the revenues of the state are not being adequately safeguarded, and from and after November 1, 1935, all such beer or other beverages of like alcoholic content must be stored in a bonded warehouse, as described in laws of the United States governing the handling of intoxicants, until such time as the beer or other beverages of like alcoholic content is re-forwarded to its final destination. 

Failure to comply with this rule will incur the tax liability measured by storage according to the provisions of 

Section 1, Chap. 69, Public Acts of 1935.

Regulation dated Nov. 22, 1935

These rules and regulations relating to Alcoholic Beverages shall be in full force and effect after December 1, 1935.
