Manufacture and Sale Legalized- Law. Section 1. 

Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the state of Tennessee: 

That it shall hereafter be lawful in this State to transport, store, sell, distribute, possess, receive and/or manufacture beer of alcoholic content of not more than five per cent by weight, or any other beverage of like alcoholic content, subject to the privilege taxes and regulations hereinafter set out and provided, but no brewer or wholesaler of any such beverage or their agent or agents shall be permitted to make any loan or furnish any fixtures of any kind or have any interest, direct or indirect, in the business of any retailer of such beverages, or in the premises occupied by such retailer. 

This section legalizes the sale, manufacture, importation, possession, storing, distribution, and transportation of beer and other beverages having an alcoholic content of not more than five per cent, by weight, subject to certain regulations and certain privilege taxes. 

The original Act (Chapter 69, Acts of 1933) fixed the alcoholic content of beer and other beverages at 3.2 per cent, by weight; this was increased to five per cent under provisions of Chapter 170, Acts of 1935. 

This section prohibits "brewers" and "wholesalers' of beer and beverages of like alcoholic content to deal or handle any of the following transactions with a "retailer." (a) Make or negotiate any kind of loan. (b) Furnish or sell fixtures of any kind. (c) Have any direct or indirect interest in such business, or (d) Have any direct or indirect interest in the premises occupied.

Ch. 10) 819 

BEER TAX 

The above provisions are far reaching and brewers and wholesalers should use extreme care in all business relationship with retailers in order to avoid the fines and penalties prescribed in the Act. 

Rate of Tax Imposed- Law. Section 2. 

That every person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association in this State storing, selling, distributing or manufacturing such beer or such other beverages as are described above, shall pay a special privilege tax, in addition to all other taxes, in an amount equal to One and 70/100 ($1.70) Dollars per barrel of thirtyone (31) liquid gallons stored, sold, distributed by gift or sale, or manufactured in this State. The tax upon barrels containing more or less than thirty-one (31) gallons shall be at a proportionate rate. 

The tax is a "special privilege" tax imposed upon all persons, firms, corporations, joint stock companies, syndicates or associations storing, selling, distributing, (by gift or sale) or manufacturing beer or other beverages of like alcoholic content in Tennessee and is in addition to all other taxes.

The rate of tax is $1.70 per barrel of 31 liquid gallons. 

Barrels and other containers with a capacity of more or less than 31 gallons are taxed proportionately; to illustrate: 

Half Barrel-16 Gallons-Tax .85 Cents Quarter Barrel-8 Gallons-Tax .425 Cents Cases-24-12 oz. Bottles-Tax .1234 Cents per case. 

The "special privilege” tax is measured by the number of gallons manufactured, imported, distributed, or stored for the purpose of gift or sale and the tax accrues immediately the beer or other beverage comes to "rest" or the manufacture of same is completed in Tennessee. 

Exported Products Conditionally Exempt- 

Law. Section 2. 

Beer or other such beverage manufactured in Tennessee and thereafter exported for sale, distribution or gift shall not be included in the measure of the tax liability hereby provided for. The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is authorized to promulgate rules and regulations for the purpose of securing the exemption hereby given and for the purpose of preventing such exemption from being claimed in the case of beer sold, distributed or given away in Tennessee. The burden

(Ch. 10 

shall be on the manufacturer claiming exemption to establish to the satisfaction of the collecting officers that the beverage manufactured in Tennessee is exempt under this paragraph. 

Beer and other beverages taxed under this Act are not to be included in the "measure of tax" if shipped out of Tennessee for the purpose of sale or distribution. This portion of the Act was inserted by amendment, Chapter 88, Acts of 1937. Prior to this amendment all beer and other beverages manufactured in Tennessee was subject to the tax, i.e., beer manufactured in Tennessee and exported to other states was taxable. See Lindsey V. Wm. Gerst 

Brewing Company, 168 Tennessee 62.

Assuming that a Tennessee Brewer or Wholesaler manufactured or purchased 5,000 barrels of beer during a given month the computation of the tax "measure" would be as follows: 

1. Beer manufactured or purchased 

2. Exported-Shipped out of the State: (a) Kentucky (b) Georgia (c) Arkansas

1,500 

3. Tax Measure" 

3,500 Barrels

The Act places the burden upon the manufacturer or wholesaler to establish his right to the "export" beer exemption to the satisfaction of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation; and upon the submission of proof in accordance with the rules and regulations, credit must be given for such beer or other beverage exported. 

State Tax Only— Law. Section 2. 

The tax above levied shall be a State tax and no county, municipality or taxing district shall have power to levy any like tax. This tax shall not apply to beverages previously used as a measure of tax under the provisions of this Act. 

The special privilege tax imposed by this Act is for State purposes only. Cities, towns, counties and taxing districts are prohibited from imposing a similar tax; moreover, this tax cannot apply to beverages previously used as a measure of tax under this Act.

Ch. 10) 821 

BEER TAX 

Supervision and Collection of Tax- 

Law. Section 3. 

That the supervision and collection of the tax herein before imposed shall be under the direction of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. He shall expend so much of four per centum of the amount received hereunder each year as may be necessary to defray the expenses, including clerical and mechanical help and transportation arising out of the administration of this Act. 

The supervision and collection of the tax is placed under the direction of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. While he is authorized to expend so much of 4% of the taxes collected, this provision appears to be inoperative since the passage of Chapters 33 and 211, Acts of 1937. 

State Employees Cannot be Interested in Beer Business 

Law. 

Section 3. 

No employee of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall, while so employed, be interested, directly or indirectly in the vending, storing, distributing and/or manufacturing of such beer, and/or any other beverage under the penalty of dismissal from office and of Five Hundred ($500.00) Dollars fine, to be recovered by indictment or presentment.

While the exact meaning of this paragraph of the law is not clear, however, it is obvious that the Legislature intended that the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and employees of the Department of Finance and Taxation should not be directly, or indirectly, interested in or connected with the beer or beverage business. This provision is so far reaching that it is doubtful whether an employee could lease his property to be used for storing beer or other taxable beverages.

Payment of Tax- Law. Section 4. 

That such tax shall be paid to the State Comptroller through the 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation on or before the tenth (10th) of the month following the month in which the tax as above described accrues.

The tax is payable to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and must be paid on or before the 10th day of each month; i.e., the tax accrues upon manufacture or importation and must be paid on or before the 10th day of the month following such manufacture or importation.

(Ch. 10  Annual Registration- Law. Section 5. 

That every person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association in this State, storing, selling, distributing and/or manufacturing such beer and/or any other such beverages as described above shall be required to first register their names and addresses, by mail or in person, at the office of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and to receive and keep posted at their usual place of business a certificate of registration bearing a serial number, which serial number shall be assigned to such person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association in this State by the Commissioner of 

Finance and Taxation.

Before storing, selling, distributing or manufacturing beer or beverages in Tennessee, the name and address must be registered with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. Upon such registration, the Commissioner will issue "certificate of registration" and assign a serial number. 

The certificate of registration must be posted at the usual place of business. 

Registration Fee $1.00 

Law. Section 5. 

Cost of such registration is hereby fixed at one ($1.00) Dollar, to be paid by applicant before certificate is issued. Such certificate must be renewed annually on or before the 1st. day of January, upon the payment of a registered fee of one ($1.00) dollar. Any person required by this section to be registered who is not registered with the Commissioner as required, or who has not obtained a renewal of such registration for the current year shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and punished by a fine of not exceeding Fifty ($50.00) Dollars. 

Every person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association, before being permitted to store, sell, distribute and/or manufacture such beverages shall pay such license, and comply with such regulations and ordinances as may be passed by the county courts of the counties and/or enacted by the proper municipal authorities of the cities and towns where such persons, firms, corporations, joint stock companies, syndicates or associations may do business in the manner hereinafter provided. 

This paragraph provides for the payment of $1.00 to the Commissioner before issuance of certificate of registration. The certificate is to be obtained each year. Under the provisions of this section as contained in Chapter 69, Acts of 1933, there was some question as to whether the $1.00 fee was to be paid anually; however, Chapter 198, Acts of 1937, removes any question in this regard and provides that the fee must be paid for each year the business is operated.

Ch. 10) 823 

BEER TAX 

The fee must be paid and the certificate renewed on or before January 1st of each year. Failure to renew the certificate of registration subjects the person to fine not to exceed $50.00.

Persons entering business at any time prior to January 1st. of each year are required to pay the full fee, despite the fact that they will be in business for a period less than twelve months.

Form AB-1-516-July 6, 1837 Bond to Secure Payment of Tax- Law. Section 6. 

That all persons, firms, corporations, joint stock companies, syndicates or associations in this State storing, selling, distributing and/or manufacturing in this State such beer and/or any other such beverage as described above shall execute a bond securing the payment of the taxes levied, as the State privilege tax, under provisions of this Act, said bond to be payable to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and to be signed by some solvent surety company residing in or having an office or agent in the State of Tennessee, or by solvent personal surety, and to be approved by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. The penalty of said bond shall be in a sum equal to twice the amount of the tax required to be paid by such person per month and shall be determined by averaging such tax over the period of six (6) months immediately preceding the execution of said bond, and if such person shall not have been in business for a period of six (6) months, the penalty of said bond shall be determined on the average tax per month during the actual time such person has been engaged in business. 

In the event such person shall not have previously engaged in said business, the penalty of said bond shall be fixed at Five Thousand ($5,000.00) 

Dollars during the first month and thereafter said penalty shall be governed by the provisions of this Act; provided, however, that in no event shall the penalty of bond therein provided for exceed the sum of Twenty Thousand ($20,000.00) Dollars irrespective of the volume of business. If at any time after the execution of said bond the surety thereon shall become insolvent the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may require the execution of a new bond with good and solvent

(Ch. 10  

surety in the same manner and with the same penalty as aforesaid, and subject to the approval of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, and any person executing a bond under the provisions of this law, may at any time prior to default under any existing bond, apply to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation for cancellation of the existing bond and for leave to file a new bond with new surety thereon in accordance with the provisions aforesaid, and shall have the right to file such new bond, at such time, by and with the approval of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation.

It is mandatory that each person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association storing, selling, distributing or manufacturing beer or other taxable beverage in Tennessee execute a bond securing the payment of the tax imposed by the State. 

The amount of the bond, can in no case, exceed the sum of $20,000.00; in case the taxpayer has not previously engaged in business the bond is to be $5,000.00 and this amount may be reduced to an amount equal to twice the average monthly tax payments for a period of six months. 

Manufacturers, wholesalers or distributors commencing business should execute $5,000.00 bond and later secure adjustment in accordance with the provisions of this section. 

The bond may be a "corporate surety" or a "solvent personal" bond. All bonds are to be filed with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and subject to his approval, and cannot be cancelled or sureties withdrawn without his permission.

Delinquents; Penalties; Issuance of Distress War rants- 

Law. Section 7. 

That if any such person shall at any time make default in the payment of the State privilege taxes levied under provisions of this 

Act, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall send by registered mail, with return receipt requested, written notice and demand for payment of such delinquent tax, showing the amount thereof due and unpaid, to the surety or sureties on said bond, at the address shown thereon or to the last known address, and if said delinquent tax and all interest and penalties legally due thereon shall not be paid within ten (10) days after the mailing of such notice, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall cancel the certificate described under Section 5 hereof and proceed against delinquent under Section 9316 and 9317 of the Code of Tennessee, 1932, and the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is authorized and empowered, and it shall be his duty to issue a distress warrant for the collection of all delinquent State privilege taxes due under the provisions of this Act, with interest and penalty in the sum of ten per cent.

Ch. 10) 825 

BEER TAX 

Taxpayers failing to pay the tax due on or before the 10th of each month become delinquent and it becomes the duty of the Commissioner to notify the surety or sureties of such delinquency. The Commissioner must give written notice by registered mail to the last known address of such surety or sureties on the bond and if the tax, penalty and interest due by such delinquent taxpayer is not paid within ten days from the date of notice the "registration certificate" of the taxpayer must be cancelled and action taken under sections 9316 and 9317 of the Code of Tennessee. 

The above code sections are as follows: "Section 9316. 

The carrying on, conducting, or practice of any profession, business, or occupation which is prohibited by law, unless the person so engaging in such profession, business or occupation is in the possession of or holds a license issued by some board or other authority organized under the laws of the State, by any person not possessed of or holding the required license, is hereby declared to be a public nuisance, and the same may be abated under any procedure now provided by law for the abatement of any public nuisance, and such abatement may be accomplished by injunction.'' "Section 9317. 

The writ of injunction may be sued out by the Board or Commissioner, charged with the supervision of the particular business or profession; or by any person affected by such nuisance.'' 

Simultaneous with the cancellation of the "certificate of registration" the Commissioner is directed to issue a distress warrant for the collection of the tax plus interest and penalty of ten per cent. It appears that such warrant should be issued jointly and directed against both taxpayer and surety.

Inspection of Products and Examination of Records- Law. Section 8. 

That every person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association in this State engaged in the storing, sale, distribution by sale or gift and/or manufacture in this State of such beer and/or beverage shall keep invoices and all other memoranda fully descriptive thereof and shall permit the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation or his authorized agents, representatives or employees to inspect, at any time during the business hours of the day, all such articles, containers, packages, invoices, books, papers and memoranda as may be deemed necessary in the opinion of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, or his authorized agent, representative or employee, in ascertaining whether or not the State privilege tax levied under the provisions of this Act has been paid or in determining the amount of such tax as may be due.

(Ch. 10  

Taxpayers must keep invoices, papers, records and all memoranda pertaining to the manufacture, sale, distribution, storage and transportation of beer and other taxable beverages, and shall permit representatives of the Commissioner to inspect such products and records at any time during the business hours of the day. Such inspection and examination must be for the purpose of ascertaining whether the tax has been paid or to determine the amount of tax due. 

Report Required- Law. Section 8. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall have the power to require any person engaged in the storing, sale, distribution by sale or gift, and/or manufacture, in this State, of such beer and/or any other such beverages, as described above, to furnish any reports, statements or information, under oath, which may be deemed, in the opinion of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, necessary for the purpose of enforcing a compliance with this Act. 

This paragraph authorizes the Commissioner to require, under oath: 

(a) Reports. 

(b) Statements, or 

(c) Information deemed necessary for the enforcement of the Act.

Rules and Regulations- Law. Section 8. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is hereby authorized and it shall be his duty to make rules and regulations necessary, in his opinion, to effectuate the purposes and carry out the provisions of this Act, which rules and regulations shall have the force and effect of law if not in conflict with express statutory provision.

Rules and Regulations have the force and effect of law when: (a) Adopted by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, (b) Necessary to enforce the provisions of the Act, (c) Not in conflict with the provisions of the Act.

Sales to Minors; Employment of Certain Persons;

Prohibited- 

Law. 

Section 9a. 

That no person engaging in the business regulated hereunder shall make or permit to be made any sales to minors; shall employ any person

Ch. 10) 829 

BEER TAX 

in the storage, sale or manufacture of any of said beverages except citizens of the United States; that neither the person engaging in such business nor persons employed by him shall be a person who has been convicted of any violation of the laws against possession, sale manufacture and transportation of intoxicating liquor or any crime involving moral turpitudes within the last ten years. 

The sale of beer, or other beverage of like alcoholic content, to minors, is prohibited. However, it is lawful for minors to be employed in the sale of beer and other beverages so long as they are citizens of the United States and have not been convicted of violating the liquor or laws involving moral turpitude.

The provisions of this section are very far reaching and persons engaged in the beer or beverage business should use extreme care to refrain from subjecting themselves to prosecution under this Act. 

Since this Act is both a regulatory law and a revenue measure, it is but natural for those engaged in the business to acquire the feeling of security so long as the tax imposed is paid, and while there does not appear to be any great immediate concern over the regulatory features of this Act it is possible that a laxity in observance may prove very expensive to those dealing in beer and similar alcoholic beverages.

Aliens Cannot Secure "Permit”— Law. Section 9b. 

That no permit to engage in such business shall be granted by the State, any county or any municipality to one not a citizen of the United States, or to any syndicate or association unless all of the members thereof are citizens of the United States. 

The State, Counties, and Municipalities are prohibited from granting "permits" to any person who is not a citizen of the United States; or to any syndicate or association unless all the members are citizens of the United States. 

However, there is no such requirement as to the members of corporations and joint stock companies. 

County and City Permit Must be Obtained—

Law. Section 9c. 

That it shall be unlawful for any person to sell, distribute and manufacture the beverages prescribed herein without first having made appli-

(Ch. 10  

cation to and obtained a permit from the county and/or city where such business is to be conducted and the authority herein delegated to said counties and cities.

Before engaging in the business of selling, distributing, and manufacturing beer or beverages of like alcoholic content a permit must be obtained from the county and municipality. This section appears to apply only to persons engaged in the business of selling, distributing, and manufacturing. 

Pool or Billard Rooms- Law. Section 9d. 

That no permit shall be issued to authorize the sale of any beverages coming within the provisions of this Act to be sold or consumed within a room or place used to carry on the business of playing pool or billiards. 

Provided, further, that it may be sold in the front of such room or place if a partition or wall separates the place from the pool or billiard parlor. 

This section of the Act is deemed to be sufficiently clear and comment is unnecessary.

County Regulations; City Ordinances- Law. Section 10. 

That before any person, firm, corporation, joint-stock company, syndicate or association shall be authorized to sell, store, and/or manufacture such beer and/or beverages as prescribed herein, in any county outside the limits of any town or city now incorporated he shall apply to the County Court or to a Committee appointed by said County Court, and shall establish: 

First, that the applicant is a citizen of the United States, or if a syndicate or association; that all of the members are citizens of the 

United States.

Second, that no persons will be employed in the storage, sale or manufacture of any such beverages except citizens of the United States. 

Third, that no such beverages will be sold except at places where such sale will not cause congestion of traffic or interference with schools, churches, or other places of public gathering, or otherwise interfere with public health, safety and morals; the County Court having the right to forbid such storage, sale or manufacture at places within two thousand (2,000) feet of such place of public gathering in its discretion. 

Fifth, that no sale shall be made to minors. 

Sixth, that neither the applicant nor any person employed by him in such distribution or sale shall be a person who has been convicted of any violation of the laws against possession, sale, manufacture, or transportation of intoxicating liquor or any crime involving moral turpitude within the past ten years.

The application shall distinctly state whether the person so applying will conduct the business in person, or whether he is acting as agent for any other person, firm, corporation, syndicate, association or joint-stock company, and any person making false statement in said application shall forfeit his permit and shall not be eligible to receive any permit for a period of ten years, provided, however, that the County Court or the

Ch. 10) 831 

BEER TAX 

Committee appointed by them shall have the right to license any person, firm, corporation, syndicate, joint-stock company or association carrying on any other regular business to store and sell in connection therewith such beer and/or other beverage. 

That all incorporated cities and towns in the State of Tennessee are authorized to pass proper ordinances governing the issuance and revocation of licenses for the storage, sale, manufacture and/or distribution of such beer and/or other beverages as herein prescribed within the corporate limits, provided a Board of persons before whom such application shall be made, but the power of such cities to issue licenses shall in no event be greater than the power herein granted to counties; but cities and towns may impose additional restrictions, fixing zones and territories and providing hours of opening and closing and such other rules and regulations as will promote public health, morals and safety as they may by ordinance provide. 

Providing, further, that the cities may authorize the sale of such beer and/or other beverages described above in hotel rooms of regularly conducted hotels and in regularly incorporated clubs and lodges. Any person, firm, corporation, syndicate, joint-stock company, association, operating without a permit or license from the City or County shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. 

Every person, firm, corporation, joint-stock company, syndicate or association, before being licensed, registered, and/or permitted to sell at retail any beverage permitted to be sold under the provisions of this Act shall execute and file with the clerk of the County Court in the county wherein such business is to be conducted a joint and several bond in the penalty of $500.00 and payable to the State of Tennessee, conditioned that the principal thereof will pay any fine which may be assessed against such principal by any court of competent jurisdiction for any violation of the terms of this Act. Said bond shall be executed by some solvent surety company authorized to do business in the State of Tennessee, or by some solvent personal sureties approved by the County Court clerk, with whom said bond is filed, and it shall be the duty of said County Court clerk to see to it that said bond is kept in full force and effect during the continuance in business of the principal named in said bond. 

Distribution of Collected Revenues- Law. Section 11. 

That the State privilege tax collected hereunder shall be paid into the State Treasury and shall be divided as follows: 

From the proceeds of the amount so collected four-seventeenths (17) shall be paid to the several counties equally, to be used by them for general purposes and four-seventeenth (17) shall be divided among the existing incorporated municipalities according to population; to be used by them for general purposes.

The remainder of the tax collected hereunder shall become a part of the general fund of the State. 

Constitutionality of Act- 

Law. Section 12. 

That it is hereby declared that it is the legislative intent that this Act, and every section, paragraph, sentence, clause, word or words thereof, privileges the lawful sale and manufacture of the beverages described herein within this State; and that the provisions of this Act are sever-

(Ch. 10 

able, and if any word, clause, sentence, paragraph, or part thereof, section or sections of this Act shall be held uneonstitutional by the valid judgment or decrees of any court of competent jurisdiction, the same shall not effect any of the remaining sections, paragraphs, sentences, clauses, word or words of this Act. 

Violations; Penalties- Law. Section 13. 

That any violation of the provisions of this Act or rule or regulation of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation or the violation of any rule or regulation of the County Court or City Legislative bodies relative to the conducting of this business shall be a misdemeanor and where the punishment is not otherwise fixed herein, the offender shall be punished by a fine of not more than Five hundred ($500.00) dollars and imprisonment for not more than six (6) months in the discretion of the court. 

Effective Date of Act— Law. Section 14. 

That this Act take effect from and after May 1, 1933 the public welfare requiring it.

The above sections (10 to 14 inclusive) of the Act are regulatory and general provisions. The regulations and procedures set forth are deemed to be sufficiently clear and therefore comment is considered unnecessary.

1. We think the contention of complainant that it would be entitled to the reduction in tax, set forth in the proviso to sections (d) to 1 and 2, if some of the brewers which it represents as distributor have domesticated and paid the required tax, is untenable. If complainant be a distributor for any brewer not domesticated and not having paid the required tax, then it is not entitled to the reduction or exemption provided for in the 

Act. 

2. Complainant, upon paying the proper tax is a wholesale distributor of beer at its situs or principal place of business, is entitled, under chapter 115, Public Acts 1933, to make sales and deliveries by truck in other counties where it does not maintain a place of business, upon the payment of the maximum tax of $10 to each county and to each city in which it carries on business in this manner. 

Opinion by Justice DeHaven 

(1) This is a suit brought under the Declaratory Judgments Act seeking a construction of the privilege tax pro visions of chapter 115, Public Acts 1933. Under section 1 

of said Act, the carrying on or engaging in the business of the sale, storage, manufacture, or distribution of beer, or other beverages of like alcoholic content, as authorized by chapter 69, Public Acts 1933, or by any other Acts, is declared to be a privilege, and there is levied on every such privilege for general State purposes certain specified annual taxes, the following provisions only being pertinent to the questions made in this cause: 833

(Ch. 10 

"'I. "In Counties or Cities of 100,000 population or over: "" (d) Each brewer or each brewery and/or each agent or distributor at wholesale for many such brewer 

II. 

"In Counties or Cities of less than 100,000 population:

$300.00 "(d) Each brewer or each brewery and/or each agent or distributor at wholesale for any such brewer $150.00 "Provided, that any agent or distributor of beer at wholesale for a brewer who pays the brewers' tax as above set out and the tax imposed by Chapter 69 of the Acts of 1933 shall pay only one-fourth of the tax levied in paragraphs (d), Sections I and II hereof. 'Provided, further, that any agent or distributor of beer at wholesale for a brewer who pays the brewers' tax as above set out and the tax imposed by Chapter 69 of the Acts of 1933, when such agent or distributor pays the tax as set out in the proviso next above in the County or City where he has his situs or principal place of business, such agent or distributor shall not be liable for any other State tax in any other County or City in which he does business but shall be liable for a County and municipal tax in such additional County or City for an amount not to exceed $10.00 to any such County and/or City. 

And, provided, further, that a warehouseman having an established place of business who merely stores for the agent distributor or owner paying the taxes provided by this Act shall not be liable for any tax hereunder. "Sec. 2.  That each County and municipality of the State is hereby authorized to levy a like privilege tax on the privileges enumerated in Section 1 of this Act but not to exceed the amounts levied for State purposes in Section 1."

It is further provided in the Act that when said tax is levied by any county or city of the State, the same shall be in lieu of all other taxes that any county or city may levy or collect on the privilege herein defined; but shall not be in lieu of those imposed by chapter 69, Public Acts 1933, nor in lieu of any other privilege taxes payable by any person engaged in any of the businesses declared a privilege and taxed under any general revenue act of the State. The Act then provides: "The tax herein levied shall be enforced and collected in the same manner as other privilege taxes under any general revenue law of the 

State.'' (2) The complainant, Midwest Dairy Products Cor poration, is a Tennessee corporation engaged in the wholesale distribution of beer, with its situs or principal place of business at Jackson, Madison County, Tennessee, and also maintains a permanent plant, branch, or point of distribution at Dyersburg, Dyer County, Tennessee, and another such plant at Memphis, Shelby County, Tennessee. The

Ch. 10) 

835 

BEER TAX 

beer distributed by the corporation is manufactured outside the State of Tennessee and imported into Tennessee by said corporation to its principal plant, and also to its two branch plants, and is distributed from all its said plants at wholesale within the surrounding territory. 

Complainant distributes beer for six breweries, all being outside the State of Tennessee, but four of the six breweries have qualified under the laws of Tennessee as foreign corporations, and have paid the "brewers' tax" as levied by the Act here under consideration, while two of the six breweries have not qualified as foreign corporations, nor paid said "brewers' tax."

Complainant has paid to the State of Tennessee, the County of Madison, and the City of Jackson $150, each, or a total of $450, as the full tax required of wholesale distributors of beer in counties of that population, and no exemption whatever was allowed at that point. 

Complainant, sought to pay to Shelby County and the City of Memphis the minimum tax of $10 to each, upon the theory that it had paid the full tax as a wholesale distributor of beer at the situs of its principal place of business at Jackson, Madison County, Tennessee. The city and the county demanded the payment of the full tax of $300, each, for the operation of complainant's business at Memphis. 

Complainant paid, under protest, as a wholesale beer distributor in Shelby County, the sum of $300 to the state and $300 to the county, together with $81.25 penalties and costs upon a distress warrant issued by the clerk of the county court, and has sued to recover the same. To stay the collection of this tax by the City of Memphis, complainant filed an injunction bill upon which a stop order was granted pending the final hearing of the two cases. 

In view of the fact that the above-mentioned litigation related alone to complainant's liability for privilege taxes as a wholesale beer distributor in Memphis and Shelby County, it filed an original bill for a declaratory judgment construing the beer privilege tax statute, chapter 115, Public Acts 1933, and determining and fixing its liability for privilege taxes thereunder in the various counties of the State in which it maintains permanent branch plants, or in

(Ch. 10 

which it delivers and sells beer at wholesale from trucks. 

Complainant contends (1) that having paid the tax levied by sections (d) of I and II of said Act at Jackson, Madison County, it is entitled to the exemptions set forth in the proviso following said sections; (2) that inasmuch as a part of the brewers for which complainant is a distributor of beer at wholesale for several brewers who have themselves paid the brewers' tax levied by sections (d) of I and II of said Act, and having itself paid said tax at its principal place of business, it is liable for no other state tax, and is liable in all other counties than Madison, and in all other cities than Jackson, for a tax not to exceed $10 to any other county or city.

In other words, it is complainant's insistence that representing several brewers who have themselves paid the brewers' tax, it is liable only for a tax of $37.50 to the City of Jackson, County of Madison, and State of Tennessee, respectively, to be paid at Jackson, and need pay a maximum of $10 tax only to any other city or county in which it operates. 

It is the contention of defendants that complainant is liable for the full tax, with no exemption, in every county and city where it maintains a place of business, and for a tax of $10 in every other county and city where it might make sales and deliveries by truck. 

The chancellor found (1) assuming that all brewers for which complainant distributes beer have qualified to do business in Tennessee, and have paid the brewers' tax as set forth in said Act, it is liable for one fourth of the tax levied -that is $37.50, each, to the city, county, and the state, at 

Jackson, where it conducts its principal place of business, and (2) is liable for a maximum of $10, each, in every other county and city in which it operates; (3) assuming that complainant represents brewers who have domesticated and paid the brewers' tax, and also represents brewers who have not domesticated and paid the brewers' tax, as levied by said Act, it is liable for $150, each, to the city, county, and state, at Jackson, and is liable for the maximum tax, dependent upon the population classification set forth in the Act, in every other city and county in which it operates:

Ch. 10) 837 

BEER TAX 

(4) assuming that complainant distributes beer by truck and without the establishment of a permanent branch plant in other counties, or within incorporated municipalities therein, the tax liability of complainant shall be the same as though permanent branch plants were maintained in said counties or municipalities therein, and shall be determined in accordance with the first, second, and third findings above set forth, dependent upon the fact as to whether the representation is of domesticated or undomesticated brewers; (5) that for the purpose of determining the tax liability of complainant to the various cities and counties of the State, it is immaterial whether the brewers represented by complainant domesticate and pay the brewers' tax in counties and cities of more than 100,000 population, or in those of less population, provided such domestication and maintenance of principal place of business in connection therewith is bona fide.

Defendants excepted to findings 1, 2, 3, and 5, and complainants excepted to findings 3 and 4, and all parties appealed to this Court and have assigned errors. (3) Chapter 115, Public Acts 1933, here under consideration, is a revenue measure and must be construed in pari materia with the General Revenue Bill of 1931 as amended, which provides in subsection 13 of section 1 the following: "Every person conducting business from more than one established place in a county shall be liable for the privilege tax on business done at each place. "Should he conduct business from an established place in more than one county, he shall pay the privilege tax in each county. "Should he maintain only one place of business in a county, but from that place extend his operations into adjoining counties (without establishing a regular branch office therein) he shall be liable for both State and County tax in County where the permanent place of business is located, but only for the County tax in any other county." (A) Construing the two Acts together, we think it evident that complainant, if it represents brewers who have domesticated in this State and paid the brewers' tax required by sections (d) of I and II of chapter 115, Public Acts 1933, would be liable under the priviso of said sections to a tax of one fourth of the amount of said tax to the state, county, and city, respectively, at the place of its situs,

(Ch. 10 

and a like amount to the state in all other counties where it maintains a place of business, and to such counties and cities, dependent upon the population classification set forth in said Act of 1933. If, however, complainant be engaged in the distribution of beer for any brewer who has not domesticated in this State and paid said brewers' tax, then complainant would be liable for the full amount of said tax to the State in all counties where it maintains a place of business, and to such counties and to the cities where such places of business are located. 

We think the contention of complainant that it would be entitled to the reduction in tax, set forth in the proviso to sections (d) to I and II, if some of the brewers which it represents as distributor have domesticated and paid the required tax, is untenable. If complainant be a distributor for any brewer not domesticated and not having paid the required tax, then it is not entitled to the reduction or exemption provided for in the Act. (B) Complainant, upon paying the proper tax as a wholesale distributor of beer at its situs or principal place of business, is entitled, under chapter 115, Public Acts 1933, to make sales and deliveries by truck in other counties and cities where it does not maintain a place of business, upon the payment of the maximum tax of $10 to each county and to each city in which it carries on business in this manner. (C) A foreign brewer becoming domesticated in Tennessee and qualifying to do business, is liable for a tax of $900 as a brewer if its situs or principal place of business be fixed in either of the four counties of the State containing 100,000, or more, population. The three Tennessee breweries are each located in one of the large counties. It is the insistence of the State that where a foreign brewer voluntarily comes into the State and elects to pay the privilege tax levied upon brewers for the sole purpose of placing its agents upon the same tax basis as agents of Tennessee brewers, and having no physical properties, record, officers, or corporate property within the State, it becomes incumbent upon such corporation to fix its situs for privilege taxation in a county where the largest business in the distribution of its beer is done. We have no statute in Ten-

Ch. 10) 839 

BEER TAX 

nessee authorizing either the taxing officials, or the courts, to fix the situs of a foreign corporation domesticating in Tennessee, under the conditions and circumstances above mentioned. The remedy for any inequality of taxation that may arise from foreign brewers domesticating in counties under 100,000 population must be granted by the legislature and not by the courts.

The decree of the chancellor will be modified in accord with the foregoing declarations. Complainant will pay the costs of the appeal.

MIDWEST DAIRY PRODUCTS) CORPORATION V. 

ED B. CRENSHAW, COUNTY COURT CLERK OF SHELBY COUNTY, ET AL.

Dick Lindsey, et al

V. 

WILLIAM GERST BREWING COMPANY, INC. 

73 S. W. (2nd) 703.

1. Questioning the applicability of the privilege tax, laid by Section 

2, Chapter 69, of the Acts of 1933, on the business of manufacturing, storing and selling beer, conducted in Tennessee, to such portions of its product as might be sold after manufacture outside of this State, and the constitutionality of the Act. 

2. We are unable to agree with learned counsel for the Brewing Company that, because a small portion of its product is sold and shipped to other States, this tax per barrel on the privilege of doing this manufacturing business in Tennessee imposes an unlawful burden on interstate commerce.

Opinion by Justice Chambliss 

Questioning (1) the applicability of the privilege tax, laid by Section 2, Chapter 69, of the Acts of 1933, on the business of manufacturing, storing and selling beer, conducted in Tennessee, to such portions of its product as might be sold after manufacture outside of this State, and (2) the constitutionality of the Act, if so construed and applied; the Brewing Company paid under protest the tax accruing under this disputed provision of the Act, and brought this suit to recover. The section of the Act in ques tion reads as follows:- 

"Sec. 2. BE IT FURTHER ENACTED, That every person, firm corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association in this State storing, selling, distributing and/or manufacturing such beer, and/or such other beverages as described above in this State shall pay a special privilege tax, in addition to all other taxes in an amount equal to One and 20/100 ($1.20) Dollars per barrel of thirty-one (31) liquid gallons stored, sold, distributed by gift or sale and/or manufactured in this State. 

Provided that the tax herein imposed is a State Tax and no County or municipality or taxing district shall have power to levy any like tax. "This tax shall not apply to re-storage, re-sale, or re-distribution of beverages previously used as a measure of tax under the provisions of this Act."

Its enforcement, as above indicated, is challenged only as to its application to that small proportion of the product, less than 10%, sold beyond State lines, and, as alleged, in 840

Ch. 10) 841 

BEER TAX 

prohibitive competition with breweries located outside of Tennessee. The theory of the Brewing Company is thus set forth, following the declaration, on its brief: "I. The proper construction of Section Two of the Act in question does not lay this tax upon beer shipped outside the State. ''II. To declare that it does so levy this gallonage tax upon beer shipped outside of the State is to destroy the interstate commerce from Tennessee without any resulting benefit to the State, its treasury, its industry, or its labor and is therefore a void burden upon interstate commerce. "III. At the time of the passage of Chapter 69 of the Acts of 1933, April 14, 1933, breweries were the exclusive creatures of the Federal Government and the power to tax and regulate. was exclusively in the Federal 

Government; and the only power the State had, then or now, was the concurrent power with the Federal Government to exercise the Police Power over its manufacture and had no power to impose a revenue tax. "IV. This privilege tax conflicts with and destroys as to this subject, the interstate shipment of beer, the National Recovery Act and the Federal Alcohol Control Act, and for this reason would be void.' 

The trial Judge overruled the demurrer of the defendants, the County Court Clerk and State Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, respectively, and they have appealed. 

The demurrer challenged the sufficiency of the declaration, insisting (1) that the Act imposes a tax on the privilege of manufacturing beer in Tennessee, that business or occupation, and lays no discriminatory, or unlawful, burden on interstate commerce; (2) that the Act imposing this tax in no way conflicts with the 18th Amendment to the Federal Constitution, or with any Act of Congress; nor has the Federal Government assumed or acquired exclusive control over the sale of beer; and (3) that the National 

Recovery Act is without application, and in no manner affects or impairs the right of the State to impose this privilege tax on the business of manufacturing this product. 

We are unable to agree with learned counsel for the Brewing Company that, because a small portion of its product is sold and shipped to other states, this tax per barrel on the privilege of doing this manufacturing business in Tennessee imposes an unlawful burden on interstate commerce. Learned counsel quite apparently concede that manufacture is not commerce. They, of course, recognize that, in a long line of decisions, the United States Supreme Court has made the distinction clear between the unlimited

(Ch. 10 

power of the States to tax articles in process of manufacture, and the lack of power to tax articles in interstate transit; and that the articles are manufactured, (or the electricity generated, or the ore mined, or the gas produced), with the intent to ship the product interstate does not affect the rule. Crescent Cotton Oil Co. v. Mississippi, 257 U. S., 129, 66 L. ed. 170; Utah Power & Light Co. v. 

Pfost, 76 L. ed. 1038; Hope Natural Gas Co. v. Hall, 274 

U. S., 284, 71 L. ed. 1049; Oliver Iron Mining Co. v. Lord, 262 U. S. 172, 67 L. ed. 929; Kidd v. Pearson, 126 U. S. 350, 32 L. ed. 346. A case much in point on questions made here is United, etc., Union v. Herkert, etc., Co., 265 U. S. 457, 68

L. ed. 1104. In that case, Chief Justice Taft, distinguishing other decisions, quotes with approval from earlier cases: "The making of goods and the mining of coal are not commerce, nor does the fact that these things are to be afterwards shipped or used in interstate commerce make their production a part thereof." And again, "Obstruction to coal mining is not a direct obstruction to interstate commerce in coal, although it, of course, may affect it by reducing the amount of coal to be carried in that commerce. 

This case clearly lays down the principle that mere reduction in the amount of products to be shipped, does not lay a burden upon interstate commerce prohibited by federal law.

The insistence for the Brewing Company seems to be that interstate commerce is restricted or reduced, and in that sense "burdened," in this indirect manner: The amount of the tax levied on the business of manufacturing this beer is fixed by the act proportionately to the amount of beer manufactured, being $1.20 per barrel of beer. It is said that the State officials collect the tax monthly on the basis, not of the barrels manufactured, but of those sold in the preceding month; that the tax is therefore treated officially as a sales tax, and that, as to that portion of the sales shipped interstate, the tax is laid on goods in interstate commerce; that a burden is imposed thereby, in that the manufacturer in Tennessee is thus made to pay on goods sold in a foreign state a tax which manufacturers in such state and shippers into such state from other states do not

Ch. 10) 843 

BEER TAX 

have to pay; that the Tennessee manufacturer cannot meet this competition carrying this handicap; that the result is and will be that beer manufactured in Tennessee will not be shipped interstate, and thus interstate traffic will be restricted and interstate commerce unlawfully burdened. 

The predicate of this argument seems to us to be unsound. The tax is expressly laid on the manufacturer, or the seller, or the storer. The use of the "ands" and the "ors" extends the application to those who store only, or who sell only, or who manufacture only; to those who do either, or all. The defendant in error is a manufacturer of beer, and the fact that the collecting officers use the sales index for convenience does not change the law, or the character of the tax. 

So we have here a case simply of a manufacturer of a commodity within this State insisting that a privilege tax on its business of manufacturing, (graduated in amount according to the volume of production), has no lawful application to such of its product as it may elect to sell and ship over the State line; that just in proportion as it sells its beer in some other state, or ships it there for sale, it is free from this tax obligation to the State, in which it exercises the privilege of conducting its manufacturing business, and produces for export this alleged exempt portion of it. The argument that this tax is a sales tax, and a tax on interstate sales, apparently rests on (1) the circumstance of the method adopted by the Legislature of computing, or measuring, the tax. (With the evident design of distributing this tax burden fairly, instead of naming a fixed sum for each and every manufacturer to pay proportioned to his capital, or his investment, or the quantity and size of his machinery, without reference to actual production, this more equitable method was chosen.) And on (2) the theory that the Act applies only to those who both manufacture and sell, despite the careful and repeated use of the alternative "or" in the designatory clauses of the Act. It is suggested on the briefs that this alternative "or" does not appear in the caption. 

It was not called for there. The caption was generally inclusive, enumerating all the different classes, or branches of the business regulated by the Act, namely, "the sale,

transportation, storage, possession, receipt, manufacture and distribution" of beer. Notice was given that all or any of these were to be regulated and taxed by the Act. But this did not imply that one would be affected only in case he did all of these things. 

We find no support for the insistence that the Federal Government has preempted the field of control of the manufacture and traffic in beer. We find no conflict between the 

Eighteenth Amendment or the Act of Congress and the right of the State to tax the business of manufacturing of beer.

Nor can we agree that the National Recovery Act, as ingeniously argued, is to be construed as such a taking over by Congress of the regulation and control of this and other private manufacturing business as to deprive the states of the power to exercise their taxing privileges thereon. If this is true of the business or occupation of manufacturing beer, then it must be likewise true of all other products brought by that Act under code regulations. And the argument applies no more, upon analysis, to tax burdens resulting from the levy of privileges, than to those resulting from ad valorem levies. Manifestly, this act of Congress can be given no such far reaching and State sovereignty destroying effect. The judgment is reversed and the suit dismissed.

HISTORY OF  

The first reference to this tax appears to have been made by Governor Horton in his message to the 66th General Assembly under date January 21, 1929, he states; "" A light tax upon malt beverages, malt extracts, and process syrups from which carbonic beverages are made would produce according to my estimates, approximately $700,000.00.❞

Governor Horton was committed to the elimination of the tax imposed on land for State purposes and it appears that his recommendation of a tax upon "malt extracts' was made with the hope that through such a tax, and other new forms of taxation, the tax on land could be eliminated or greatly reduced.

The Legislature enacted Chapter 67, which is the "malt extracts tax law." The statute has been amended in several unimportant particulars since its passage, however, since the passage of the Beer Tax Law in 1933 the revenue from the tax on malt extracts has decreased until to-day it is not large enough to be given consideration as a revenue measure. 847

Section 1192: 

Definitions- The term "person" means and includes every individual, firm, corporation, joint-stock company, syndicate and association. 

The terms "malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof" mean and include all extracts, combinations and derivatives commonly called "malt" or "malt extract,' and further mean and include all combinations or extracts that are derivatives of sprouted barley or any extract or product prepared in whole or in part from or of barley, or products of barley, which may be used as a base or content in the manufacture, making or perfection of any beverage. 

The term "dealer" means and includes every person who engages in the business in this state of manufacturing or receiving malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof and making the original sale or gift of the same in this state; and includes every person who engages in the business in this state of selling and/or distributing by sale or gift malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof within this state. 

Section 1193: 

Rate and Imposition of Special Privilege Tax- 

Every such dealer shall pay to the state, for the exclusive use of the state, a special privilege tax, in addition to

Ch. 11) 851 

all other taxes in an amount equal to five cents on each pound of sixteen ounces or fraction thereof of all such malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof sold and/or distributed by sale or gift by such dealer in this state. Such tax shall be paid and the stamps hereinafter provided for affixed by the person and/or dealer having possession and ownership of such malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof, after same shall have come to rest in this state, and intended to be sold and/or distributed by sale or gift in this state; provided, however, it shall not be a privilege taxable under this statute for the sale and/or distribution by sale or gift in this state of any such malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof if the container or containers of same have already been stamped theretofore in the amount required by this statute and such stamps remain on the container or containers of such malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof while in the possession of a dealer and at the time of sale and/or distribution by sale or gift by him; and, hence no dealer need affix any stamps to any such container of malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof already theretofore properly stamped in the amount required by this statute, and upon which stamps remain while in his possession and at the time of sale and/or distribution by sale or gift by him.

Section 1194: 

Tax Collected by Sale of Stamps- 

Such tax shall be paid by the purchase from the Commissioner of finance and taxation of stamps of such design and denominations as may be prescribed by said. commissioner; and it shall be the duty of such dealer to affix to each container of malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof, a stamp or stamps in the proper amount so purchased from and furnished by said commissioner, and which stamps so affixed shall evidence the payment of the tax imposed by this statute; and such stamps shall be canceled as soon as they shall be affixed to such container. 

Stamps so required shall be affixed in such manner that their removal will require continued application of steam

(Ch. 11  

or water and shall be canceled by placing thereon the date of such affixing. Said stamps shall be affixed, in each instance, by the dealer on the smallest containers or packages that may be handled, sold and/or distributed by sale or gift to the consumers, so as to permit the commissioner, his agent, representative or employee to readily ascertain by an inspection of any dealer's stock on hand whether or not said tax has been paid as provided in this statute. 

Section 1195: 

Sale of Stamps by Agents:-Discount- 

The commissioner is empowered to engage any person to sell such stamps, and shall allow any such person as compensation for receiving, selling and accounting for such stamps, a commission of two per cent; provided, that the commissioner may sell such stamps to banks, bankers, manufacturers, wholesalers, jobbers and retailers, for cash, in lots of twenty-five dollars worth or more at a discount of five per cent. 

Section 1196: 

Dealers to Keep Invoices, etc.; Commissioner to

Examine- 

Each such dealer shall keep invoices and all other memoranda fully descriptive thereof, and shall permit the commissioner or his authorized agent, representative or employee to inspect at any time during the business hours. of the day, all such articles, containers, packages, invoices, books, papers and memoranda as may be deemed necessary, in the opinion of the commissioner or his authorized agent, representative or employee, in ascertaining whether or not the tax levied under the provisions of this statute has been paid, or in determining the amount of such tax as may be due. 

Section 1197: 

Reports and Statements Required- 

The commissioner shall have the power to require any person so engaged to furnish any reports, statements or

Ch. 11) 853 

information, under oath, which may be deemed, in the opinion of the commissioner, necessary for the purpose of enforcing a compliance with this statute. 

Section 1198: 

Additional and Delinquent Tax- 

If any such examination or inspection, or if any such report, statement or information, discloses that the full amount of the tax provided in this statute has not been paid, the commissioner, or his authorized agent, representative or employee, may notify in writing, such person of the amount due, and in the event such person shall not, within five days after such notification, make a proper report and pay the full amount due, the commissioner may issue a distress warrant against such delinquent for the amount due, together with interest and penalties as provided in section 1208. 

Section 1199: 

Violation, Misdemeanor-Penalty- 

The failure of any person, required to pay the taxes. levied by this statute, to preserve said invoices or memoranda required, or to permit the inspection and examination of such containers, packages or articles used as the measure of the tax, and/or invoices, books, papers and memoranda at the request of the commissioner or his authorized agent, representative or employee, or the failure by any such person to make or furnish any report which the commissioner is authorized to require, when so demanded, shall, each, be deemed a violation of this statute. 

Any person violating this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and be fined not less than twenty-five dollars nor more than fifty dollars for each offense. 

Section 1200: 

Misdemeanor to Sell without Tax Stamps- It shall be a misdemeanor for any dealer to sell or offer for sale, or to distribute by sale and/or gift, or to display for sale or distribution, in this state, or to possess, for the purpose of sale or distribution by sale and/or gift,

(Ch. 11  

in this state, after the same has come to rest in this state for and/or after twenty-four hours, any package or container of malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof, to which or on which the stamp or stamps in the proper amount are not affixed, which under the provisions of this statute are required to be affixed; and any such dealer shall be fined in a sum-not less than fifty dollars nor more than one thousand dollars for each offense. 

Section 1201: 

Unstamped Products-Interstate Shipments— 

The commissioner of finance and taxation may, in his discretion, where it is practicable and reasonable for the enforcement of the collection of the taxes provided hereunder, promulgate such rules and regulations as to permit malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof and the container or containers thereof to remain unstamped in the hands of the manufacturers, wholesalers and jobbers until the original case or crate is broken, unpacked or sold; provided, that the commissioner may issue permits in his discretion, and under rules and regulations he may deem necessary, waiving the necessity of the affixing of stamps to any of the articles herein enumerated by the manufacturers, wholesalers and/or jobbers thereof in this state, where such particular malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof or the container or containers thereof are held by such manufacturer, wholesaler, or jobber pending sale and/or shipment without the limits of the state.

Section 1202: 

Refund Shipments Out-Of-State- 

In the case of any malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof, or the container or containers thereof, to which the stamps described have been regularly affixed, and which may have thereafter been sold and/or shipped in interstate commerce by the dealer affixing such stamps, then such seller in this state shall be entitled to a refund of the actual amount of the tax paid upon condition that such seller in this state shall make an affidavit and furnish

Ch. 11) 855 

satisfactory proof that such articles were sold and shipped without the state, and that the purchaser had received such goods, and shall further make affidavit and furnish satisfactory proof of the amount of stamps attached to such articles so shipped without the state, whereupon the commissioner shall refund the amount of such stamps to such seller. Any such refund shall be upon proper voucher and out of the funds collected under this statute. 

Section 1203: 

Refund Unmarketable Products The commissioner is empowered, and it shall be his duty, to refund all sums paid for stamps which have been affixed as above, where such products have for any cause become unsalable or unmarketable. 

Section 1204: 

Counterfeit Stamps: Felony 

Any person who shall falsely and fraudulently make, forge, alter or counterfeit a stamp or stamps so prescribed by the Commissioner (or who shall assist therein), or who shall cause or procure to be falsely or fraudulently made, forged, altered or counterfeited, any such stamps, or who shall knowingly and wilfully utter, publish, pass or tender as true any false, altered, forged or counterfeited stamps prescribed under the provisions of this statute shall be guilty of a felony, and be punished by imprisonment in the state penitentiary for not less than one year nor more than five years.

Section 1205: 

Duty of Sheriff and Peace Officers- 

All sheriffs and other peace officers charged with the enforcement of the laws of the state are required to enforce the provisions hereof; and all fines collected under this statute shall go to the state, to be transmitted to the state treasurer by the clerks of the respective courts when collected.

(Ch. 11 

 Section 1206: 

Administration- The administration of this law shall be by the department of finance and taxation, and the expenses of carrying out its provisions, including the necessary clerical help, the cost of all stamps, the employment of necessary agents, representatives and employees, and incidental expenses, shall be defrayed out of the funds collected, hereunder; not, however, to exceed four per cent of such collections, all of such expenses to be approved by the said commissioner.

Section 1207: 

Rules and Regulations- 

The commissioner of finance and taxation may make all reasonable rules and regulations necessary, in his opinion, to carry out the provisions of this statute. 

Section 1208: 

Special Rules- 

In all things connected with or relating to the carrying out of the provisions of this law requiring the exercise of judgment or discretion, the judgment of the Commissioner shall be final and conclusive and shall not be subject to review, excepting the constitutional right of redress in the courts.

Section 1209: 

Commissioner to Report to Comptroller- The commissioner of finance and taxation shall make a complete and itemized report to the state comptroller on or before the twenty-fifth day of each month covering the receipts and expenditures under the provisions of this law for the preceding month, and shall, at the same time, remit to the comptroller the amount collected, less the authorized expenditures.

Ch. 11) 857 

 Section 1210: 

General Fund Revenue— 

It shall be the duty of the comptroller to issue receipts to the commissioner of finance and taxation for the remittance of taxes and penalties accruing under this statute, and to pay over the funds so received to the treasurer of the state, who shall place them to the credit of the general fund.

Section 1211: 

Purpose of the Law- 

It is the purpose of this law to require payment of the tax herein imposed at the earliest time the same may be legally due, and to require all dealers to exercise due care that the product described herein shall have been properly stamped, either before the same is in any manner taken into stock or handled by them, or, if not before that time, that such dealer shall make payment of said tax and properly stamp such product before proceeding in any manner to handle the same, and within twenty-four hours of the receipt thereof.

Section 1212: 

Construction— 

The tax provided in this statute is not intended to be a tax for the privilege of engaging in interstate or foreign commerce; nor is it intended to be a tax having any relation to interstate or foreign commerce protected by the Constitution of the United States from state taxation; nor is it intended to be a tax having any relation to interstate or foreign sales or distribution or commerce of the articles herein mentioned in which any person may be engaged in addition to his business in this state, and such excepted business, sales and distribution are not taxed.
