Definitions- 

Law. Section 1192. 

The term "person" means and includes every individual, firm, corporation, joint-stock company, syndicate and association. 

The terms "malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof" mean and include all extracts, combinations and derivatives commonly called "malt" or "malt extract,'' and further mean and include all combinations or extracts that are derivatives of sprouted barley or any extracts or product prepared in whole or in part from or of barley, or products of barley, which may be used as a base or content in the manufacture, making or perfection of any beverage. 

The term "dealer" means and includes every person who engages in the business in this state of manufacturing or receiving malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof and making the original sale or gift of the same in this state; and includes every person who engages in the business in this state of selling and/or distributing by sale or gift malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof within this state. "Person" includes all classes of organizations and individuals dealing in or receiving "malt extract." "Malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof" includes all "malt extracts" prepared in whole or in part from barley. "Dealer" includes all "persons" receiving, manufacturing, selling or distributing by sale or gift "malt extracts" in Tennessee. It appears that persons importing “malt extract” for their own consumption are not included in the definition; therefore, should a brewery use "malt extract" in the manufacture of beer, it appears that such brewery is not defined to be a "dealer" and is not subject to the tax.

(Ch. 11  Rate and Kind of Tax- Law. Section 1193. 

Every such dealer shall pay to the state, for the exclusive use of the state, a special privilege tax, in addition to all other taxes in an amount equal to five cents on each pound of sixteen ounces or fraction thereof of all such malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof sold and/or distributed by sale or gift by such dealer in this state. Such tax shall be paid and the stamps hereinafter provided for affixed by the person and/or dealer having possession and ownership of such malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof, after same shall have come to rest in this state, and intended to be sold and/or distributed by sale or gift in this state; provided, however, it shall not be a privilege taxable under this statute for the sale and/or distribution by sale or gift in this state of any such malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof if the container or containers of same have already been stamped theretofore in the amount required by this statute and such stamps remain on the container or containers of such malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof while in the possession of a dealer and at the time of sale and/or distribution by sale or gift by him; and, hence no dealer need affix any stamps to any such container of malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof already theretofore properly stamped in the amount required by this statute, and upon which stamps remain while in his possession and at the time of sale and/or distribution by sale or gift by him.

The tax on "malt extracts" is a "special privilege" tax imposed in "addition" to all other taxes and is imposed upon the privilege granted to "dealer" to "receive, manufacture, sell, or distribute by gift or sale." It should be remembered that at the time of the passage of this Act, (Chapter 67, Acts of 1929) the manufacture and sale of beer was illegal in Tennessee, although the manufacture and sale of "malt extract" used in making what was commonly known as "home brew" was legal, therefore, it appears that the Legislature sought to restrict the use of "home brew" by declaring the manufacture and sale of "malt extract" to be a "special privilege" and taxing it as such.

The tax is imposed at the rate of 5¢ per pound or fraction thereof and is for the exclusive use of the state. 

Counties, cities and towns cannot impose a similar tax. 

This tax is measured by the number of pounds in each container manufactured or imported for the purpose of distribution by gift or sale in Tennessee and accrues immediately upon manufacture or the "coming to rest" in the State of such malt extracts.

Ch. 11) 861 

Payment of Tax- Law. Section 1194. 

Such tax shall be paid by the purchase from the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation of stamps of such design and denomination as may be prescribed by said Commissioner; and it shall be the duty of such dealer to affix to each container of malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof, a stamp or stamps in the proper amount so purchased from and furnished by said commissioner, and which stamps so affixed shall evidence the payment of the tax imposed by this statute; and such stamps shall be canceled as soon as they shall be affixed to such container. Stamps so required shall be affixed in such manner that their removal will require continued application of steam or water and shall be canceled by placing thereon the date of such affixing. Said stamps shall be affixed, in each instance, by the dealer on the smallest containers or packages that may be handled, sold and/or distributed by sale or gift to the consumers, so as to permit the commissioner, his agent, representative or employee to readily ascertain by an inspection of any dealer's stock on hand whether or not said tax has been paid as provided in this statute. 

The tax is to be paid by the purchase of tax stamps from the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, and such stamps must be affixed to the containers of "malt extract" by the dealer. Tax stamps must be canceled by placing on each stamp the date same was affixed to the container. 

Sale of Tax Stamps: Discount- Law. Section 1195. 

The commissioner is empowered to engage any person to sell such stamps, and shall allow any such person as compensation for receiving, selling and accounting for such stamps, a commission of two per cent; provided, that the commissioner may sell such stamps to banks, bankers, manufacturers, wholesalers, jobbers and retailers, for cash, in lots of twenty-five dollars worth or more at a discount of five per cent. 

The Commissioner is authorized to engage any person to act as his agent to sell "malt tax stamps" and must allow any such agent a commission of two per cent. 

It is left to the discretion of the commissioner as to whether he will allow dealer a discount of 5%, and before any such commission may be allowed dealers must: (a) Buy stamps in lots of $25.00 worth or more, and (b) Buy "for cash.''

Dealers to Keep Records- Law. Section 1196. 

Each such dealer shall keep invoices and all other memoranda fully descriptive thereof, and shall permit the commissioner or his authorized agent, representative or employee to inspect at any time during the business hours of the day, all such articles, containers, packages, invoices, books, papers and memoranda as may be deemed necessary, in the opinion of the

(Ch. 11  

commissioner or his authorized agent, representative or employee, in ascertaining whether or not the tax levied under the provisions of this statute has been paid, or in determining the amount of such tax as may be due.

This section requires dealers to keep all invoices and other memoranda pertaining to the handling or sale of "malt extracts." 

While the section does not state the length of time such invoices and memoranda shall be kept it is assumed that such records should not be destroyed until they have been checked by a representative of the Department of Finance and Taxation. Section 1199 of the Act imposes a fine for failure to comply with this section, and, to eliminate possibility of penalty, dealers should secure the permission of the Commissioner before destroying such records. 

This section also authorizes the Commissioner, or his representatives, to inspect all containers of "malt extracts" and to examine all books and records pertaining to "malt extracts"; however, such inspection and examination must be done during business hours. 

Reports and Statements- Law. Section 1197. 

The Commissioner shall have the power to require any person so engaged to furnish any reports, statements or information, under oath, which may be deemed, in the opinion of the Commissioner, necessary for the purpose of enforcing a compliance with this statute. 

The Commissioner is authorized to require dealers to furnish any report or statement under oath which he may deem necessary for the purpose of enforcing the collection of the tax. The only form of report required is an application to the Commissioner for the purchase of tax stamps.

Assessment of Additional Tax- Law. Section 1198. 

If any such examination or inspection, or if any such report, statement or information, discloses that the full amount of the tax provided in this statute has not been paid, the Commissioner, or his authorized agent, representative or employee, may notify in writing, such person of the amount due, and in the event such person shall not, within five days after such notification, make a proper report and pay the full amount due, the Commissioner may issue a distress warrant against such delinquent for the amount due, together with interest and penalties as provided in section 1208.

Ch. 11) 863 

Should the inspection or examination of the books and records of the dealer disclose the receipt or sale of any malt extract upon which the tax was not paid, such tax must be assessed and the dealer notified in writing. If the tax is not paid within five days after such notification the Commissioner may issue distress warrant for the collection of the tax. If the tax is paid within the five day period no penalty or interest accrues; however, if not paid within the above period the act requires the payment of interest and penalties "as prescribed in section 1208"; this section imposes no interest or penalties. 

Violation—Misdemeanor- Law. Section 1199. 

The failure of any person, required to pay the taxes levied by this statute, to preserve said invoices or memoranda required, or to permit the inspection and examination of such containers, packages or articles used as the measure of the tax, and/or invoices, books, papers and memoranda at the request of the Commissioner or his authorized agent, representative or employee, or the failure by any person to make or furnish any report which the Commissioner is authorized to require, when so demanded, shall, each, be deemed a violation of this statute. Any person violating this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and be fined not less than twentyfive dollars nor more than fifty dollars for each offense. 

This section of the Act makes the failure to do the following things a misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of $25.00 to $50.00: (a) Pay the taxes levied. (b) Preserve invoices and memoranda. (c) Permit inspection of taxable products. (d) Permit examination of books and records. (e) Furnish any report or statement required by the Commissioner. 

Tax Stamps Must Be Affixed within Twenty-four 

Hours- 

Law. Section 1200. 

It shall be a misdemeanor for any dealer to sell or offer for sale, or to distribute by sale and/or gift, or to display for sale or distribution by sale and/or gift, in this state, after the same has come to rest in this state for and/or after twenty-four hours, any package or container of malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof, to which or on which the stamp or stamps in the proper amount are not affixed, which under the provisions of this statute are required to be affixed; and any such dealer shall be fined in a sum not less than fifty dollars nor more than one thousand dollars for each offense.

The stamps must be affixed to all "malt extracts" within twenty-four hours after the same has "come to

(Ch. 11  

rest" in Tennessee. The term "come to rest" is usually understood to mean after delivery to the dealer. It is not understood to include malt extracts consigned to a dealer and remaining in the possession of a transportation company or railroad at the point of destination. 

The failure to secure and affix tax stamps to packages or containers of "malt extracts" intended for (a) Display for purpose of sale. (b) Sale or gift. (c) Distribution. constitutes a misdemeanor, and upon conviction, subjects such dealer to fine of from $50.00 to $1,000.00, therefore care should be used to see that stamps are properly affixed. 

Interstate Shipments- Law. Section 1201. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may, in his discretion, where it is practicable and reasonable for the enforcement of the collection of the taxes provided hereunder, promulgate such rules and regulations as to permit malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof and the container or containers thereof to remain unstamped in the hands of the manufacturers, wholesalers and jobbers until the original case or crate is broken, unpacked or sold; provided, that the commissioner may issue permits in his discretion, and under rules and regulations he may deem necessary, waiving the necessity of the affixing of stamps to any of the articles herein enumerated by the manufacturers, wholesalers and/or jobbers thereof in this state, where such particular malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof or the container or containers thereof are held by such manufacturer, wholesaler, or jobber pending sale and/or shipment without the limits of the state.

The commissioner is authorized to issue rules and regulations permitting "malt extracts" to remain on hand unstamped for a length of time in excess of 24 hours; however, such rules and regulations shall comply with the fol lowing requirements of this Section: 

(a) Apply only to manufacturers, wholesalers and jobbers, (b) Issue permit authorizing a certain quantity to remain unstamped. c) Unstamped "malt extract" allowed only for export or shipment out of the State. 

Refund of Tax; Interstate Shipments 

Law. Section 1202. 

In the case of any malt extract, derivatives or combinations thereof, or the container or containers thereof, to which the stamps described have been regularly affixed, and which may have thereafter been sold and/or shipped in interstate commerce by the dealer affixing such stamps, then such seller in this state shall be entitled to a refund of the actual amount

Ch. 11) 865 

of the tax paid upon condition that such seller in this state shall make an affidavit and furnish satisfactory proof that such articles were sold and shipped without the state, and that the purchaser had received such goods, and shall further make affidavit and furnish satisfactory proof of the amount of stamps attached to such articles so shipped without the state, whereupon the Commissioner shall refund the amount of such stamps to such seller. Any such refund shall be upon proper voucher and out of the funds collected under this statute. 

The tax paid on "malt extract" subsequently shipped out of the state in interstate commerce may be refunded by the Commissioner. To secure such a refund of taxes paid the dealer must execute and file claim with the Commissioner, supported by affidavit and such other proof as he may require. All refunds are to be made upon state warrant in the manner prescribed by law. 

In this connection attention is directed to Chapter 167, Acts of 1935, which is as follows: 

"That any claim for refund by the state of taxes or revenue alleged to have been erroneously or illegally paid shall be filed with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, supported by proper proof within one year from the date of payment, otherwise the taxpayer shall not be entitled to refund and said claim for refund shall be barred." 

Refunds: Unmarketable Products— Law. Section 1203. 

The Commissioner is empowered, and it shall be his duty, to refund all sums paid for stamps which have been affixed as above, where such products have for any cause become unsalable or unmarketable. 

This section authorizes the refund of tax paid upon "malt extract" which becomes, for any reason, unsalable. 

Claims for refund shall be filed in the same manner as prescribed and discussed under section 1202 above. Care should be used to see that all unsalable "malt extract" is not destroyed until same has been inspected by a representative of the Department of Finance and Taxation, or permission to destroy has been obtained from the Commissioner.

Counterfeit Stamps-Felony— Law. Section 1204. 

Any person who shall falsely and fraudulently make, forge, alter or counterfeit a stamp or stamps so prescribed by the Commissioner (or who shall assist), or who shall cause or procure to be falsely or fraudulently made, forged, altered or counterfeited, any such stamps, or who shall knowingly and wilfully utter, publish, pass or tender as true any false, altered, forged or counterfeited stamps prescribed under the provisions

(Ch. 11 

of this statute shall be guilty of a felony, and be punished by imprisonment in the state penitentiary for not less than one year nor more than five years. 

Sheriff to Assist in Enforcement 

Law. Section 1205. 

All sheriffs and other peace officers charged with the enforcement of the laws of the state are required to enforce the provisions hereof; and all fines collected under this statute shall go to the state, to be transmitted to the state treasurer by the clerks of the respective courts when collected.

Administration- Law. Section 1206. 

The administration of this law shall be by the department of finance and taxation, and the expenses of carrying out its provisions, including the necessary clerical help, the cost of all stamps, the employment of necessary agents, representatives and employees, and incidental expenses, shall be defrayed out of the funds collected, hereunder; not, however, to exceed four per cent of such collections, all of such expenses to be approved by the said Commissioner.

Rules and Regulations— Law. Section 1207. 

The Commissioner of finance and taxation may make all reasonable rules and regulations necessary, in his opinion, to carry out the provisions of this statute.

Commissioner's Ruling Final- Law. Section 1208. 

In all things connected with or relating to the carrying out of the provisions of this law requiring the exercise of judgment or discretion, the judgment of the Commissioner shall be final and conclusive and shall not be subject to review, excepting the constitutional right of redress in the courts.

Reports- Law. Section 1209. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall make a complete and itemized report to the state comptroller on or before the twenty-fifth day of each month covering the receipts and expenditures under the provisions of this law for the preceding month, and shall, at the same time, remit to the comptroller the amount collected, less the authorized expenditures. 

General Fund Revenue- Law. Section 1210. 

It shall be the duty of the comptroller to issue receipts to the commissioner of finance and taxation for the remittance of taxes and penalties accruing under this statute, and to pay over the funds so received to the treasurer of the state, who shall place them to the credit of the general fund.

Ch. 11) 867 

 Purpose of the Law- Law. Section 1211. 

It is the purpose of this law to require payment of the tax herein imposed at the earliest time the same may be legally due, and to require all dealers to exercise due care that the product described herein shall have been properly stamped, either before the same is in any manner taken into stock or handled by them, or, if not before that time, that such dealer shall make payment of said tax and properly stamp such product before proceeding in any manner to handle the same, and within twenty-four hours of the receipt thereof. 

Construction- Law. Section 1212. 

The tax provided in this statute is not intended to be a tax for the privilege of engaging in interstate or foreign commerce; nor is it intended to be a tax having any relation to interstate or foreign commerce protected by the Constitution of the United States from state taxation; nor is it intended to be a tax having any relation to interstate or foreign sales or distribution or commerce of the articles herein mentioned in which any person may be engaged in addition to his business in this state, and such excepted business, sales and distribution are not taxed. 

The above Sections of the Act, from 1204 to 1212 inclusive are deemed sufficiently clear and comment unnecessary.

HISTORY OF  

Under date, January 21, 1929 Governor Horton sent his second message to the 66th General Assembly. This message deals with questions of taxation and it appears that the tax was imposed upon carbonic acid gas as an alternative. The Governor states: 

"A light tax upon malt beverages, malt extracts, and process syrups from which carbonated beverages are made would produce, according to my estimates, approximately $700,000.00. This tax on process syrups from which carbonated beverages are made need not be more than ten cents per gallon. Approximately eighty to one hundred twenty glasses of coca cola can be made from one gallon of coca cola syrup, so that the tax per glass would burden the traffic but about one-tenth of one cent. 

It seems unlikely that such a tax would be passed along to the consumer with each individual purchase of a five cent drink made by him. If any vendor should seek to add an extra cent to the conventional five cent selling price of a drink, giving as his excuse the one-tenth of a cent that he would pay as tax, competition would soon call him to account. 

The same end might be secured by placing the tax upon liquid carbonic acid gas from which such drinks are made. The malt extracts now sold in increasing quantity in this State could readily bear their share of this proposed tax."

It appears that the Legislature elected to tax carbonic gas rather than the syrup, and enacted Chapter 92, which imposes a tax upon each pound of "liquid carbonic gas.' 

The original Act remained in force without amendment until 1933, at which time it was amended by Chapter 80, Acts of 1933. This amendment imposes the tax upon "solid carbonic acid gas." 871

Section 1167: 

Definitions- The term "person" means and includes every individual, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate and association.

The term "distributor" includes every person who engages in the business in the state of manufacturing, compounding or producing liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor and selling same in this state; and also every person who engages in the business in this state of shipping, transporting or importing any liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor into and making original sales of the same in this state. 

The term "dealer" includes every person, other than a distributor, who, in the course or conduct of, or as an incident to, his business in this state, uses liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor in the preparation and/or mix-

Ch. 12) 875 

ing and/or sale of soft drinks or other beverages or for any other purpose.

Section 1168: 

Rate and Imposition of Tax-Distributor— 

Every distributor shall each year, pay to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, for the exclusive use of the state, a special privilege tax, in addition to all other taxes, for engaging in and carrying on such business in this state, the amount of such tax to be computed as follows: an amount equal to five cents per pound for each pound of sixteen ounces of all liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor manufactured, compounded, or produced by such distributor and sold by him in this state during such year, or shipped, transported or imported by such distributor into this state and sold by him in this state during such year; provided, however, that no liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor sold by any such distributor without the limits of the state, nor any such liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor sold by any such distributor in the original packages in which the same were shipped, transported or imported into this state, unless such package or packages shall have previously come to rest in this state, shall be included or considered in determining the amount of such privilege tax, but only such liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor as has been manufactured, compounded or produced by such distributor and sold in this state, and/or such liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor as has been shipped, transported or imported into this state and thereafter sold by such distributor in this state in broken packages and/or such original packages as may have been shipped into this state as such, and thereafter resold in this state after having come to rest in this state, shall be included in computing the amount of the privilege tax to be paid by such distributor.

Provided, that solid carbonic acid gas is hereby defined as a substitute for liquid carbonic acid gas and for convenience of department of finance and taxation, the tax,

(Ch. 12  

when measured by such gas in its solid state, shall be computed at the rate of two cents for each sixteen ounces. 

Section 1169: 

Rate and Imposition of Tax-Dealer- 

Every dealer shall, for each year, pay to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, for the exclusive use of the state, a special privilege tax, in addition to all other taxes, for exercising such privilege in this state, the amount of such tax to be computed as follows: an amount equal to five cents per pound for each pound of sixteen ounces of all liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor used in the preparation and/or mixing and/or sale of soft drinks or other beverages, or for any other purpose, by such dealer in this state, during such year; provided, however, that no liquid carbonic acid gas or substitute therefor used in the preparation and/or mixing and/or sale of soft drinks or other beverages, or for any other purpose, by such dealer, which was manufactured, compounded or produced by a distributor and sold in this state, or which was shipped, transported, or imported into this state by any distributor and which came to rest within this state, and thereafter was sold in this state by such distributor in the original package in which the same was shipped into this state, or was shipped, transported or imported into this state by any distributor, and thereafter the original package was broken and the contents thereof resold in this state by such distributor in broken packages, shall be included or considered in determining the amount of such privilege tax to be paid by such dealer, but only such liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor as was shipped, transported or imported into this state by such dealer or which was shipped, transported or imported into this state and purchased by such dealer in the original package in which so shipped, transported, or imported into this state and which had not come to rest in this state prior to such purchase by such dealer, or which was manufactured, compounded or produced by such dealer in this state, and thereafter used in the preparation and/or mixing and/or sale of soft drinks or other beverage or for any

Ch. 12) 877 

other purpose by such dealer shall be included or considered for the purpose of computing the amount of such privilege tax.

Provided, that solid carbonic acid gas is hereby defined as a substitute for liquid carbonic acid gas and for convenience of department of finance and taxation, the tax, when measured by such gas in its solid state, shall be computed at the rate of two cents for each sixteen ounces. 

Section 1170: 

Tax Payable Monthly- 

Such tax shall be paid in monthly installments, and the amount of such privilege tax becoming due for each month shall be paid to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation within twenty (20) days after the end of the month for which the same is due. 

Section 1171: 

Administration— 

The administration of the provisions of this law shall be by the Department of Finance and Taxation, and the expense of carrying out its provisions, including the employment of necessary agents, representatives or clerical assistants and all incidental expenses, shall be defrayed out of the funds collected hereunder, not to exceed two and one-half per centum of such collections, such expenditures to be approved by the Commissioner. 

Section 1172: 

Distributor to Keep Records— 

Each distributor shall keep a record, in such form as the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall require, showing the total number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor manufactured, compounded or produced and sold by such distributor within this state during such month; and showing the total number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor shipped, transported or imported into this state by such distributor during such month; the number of pounds thereof sold by such distributor in this state during such

(Ch. 12 

month in the original packages in which shipped, transported or imported into this state and which had come to rest in this state prior to such sale by such distributor, the number of pounds thereof sold in this state during such month by such distributor after breaking the original packages in which the same were shipped, transported or imported into this state; and such distributor shall keep a like record containing such other information as the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may require. 

Section 1173: 

Dealers to Keep Records- Every dealer shall keep a like record showing the total number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor used in the preparation and/or mixing and/or sales of soft drinks or other beverages or for any other purpose by such dealer in this state during such month; the total number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor so used by him in this state. during such month, which was shipped, transported or imported into this state by such dealer; the number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor so used by him in this state during such month, which was shipped, transported, or imported into this state and which was purchased by him in the original package or packages in which so shipped, transported or imported into this state and which had not come to rest in this state prior to the purchase thereof by such dealer; and such dealer shall keep a like record containing such other information as the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may require. 

Section 1174: 

Commissioner and Agents to Examine Records- All of such records which such distributors and/or dealers are required to keep, or which the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is authorized to and does require, shall at all times during the business hours of each day be subject to inspection by the said Commissioner, his agents, representatives and/or employees.

Ch. 12) 879 

 Section 1175: 

Distributors to File Monthly Reports- 

Every distributor shall, within twenty (20) days after the end of each month, make out, in duplicate, on forms to be prescribed by the Commissioner, and deliver to the Commissioner a report showing each and all of the data, information, things and matters contained in the records, required by the above sections, for the preceding month; such reports shall also show the amount of tax due to the state for such month and shall contain all such other matters and information as the Commissioner may require. 

Section 1176: 

Dealers to File Monthly Reports- Every dealer shall, within twenty days after the end of each month, make out, in duplicate, on forms to be prescribed by the Commissioner and deliver to the Commissioner a report showing each and all of the data, information, things and matters contained in the records required by said sections for the preceding month; such reports shall also show the amount of the tax due to the state for such month and shall contain all such other matters and information as the Commissioner may require. 

Section 1177: 

Reports to be Made Under Oath-Duplicate Reports- 

All of such statements or reports shall be in duplicate, and shall be signed and verified by the oath of the individual or individuals or by the president, vice-president, treasurer, assistant treasurer or managing agent in this state of the person making the same. 

Section 1178: 

Rules and Regulations 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall have the power to require such other information from each such distributor and/or dealer as, in his opinion, may be necessary to effectuate the purposes of this statute. He

(Ch. 12  

shall have the power to make all reasonable rules and regulations necessary to carry out the provisions of this law, and in all matters, connected with the administration of its provisions, requiring the exercise of judgment and discretion, the judgment and opinion of said Commissioner shall be final and conclusive, and there shall be no review thereof; except the constitutional right of redress in the courts under the law.

Section 1179: 

False Reports- 

Any distributor and/or dealer and/or any other person preparing or filing, or assisting in preparing or filing, a false report or statement or a report or statement containing false statements, shall be guilty of perjury, and be punished as provided in other cases of perjury. 

Section 1180: 

Fines for Violations Any distributor and/or dealer, required to pay the taxes levied herein, who fails to pay the tax or taxes when due; or who fails to keep and preserve the records herein required, or which the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is authorized to and does require; or who fails to permit an examination and investigation of such records by said Commissioner or his authorized agent, representative and/or employee; or who fails to furnish the reports or statements herein required, or which the said Commissioner is authorized to and does require, when due, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and be punished by a fine of not less than twenty-five ($25.00) dollars nor more than fifty ($50.00) dollars for each offense.

Section 1181: 

Tax Payable on or before 20th of Each Month- Each distributor and each dealer shall, within twenty (20) days after the end of each such month, and at the time of the filing with the Commissioner of the report, required by this statute, pay to the Commissioner the amount

Ch. 12) 881 

of the privilege tax due from such distributor or dealer for the taxable month for which the statement is made and filed, and upon receipt thereof, the Commissioner will issue his receipt for the amount thereof. 

Section 1182: 

Assessment by Commissioner-Penalty 25 per cent— 

If any distributor or dealer shall fail, neglect or refuse to prepare and/or file any report required by this statute within the time provided therein, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall, immediately after such time has expired, proceed to inform himself as best he may regarding the matters and things required to be set forth in such statement; and, from such information as he may be able to obtain, to make a statement showing such matters and things, and determine and fix the amount of the privilege tax due the state from such delinquent distributor or dealer for such month, adding to the amount of such privilege tax a penalty equal to twenty-five per centum of the amount of the tax, to be in addition to the penalty provided by the next following section.

Section 1183: 

Delinquent Tax-Penalty and Interest-Distress 

Warrant

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is empowered, and it shall be his duty, to issue a distress warrant in the name of the state for the collection of the tax imposed under the provisions of this statute, when past due, and for all penalties, interest and cost. Interest at six per centum per annum shall be due and payable on any tax not paid when due. A penalty of one per centum per day is imposed for failure to pay such tax when due; provided, however, that when the penalty reaches fifty per centum no further penalty shall accrue. Said distress warrant or warrants shall be issued against any delinquent or delinquents and shall be addressed and delivered by the Commissioner to the sheriff of the county wherein such delinquent person has his principal office or place of business, or to the sheriff of any county in which the Commis-

(Ch. 12  

sioner has reason to believe property of such delinquent 

Alias and/or pluries distress warrants may be found. may be likewise issued when necessary. 

Section 1184: 

Sheriff to Execute Distress Warrant-Personal Property- 

The sheriff into whose hands such distress warrant may come, or his deputy, may execute same by distraint and sale of personal property belonging to such delinquent, and the proceedings in respect thereto shall be the same as are provided by law for proceedings under an execution at law from a court of record, and the executing officer shall be entitled to the same fees, commissions and necessary expenses of removing and keeping property distrained as in cases of an execution for a court of record. 

Section 1185: 

Sheriff to Execute Distress Warrant-Real Property- 

If the officer cannot find personal property to satisfy said distress warrant, he may levy same upon any real estate in his county belonging to such delinquent; and if levied on land, said distress warrant, together with the officer's return thereon, shall be returned to the circuit court of the county wherein the land lies, and the land shall be condemned and sold under the orders of the circuit court in the same manner as in the case of the levy on land of an execution issued by a justice of the peace. 

Section 1186: 

Commissioner May Sue for Collection of Tax- 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may, in his discretion, institute suit in the name of the State of Tennessee, in any court of competent jurisdiction, for the collection of the tax levied herein against any distributor, or dealer, failing to pay same when due. Such suit or suits shall be for the amount of the tax or taxes due, or any part thereof, with the penalty, or penalties, and interest herein provided.

Ch. 12) 883 

 Section 1187: 

Distributors Must Furnish Invoices to Customers— 

Every distributor selling any liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor in this state, in the original packages in which shipped, transported or imported into this state by such distributor, and which had, prior to such sale in this state by such distributor, come to rest within this state, shall, at the time of making such sale, make out and deliver to the purchaser thereof an invoice in which shall be stated the number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor covered by such invoice, and that the same has been sold in the original package or packages in which the same was shipped, transported or imported into this state, and that such original package or packages had come to rest within this state prior to such sale. 

Section 1188: 

No Tax on Foreign or Interstate Commerce- 

None of the provisions of this law shall apply to the sales of liquid carbonic acid gas sold or exported out of the state. It is not intended by the terms thereof to levy a tax on interstate or foreign commerce, and none of its provisions shall be construed to affect, impair or burden interstate or foreign commerce. The tax imposed shall not be construed to be a tax upon interstate or foreign commerce, or a tax having any relation to interstate or foreign sales or commerce.

Section 1189: 

Fines-General Fund Revenue- 

All fines collected under the provisions of this law shall go to the State of Tennessee, to be transmitted, when collected, to the State Comptroller, and shall constitute a part of the receipts of the tax levied under this statute. 

Section 1190: 

Commissioner to Report to Comptroller— The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall make a complete and itemized report to the state Comptroller on

(Ch. 12 

or before the tenth day of each month, covering the receipts and expenditures under this law for the preceding month, and shall at the same time submit a report of the receipts collected, less the authorized expenditures. 

Section 1191: 

Comptroller to Issue Receipts to Commissioner- It shall be the duty of the State Comptroller to issue receipt to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation for the remittance of taxes accruing under this law, and to pay over the funds so received to the State Treasurer, who shall place them to the credit of the general funds.

When payable 893 Definitions- 

Law. Section 1167. 

The term "person" means and includes every individual, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate and association. 

The term "distributor" includes every person who engages in the business in the state of manufacturing, compounding or producing liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor and selling same in this state; and also every person who engages in the business in this state of shipping, transporting or importing any liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor into and making original sales of the same in this state. ,

The term "dealer" includes every person, other than a distributor, who, in the course or conduct of, or as an incident to, his business in this state, uses liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor in the preparation and/or mixing and/or sale of soft drinks or other beverages or for any other purpose. "Person" includes all classes of organizations and individuals. "Distributor" includes all "persons" engaged in the business of: (a) Manufacturing, compounding or producing liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor, and selling same in Tennessee, or (b) Shipping, transporting, importing liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes and making original sale in Tennessee. "Dealer" includes all persons other than "distributor" using liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes in the conduct

Ch. 12) 887 

of business or as incident thereto, such as bottles of soft drinks, soda fountains, etc.

Rate and Measure of Tax-Distributors— Law. Section 1168. 

Every distributor shall each year, pay to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, for the exclusive use of the state, a special privilege_tax, in addition to all other taxes, for engaging in and carrying on such business in this state, the amount of such tax to be computed as follows: an amount equal to five cents per pound for each pound of sixteen ounces of all liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor manufactured, compounded, or produced by such distributor and sold by him in this state during such year, or shipped, transported or imported by such distributor into this state and sold by him in this state during such year; provided, however, that no liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor sold by any such distributor without the limits of the state, nor any such liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor sold by any such distributor in the original packages in which the same were shipped, transported or imported into this state, unless such package or packages shall have previously come to rest in this state, shall be included or considered in determining the amount of such privilege tax, but only such liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor as has been manufactured, compounded or produced by such distributor and sold in this state, and/or such liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor as has been shipped, transported or imported into this state and thereafter sold by such distributor in this state in broken packages and/or such original packages as may have been shipped into this state as such, and thereafter resold in this state after having come to rest in this state, shall be included in computing the amount of the privilege tax to be paid by such distributor. 

Provided, that solid carbonic acid gas is hereby defined as a substitute for liquid carbonic acid gas and for convenience of department of finance and taxation, the tax, when measured by such gas in its solid state, shall be computed at the rate of two cents for each sixteen ounces. 

The tax imposed is a special privilege tax. The right to manufacture, compound, produce, or import for the purpose of sale in Tennessee is declared to be a "privilege” and is taxed. The special privilege tax is imposed "in addition to all other taxes" and is an exclusive State tax. 

Counties, cities, and towns cannot impose a similar tax. 

The tax is measured by the number of pounds of "liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes" manufactured, compounded, produced, or imported for sale in Tennessee, and the tax accrues when such products come to rest in Tennessee. Obviously, this section imposed the tax "at the source," i.e., upon the manufacturer or upon the distributor importing such products in Tennessee. The tax does not apply to products shipped in interstate commerce to points outside of Tennessee. 

The rate of tax is:

(Ch. 12 

(a) Five cents per pound of "liquid carbonic acid gas.' (b) Two cents per pound of "solid carbonic acid gas and other substitutes.'' 

The "pound" referred to is 16 ounces, and the tax must be measured by the total pounds manufactured or sold in Tennessee during each year. Fractions of pounds do not appear to be taxed. 

Rate and Measure of Tax-Dealer- Law. Section 1169. 

Every dealer shall, for each year, pay to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, for the exclusive use of the state, a special privilege tax, in addition to all other taxes, for exercising such privilege in this state, the amount of such tax to be computed as follows: An amount equal to five cents per pound for each pound of sixteen ounces of all liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor used in the preparation and/or mixing and/or sale of soft drinks or other beverages, or for any other purpose, by such dealer in this state, during such year; provided, however, that no liquid carbonic acid gas or substitute there for used in the preparation and/or mixing and/or sale of soft drinks or other beverages, or for any other purpose, by such dealer, which was manufactured, compounded or produced by a distributor and sold in this state, or which was shipped, transported, or imported into this state by any distributor and which came to rest within this state, and thereafter was sold in this state by such distributor in the original packages in which the same was shipped into this state, or was shipped, transported or imported into this state by any distributor, and thereafter the original package was broken and the contents thereof resold in this state by such distributor in broken packages, shall be included or considered in determining the amount of such privilege tax to be paid by such dealer, but only such liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor as was shipped, transported or imported into this state by such dealer or which was shipped, transported or imported into this state and purchased by such dealer in the original package in which so shipped, transported or imported into this state and which had not come to rest in this state prior to such purchase by such dealer, or which was manufactured, compounded or produced by such dealer in this state, and thereafter used in the preparation and/or mixing and/or sale of soft drinks or other beverages or for any other purpose by such dealer shall be included or considered for the purpose of computing the amount of such privilege tax.

Provided, that solid carbonic acid gas is hereby defined as a substitute for liquid carbonic gas and for convenience of department of finance and taxation, the tax, when measured by such gas in its solid state, shall be computed at the rate of two cents for each sixteen ounces. 

The right to use "liquid carbonic acid gas" in the manufacture of beverages or for any other purpose is also declared to be a special privilege and is taxed. This tax is also in addition to "all other taxes" and is a tax exclusive for state purposes. Counties, cities and towns cannot levy a similar tax.

The tax is measured by the total number of pounds used by the "dealer" during the year in the manufacture of

Ch. 12) 889 

beverages or for any other purpose; however, the tax applies only to the liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes which has not been previously used as a measure of the tax due by a "distributor," i.e., the "dealer" and the "distributor" are not taxed upon the same product. Gas purchased from a "distributor" in Tennessee would not, ordinarily, be taxable to the "dealer." 

The rate of tax is: (a) Five cents per pound of "liquid carbonic acid gas.' (b) Two cents per pound of "solid carbonic acid gas or substitutes.'' 

Tax Payable Monthly 

Law. Section 1170. 

Such tax shall be paid in monthly installments, and the amount of such privilege tax becoming due for each month shall be paid to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation within twenty (20) days after the end of the month for which the same is due. 

The tax is payable on or before the twentieth day of each month, succeeding the month in which the tax accrues, and is to be paid to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. The tax may be paid by checks, money order, draft or in cash. Checks, money orders, and drafts should be made payable to Commissioner of Finance and Taxation.

Administration_ 

Law. Section 1171. 

The administration of the provisions of this law shall be by the Department of Finance and Taxation, and the expense of carrying out its provisions, including the employment of necessary agents, representatives or clerical assistants and all incidental expenses, shall be defrayed out of the funds collected hereunder, not to exceed two and one-half per centum of such collections, such expenditures to be approved by the Commissioner. 

The administration of the Act is placed under the supervision of the Department of Finance and Taxation.

While this section appropriates 22% of the taxes collected for expense of administration, this provision appears to be inoperative since the enactment of Chapter 33 and 211, Acts of 1937. 

Distributor to Keep Records 

Law. Section 1172. 

Each distributor shall keep a record, in such form as the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall require, showing the total number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor manufactured,

(Ch. 12 

compounded or produced and sold by such distributor within this state during such month; and showing the total number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefore shipped, transported or imported into this state by such distributor during such month; the number of pounds thereof sold by such distributor in this state during such month in the original packages in which shipped, transported or imported into this state and which had come to rest in this state prior to such sale by such distributor, the number of pounds thereof sold in this state during such month by such distributor after breaking the original packages in which the same were shipped, transported, or imported into this state; and such distributor shall keep a like record containing such other information as the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may require. 

Distributors are required to keep records in such form as the Commissioner shall require, however, this section makes it mandatory that each "distributor" keep the following records: (a) Total number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes manufactured, compounded, or produced and sold in Tennessee during each month. (b) Total number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes shipped, transported or imported into Tennessee during each month. (c) Number of pounds sold in the original package during each month. (d) Number of pounds sold but not in original package during each month. (e) Such other information as may be required by the Commissioner. 

Dealers to Keep Records 

Law. Section 1173. 

Every dealer shall keep a like record showing the total number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor used in the preparation and/or mixing and/or sale of soft drinks or other beverages or for any other purpose by such dealer in this state during such month; the total number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor so used by him in this state during such month, which was shipped, transported or imported into this state by such dealer; the number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor so used by him in this State during such month, which was shipped, transported or imported into this state and which was purchased by him in the original package or packages in which so shipped, transported or imported into this state and which had not come to rest in this state prior to the purchase thereof by such dealer; and such dealer shall keep a like record containing such other information as the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may require. 

Dealers are required to keep records of all liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes used in mixing beverages or for any other purpose. Such records must show the following information: (a) Number of pounds of such gas imported in the original package by such dealer. (b) Number of pounds of such gas purchased and delivered to such dealer by distributors located in Tennessee. (c) Such other information as may be required by the Commissioner.

Ch. 12) 891 

Attention is drawn to the provisions of Section 1180, and care should be used by distributors and dealers to maintain all records required in this and the preceding section in order that the fines imposed may be avoided. 

Inspection of Records- Law. Section 1174. 

All of such records which such distributors and/or dealers are required to keep, or which the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is authorized to and does require, shall at all times during the business hours of each day be subject to inspection by the said Commissioner, his agents, representatives and/or employees.

This section is deemed sufficiently clear and no comment is made.

Monthly Reports-Distribution- 

Law. Section 1175. 

Every distributor shall, within twenty (20) days after the end of each month, make out, in duplicate, on forms to be prescribed by the Commissioner, and deliver to the Commissioner a report showing each and all of the data, information, things and matters contained in the records, required by the above sections, for the preceding month; such report shall also show the amount of tax due to the state for such month and shall contain all such other matters and information as the Commissioner may require. 

Distributors are required to file monthly reports, in duplicate, showing the amount of tax due, with the Commissioner on or before the twentieth of each month. The remittance covering the tax due should accompany the report.

Monthly Reports-Dealers— Law. Section 1176. 

Every dealer shall, within twenty days after the end of each month, make out, in duplicate, on forms to be prescribed by the Commissioner and deliver to the Commissioner a report showing each and all of the data, information, things and matters contained in the records required by said sections for the preceding month; such reports shall also show the amount of the tax due to the state for such month and shall contain all such other matters and information as the Commissioner may require. 

The comments made relative to Section 1175 apply here also.

Sworn Reports- Law. Section 1177. 

All of such statements or reports shall be in duplicate, and shall be signed and verified by the oath of the individual or individuals or by the president, vice-president, treasurer, assistant treasurer or managing agent in this state of the person making the same.

(Ch. 12  

All reports and statements required to be filed under the provisions of this Act must be sworn to and filed in duplicate. Reports may be jurated before any person authorized to administer oaths. 

Rules and Regulations- Law. Section 1178. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall have the power to require such other information from each such distributor and/or dealer as, in his opinion, may be necessary to effectuate the purposes of this statute. He shall have the power to make all reasonable rules and regulations necessary to carry out the provisions of this law, and in all matters, connected with the administration of its provisions, requiring the exercise of judgment and discretion, the judgment and opinion of said Commissioner shall be final and conclusive, and there shall be no review thereof; except the constitutional right of redress in the courts under the law. 

The Commissioner is authorized to require any information which he deems necessary to enforce the provisions of this Act and to make reasonable rules and regulations to carry out the provisions thereof. 

This section makes the judgment of the Commissioner final; however, an appeal may be taken to any court of competent jurisdiction in case of adverse decision. 

False Reports-Perjury- Law. Section 1179. 

Any distributor and/or dealer and/or any other person preparing or filing, or assisting in preparing or filing, a false report or statement or a report or statement containing false statements, shall be guilty of perjury, and be punished as provided in other cases of perjury. 

Attention is drawn to the fact that any false report or statement made, not only by the taxpayer, but by any person assisting in the preparation of such report or statement is subject to prosecution for perjury. 

Violation-Misdemeanor- Law. Section 1180. 

Any distributor and/or dealer, required to pay the taxes levied herein, who fails to pay the tax or taxes when due; or who fails to keep and preserve the records herein required, or which the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is authorized to and does require; or who fails to permit an examination and investigation of such records by said Commissioner or his authorized agent, representative and/or employee; or who fails to furnish the reports or statements herein required, or which said Commissioner is authorized to and does require, when due, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and be punished by a fine of not less than twenty-five dollars nor more than fifty dollars for each offense.

Ch. 12) 893 

Failure of a "distributor" or a "dealer" to: (a) Pay the tax when due, (b) Keep and preserve records, Permit inspection and examination by the Commissioner or his representative, (d) Furnish reports and statements required. is guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction is subject to fine of from $25.00 to $50.00 for each offense. 

Receipt for Tax Paid- Law. Section 1181. 

Each distributor and each dealer shall, within twenty (20) days after the end of each such month, and at the time of the filing with the Commissioner of the report, required by this statute, pay to the Commissioner the amount of the privilege tax due from such distributor or dealer for the taxable month for which the statement is made and filed, and upon receipt thereof, the Commissioner will issue his receipt for the amount thereof.

The provisions of this section are deemed sufficiently clear and comment unnecessary.

Assessment of Tax by Commissioner- Law. Section 1182. 

If any distributor or dealer shall fail, neglect or refuse to prepare and/or file any report required by this statute within the time provided therein, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall, immediately after such time has expired, proceed to inform himself as best he may regarding the matters and things required to be set forth in such statement; and, from such information as he may be able to obtain, to make a statement showing such matters and things, and determine and fix the amount of the privilege tax due the state from such delinquent distributor or dealer for such month, adding to the amount of such privilege tax a penalty equal to twenty-five per centum of the amount of the tax, to be in addition to the penalty provided by the next following section. 

If no report is filed pursuant to the provisions of this Act, the Commissioner is authorized to assess the tax from any information available. There is to be added to taxes so assessed a penalty of 25% in addition to the interest and penalty provided in Section 1183. Care should be taken to file the monthly reports on or before the twentieth of each month in order that these very heavy penalties may be avoided. 

Delinquent Tax- Law. Section 1183. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is empowered, and it shall be his duty, to issue a distress warrant in the name of the state for the

(Ch. 12 

collection of the tax imposed under the provisions of this statute, when past due, and for all penalties, interest and cost. Interest at six per centum per annum shall be due and payable on any tax not paid when due. A penalty of one per centum per day is imposed for failure to pay such tax when due; provided, however, that when the penalty reaches fifty per centum no further penalty shall accrue. Said distress warrant or warrants shall be issued against any delinquent or delinquents and shall be addressed and delivered by the Commissioner to the sheriff of the county wherein such delinquent person has his principal office or place of business, or to the sheriff of any county in which the Commissioner has reason to believe property of such delinquent may be found. Alias and/or pluries distress warrants may be likewise issued when necessary. 

The failure to pay the tax within the time fixed by the statute (on or before the 20th of each month) subjects the taxpayer to the following penalty and interest: (a) Interest at the rate of 6% per annum computed upon the amount of tax due. (b) Penalty of 1% per day for each day of delinquency computed upon the amount of tax due. However, such penalty cannot exceed 50% of the tax.

It is mandatory that the above penalty and interest be charged, and the section contains no provision relative to the waiver of penalty. It is also mandatory that distress warrant be issued to enforce collection of the tax. 

Distress Warrant-Levy upon Personal Property- Law. Section 1184. 

The sheriff into whose hands such distress warrant may come, or his deputy, may execute same by distraint and sale of personal property belonging to such delinquent, and the proceedings in respect thereto shall be the same as are provided by laws for proceedings under an execution at law from a court of record, and the executing officer shall be entitled to the same fees, commissions and necessary expenses of removing and keeping property distrained as in cases of an execution for a court of record.

Distress Warrant-Levy upon Real Property- 

Law. Section 1185. 

If the officer cannot find personal property to satisfy said distress warrant, he may levy same upon any real estate in his county belonging to such delinquent; and if levied on land, said distress warrant, together with the officer's return thereon, shall be returned to the circuit court of the county wherein the land lies, and the land shall be condemned and sold under the orders of the circuit court in the same manner as in the case of the levy on land of an execution issued by a justice of the peace. 

Suit for Collection of Tax- Law.

Section 1186. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may, in his discretion, institute suit in the name of the State of Tennessee, in any court of competent jurisdiction, for the collection of the tax levied herein against any

Ch. 12) 895 

distributor, or dealer, failing to pay same when due. Such suit or suits shall be for the amount of the tax or taxes due, or any part thereof, with the penalty, or penalties, and interest herein provided. 

Distributors to Furnish Invoices— Law. Section 1187. 

Every distributor selling any liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor in this state, in the original packages in which shipped, transported or imported into this state by such distributor, and which had, prior to such sale in this state by such distributor, come to rest within this state, shall, at the time of making such sale, make out and deliver to the purchaser thereof an invoice in which shall be stated the number of pounds of liquid carbonic acid gas or substitutes therefor covered by such invoice, and that the same has been sold in the original package or packages in which the same was shipped, transported or imported into this state, and that such original package or packages had come to rest within this state prior to such sale.

Interstate Commerce- Law. Section 1188. 

None of the provisions of this law shall apply to the sales of liquid carbonic acid gas sold or exported out of the state. It is not intended by the terms thereof to levy a tax on interstate or foreign commerce, and none of its provisions shall be construed to affect, impair or burden interstate or foreign commerce. The tax imposed shall not be construed to be a tax upon interstate or foreign commerce, or a tax having any relation to interstate or foreign sales or commerce. 

Fines-General Fund Revenue- Law. Section 1189. 

All fines collected under the provisions of this law shall go to the state of Tennessee, to be transmitted, when collected, to the State Comptroller, and shall constitute a part of the receipts of the tax levied under this statute.

Commissioner to Report to Comptroller- 

Law. Section 1190. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall make a complete and itemized report to the State Comptroller on or before the tenth day of each month, covering the receipts and expenditures under this law for the preceding month, and shall at the same time submit a report of the receipts collected, less the authorized expenditures. 

Comptroller to Issue Receipts— Law. Section 1191. 

It shall be the duty of the State Comptroller to issue receipt to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation for the remittance of taxes accruing under this law, and to pay over the funds so received to the State Treasurer, who shall place them to the credit of the general fund. 

Sections 1184 to 1191 inclusive relates to matters of a general nature and are deemed sufficiently clear; for this reason comment is unnecessary.
