Title of Act. 

Chapter 55, Acts of 1935 as Amended by Chapter 

257, Acts of 1937

AN ACT providing for and requiring the registration of motor vehicles and fixing the amount of the registration fees and providing for the collection thereof and appropriating the funds arising from the collection of said fees and providing penalties for violation of any of the provisions of this Act and repealing Section 1149 to 1166 inclusive of the Code of Tennessee enacted by the General Assembly of 1931 and also repealing Chapter 36 of the Public Acts of 1933, which Act and Code Sections so repealed all relate to motor vehicle registration.

(Ch. 13  Section 1: 

Definitions- Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of Tennessee, That for the purposes of this Act, the terms "motor vehicle" and "motor vehicles" shall be construed to mean any automobile, automobile truck, automobile trailer, automobile tractor, motorcycle, electric automobile, electric automobile truck or tractor, or any other vehicle of like character regardless of whether the same falls within the descriptions enumerated herein, propelled over the highways of the State by either steam, distillate, gasoline, electricity, or other mechanical power for the purpose of transporting persons or property. 

Section 2: 

Registration of Motor Vehicle- 

 That as a condition precedent to the operation of any motor vehicle upon any highway, road, street or other public thoroughfare in Tennessee, the owner thereof shall first register such vehicle with the Department of Finance and Taxation in the manner hereinafter provided, and shall pay the registration fees hereinafter imposed. Registration shall be effected through the County Court Clerk in the county wherein the owner resides or maintains headquarters of citizenship in this State when such residence or headquarters is capable of identification, and in such manner as the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may prescribe when no resident or headquarters in this State is readily ascertainable. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall adopt and promulgate rules and regulations adapted to the enforcement of this Section and succeeding sections relating to motor vehicle registration, which rules and regulations shall have the force and effect of law; they shall include the following provisions: 

(1) No registration of any motor vehicle shall be issued by the registering official unless the owner shall present satisfactory evidence of title. (2) No motor vehicle shall be subject to registration under the provisions of this law unless said vehicle is suitable and safe for use on the highways.

Ch. 13) 903 

When used in this Section or other sections relating to motor vehicle registration, the term "suitable and safe for use on the highways" means: (a) That the provisions of Section 2693, 2694, and 2695 of the Code of Tennessee for 1932 have been complied with. (b) That the provisions of Chapter 35, Public Acts of 1933 have been complied with. (c) That the vehicle is equipped with brakes adequate to control the movement of, and to stop and hold such vehicle, including two separate means of applying the brakes to at least two wheels and so constructed that no part which is liable to failure shall be common to the two, except that a motorcycle need be equipped with only one brake. All such brakes shall be maintained in good working order. (3) The correct motor number or serial number shall be given in each instance before registration is effected. 

Section 3: 

Classification of Vehicles and Imposition of Fees— 

 That in order to facilitate efficient and uniform enforcement of this law motor vehicles are hereby classified and the respective registration fees imposed are fixed as follows:

Class A. Motorcycles with two wheels. Registration Fee $3.00. 

Class B. Motorcycle with three wheels. Registration Fee $5.00.

Class C. Passenger motor vehicles weighing not exceeding 3,500 pounds. Registration Fee $7.50.

Class D. Passenger motor vehicles weighing over 3,500 pounds. Registration Fee $10.00.

Class 1. Freight motor vehicles with declared maximum gross weight including vehicle and load of not more than 8,000 pounds. Registration 

Fee $15.00.

Class 2. Freight motor vehicles with declared maximum gross weight including vehicle and load over 8,000 pounds and not exceeding 14,000 pounds. Registration Fee $25.00.

Class 3. Freight motor vehicle with declared maximum gross weight including vehicle and load over 14,000 pounds and not exceeding 18,000 pounds. Registration Fee $50.00.

Class 4. Freight motor vehicles with declared maximums gross weight including vehicle and load over 18,000 pounds and not exceeding 24,000 pounds. Registration Fee $75.00.

Class 5. Freight motor vehicles with declared maximum gross weight including vehicle and load over 24,000 pounds. Registration Fee $125.00. 

Class 6. Tractors used for purposes other than transporting freight. 

Registration Fee $25.00. Provided, that such registration fee shall not apply to farm tractors used for agricultural purposes. 

The combined weight of tractors and trailer or tractors and semi-trailers or motor truck with trailer or semitrailer attached shall be used in determining declared maximum gross weight for purpose of classification. Provided, further, that an allowance of 10% over the declared

(Ch. 13  

maximum gross load of weight in each classification be granted the truck owner or operator. 

The declared maximum gross weight including motor vehicle and load shall be painted with durable paint in letters and figures not less than four inches in height on right side of said vehicle within five feet of front wheel. 

The official effecting registration shall receive as compensation therefor the sum of thirty-five (35) cents, and said amount shall be his full compensation, and in lieu of all other compensation for registration of motor vehicles. 

Provided, that fees on trucks used by the owner exclusively for farm purposes, and/or for the purpose of transporting farm and/or dairy products, produced by the owner of the trucks, shall be at the rate of fifty (50%) per cent of the fees above set out; provided further, that each owner of such truck claiming it to be used exclusively for farm purposes, or the transportation of farm or dairy products, shall make affidavit on the blanks to be furnished by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, that the truck for which application for registration is being made, is owned and used by the owner exclusively for farm purposes and/or for the purpose of transporting farm and/or dairy products produced or grown by him or her. And if such affidavit is not so made then the truck shall be charged at the full rate as above set out. And it shall be a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of Fifty ($50.00) Dollars and/or removal from office for the county Court Clerks or any of their deputies charged with the duty of registering trucks to charge such reduced rates unless said affidavit is first made; Provided, further, that any motor vehicle which serves the same purpose of a truck by an alteration in or modification of its original structure, shall be classed as a freight motor vehicle and shall be taxed as such notwithstanding that such vehicle was not originally manufactured as a truck. 

It is hereby expressly stipulated that no registration fee shall be charged for any trailer or semi-trailer attached to or drawn by a passenger automobile, motorcycle, or other vehicle of like character (excluding trucks) belonging to and used by the owner in transporting farm and/or dairy products (not for hire) over any of the roads, high-

Ch. 13) 905 

ways or streets of this state from the place of production. 

Nothing in this Section shall be construed as a grant of authority for the use on the public highways of the State of any motor vehicle which now is or may hereafter by law be prohibited from such use. 

When used in this Section and subsequent sections relating to motor vehicles: (a) The word "freight" means all tangible personal property. (b) The term "freight vehicle" and the plural as well as the singular number means a vehicle used to transport tangible personal property. 

Failure of any person, firm, corporation, joint-stock company, syndicate or association to comply with the provisions of this section shall be deemed a violation thereof and any such person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association violating this Section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not less than Two-fifty ($2.50) Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00) Dollars for each offense, and all fines collected hereunder shall go to the State of Tennessee, to be, when collected, transmitted to the Comptroller through the Department of Finance and Taxation. Provided, further, that no license fee shall be charged for any trailer or semi-trailer attached to or drawn by a passenger automobile, motorcycle, or other vehicle of like character (excluding trucks) belonging to and used by the owner in transporting farm and/or dairy products (not for hire) over any of the roads, highways, or streets of this State from the place of production. 

Section 4: 

Registration Fees Motor Vehicles Operating for 

Hire-  That in addition to the registration fees described in Section 3 hereof, passenger motor vehicles operating for hire shall pay at the time of registration the following fees, to-wit:

Motor vehicles with two seats for passengers. 

Motor vehicles with over two and not more than five seats for passengers .$ 4.00 10.00

(Ch. 13  

Motor vehicles with over five and not more than seven seats for passengers

Motor vehicles with over seven seats for passengers, an amount equal to $2.00 for each seat. 14.00

The declared seating capacity of each such motor vehicle operating for hire shall be painted in letters and figures not less than one and one-half (12) inches high on the right side of said vehicle within five (5) feet of the front wheel.

Failure of any person, firm corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association to comply with the provisions of this Section shall be deemed a violation thereof any (and*) such person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association violating this Section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof shall be fined not less than Two-fifty ($2.50) Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00) Dollars for each offense, and all fines collected hereunder shall go to the State of Tennessee, to be, when collected, transmitted to the Comptroller through the Department of Finance and Taxation.

Section 5: 

Discount, Reduction, Allowance  That if registration as provided in the preceding Sections is effected during the first three months of the calendar year, an allowance, discount or reduction shall be allowed equal to three-fifths of the stipulated registration fee for the annual registration. This section shall not apply to the purchase of tags during the first three calendar months of 1935.

Section 6: 

Non-Resident Owners Be it further enacted, That non-resident owners of regularly licensed passenger motor vehicles not operated for hire, registered in any state or territory of the United States, Canada or Mexico, may have the privilege of operating upon the public roads of the State for a period of not exceeding thirty days.

Ch. 13) 907 

Non-resident owners of freight carrying motor vehicles operating for any purpose whatsoever and passenger vehicles operating for hire, regularly licensed and/or registered in any state or territory of the United States, Canada, or Mexico, may operate upon the public roads of the State under the following conditions only, to-wit: 

Application for temporary registration shall be made to the County Court Clerk of the County of entry, or any designated office of the Department of Finance and Taxation.

Application shall declare mileage to be traveled and time necessary to complete trip.

Application shall be accompanied by temporary registration fee equal to one and one-half cents per mile of said declared mileage, together with compensation for the registering official in the sum of thirty-five (35¢) cents, which said sum shall be his full compensation and in lieu of all other compensation for registration of motor vehicles. 

Temporary registration certificate shall be retained by the person in charge of the vehicle while said vehicle is in this State. 

Failure of any person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association to comply with the provisions of this Section shall be deemed a violation thereof and any such person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association violating this Section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not less than two-fifty ($2.50) Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00) 

Dollars for each offense, and all fines collected hereunder shall go to the State of Tennessee, to be, when collected, transmitted to the Comptroller through the Department of Finance and Taxation. 

The County Court Clerk collecting the registration fee from nonresident owners of motor vehicles operating over the highways of the State shall transmit the same to the Comptroller through the Department of Finance and Taxation in the manner provided by law for the transmission of other fees and the funds so collected shall be covered into the general highway fund for use in the construction and maintenance of the State highways. Said registration fees shall be in addition to all other fees, taxes or compensation imposed by law on non-resident operators of motor vehicles over the State highways. Likewise, fines collected under this section of this Act shall go to the general highway fund. 

Section 7: 

Changes in Ownership  That whenever the ownership of any such motor vehicle shall become changed by sale or otherwise, the registration number or license plates shall remain upon such vehicle as a part thereof until such registration expires by law; but the purchaser thereof shall be required to immediately notify the said Department of Finance and Taxation through the County Court Clerk of such transfer and receive a transfer certificate in his name, for which he shall pay a fee of One ($1.00) Dollar, and the Clerk shall indicate the change of ownership on his

(Ch. 13 

records. When motor vehicles are transferred, sold or given away, the dealer (or if the seller or donor is not a dealer, then the owner) as well as the new owner shall be responsible for the recording of such transfer, sale or gift in the office of the County Court Clerk in the County where such transfer, sale or gift is made.

In the event any registered motor vehicle is wrecked, destroyed or otherwise rendered unsuitable or unsafe for use and/or operation on the highways of the State, the owner and/or operator shall immediately remove therefrom the license plates theretofor purchased for such motor vehicle and return the same immediately to the County Court Clerk from whom they were purchased and it shall be the duty of the County Court Clerk to issue to the holder of said license plates a new set of plates charging a fee of 

One Dollar Fifty ($1.50) cents plus the Clerk's registration fee for effecting registration, and to return said plates to the Department of Finance and Taxation. No license shall be purchased by anyone except from the Department of Finance and Taxation direct or from said Department through the County Court Clerk of the county where the owner of the motor vehicle sought to be registered resides; provided, however, that when a registered motor vehicle which is still suitable and safe for use and operation on the highways of the State is sold or transferred by the owner thereof the license plates already purchased by the original owner and attached to said motor vehicle may be sold or transferred by the original owner to the new owner as a part of the motor vehicle involved in the sale but both the seller and purchaser shall see to it that the provisions of Section 7 hereof are immediately complied with; and where any registered motor vehicle is wrecked, destroyed or otherwise rendered unsuitable or unsafe for use and/or operation on the highways of the State, the owner may obtain a new set of tags for another vehicle as provided for in this section. Failure to comply with any provision of this Section shall be deemed a violation thereof and the person violating the same shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not less than 

Two-fifty ($2.50) Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00) Dol-

Ch. 13) 909 

lars for each offense. All fines collected hereunder shall go to the State of Tennessee, to be, when collected, transmitted to the Comptroller through the Department of 

Finance and Taxation. 

Section 8: 

Motor Vehicles Owned by Government— 

 That upon the sworn statement from the head of any department of the State government or the county judge or the chairman of the county court of any county, or the mayor of any town or city or upon certification of authorized officials of the United States Government, that the motor vehicle for which application is made for registration, is owned by the state, the county, the city, the town or the United States Government and operated exclusively for essential governmental purposes, the State Department of Finance and Taxation, through the County Court Clerk, shall issue a license and number plate as above provided upon payment of fifteen cents to cover cost of manufacturing and packing each set of two plates; but the County Court Clerk shall have the right to collect the fee of thirty-five cents for registration, but in all such cases the application must be accompanied by a sworn statement as above provided, and the County Court Clerk shall not issue any number plate until special authority is obtained from the State Department of Finance and Taxation.

Section 9: 

Display of Number Plates— 

Be it further enacted, That the owner and/or operator of such motor vehicle is required to display, in a conspicuous manner at both front and rear of such motor vehicle, a number plate of suitable size, color, dimension, and character as the Department of Finance and Taxation may designate; provided, that the size of the number plate shall be the same each year and shall be designed to fit all classes of motor vehicles. The number plate shall show, in addition to the registration number of such machine, the year and the abbreviation of Tennessee;

(Ch. 13 

provided, further, that the Department of Finance and Taxation, through the County Court Clerk, shall furnish, without additional cost to the owner of such machine a set of two number plates, and owners are required to use these number plates on their machines, and no other number plates shall be used. 

Section 10: 

Dealers and Manufacturers-  That all dealers in or manufacturers of motor vehicles shall instead of registering each such motor vehicle owned by him, make application to and receive from the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation through the County Court Clerk a general distinguishing number or mark. This certificate and number shall be of a different color and number from that of any other owner of a motor vehicle, and shall be known as a dealer's number, and said number may be used by said dealer or manufacturer upon any new or second-hand motor vehicle the property of the dealer held for the purpose of trade or resale, but said number shall not be used on motor vehicles used for other than strictly business purposes. Said dealer or manufacturer shall register with and pay to the said Commissioner of Finance and Taxation through the County Court Clerk for such special .dealers' number, the sum of 

Fifty ($50.00) Dollars. This registration shall be renewed annually as other registrations and the annual registration fee shall be Fifty ($50.00) Dollars and the owner shall register same with the County Court Clerk and pay a fee of thirty-five (354) cents. Duplicate dealers' number plates in series not to exceed twenty duplicate plates of any one number shall be issued by the County Court Clerk, upon payment, due to the State, of a license fee of One ($1.00) Dollar for each such additional pair of plates; provided, that when not over four duplicate plates are issued the fee for same shall be Thirty ($30.00) Dollars. 

In the case of the dealer or manufacturer of motorcycles, said dealer or manufacturer shall register with and pay to said Commissioner of Finance and Taxation through the County Court Clerk for such special dealers' number the

Ch. 13) 911 

sum of Ten ($10.00) Dollars. This registration shall also be renewed annually as other registration and the annual registration fee shall be Ten ($10.00) Dollars, and the owner shall register same with the County Court Clerk and pay fee of thirty-five (35¢) cents. Duplicate motorcycle dealers' number plates in series not to exceed three duplicate plates of any one number shall be issued by the County Court Clerk, upon payment, due to the State, of a license fee of Thirty-five (354) cents for each such additional pair of plates. The County Court Clerk shall receive no additional fee for the issuance of these duplicate dealers' number plates; provided, that anyone using any duplicate plates other than those herein authorized shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and on conviction thereof shall be fined not less than Two-fifty ($2.50) Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00) dollars.

Section 11: 

Drive-Out Cards— 

 That it shall be the duty of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation to provide for distribution to all dealers in motor propelled vehicles applying for the same, cards in pairs of suitable size and character to fit all classes of motor vehicles, bearing thereon in type large enough to be plainly seen the word "Dealer" and a serial number, together with the words "This tag expires ," and it shall be the duty of said Commissioner to keep or have kept a record of each pair of tags issued, showing a serial number, date issued and to whom issued; these tags shall be issued in pairs to dealers in such motor vehicles applying therefor, who shall pay for each pair of tags so issued One ($1.00) Dollar, except in the case of motorcycle dealers who shall pay for each pair of tags so issued thirty-five (35¢) cents.

Section 12: 

Dealer to Issue Drive-Out Cards- 

Be it further enacted, That every dealer in motor vehicles propelled by other than muscular power shall issue to the purchaser of each vehicle a pair of such tags,

(Ch. 13  

and it shall be the duty of each purchaser to affix or have affixed one of said tags on the front, one on the rear of such motor vehicles in such manner as to be plainly seen before driving such motor vehicles on any highway of the State. 

The dealer selling such motor vehicles shall plainly write in ink on the blank left on each tag for the purpose, the day and hour such tag expires, and shall keep a record of each pair of tags issued, and to whom issued; the kind, name of manufacturers and factory, motor or manufacturers' number of such motor vehicle; date and hour when issued, by whom issued, and when said tag was marked to expire. In no case shall the dealer mark such tag to expire more than forty-eight hours after issuance; and such tag shall be good only for the time marked thereon, but in no event more than forty-eight hours. 

Section 13: 

Misdemeanor to Operate Vehicle Without Tags- 

 That it shall be unlawful for any person who has not obtained the license, required by law for vehicles, to operate any motor vehicles propelled by other than muscular power on front and rear of such vehicles the tag required by the preceding section hereof. 

Any violation of this Section shall be a misdemeanor, and the person violating it shall be fined not less than Twofifty ($2.50) Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00) Dollars.

Section 14: 

Drive-Out Card Expires-Forty-Eight Hours- 

Be it further enacted, That no dealer or his agent shall issue any tag described in Sections 11 et seq. hereof, except for a motor vehicle actually delivered to a purchaser or his agent or servant; nor shall he mark the time of expiration of such tag beyond forty-eight hours after the time of actual delivery of such vehicles; nor shall there be issued more than one pair of tags for each vehicle; nor shall he fail to keep an actual record of tags as hereinabove provided for; nor shall he use any such tags on any motor vehicle not actually delivered to purchaser or purchaser's agent; nor on any motor vehicle for which state or city

Ch. 13) 913 

licenses and number shall have been issued. Any violation of this Section shall be a misdemeanor and any person convicted shall be fined not less than Two-fifty ($2.50) Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00) Dollars.

Section 15: 

Registration Date-April 1, of each Year- 

Be it enacted, That each owner of a motor vehicle, who has not effected registration of his or her motor vehicle for the year 1935 and who desires to operate the same over the highways of the State during the calendar year 1935, and for the first three months of the year 1936, shall pay for said privilege the rate set forth in this bill for the calendar year 1935, and shall operate such registered motor vehicles. until April 1, 1936; provided further, that each person, firm or corporation that has effected registration of motor vehicles under the law prior to the passage of this Act, shall operate such vehicles over the highways of the State for the year 1935 and to April 1st, 1936, without paying any additional registration fees; provided further, that any owner of any motor vehicle, automobile, motocycle (motorcycle*) truck or other motor vehicle of like character who has paid the license fees under the law existing prior to the passage of this Act for operating any such motor vehicle on the public roads, streets, or highways of this State for the year 1935 under the law existing prior to the passage of this Act, shall be and is hereby declared to be entitled to have any excess so paid by any person, firm or corporation, above the amounts fixed under the provisions of this Act, refunded to the person, firm, or corporation paying same by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation acting for the Department of Finance and Taxation for the State of Tennessee upon the person, firm or corporation making application for such refund within the time and in such manner and under such rules and regulations as may be promulgated by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation who is hereby authorized to make such reasonable rules and regulations governing such application for refund as the said Commissioner may seem proper; and the Treasurer of the 

State of Tennessee is hereby directed upon warrant of the

(Ch. 13 

Comptroller drawn upon the approval of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, to repay such applicant, the 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation being authorized to demand such evidence of such payment as to him may seem sufficient of the payment of such license fee to the County Court Clerk issuing same for the year 1935 and prior to the passage of this Act. 

After the passage of this Act, registration shall be made under the provisions of this Act and the annual registration of motor vehicles shall be had on the first day of April 1936 and annually thereafter. Such registration shall entitle the owner of the motor vehicle so registered to operate the same over the highways of the State for a period of twelve months from and after the first day of April in which the registration takes place. Applications for registration shall be made to the Department of Finance and Taxation through the County Court Clerk, with the applicant giving the same information and paying the same fees required under this Act; and upon the payment of such fees, the applicant shall receive from the Department of Finance and Taxation through the County Court Clerk a certificate showing such registration and he shall also receive from the same source a set consisting of two number plates on which shall appear the year and the abbreviation of the word "Tennessee" in addition to the registration number.

Section 16: 

Duties of County Court Clerk-  That it shall be the duty of the County Court Clerk of each County to enforce the provisions of this Statute and in so doing he shall: (a) Ascertain the names of the owners of all wheeled vehicles above described and included, in his county, and issue distress warrants against the owner operating any such motor vehicle in violation of the provisions of this law, after April 1, of the year for which the tax in question may be due. In case of the issuance of such distress warrant such Clerk shall be entitled to collect the fees now provided by law for the issuance of distress warrants. (b) Take registration applications from the owner of any vehicle designated in this law. (c) Collect the fees provided for in this law.

Ch. 13) 915 

(d) Distribute the number plates provided by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and keep a complete record in his office, for the benefit of the general public, of all such motor vehicles registered in his county. (e) Remit and report on the first day of each month to the Department of Finance and Taxation, all monies at that time on hand collected by him under the provisions of this law, and report to the Department of Finance and Taxation the list of registrations made in his office for the preceding month. (f) Account to the Department of Finance and Taxation for all number plates so consigned to him. (g) Collect from the owner making application for the registration of a motor vehicle required to be registered under the provisions of this law a fee of thirty-five (35¢) cents, which shall be his compensation in full.

If any County Court Clerk shall be delinquent as much as ten days in making the report hereinabove required to be made he shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall be fined not less than Two-fifty ($2.50) Dollars nor more than 

Fifty ($50.00) Dollars.

Section 17: 

Department to Remit to State Treasury— 

 That the Department of Finance and Taxation on or before the tenth day of the succeeding month shall report and remit to the State Treasury all monies so received during a given month by the Department from County Court Clerks or from any and all other sources, under this law, without any deduction on account of salaries, fees, costs, expenses or claims of any description whatsoever. 

Section 18: 

Sections 1149 to 1166 Inclusive of Code Repealed- 

Be it further enacted, That Sections 1149 to 1166 inclusive of the Code of Tennessee enacted by the General Assembly of 1931, said Sections relating to motor vehicle registration, are hereby repealed.

Section 19: 

Other Laws Repealed— 

Be it further enacted, That Chapter 36 of the Public Acts of 1933, entitled "An Act to amend Section 1149 of the Official Code of Tennessee passed at the regular session

(Ch. 13  

of the General Assembly of 1931, said section of the Code providing for the registration of automobiles, trucks and motor vehicles of all kinds, so as to reduce the registration fee from fifty cents per rated horsepower of such motor vehicles to thirty-seven and one-half cents. And to provide a refund to all who have paid the registration fee for the year 1933 so as to equalize such payments and place them on the same basis as those who pay after the passage of this Act," be and the same is hereby repealed. 

Section 20: 

Highway Fund Revenue- 

 That the funds derived from the registration fees collected under this Act shall be covered into the General Treasury of the State and shall be expended for the construction and maintenance of the highways of the State in the manner provided in Sections 3184 and 11,464 of the Code of Tennessee, and the Comptroller, Treasurer, Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and

Commissioner of Highways and Public Works shall accord ingly keep their records to show the distribution and expenditure of said funds. 

Section 21: 

Fines and Penalties-Highway Fund- 

Be it further enacted, That all fines and penalties collected for prosecutions instituted and convictions had for violations of the provisions of this Act shall belong to the State and shall be transmitted to the State Treasury by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and shall become a part of the highway funds to be expended as provided in the preceding section of this Act. 

Section 22: 

Constitutional Provision- 

Be it further enacted, That if any section, paragraph or clause of this Act for any reason be declared unconstitutional, such declaration of invalidity or unconstitutionality shall not affect any other portion of the Act, it being the

RULES AND REGULATIONS  Chapter 55, Public Acts of 1935 

No motor vehicle shall be subject to registration unless owner shall present satisfactory evidence of title. (Subsection 1 of Section 2.) Presentation to the county court clerk of either bill of sale or previous year's certificate of registration is deemed compliance with this provision of the Act.

A motor-number file is maintained for the protection of registrants, to assist in finding lost or stolen motor vehicles. 

Therefore such registrants should be careful to give the number on the motor, rather than the number on some other part of the vehicle, as often is done. 

Subsection (b) of Section 3 defines the term "freight vehicle" to mean "a vehicle used to transport tangible personal property." Therefore, wreckers and service cars. should be registered as freight motor vehicles. 

New number plates shall be made available for sale before March 1.

There will be no period of grace after changing point, which is fixed by law as April 1. 

Purchasers of new cars during month of March fully comply with the law by purchase of number plates covering the new registration period.

Phrase reading "may operate upon the public roads of the state under the following conditions only" refers to vehicles belonging to nonresident owners which have not been registered in this state. 

When ownership of an automobile agency changes, and is regularly transferred, dealers' number plates assigned to said automobile agency may be transferred as an asset. "Until such registration expires by law" (Section 7) is construed to mean either until the close of the registration year, or until the purpose for which the vehicle is used is changed. When, for instance, a passenger car is converted into a freight motor vehicle, the registered owner may return the license plates to the county court clerk and exchange them for tags designating the new classification of the vehicle. Credit is allowed for the returned plates. 

Under Section 7, license plates taken from a destroyed 918

Ch. 13) 919 

motor vehicle may be applied toward the purchase of tags for another vehicle by the registered owner of the "junked" vehicle, if: 

1. Plates are returned immediately to the county court clerk from whom they were obtained. 

2. Affidavit is made by its registered owner that the vehicle from which the tags were taken has been "wrecked, destroyed, or otherwise rendered unsuitable or unsafe for use and/or operation on the highways of the state." 

3. Vehicle, the registration of which is applied for, is in the same classification as the destroyed vehicle. 

It shall be the duty of the county court clerk of each county to enforce the provisions of the Motor Vehicle Law, and in so doing he shall: 

Account to the Department of Finance and Taxation for all number plates consigned to him. 

At the end of registration periods all unsold number plates must be returned to Department of Finance and Taxation.

If any county court clerk shall be delinquent as much as ten days in making report of unsold number plates and accounting therefor, he is guilty of a misdemeanor. 

(Signed) WALTER STOKES, JR., 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation.

Approved: (Signed) ROY H. BEELER, Attorney-General.

Law. Section 1 

Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of Tennessee, That for the purpose of this Act, the terms "motor vehicle" and "motor vehicles' shall be construed to mean any automobile, automobile truck, automobile trailer, automobile tractor, motorcycle, electric automobile truck or tractor, or any other vehicle of like character regardless of whether the same falls within the descriptions enumerated herein, propelled over the highways of the State by either steam, distillate, gasoline, electricity or other mechanical power for the purpose of transporting persons or property. "Motor vehicle" and "motor vehicles" includes automobiles, motor trucks, trailers, tractors, motorcycles, electric automobiles, trucks, tractors, and all other selfpropelled vehicles. Prior to the enactment of this Act 

Vehicles operated by electricity were not subject to the fee imposed. (See Memphis Street Railway Company V. 

Crenshaw, 165 Tennessee 536.)

(Ch. 13 

 Registration of Motor Vehicles- Law. Section 2 

 That as a condition precedent to the operation of any motor vehicle upon any highway, road, street or other public thoroughfare in Tennessee, the owner thereof shall first register such vehicle with the Department of Finance and Taxation in the manner hereinafter provided, and shall pay the registration fees hereinafter imposed. Registration shall be effected through the County Court Clerk in the county wherein the owner resides or maintains headquarters of citizenship in this State when such residence or headquarters is capable of indentification, and in such manner as the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may prescribe when no resident or headquarters in this State is readily ascertainable. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall adopt and promulgate rules and regulations adapted to the enforcement of this Section and succeeding sections relating to motor vehicle registration, which rules and regulations shall have the force and effect of law; they shall include the following provisions: 

(1) No registration of any motor vehicle shall be issued by the registering official unless the owner shall present satisfactory evidence of title. (2) No motor vehicle shall be subject to registration under the provisions of this law unless said vehicle is suitable and safe for use on the highways.

When used in this section or other sections relating to motor vehicle registration, the term "suitable and safe for use on the highways" means: (a) That the provisions of Sections 2693, 2694 and 2695 of the Code of Tennessee for 1932 have been complied with. (b) That the provisions of Chapter 35, Public Acts of 1933 have been complied with. (c) That the vehicle is equipped with brakes adequate to control the movement of, and to stop and hold such vehicle, including two separate means of applying the brakes to at least two wheels and so constructed that no part which is liable to failure shall be common to the two, except that a motorcycle need be equipped with only one brake. All such brakes shall be maintained in good working order. (3) The correct motor number or serial number shall be given in each instance before registration is effected. 

Owners of motor vehicles must register such vehicle and pay the fee imposed to the county court clerk of the county in which such owner resides or maintains headquarters. 

Registration with the county court clerk constitutes registration with the Department of Finance and Taxation, the clerk being the agent or representative of the Department, and such registration must be effected prior to the operation of the vehicle upon the highways of Tennessee. 

Non-resident owners desiring to operate motor vehicles in Tennessee must register such vehicle in accordance with rules and regulations prescribed by the Commissioner of 

Finance and Taxation.

Ch. 13) 923 

The Commissioner is authorized to promulgate rules and regulations for the enforcement of all sections of this Act relating to the registration of motor vehicles. Such rules and regulations have the force and effect of law and must include the following requirements: 

1. The vehicle owner must present satisfactory proof of ownership. 

2. The vehicle must be "safe and suitable for use on the highways." 

3. Correct motor or serial number must be given. 

The term "suitable and safe for use on the highways" is defined to mean that such vehicle is equipped with adequate brakes and that the provisions of sections 2693 to 2695 inclusive, Code of Tennessee and Chapter 35, Acts of 1933, have been been complied with. 

Sections 2693 to 2695, inclusive, provides that motor vehicles shall be equipped with: horn, muffler and adequate lights, while Chapter 35, Acts of 1933, relates to the operation of motor vehicles designed and used for hauling passengers and freight.

Classification of Vehicles and Imposition of Fees- Law. Section 3 

 That in order to facilitate efficient and uniform enforcement of this law, motor vehicles are hereby classified and the respective registration fees imposed are fixed as follows:

Class A. Motorcycles with two wheels. Registration fee $3.00 

Class B. Motorcycle with three wheels. 

Registration fee $5.00

Class C. Passenger motor vehicles weighing not exceeding 3,500 pounds. Registration fee $7.50. 

Class D. Passenger motor vehicles weighing over 3,500 pounds. 

Registration fee $10.00.

Class 1. Freight motor vehicles with declared maximum gross weight including vehicle and load of not more than 8,000 pounds. Registration fee $15.00.

Class 2. Freight motor vehicles with declared maximum gross weight including vehicle and load over 8,000 pounds and not exceeding 14,000 pounds. Registration fee $25.00.

Class 3. Freight motor vehicle with declared maximum gross weight including vehicle and load over 14,000 pounds and not exceeding 18,000 pounds. Registration fee $50.00.

Class 4. Freight motor vehicles with declared maximum gross weight including vehicle and load over 18,000 pounds and not exceeding 24,000 pounds. Registration fee $75.00.

Class 5. Freight motor vehicles with declared maximum gross weight including vehicle and load over 24,000 pounds. Registration fee $125.00. 

Class 6. Tractors used for purposes other than transporting freight. 

Registration fee $25.00. Provided, that such registration fee shall not apply to farm tractors used for agricultural purposes.

(Ch. 13  

The combined weight of tractors and trailer or tractors and semitrailers or motor truck with trailer or semi-trailer attached shall be used in determining declared maximum gross weight for purpose of classification. Provided, further, that an allowance of 10% over the declared maximum gross load of weight in each classification be granted the truck owner or operator.

The declared maximum gross weight, including motor vehicle and load, shall be painted with durable paint in letters and figures not less than four inches in height on right side of said vehicle within five feet of front wheel.

The official effecting registration shall receive as compensation therefore the sum of thirty-five (354) cents, and said amount shall be his full compensation, and in lieu of all other compensation for registration of motor vehicles. Provided, that fees on trucks used by the owner exclusively for farm purposes, and/or for the purpose of transporting farm and/or dairy products, produced by the owner of the trucks, shall be at the rate of fifty (50%) per cent of the fees above set out; provided further, that each owner of such truck claiming it to be used exclusively for farm purposes, or the transportation of farm or dairy products, shall make affidavit on the blanks to be furnished by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, that the truck for which application for registration is being made, is owned and used by the owner exclusively for farm purposes and/or for the purpose of transporting farm and/or dairy products produced or grown by him or her. And if such affidavit is not so made then the truck shall be charged at the full rate as above set out. And it shall be a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of Fifty ($50.00) Dollars and/or removal from office of the county court clerks or any of their deputies charged with the duty of registering trucks to charge such reduced rates unless said affidavit is first made; Provided, further, that any motor vehicle which serves the same purpose of a truck by an alteration in or modification of its original structure, shall be classed as a freight motor vehicle and shall be taxed as such notwithstanding that such vehicle was not originally manufactured as a truck.

It is hereby expressly stipulated that no registration fee shall be charged for any trailer or semi-trailer attached to or drawn by a passenger automobile, motorcycle, or other vehicle of like character (excluding trucks) belonging to and used by the owner in transporting farm and/or dairy products (not for hire) over any of the roads, highways or streets of this state from the place of production. 

Nothing in this section shall be construed as a grant of authority for the use on the public highways of the state of any motor vehicle which now is or may hereafter by law be prohibited from such use. 

When used in this section and subsequent sections relating to motor vehicles: (a) The word "freight" means all tangible personal property. (b) The term "freight vehicle" and the plural as well as the singular number means a vehicle used to transport tangible personal property. 

Failure of any person, firm, corporation, joint-stock company, syndicate or association to comply with the provisions of this section shall be deemed a violation thereof and any such person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association violating this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not less than two-fifty ($2.50) dollars nor more than fifty ($50.00) dollars for each offense, and all fines collected hereunder shall go to the State of Tennessee to be, when collected, transmitted to the Comptroller through the Department of Finance and Taxation. Provided, further, that no license fee shall be charged for any trailer or semi-trailer attached to or drawn by a passenger automobile, motorcycle, or other vehicle of like character

Ch. 13) 925

(excluding trucks) belonging to and used by the owner in transporting farm and/or dairy products (not for hire) over any of the roads, highways, or streets of this State from the place of production.

Discount, Allowance, Reduction 

Law. Section 5. 

Be it further enacted, That if registration as provided in the preceding sections is effected during the first three months of the calendar year,

Ch. 13) 929 

an allowance, discount or reduction shall be allowed equal to three-fifths of the stipulated registration fee for the annual registration. This section shall not apply to the purchase of tags during the first three calendar months of 1935. 

The registration year begins April 1st. and expires

March 31st. of each year, therefore vehicles registered during the months of January, February or March of each year may be registered for two-fifths of the annual registration fee. It should be noted that the first quarter of the calendar year is the last quarter of the registration or tax year.

A motor vehicle owner registering the vehicle in December of 1936 would be liable for the full registration fee, while an owner registering in January 1937 would be liable for only two-fifths of the annual fee. Non Residents—

Application for temporary registration shall be made to the County Court Clerk of the County of entry, or any designated office of the Department of Finance and Taxation.

Application shall declare mileage to be traveled and time necessary to complete trip.

Application shall be accompanied by temporary registration fee equal to one and one-half cents per mile of said declared mileage, together with compensation for the registering official in the sum of thirty-five (35¢) cents, which said sum shall be his full compensation and in lieu of all other compensation for registration of motor vehicles. 

Temporary registration certificate shall be retained by the person in charge of the vehicle while said vehicle is in this State. 

Failure of any person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association to comply with the provisions of this section shall be deemed a violation thereof and any such person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate or association violating this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not less than two-fifty ($2.50) Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00)

Dollars for each offense, and all fines collected hereunder shall go to the State of Tennessee, to be, when collected, transmitted to the Comptroller through the Department of Finance and Taxation.

The County Court Clerk collecting the registration fee from nonresident owners of motor vehicles operating over the highways of the State shall transmit the same to the Comptroller through the Department of

(Ch. 13 

Finance and Taxation in the manner provided by law for the transmission of other fees and the funds so collected shall be covered into the general highway fund for use in the construction and maintenance of the State highways. Said registration fees shall be in addition to all other fees, taxes or compensation imposed by law on non-resident operators of motor vehicles over the State highways. Likewise, fines collected under this section of this Act shall go to the general highway fund. 

Non-residents operating passenger motor vehicles upon the roads of Tennessee for a period in excess of thirty days are required to register such vehicles in Tennessee. 

Non-residents operating motor vehicles for the transporting of freight and passengers must effect temporary registration of such vehicles and pay the "mileage tax" imposed under Chapter 114, Acts of 1933 as amended, unless such non-resident resides in a State with which Tennessee has a reciprocal agreement. Such agreements are authorized by law.

Violation of this Section constitutes a misdemeanor subject to fine of $2.50 to $50.00 for each offense. 

Changes in Ownership 

Law. Section 7 

 That whenever the ownership of any such motor vehicle shall become changed by sale or otherwise, the registration number or license plates shall remain upon such vehicle as a part thereof until such registration expires by law; but the purchaser thereof shall be required to immediately notify the said Department of Finance and Taxation through the county court clerk of such transfer and receive a transfer certificate in his name, for which he shall pay a fee of One ($1.00) Dollar, and the Clerk shall indicate the change of ownership on his records. When motor vehicles are transferred, sold or given away, the dealer (or if the seller or donor is not a dealer, then the owner) as well as the new owner shall be responsible for the recording of such transfer, sale or gift in the office of the county court clerk in the county where such transfer, sale or gift is made.

In the event any registered motor vehicle is wrecked, destroyed or otherwise rendered unsuitable or unsafe for use and/or operation on the highways of the State, the owner and/or operator shall immediately remove therefrom the license plates theretofor purchased for such motor vehicle and return the same immediately to the county court clerk from whom they were purchased and it shall be the duty of the county court clerk to issue to the holder of said license plates a new set of plates charging a fee of 

One Dollar Fifty ($1.50) cents plus the clerk's registration fee for effecting registration, and to return said plates to the Department of Finance and Taxation. No license shall be purchased by anyone except from the Department of Finance and Taxation direct or from said Department through the county court clerk of the county where the owner of the motor vehicle sought to be registered resides; provided, however, that when a registered motor vehicle which is still suitable and safe for use and operation on the highways of the State is sold or transferred by the owner thereof the license plate already purchased by the original owner and attached to said

Ch. 13) 931 

motor vehicle may be sold or transferred by the original owner to the new owner as a part of the motor vehicle involved in the sale but both the seller and purchaser shall see to it that the provisions of Section 7 hereof are immediately complied with; and where any registered motor vehicle is wrecked, destroyed or otherwise rendered unsuitable or unsafe for use and/or operation on the highways of the State, the owner may obtain a new set of tags for another vehicle as provided for in this section. Failure to comply with any provision of this section shall be deemed a violation thereof and the person violating the same shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not less than Two-fifty ($2.50) 

Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00) Dollars for each offense. All fines collected hereunder shall go to the State of Tennessee, to be, when collected, transmitted to the Comptroller through the Department of Finance and Taxation.

In instances where the ownership of motor vehicles change during the registration year a transfer fee of $1.00 is imposed. The purchaser of such vehicle must immediately notify the county court clerk and apply for a transfer certificate. It is the duty of the seller as well as the purchaser to see that such transfer, by gift or sale, is recorded in the office of the county court clerk. 

Duplicate license plates may be secured upon the payment of $1.50 plus clerk's fee of 35¢ in instances where the vehicle is rendered useless by wreck or other causes; however, the original license plates are to be returned or proper affidavit made in case such plates are lost. 

Persons dealing in secondhand automobiles should be careful to see that the provisions of this section are complied with, since the violation of this section is a misdemeanor punishable by fine of $2.50 to $50.00 for each offence.

Free Plates- Law. 

Section 8 

 That upon the sworn statement from the head of any department of the State government or the county judge or the chairman of the county court of any county, or the mayor of any town or city or upon certification of authorized officials of the United States Government, that the motor vehicle for which application is made for registration, is owned by the state, the county, the city, the town or the United States Government and operated exclusively for essential governmental purposes, the State Department of Finance and Taxation, through the County Court Clerk, shall issue a license and number plate as above provided upon payment of fifteen cents to cover cost of manufacturing and packing each set of two plates; but the County Court Clerk shall have the right to collect the fee of thirty-five cents for registration, but in all such cases the application must be accompanied by a sworn statement as above provided, and the County Court Clerk shall not issue any number plate until special authority is obtained from the State Department of Finance and Taxation.

This section is deemed sufficiently clear and since it has no application to the general public, comment is considered unnecessary. 

Number Plate to Be Displayed- Law. Section 9 

 That the owner and/or operator of such motor vehicle is required to display, in a conspicuous manner at both front and rear of such motor vehicle, a number plate of suitable size, color, dimension, and character as the Department of Finance and Taxation may designate; provided, that the size of the number plate shall be the same each year and shall be designed to fit all classes of motor vehicles. The number plate shall show, in addition to the registration number of such machine, the year and the abbreviation of Tennessee; provided, further, that the Department of Finance and Taxation, through the County Court Clerk, shall furnish without additional cost to the owner of such machine a set of two number plates, and owners are required to use these number plates on their machines, and no other number plates shall be used. 

Upon the registration of the motor vehicle the owner is issued a pair of number plates which shall be designed by the Department of Finance and Taxation in such size as will fit all classes of vehicles. These plates are to be affixed to the front and rear of the vehicle and shall be displayed at all times. Number plates cannot be transferred from one vehicle to another and no other number plate is to be used.

Dealers and Manufacturers- Law. Section 10 

Be it further enacted, That all dealers in or manufacturers of motor vehicles shall instead of registering each such motor vehicle owned by him, make application to and receive from the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation through the County Court Clerk a general distinguishing number or mark.

This certificate and number shall be of a different color and number from that of any other owner of a motor vehicle, and shall be known as a dealer's number, and said number may be used by said dealer or manufacturer upon any new or second-hand motor vehicle the property of the dealer held for the purpose of trade or resale, but said number shall not be used on motor vehicles used for other than strictly business purposes. 

Said dealer or manufacturer shall register with and pay to the said Commissioner of Finance and Taxation through the County Court Clerk for such special dealers' number, the sum of Fifty ($50.00) Dollars.

This regis- tration shall be renewed annually as other registrations and the annual registration fee shall be Fifty ($50.00) Dollars and the owner shall register same with the County Court Clerk and pay a fee of thirty-five (354) cents. 

Duplicate dealers' number plates in series not to exceed twenty duplicate plates of any one number shall be issued by the County Court Clerk, upon payment, due to the State, of a license fee of One ($1.00) Dollar for each such additional pair of plates; provided, that when not over four duplicate plates are issued the fee for same shall be Thirty ($30.00) Dollars. In

the case of the dealer or manufacturer of motorcycles, said dealer or manufacturer shall register with and pay to said Commissioner of Finance and Taxation through the County Court Clerk for such special dealers' number the sum of Ten ($10.00) Dollars. Duplicate motorcycle dealers' number plates in series not to exceed three duplicate plates of any one number shall be issued by the County Court Clerk, upon payment, due to the State, of a license fee of Thirty-five (35¢) cents for each such additional pair of plates. The County Court Clerk shall receive no additional fee for the issuance of these duplicate dealers' number plates; provided, that anyone using any duplicate plates other than those herein authorized shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and on conviction thereof shall be fined not less than Two-Fifty ($2.50) Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00) Dollars.

Dealers in motor vehicles are not required to register vehicles owned for the purpose of sale, but must secure dealers' number plates for use on demonstrators. The fee is fixed at $50.00 and additional number plates may be secured in accordance with the terms of this section. This section applies to motorcycle dealers, secondhand automobile dealers and truck dealers.

Drive-out Cards or Tags-- Law. Section 11 

 That it shall be the duty of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation to provide for distribution to all dealers in motor propelled vehicles applying for the same, cards in pairs of suitable size and character to fit all classes of motor vehicles, bearing thereon in type large enough to be plainly seen the word "dealer” and a serial number, together with the words "This Tag Expires " and it shall be the duty of said Commissioner to keep or have kept a record of each pair of tags issued, showing a serial number, date issued and to whom issued; these tags shall be issued in pairs to dealers in such motor vehicles applying therefor, who shall pay for each pair of tags so issued One ($1.00) Dollar, except in the case of motorcycle dealers who shall pay for each pair of tags so issued thirty-five (354) cents.

Motor vehicle owners are required to register such vehicle in the county in which they reside, therefore, if a resident of Davidson County purchases an automobile from a dealer in Cheatham County, such dealer must issue to the purchaser a drive-out tag. This tag entitles the owner to drive the vehicle for a period not to exceed 48 hours and is to be designed and furnished by the Commissioner and issued by the dealer. The cost of such registration is $1.00 and must be remitted to the Commissioner by the dealer issuing the same.

(Ch. 13  Drive-out Cards for Each Vehicle Sold- Law. Section 12. 

 That every dealer in motor vehicles propelled by other than muscular power shall issue to the purchaser of each vehicle a pair of such tags, and it shall be the duty of each purchaser to affix or have affixed one of said tags on the front, one on the rear of such motor vehicles in such manner as to be plainly seen before driving such motor vehicles on any highway of the State. The dealer selling such motor vehicles shall plainly write in ink on the blank left on each tag for the purpose, the day and hour such tag expires, and shall keep a record of each pair of tags issued, and to whom issued; the kind, name of manufacturers and factory, motor or manufacturers' number of such motor vehicle; date and hour when issued, by whom issued, and when said tag was marked to expire. In no case shall the dealer mark such tag to expire more than forty-eight hours after issuance; and such tag shall be good only for the time marked thereon, but in no event more than forty-eight hours. 

While this section appears to require the issuance of Drive-out Cards for each vehicle sold, it would also appear that the issuance of such a card would be unnecessary in instances where the vehicle has the regular registration number plates attached before such vehicle is operated upon the highways of the State. It appears that the 

Legislature intended such drive-out tags for use in cases where the purchaser resided out of the State or in another county.

Operation without Registration-Misdemeanor- Law. Section 13 

Be it further enacted, That it shall be unlawful for any person who has not obtained the license, required by law for vehicles to operate any motor vehicles propelled by other than muscular power on any highway of the State, without having affixed on front and rear of such vehicles the tags required by the preceding section hereof. Any violation of this Section shall be a misdemeanor, and the person violating it shall be fined not less than Two-fifty ($2.50) Dollars nor more than Fifty ($50.00) Dollars.

It is unlawful for any person to operate a motor vehicle upon the highways of Tennessee without having either the drive-out card or the regular license or number plate affixed to the front and rear of such vehicle. Violation of this section is a misdemeanor and upon conviction the offender may be fined $2.50 to $50.00.

Expiration of Drive-out Tag- Law. Section 14 

Be it further enacted, That no dealer or his agent shall issue any tag described in Sections 11 et seq hereof, except for a motor vehicle actually delivered to a purchaser or his agent or servant; nor shall he mark the

Ch. 13) 935 

time of expiration of such tag beyond forty-eight hours after the time of actual delivery of such vehicles; nor shall there be issued more than one pair of tags for each vehicle; nor shall he fail to keep an actual record of tags as hereinabove provided for; nor shall he use any such tags on any motor vehicle not actually delivered to purchaser or purchaser's agent; nor on any motor vehicle for which state and city licenses and number shall have been issued. Any violation of this section shall be a misdemeanor and any person convicted shall be fined not less than two-fifty ($2.50) dollars nor more than fifty ($50.00) dollars. 

The tag cannot be issued for a motor vehicle which was not delivered by the dealer issuing such drive-out card or tag and such tag cannot be issued for a period of time in excess of forty-eight hours. Attention is drawn to the fact that dealers are required to keep accurate records of tags issued and that the violation of this section is a misdemeanor punishable by fine of $2.50 to $50.00. 

Refunds-Registration Year- Law. Section 15 

 That each owner of a motor vehicle, who has not effected registration of his or her motor vehicle for the year 1935 and who desires to operate the same over the highways of the State during the calendar year 1935, and for the first three months of the year 1936, shall pay for said privilege the rate set forth in this bill for the calendar year 1935, and shall operate such registered motor vehicles until April 1, 1936; provided, further, that each person, firm or corporation that has effected registration of motor vehicles under the law prior to the passage of this Act, shall operate such vehicles over the highways of the State for the year 1935 and to April 1, 1936 without paying any additional registration fees; provided further, that any owner of any motor vehicle, automobile, motocycle (motorcycle*) truck or other motor vehicle of like character who has paid the license fees under the law existing prior to the passage of this Act for operating any such motor vehicle on the public roads, streets, or highways of this state for the year 1935 under the law existing prior to the passage of this Act, shall be and is hereby declared to be entitled to have any excess, so paid by any person, firm or corporation, above the amounts fixed under the provisions of this Act, refunded to the person, firm, or corporation paying same by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation acting for the Department of Finance and Taxation for the State of Tennessee upon the person, firm or corporation making application for such refund within the time and in such manner and under such rules and regulations as may be promulgated by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation who is hereby authorized to make such reasonable rules and regulations governing such application for refund of the said Commissioner may seem proper; and the Treasurer of the State of Tennessee is hereby directed upon warrant of the Comptroller drawn upon the approval of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, to repay such applicant, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation being authorized to demand such evidence of such payment as to him may seem sufficient of the payment of such license fee to the County Court Clerk issuing same for the year 1935 and prior to the passage of this Act. 

After the passage of this Act, registration shall be made under the provisions of this Act and the annual registration of motor vehicles shall be had on the first day of April 1936 and annually thereafter. Such

(Ch. 13  

registration shall entitle the owner of the motor vehicle so registered to operate the same over the highways of the State for a period of twelve months from and after the first day of April in which the registration takes place. Applications for registration shall be made to the Department of 

Finance and Taxation through the County Court Clerk, with the applicant giving the same information and paying the same fees required under this Act; and upon the payment of such fees, the applicant shall receive from the Department of Finance and Taxation through the County Court Clerk a certificate showing such registration and he shall also receive from the same source a set consisting of two number plates on which shall appear the year and the abbreviation of the word "Tennessee'' in addition to the registration number.

This section of the Act authorizes the refund of the difference between the fees imposed under the prior Act and those imposed under this Act. Refunds have been made and the portion of this section relating to refunds is no longer operative.

The tax or registration year is from April 1, 1936 to March 31, 1937 and annually thereafter. Upon payment of the fees required the owner is permitted to operate the vehicle on the highways of the state and shall receive certificate of registration and two number plates. 

Duties of County Court Clerk- 

Law. Section 16 

 That it shall be the duty of the County Court Clerk of each county to enforce the provisions of this Statute and in so doing he shall: (a) Ascertain the names of the owners of all wheeled vehicles above described and included, in his county, and issue distress warrants against the owner operating any such motor vehicle in violation of the provisions of this law, after April 1, of the year for which the tax in question may be due. In case of the issuance of such distress warrant such clerk shall be entitled to collect the fees now provided by law for the issuance of distress warrants. (b) Take registration applications from the owner of any vehicle designated in this law. (c) Collect the fees provided for in this law. (d) Distribute the number plates provided by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and keep a complete record in his office, for the benefit of the general public, of all such motor vehicles registered in his county. (e) Remit and report on the first day of each month to the Department of Finance and Taxation, all monies at that time on hand collected by him under the provisions of this law, and report to the Department of Finance and Taxation the list of registrations made in his office for the preceding month. (f) Account to the Department of Finance and Taxation for all number plates so consigned to him. (g) Collect from the owner making application for the registration of a motor vehicle required to be registered under the provisions of this law a fee of thirty-five (354) cents, which shall be his compensation in full.

Ch. 13) 937 

If any county court clerk shall be delinquent as much as ten days in making the report hereinabove required to be made, he shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be fined not less than two-fifty ($2.50) dollars nor more than fifty ($50.00) dollars.

The duties imposed upon county court clerks are mandatory and are very explicit and clear; further comment in this regard is unnecessary. 

Department to Remit to State Treasurer- 

Law. Section 17 

 That the Department of Finance and Taxation on or before the tenth day of the succeeding month shall report and remit to the State Treasury all monies so received during a given month by the Department from county court clerks or from any and all other sources, under this law, without any deduction on account of salaries, fees, costs, expenses or claims of any description whatsoever. 

While this section requires the Department of Finance and Taxation to remit all monies received to the State Treasury on or before the tenth day of each month, the revenue derived from the registration of motor vehicles is deposited daily to the credit of the State Treasury in State depositories. No deductions of any character are made by the Commissioner.

Explanations and discussion Page 941 944 961 964

HISTORY OF MILEAGE TAX 

Prior to the Legislative Session of 1933 there had been discussion of the question of regulating and imposition of taxes upon buses and trucks transporting freight and passengers upon the highways of Tennessee. The regulation of trucks appears to have become a serious question by 1933, and in Governor McAlister's message to the 68th 

General Assembly under date February 28, 1933 he states: 

66 The regulation by the State of the size and weight of trucks operating on our highways has become a question of grave importance to the State. It is all the more so at the present time because of the enforced reductions that are now being made in the moneys necessary to their adequate maintenance and upkeep. The question has been before several sessions of the General Assembly, and the time has come, in my opinion when we should definitely make known our policy with reference thereto. Heretofore the controversy has assumed the aspect of a dispute between the railroads operating in Tennessee and the companies operating these buses. It is a fact that these railroads have for many years been paying large sums in taxes to the various counties and cities in Tennessee, and that the loss of such sums from such local budgets does present serious problems as to how such deficiencies can be made up. However, I think the consideration that immediately concerns us is the serious damage that is being done to our highways by the unrestrained use of them by these trucks, whose length, height and weight has become entirely out of reason, when we bear in mind the purposes for which we originally began the construction of our highway system. 

In his annual message to the sixty-fifth General Assembly on January 6, 1927, Governor Peay, in referring to this question observed: "The fact of the matter is that it was never in mind, nor intended, to build a road system for such commercial uses and profit. 

The State bears the whole expense of building the highways thus being used."

Since that time the size and weights of these common carriers have vastly increased, and they are not paying for their rights to operate on these roads in just proportion to what it costs to repair the damage done by them. Most of our system was designed by our engineers for private passenger vehicles and other vehicles commensurate therewith, and the tremendously large and heavy modern truck should be required to pay for the use of these roads a sum that should be, in part, at least, sufficient to repair the damage that their movement over them necessarily does. The present use amounts to an appropriation of the capital outlay made by the State for their construction, and which in time must be compensated for by additional capital outlay furnished by the taxpayers in general. This, of course, amounts to a subsidy to this method of transportation. It is for these reasons that I recommend that legislation be passed at this session which will impose definite limits upon the length, breadth, height and the weight of these trucks, as well as limitations upon their right to operate as trains on the highways. I think these limitations should be so placed as not to include trucks that 941

(Ch. 14 

are in common use by farmers or any other person in the reasonable conduct of their own business. Such use, in my opinion, can fairly be said to have been in contemplation of the builders of our road system when it was originally commenced. Likewise, a special provision could be made that would authorize emergency use of even heavier vehicles under certain conditions. I do not intend to advocate, of course, restrictions upon the use of the highways by these heavy common carriers that will, in effect, entirely prohibit their use of the roads of the State, for I think that many of them are performing a very useful and necessary part in moving the products of farm and factory to their markets, but only that a fair regulation of them is demanded in the public interest and to protect a capital investment of more than $175,000,000, which the State has made in their construction during a period of ten years and less. As I have observed before, many States are grappling with this problem, realizing the pressing necessity for action. I, therefore, recommend that you give your assent to bills that will be introduced dealing with this very important question. 

Pursuant to the Governor's recommendation the Legislature enacted Chapter 114, which imposes the first "mileage tax" upon operators of motor vehicles used in the transportation of freight over the highways of Ten- nessee.

The Legislature of 1935 made no changes in this law and the Governor does not specifically refer to "mileage taxation" in his message to the. General Assembly. 

Governor Browning in his message to the 70th General Assembly makes the following proposal as regards mileage tax: "" I also propose to transfer mileage tax fees from the highway fund to the general fund. The highway fund, of course, needs and could use the money, but the need of the general fund is much the greater. If the gasoline tax increase persists as is now the prospect no federal aid will be lost because of this transfer. . . ." 

The Legislature of 1937 enacted Chapter 168 amending the original law; however, the Governor's recommendation regarding the transfer of the funds was not included; therefore, the original act of 1933 (Chapter 114) as amended in 1937 represents the complete history of this form of taxation of trucks transporting freight for compensation over the public highways in Tennessee.
