Chapter 114, Acts of 1933, as amended by 

Chapter 168, Acts of 1937. 

Title of the Act. 

AN ACT to require the owner and/or operator of every motor vehicle using the highways of the state for the transportation of property to pay the State reasonable compensation for the use of its highways to be expended by the State for construction, maintenance, repair and upkeep of said highways and for the cost or expense of administering the laws governing the use of such highways, including the cost or expense of administering this Act. To fix the amount of such reasonable compensation, the time and method of payment thereof; to provide means for the enforcement of this Act; to provide penalties for its violation; and to make certain exemptions from its provisions.

(Ch. 14  Section 1: 

Definitions- 

Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of Tennessee, That for the purpose of this Act, (1) the words "owner" and "operator" as used in this Act shall be held and taken to mean any person, firm, association or corporation owning and/or operating one or more motor vehicles transporting any character of property or freight along or over any public highway or highways of the State, and (2) the words "motor carrier" or "motor carriers" shall be held and taken to mean any owner and or operator of motor vehicles as defined herein using the highways of the State for the transportation of property or freight, and (3) the words "motor vehicle" shall be held and taken to mean not only a vehicle propelled by its own power but also any truck, trailer or semi-trailer attached thereto, the intent of this Act being that there shall be paid to the State the same amount for each and every tractor, truck, trailer (when lawfully operated) or semi-trailer drawing or carrying property or freight as for any motor vehicle of like capacity propelled by its own power, and (4) the term "public highway" or "highways" when used in this Act shall mean any public road, highway or thoroughfare of any kind used by the public.

Section 2: 

Certain Carriers Exempt- 

 That this Act shall not apply to a motor carrier or motor carriers operating wholly within the limits of any incorporated town or city of the State, and or within a radius of five (5) miles beyond the corporate limits of such town or city; nor to such carrier or carriers operating wholly within the limits of any incorporated town or city of the State having a population in excess of One 

Hundred Thousand (100,000) persons according to the last

Federal Census or any subsequent Census and/or within a radius of Twelve (12) miles beyond the corporate limits of such town or city; nor to the transportation of live stock, poultry, farm, forest and/or dairy products to market by

Ch. 14) 947 

MILEAGE TAX 

the owner thereof, or supplies for his own use in his own motor vehicle; nor to any motor vehicle operated by a nonprofit cooperative association carrying only property belonging to the association or its members; nor to any motor vehicle operated by the government of the United States, the State of Tennessee or any county or municipality of the State.

Neither shall this Act apply to the owner or operator of a motor vehicle or motor vehicles used exclusively in transporting poultry, dairy, farm or forest products from the farm, dairy or forest; or to or from receiving or assembling points for milk, poultry, farm or forest products to warehouse, creamery or other original storage place or market; provided, however, if this section of this Act or any portion thereof making the exemptions herein enumerated shall for any reason be held invalid, such holding shall not affect other portions of the Act, it being the legislative intent that this Act would have been passed notwithstanding the inclusion of Section 2 therein making said exemptions, and that the Act shall stand should this section of the Act be eliminated. 

Nor shall this Act apply to any owner or operator of any motor vehicle used either by said owner or operator or by his employee, in transporting his own property, of which he is the sole owner, over the highways of the State; provided that the compensation for use of the highways imposed by this Act shall apply to the operation of motor vehicles by the owner and/or operator thereof of the capacity described in Section 3 hereof, and when used in the character of transportation set forth in Section 3 hereof; provided, further, that if this paragraph of this Act or any portion thereof shall for any reason be held invalid or unconstitutional, such adjudication of invalidity or unconstitutionality shall not affect any other portion of the Act, it being the legislative intent that this Act would have been passed without this paragraph if such declaration of invalidity or unconstitutionality be made. 

Nor shall this Act apply to commission agents whose trucks transport petroleum products belonging to the owner whom the commission agents represent, and where the said com-

(Ch. 14  

mission agents receive a commission for their entire service and receive no separate compensation for transportation, provided such commission agent shall not represent, at any one time, more than one person, company, or corporation engaged in the sale of or distribution of petroleum products.

Section 3: 

Intra-County Transportation of Own Property- 

 That every owner and/or operator of any motor vehicle of three (3) tons or over carrying capacity (being the capacity on which a license plate is purchased) when such motor vehicle is used by such owner and/or operator, or by his employee, in transporting his own property or merchandise over the highways of the state, from one place to another, on fixed routes, or from a central warehouse to distribution depots or stores, either inside or outside the state, shall obtain a license, make reports and pay compensation for the use of the highways in accordance with the rates established by and under the provisions of this Act; provided, however, that this section shall not apply to any motor vehicle operating exclusively in any one county. 

Section 4: 

Tax in Lieu of those Levied in General Revenue Bill of 1931 Be it further enacted, That the compensation levied against motor carriers of freight or property by this Act for the use of the highways of the state shall be in lieu of that levied against such owners and/or operators by Item 108 of the General Revenue Bill of 1931, being Chapter 13, Public Acts of 1931, Second Extra Session; but the compensation levied against the owners and/or operators of motor vehicles carrying passengers for hire by Item 108, Chapter 13, Public Acts of 1931, Second Extra Session, is not affected by this Act nor in any wise superseded or abrogated by the terms hereof.

Ch. 14) 949 

MILEAGE TAX Section 5: 

Compensation For Use of Highways— 

 That each and every motor carrier of freight or property as defined in Sections 1 and 3 of this Act (except as exempted in Section 2 hereof), in addition to the regular license fees or taxes imposed upon such motor carrier under the laws of this State, shall pay to the State of Tennessee for the use of its highways reasonable compensation to be expended by the State solely for the construction, maintenance, repair and upkeep of said highways and for the cost or expense of administering the laws governing the use of such highways, including the cost or expense of administering this Act. Such reasonable compensation which any such motor carrier shall so pay shall be ascertained, fixed and determined as hereinafter provided.

Section 6: 

Rates of Tax or Compensation- 

Be it further enacted, That each motor carrier of property or freight as defined in Sections 1 and 3 hereof, (except as otherwise provided in Section 2 hereof), shall pay to the State of Tennessee for each motor vehicle used for transporting property or freight over the highways of the state, whether loaded or empty, for each mile of such highways traversed by such vehicle the following amount: (1) On each motor vehicle of one ton and not more than three tons capacity, one-half (2) cent per mile traveled. (2) On each motor vehicle of over three (3) tons capacity one (1) cent per mile traveled.

As to any unit composed of a tractor with a semi-trailer attached, the compensation which shall be paid shall be determined by the capacity of the semi-trailer only, based on the standard factory rating thereof. 

As to trucks with trailers lawfully attached, the compensation which shall be paid shall be on each separate unit and shall be determined by the capacity of each separate unit based upon the standard factory rating for each sepa-

(Ch. 14  

rate unit, and not upon the combined capacity of the two units considered as one. 

If any truck, trailer or semi-trailer has no standard factory rating by which its capacity can be determined, then and in that event, for the purpose of determining the compensation to be paid for its operations it shall be treated as having the same factory rating as a truck, trailer or semitrailer of like dimensions or carrying capacity which has a factory rating.

In determining the capacity of each motor vehicle whose owner or operator is required to pay the above compensation, the standard factory rating of such motor vehicle shall control.

Section 7: 

Carriers Must Comply with Other Laws- 

 That this Act shall not authorize the operation of any motor vehicle over the highways of the State in violation of the provisions of Chapter 58, Public Acts of 1929, requiring a certificate of convenience and necessity from the Railroad and Public Utilities Commission of the state authorizing such operation, or in violation of any other Act now in effect, or which may hereafter be enacted undertaking to regulate the operation of motor vehicles over the highways of the state, or fixing the weight, height, length, or other dimensions or kind or character of such vehicles. 

Section 8: 

License Must be Secured for each Vehicle Be it further enacted, That each motor carrier desiring to operate any motor vehicle over the highways of the state, and subject to the terms of this Act, shall apply to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation of the State of Tennessee at Nashville, for a license or licenses authorizing such motor carrier to operate motor vehicles over the highways of the state, a license for each motor vehicle being required. 

The license card for each motor vehicle shall be in such form as shall be prescribed by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and shall be signed by him; and for

Ch. 14) 

951 

MILEAGE TAX 

each license issued under the provisions of this Act, a fee of One ($1.00) Dollar shall be paid to the Commissioner of 

Finance and Taxation, which shall become a part of the highway fund provided by this Act. 

If for any reason the license card issued to any motor carrier shall be destroyed or lost, the operator may obtain a duplicate license card from the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, and for each such duplicate card so issued a fee of Fifty (50¢) cents shall be paid.

Such license, once the same has been issued, shall remain in effect and valid so long as the holder complies with all laws of the State of Tennessee relating to and regulating motor carriers operating over the highways of the state, but said license shall not be transferable to a new holder or to a different motor vehicle than the one for which it was issued.

The application for a license shall be signed and sworn to by the applicant and shall be in such form as the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall prescribe and shall show, among other things, the following: a. The make, kind, size, weight, carrying capacity, motor number and registration number of each motor vehicle as herein defined, to be used by the motor carrier on the public highways of the state. b. Insofar as possible, the route or routes over which each motor vehicle will be operated with the number of trips each vehicle will make each day. c. The estimated mileage that each vehicle will travel during each calendar month following the issuance of the license. d. If the carrier is the holder of a certificate of convenience and necessity issued by the Railroad and Public Utilities Commission of the State, the date of the certificate, its number and the routes covered by it. e. If the carrier is not such certificate holder, then the character of hauling that is to be done and over what routes insofar as the same may be shown. f. Any other information deemed by the Commissioner of Finance and 

Taxation necessary to a proper and efficient enforcement of this Act. 

The application for license shall be signed and sworn to by the operator before the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation who is authorized to administer oaths for this purpose, or before a notary public, and the application shall be kept on file by said Commissioner as a part of the permanent records of his office. When the applicant has complied with the provisions of this Act, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall issue the license and furnish the operator a license card in such form as the commis-

(Ch. 14  

sioner may prescribe which shall be signed by him, and said card when so furnished shall be attached to the motor vehicle in some conspicuous place so as to be open to inspection by the proper officials of the State of Tennessee and officers charged with the duty of enforcing the laws, and by such officers of the various counties and municipalities thereof at all times. 

Said license card shall show the make, kind, size, carrying capacity, motor number and license number of the vehicle which is covered by it and it shall be a misdemeanor for any motor carrier to operate any motor vehicle without such license, or with the license attached to a motor vehicle not covered by it, and the operator so offending shall, upon conviction, be fined not less than Twenty-five ($25.00) Dollars nor more than Five Hundred ($500.00) Dollars for each such offense; and each day's operation either without the license displayed in the motor vehicle or with one displayed that is not issued to cover that particular motor vehicle shall constitute a separate offense, and the venue shall be in any county in which any part of the illegal operation takes place.

Section 9: 

Certain Information to Be Painted on Each Vehicle- 

 That each motor vehicle operated. by a motor carrier required to pay the compensation provided for by this Act shall have painted or stenciled on the sides thereof in letters clearly visible, the names of the motor carrier, the location of his place of business and the capacity of the vehicle by which the compensation is measured; and it shall be a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of 

Ten ($10.00) to Fifty ($50.00) Dollars for each day's operation of a vehicle in violation of this section of this Act. 

Section 10: 

Non-Resident Carriers- 

Be it further enacted, That if any motor carrier shall be a non-resident of the state he shall, prior to operating on the highways of this state any motor vehicle subject to this Act, appoint, and so long as he operates a motor ve-

Ch. 14) 953 

MILEAGE TAX 

hicle in this state, maintain an agent upon whom process may be served, the name and residence of such agent to be filed in the office of the Secretary of State and also with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. The operation of such motor vehicle without the appointment of such agent for the service of process shall be and constitute a misdemeanor for each day's operation without the appointment of such agent. It is provided, however, that the agent appointed pursuant to this section shall not be liable to or amenable to service of process except in suits which may arise under this Act, and the appointment of such agent shall state that it is done pursuant to this Act. 

Section 11: 

Interstate Commerce  That this Act and every part thereof shall apply and be construed to apply to interstate commerce, except insofar as the same may be in conflict with the provisions of the Constitution of the United States or the lawful Act of Congress. 

Section 12: 

Commissioner to Prescribe Records— 

Be it further enacted, That in order to ascertain the mileage traveled by motor vehicles subject to this Act, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall prescribe the records to be kept by each operator of such vehicle, and on or before the twentieth (20th) day of each month each operator of a motor vehicle shall file with said Commissioner, in duplicate, a statement verified under oath by the operator or by a person having knowledge of the facts and duly designated therefor by the operator, showing the mileage traveled by each motor vehicle subject to this Act during the preceding calendar month and shall at the time of filing such report, pay to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation the tax revealed to be due by it. 

Section 13: 

Commissioner to Prescribe Appliances to be Used- Be it further enacted, That the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is empowered to prescribe and require

(Ch. 14  

the character of appliances which each operator of a motor vehicle subject to this Act shall use in order to establish the correct mileage traveled by such vehicle and to adopt rules and regulations with respect to the care and inspection of such appliances and reports of the mileage shown by said appliances.

Section 14: 

Inspection of Books and Records- 

 That the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may in his discretion require any operator of a motor vehicle subject to this Act operating such vehicle within this state to keep within this state subject to inspection at all times by said Commissioner or his agent such books of accounts or records as may be reasonably necessary to enable said Commissioner to obtain full information at all times regarding the amounts due from such operator under the provisions of this Act. Such records shall at all times be open to inspection by the Commissioner or by any agent appointed by him for such purposes. 

Section 15: 

Uniform Rules and Regulations- 

Be it further enacted, That every operator of a motor vehicle subject to this Act shall register with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation in accordance with his requirements and shall comply with the rules and regulations adopted by the Commissioner for the purpose of ascertaining the mileage traveled upon the highways of this state by each such motor vehicle. The said Commissioner shall have authority to promulgate uniform rules and regulations as to the time and manner of registration and as to the method of ascertaining the mileage traveled and the compensation due the state on account thereof; and it shall be unlawful and constitute a misdemeanor for any operator of a motor vehicle subject to this Act to operate the same on a public highway without registration and license as herein provided, punishable as aforesaid.

Ch. 14) 955 

MILEAGE TAX Section 16: 

Administration- 

 That the rights and duties given to and devolve upon the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation under the provisions of this Act shall, in the event of a change hereafter devolve upon the office or department of the state which shall succeed to and perform the duties now performed by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. 

Section 17: 

Injunction- Be it further enacted, That any operator of a motor vehicle subject to this Act, may at the instance of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation or of any person having interest in the subject matter be enjoined by the courts of this state from any violation of the provisions of this Act, or of any order, rule, regulation or requirement of said Commissioner; provided, however, that such injunction or proceedings shall in no respect affect the liability of such operator to conviction for misdemeanor as herein provided. 

Section 18: 

Audit and Investigation of Monthly Reports— Be it further enacted, That after the filing of the monthly report by the motor carrier as provided herein, it shall be the duty of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation to audit said report to make such further investigation, if any, as may be necessary to ascertain all the facts for the purpose of determining whether said report is correct and whether the full amount due the state has been paid. If, in the opinion of said Commissioner, a further sum is due from said operator, such operator shall be notified in writing, by registered mail or personal service, accordingly, and such operator shall pay said additional amount within ten days thereafter. The operator shall have the right to pay such additional amount under protest and to sue for and recover all or a portion thereof upon proper showing that the same was not properly due, but

(Ch. 14  

such suit must be brought within thirty (30) days after such payment.

No operator shall operate any motor vehicle subject to this Act on the public highways of the state after the amount as provided for shall become due and payable to the State, until the same has been paid in full and the operation by such operator of each motor vehicle each day after default in such payment shall constitute a separate misdemeanor punishable as such. 

Section 19: 

Carriers Delinquent in Tax Payment-Injunction- 

 That if any such operator subject to the provisions of this Act shall fail for thirty (30) days to make the report required by this Act or to pay the amount due to the state under this Act, then it shall be the duty of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation at once to notify the Attorney General of the State, whereupon the said Attorney General shall have the power and it is hereby made his duty to take appropriate steps to collect said amount, and to enjoin said operator from using the highways of the state until all the amounts past due hereunder, together with interest at the rate of six (6%) per cent per annum and all costs shall have been paid, provided, however, that such injunction proceedings shall in no respect affect the liability of such operator to conviction for misdemeanor as herein provided. 

Section 20: 

Failure of Carrier to Report-Assessment by Com missioner Be it further enacted, That in order to insure the prompt collection of said compensation in the event the same becomes delinquent, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is authorized from the best information available to ascertain the amount thereof due from any motor carrier and he is authorized to issue a distress warrant against any delinquent motor carrier for the collection of said compensation, which shall be levied as any other distress warrant is authorized to be levied under the law

Ch. 14) 957 

MILEAGE TAX 

and said compensation so due from any motor carrier that shall constitute a first lien on the motor vehicle or motor vehicles or other property belonging to the motor carrier, and said lien shall be prior to any liens on any such motor vehicle, including mortgages, trust deeds, bills of sale or titles retained by the seller of such vehicle, when the instruments evidencing such liens are executed after the effective date of this Act. When any motor vehicle is offered for sale under such distress warrant, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation or his agent is authorized to bid the amount of the compensation due the state plus accrued costs for the motor vehicle upon which the distress warrant is levied, and if the same is sold to him he may sell the same to such purchaser as he may find and pay the proceeds over under this Act. 

Section 21: 

Police Powers-Expense of Administration- 

 That for the enforcement of this Act, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is authorized and directed to take such steps as he considers necessary, to promulgate proper rules, and to employ necessary assistants to effectively collect said compensation and to enforce the provisions of this Act, payment of the costs of administering the Act to be made out of the funds collected under said Act. Each assistant so employed by the Commissioner shall have full police power for the enforcement of this Act and any other Acts pertaining to the use of the highways of the State and may arrest any motor carrier or the operator of any motor vehicle for violation of the terms of this Act. 

Section 22: 

Highway Fund Revenue- 

Be it further enacted, That the object of this Act is to require each motor carrier subject to the provisions of the Act and using the highways of the state to pay to the State of Tennessee reasonable compensation for the use of the highways; and the amounts required to be so paid by this 

Act shall be paid into the State Treasury to the credit of

(Ch. 14  

the general highway fund for use in the construction, maintenance, repair and upkeep of the state highways, after deducting the expense of administration and enforcement of this Act. 

Section 23: 

False Reports-Misdemeanor- 

 That the making of a knowingly false report or the wilful failure to file a report when due under the terms and provisions of this Act by any motor carrier shall constitute a misdemeanor and be punishable by law as in cases of misdemeanors. Likewise, all offenses made misdemeanors by this Act shall be punishable as provided by law in cases of misdemeanor except those herein declared punishable by specific punishments in various sections of this Act. 

Section 24: 

Duties of Highway Patrol, Judges and Toll Collec tors- Be it further enacted, That it shall be the duty of the members of the Tennessee Highway Patrol to see to it that this Act is enforced and that the amounts due the state are paid, and to that end, they shall have the right at any time to examine and inspect any motor vehicle, the license therein, and to question the operator thereof for the purpose of determining whether or not such operation is unlawful and if any is found to be unlawful they shall have the right to take such steps as may be found necessary to collect said tax and may make arrest of the operator of the vehicle for violation of this Act. 

It shall be the duty of the Judges of the Criminal and Circuit Courts of the state to give this Act in charge to the grand juries of the state; and to the end that this Act may be enforced, said grand juries are hereby clothed with inquisitorial power to inquire into and ascertain whether or not there has been violation of the provisions of this Act and to return indictments in proper cases. 

It shall be the duty of the various toll collectors on the different toll bridges of the state to inspect various motor

Ch. 14) 959 

MILEAGE TAX 

vehicles operating across said toll bridges for the purpose of ascertaining whether the operators thereof have complied with the provisions of this Act in regard to a license, payment of tax, etc.; and if any toll collector finds that this 

Act is being violated by any operator, he shall immediately report such fact to any member of the Tennessee Highway Patrol available and within reach, giving detailed information as to violation of the Act. 

Section 25: 

Gates or Barriers-  That if the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall find it necessary to properly enforce this Act, he shall have authority to establish gates or barriers on the main highways of the State for the purpose of intercepting persons violating the provisions of this Act and requiring compliance herewith. 

Section 26: 

Non-Resident Carriers: Police PowerAffecting- 

Be it further enacted, That in case a motor carrier comes into the state from points outside the state without first having obtained a license as required by this Act, such motor carrier may be stopped by any member of the Tennessee Highway Patrol or any lawful police or peace officer in the State or by any person named by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation to aid in the enforcements of this Act and may be questioned as to his destination and the route by which he proposes to reach his destination, whereupon the mileage may be ascertained and the compensation due on account of such operation paid by such motor carrier for that particular trip but the person to whom such compensation is paid shall immediately report the fact to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and transmit to the Commissioner the amount of the payment and such motor carrier shall, prior to any subsequent operation into or through the state, obtain a license as required by this Act.

(Ch. 14  Section 27: 

Provisions of the Act Severable— 

 That if any clause, sentence, section or part of this Act shall be declared unconstitutional or invalid for any reason, such declaration or holding shall not affect any other section or portion of this Act, it being a legislative intent that this Act would have been passed had such unconstitutional or invalid provisions not been included in this Act. 

Section 28: 

Effective Date of Act- 

Be it further enacted, That all laws and parts of laws in conflict with the provisions of this Act, be, and they are, hereby repealed, and this Act shall take effect thirty (30) days from and after its passage, the public welfare requiring it.

RULES AND REGULATIONS MILEAGE TAX Chapter 114, Public Acts of 1933 

In addition to monthly report provided for by Section 12, every truck owner and/or operator is required to make a report of each trip made in Tennessee by each truck, trailer, and/or semitrailer registered under Mileage Tax Law and/or on any vehicle above mentioned which is subject to registration under said law, on forms prescribed and furnished by the Department of Finance and Taxation. 

This trip report shall contain the following information: (a) Point of origin. 

(b) Date. 

(c) Destination. 

(d) Route to be traveled and number of miles. (e) Date vehicle is expected to return. 

If the vehicle makes the return trip on the same day only one report for the round trip is required, provided route for both ways is stated. Otherwise, a report of each way is required.

Daily trip reports shall be made in quadruplicate and must be readable. The original shall be mailed, or otherwise delivered, to the Mileage Tax Unit, Department of Finance and Taxation, Nashville, Tennessee; one copy shall be filed in the office of the operator; and the other two copies shall be held by the driver of the vehicle until taken up either by inspector or toll bridge collector from the Department of Finance and Taxation, who shall give receipt therefor, or left at station designated by the Commissioner for receiving these reports. 

Operators shall mail, or deliver by messenger, daily trip reports on Monday and Wednesday of each week. 

All owners and/or operators transporting exempted articles part of the time and taxable articles part time shall 961

(Ch. 14  

be liable for the total miles traveled in transporting both classes.

Nonresident motor carriers who operate over the public highways of Tennessee shall keep clear and detailed records of operation in this state. These records shall be complete and open for inspection by the Department of Finance and Taxation, and shall be kept in this state by the agent designated by such motor carrier for the service of process under Section 10 of Chapter 114, Public Acts of 1933, or by such other agent of the motor carrier in this state who shall be agreed upon by the motor carrier and the Department of 

Finance and Taxation.

It shall be the duty of Mileage Tax Inspectors to check any and all vehicles subject to the terms of the Mileage Tax Law and these Rules and Regulations to see that a copy of the above-mentioned trip report accompanies each vehicle on each trip. 

(Signed) WALTER STOKES, JR., Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. 

Approved: 

(Signed) ROY H. BEELER, Attorney-General of Tennessee. 

Subsection (b), Item O, Chapter 108, Acts of 1937 

Owners and/or operators of passenger motor vehicles subject to tax imposed by subsection (b) of Item O, Chapter 108, Public Acts of 1937, shall file with the Mileage Tax Unit of the Department of Finance and Taxation, Nashville, Tennessee, schedules of all routes traveled, showing point of origin, destination, the number of miles between termini, and the number of trips made daily by each vehicle over route specified.

In addition to the information outlined in the preceding paragraph, daily trip report shall be filed covering each special or double trip made by any vehicle registered, or that should be registered, under the Act. These daily reports shall be mailed, or otherwise delivered, to the Mileage Tax Unit on Monday and Wednesday of each week. 

When a motor vehicle subject to this Act is taken out of service for hire, the owner thereof shall immediately report

Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of Tennessee, That for the purpose of this Act, (1) the words "owner" and "operator'' as used in this Act shall be held and taken to mean any person, firm, association or corporation owning and/or operating one or more motor vehicles transporting any character of property or freight along or over any public highway or highways of the State, and (2) the words 'motor carrier' "motor carriers' shall be held and taken to mean any owner and or operator of motor vehicles as defined herein using the highways of the State for the transportation of property or freight, and (3) the words "motor vehicle" shall be held and taken to mean not only a vehicle propelled by its own power but also any truck, trailer or semi-trailer attached thereto, the intent of this Act being that there shall be paid to the State the same amount for each and every tractor, truck, trailer (when lawfully operated) or semi-trailer drawing or carrying property or freight as for any motor vehicle of like capacity propelled by its own power, and (4) the term "public highway" or "highways" when used in this Act shall mean any public road, highway or thoroughfare of any kind used by the public. "Owner" and "operator" includes all persons, firms, associations and corporations operating motor vehicles

(Ch. 14  

transporting property or freight over the highways of Tennessee. The transportation of persons is not included in the above terms. "Motor carrier" or "motor carriers" includes all persons (owners and operators) transporting property or freight (but not passengers) over the highways of Tennessee. "Motor vehicle" includes motor trucks, trailers, semitrailers or other vehicles attached to any self-propelled vehicle carrying or drawing property or freight. "Highways" includes public roads, public roads, highways or thoroughfares of all kinds used by the public. 

Certain Motor Carriers Exempt- Law. Section 2 

 that this Act shall not apply to a motor carrier or motor carriers operating wholly within the limits of any incorporated town or city of the State, and/or within a radius of five (5) miles beyond the corporate limits of such town or city; nor to such carrier or carriers operating wholly within the limits of any incorporated town or city of the State having a population in excess of One Hundred Thousand (100,000) persons according to the last Federal Census or any subsequent Census and/or within a radius of Twelve (12) miles beyond the corporate limits of such town or city; nor to the transportation of livestock, poultry, farm, forest and/or dairy products to market by the owner thereof, or supplies for his own use in his own motor vehicle; nor to any motor vehicle operated by a non-profit co-operative association carrying only property belonging to the association or its members; nor to any motor vehicle operated by the government of the United States, the State of Tennessee or any county or municipality of the State.

Neither shall this Act apply to the owner or operator of a motor vehicle or motor vehicles used exclusively in transporting poultry, dairy, farm or forest products from the farm, dairy, or forest; or to or from receiving or assembling points for milk, poultry, farm or forest products to warehouse, creamery or other original storage place or market; provided, however, if this section of this Act or any portion thereof making the exemptions herein enumerated shall for any reason be held invalid, such holding shall not affect other portions of the Act, it being the legislative intent that this Act would have been passed notwithstanding the inclusion of Section 2 therein making said exemptions, and that the Act shall stand should this section of the Act be eliminated. 

Nor shall this Act apply to any owner or operator of any motor vehicle used either by said owner or operator or by his employee, in transporting his own property, of which he is the sole owner, over the highways of the State; provided that the compensation for use of the highways imposed by this Act shall apply to the operation of motor vehicles by the owner and/or operator thereof of the capacity described in Section 3 hereof, and when used in the character of transportation set forth in Section 3 hereof; provided, further, that if this paragraph of this Act or any portion thereof shall for any reason be held invalid or unconstitutional, such adjudication of invalidity or unconstitutionality shall not affect any other portion of the Act, it being the legislative intent that this Act would have been passed

Ch. 14) 967

MILEAGE TAX 

without this paragraph if such declaration of invalidity or unconstitutionality be made. 

Nor shall this Act apply to commission agents whose trucks transport petroleum products belonging to the owner whom the commission agents represent, and where the said commission agents receive a commission for their entire service and receive no separate compensation for transportation, provided such commission agent shall not represent, at any one time, more than one person, company, or corporation engaged in the sale of or distribution of petroleum products. 

The provisions of this Act do not apply to the following "motor carriers”— (a) Carriers operating wholly within the limits, or wholly within a five mile radius beyond the corporate limits, of any incorporated city. (b) Carriers operating wholly within the limits, or wholly within a twelve mile radius beyond the corporate limits, of any city having a population of more than 100,000 persons. (c) Transporting livestock, poultry, farm, forest and dairy products to market by the owner or by non-profit co-operative associations carrying property of its members. Transporting supplies used by and belonging to farmers, etc. (d) Vehicles operated by the United States, State of Tennessee or political subdivisions thereof. (e) The exclusive transportation of livestock, poultry, farm, forest and dairy products to market or to a warehouse by persons other than the owner thereof. (f) Transportation of property owned by the "'owner'' or "operator'' of motor vehicles having a carrying capacity of less than three tons. (g) Transportation of petroleum products by Commission Agents receiving no separate compensation for transportation, and not transporting such products for more than one company. 

Attention is drawn to the fact that the tax is upon the "motor carrier" and not upon each vehicle, therefore, under this section a carrier operating vehicles both within and without the mileage limitation as stated at (A) and (B) above, would be liable for the tax on all miles operated, i.e., to obtain the exemption allowed at (A) and (B) the motor carrier must operate exclusively within those limitations.

Intra-County Operations— Law. Section 3 

 that every owner and/or operator of any motor vehicle of three (3) tons or over carrying capacity (being the capacity on which a license plate is purchased) when such motor vehicle is used by such owner and/or operator, or by his employee, in transporting his own property or merchandise over the highways of the State, from one place to another, on fixed routes, or from a central warehouse to distribution depots or stores, either inside or outside the State, shall obtain a license, make reports and pay compensation for the use of the highways in accordance

(Ch. 14 

with the rates established by and under the provisions of this Act; provided, however, that this section shall not apply to any motor vehicle operating exclusively in any one county. 

Wholesale merchants, distributors and others transporting their own property within the borders of any county are not subject to the provisions of the Act. If the transportation of such property extends beyond the boundaries of any county, or into another state, the provisions of the Act apply. However, it appears that before liability, in such cases, accrues the following must exist: (a) A motor vehicle having a carrying capacity of three tons or over must be used. (b) The vehicle must be operated over fixed routes or from a central warehouse to stores or depots. (c) The vehicle must be operated beyond the boundaries of one county. 

Attention is drawn to the fact that owners and operators transporting their own property are excluded from the provisions of the Act in Section 2 thereof and are included in Section 3; therefore, the provisions of Section 2 as regards mileage limitations do not affect the liability where the transportation falls within the provisions of Section 3 of the Act.

Present Laws in Lieu of Prior Acts— Law. Section 4 

 That the compensation levied against motor carriers of freight or property by this Act for the use of the highways of the State shall be in lieu of that levied against such owners and/or operators by item 108 of the General Revenue Bill of 1931, being Chapter 13, Public Acts of 1931, Second Extra Session; but the compensation levied against the owners and/or operators of motor vehicles carrying passengers for hire by item 108, Chapter 13, Public Acts of 1931, Second Extra Session, is not affected by this Act nor in any wise superseded or abrogated by the terms hereof. 

This section of the Act exempts motor carriers of freight or property from the payment of the privilege tax imposed under the General Revenue Bill of 1931. The present tax liability consists of 3% of gross receipts from intrastate business under the General Revenue Bill of 1937 and the mileage tax imposed under the law of 1933 herein discussed.

MILEAGE TAX 

Purpose of Tax Levy- 

Law. Section 5. 

 That each and every motor carrier of freight or property as defined in Sections 1 and 3 of this Act (except as exempted in Section 2 hereof), in addition to the regular license fees or taxes imposed upon such motor carrier under the laws of this State, shall pay to the State of Tennessee for the use of its highways reasonable compensation to be expended by the State solely for the construction, maintenance, repair and upkeep of said highways and for the cost or expense of administering the laws governing the use of such highways, including the cost or expense of administering this Act. Such reasonable compensation which any such motor carrier shall so pay shall be ascertained, fixed and determined as hereinafter provided. 

The tax imposed upon motor carriers is in addition to license fees and other taxes, and is imposed for the use of the highways of the State, since motor carriers use the highways for the purpose of carrying on their business. 

Rates of "Compensation"—

Law. Section 6 

Be it further enacted, That each motor carrier of property or freight as defined in Sections 1 and 3 hereof, (except as otherwise provided in Section 2 hereof) shall pay to the State of Tennessee for each motor vehicle used for transporting property or freight over the highways of the State, whether loaded or empty, for each mile of such highways traversed by such vehicle the following amount: (1) On each motor vehicle of one ton and not more than three tons capacity, one-half (2) cent per mile traveled. (2) On each motor vehicle of over three (3) tons capacity one (1) cent per mile traveled.

As to any unit composed of a tractor with a semi-trailer attached, the compensation which shall be paid shall be determined by the capacity of the semi-trailer only, based on the standard factory rating thereof. 

As to trucks with trailers lawfully attached, the compensation which shall be paid shall be on each separate unit and shall be determined by the capacity of each separate unit based upon the standard factory rating for each separate unit, and not upon the combined capacity of the two units considered as one.

If any truck, trailer, or semi-trailer has no standard factory rating by which its capacity can be determined, then and in that event, for the purpose of determining the compensation to be paid for its operation, it shall be treated as having the same factory rating as a truck, trailer or semitrailer of like dimensions or carrying capacity which has a factory rating. 

In determining the capacity of each motor vehicle whose owner or operator is required to pay the above compensation, the standard factory rating of such motor vehicle shall control. 

The compensation or tax is measured by each mile operated in Tennessee by each vehicle, and applies to empty as well as loaded vehicles; however, tractors with semi-

(Ch. 14  

trailers attached are taxable only on the rated capacity of the semi-trailer.

The compensation is to be computed upon factory rating of carrying capacity and if such rating cannot be obtained for a given vehicle, such vehicle must be measured and the factory rating for a vehicle of similar capacity used. The tax is not to be computed upon the total capacity of two or more units, but upon the rated carrying capacity of each unit.

Rates: 

(a) One to three tons-½¢ per mile. (b) Three tons and over-1¢ per mile. 

Carriers Must Comply with Other Laws- Law. Section 7 

 That this Act shall not authorize the operation of any motor vehicle over the highways of the State in violation of the provisions of Chapter 58, Public Acts of 1929, requiring a certificate of convenience and necessity from the Railroad and Public Utilities Commission of the State authorizing such operation, or in violation of any other Act now in effect, or which may hereafter be enacted undertaking to regulate the operation of motor vehicles over the highways of the state, or fixing the weight, height, length or other dimensions or kind or character of such vehicles. 

Motor carriers of freight or property, operating under certificate of convenience and necessity, issued by the Railroad and Public Utilities Commission, under the provisions of Chapter 58, Acts of 1929, are subject to the tax herein levied. The payment of the tax does not legalize the operation of vehicles where the right to operate has been refused. 

The provisions of this Act do not affect any other laws regulating the operations of motor vehicles upon the highways of Tennessee.

License to Be Obtained- 

Law. Section 8 

Be it further enacted, That each motor carrier desiring to operate any motor vehicle over the highways of the State, and subject to the terms of this Act, shall apply to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation of the State of Tennessee at Nashville, for a license or licenses authorizing such motor carrier to operate motor vehicles over the highways of the State, a license for each motor vehicle being required. The license card for each motor vehicle shall be in such form as shall be prescribed by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and shall be signed by him; and for each license issued under the provisions of this Act, a fee of One ($1.00)

Ch. 14) 971

MILEAGE TAX 

Dollar shall be paid to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, which shall become a part of the highway fund provided by this Act. 

If for any reason the license card issued to any motor carrier shall be destroyed or lost, the operator may obtain a duplicate license card from the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation; and for each such duplicate card so issued a fee of Fifty (504) cents shall be paid. 

Such license, once the same has been issued, shall remain in effect and valid so long as the holder complies with all laws of the State of Tennessee relating to and regulating motor carriers operating over the highways of the State, but said license shall not be transferable to a new holder or to a different motor vehicle than the one for which it was issued. 

The application for a license shall be signed and sworn to by the applicant and shall be in such form as the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall prescribe and shall show, among other things, the following: (a) The make, kind, size, weight, carrying capacity, motor number and registration number of each motor vehicle as herein defined, to be used by the motor carrier on the public highways of the State. (b) Insofar as possible, the route or routes over which each motor vehicle will be operated with the number of trips each vehicle will make each day. (c) The estimated mileage that each vehicle will travel during each calendar month following the issuance of the license. (d) If the carrier is the holder of a certificate of convenience and necessity issued by the Railroad and Public Utilities Commission of the State, the date of the certificate, its number and the routes covered by it. (e) If the carrier is not such certificate holder, then the character of hauling that is to be done and over what routes insofar as the same may be shown. (f) Any other information deemed by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation necessary to a proper and efficient enforcement of this Act. 

The application for license shall be signed and sworn to by the operator before the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation who is authorized to administer oaths for this purpose, or before a notary public, and the application shall be kept on file by said Commissioner as a part of the permanent records of his office. When the applicant has complied with the provisions of this Act, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall issue the license and furnish the operator a license card in such form as the Commissioner may prescribe which shall be signed by him, and said card when so furnished shall be attached to the motor vehicle in some conspicuous place so as to be open to inspection by the proper officials of the State of Tennessee and officers charged with the duty of enforcing the laws, and by such officers of the various counties and municipalities thereof at all times.

Said license card shall show the make, kind, size, carrying capacity, motor number and license number of the vehicle which is covered by it and it shall be a misdemeanor for any motor carrier to operate any motor vehicle without such license, or with the license attached to a motor vehicle not covered by it, and the operator so offending shall, upon conviction, be fined not less than Twenty-Five ($25.00) Dollars nor more than Five 

Hundred ($500.00) Dollars for each such offense; and each day's operation either without the license displayed in the motor vehicle or with one displayed that is not issued to cover that particular motor vehicle shall constitute a separate offense, and the venue shall be in any county in which any part of the illegal operation takes place. 

The provisions of this section are deemed sufficiently clear; however, attention is drawn to the following:

(Ch. 14  

(a) The license is not transferable. (b) It must be attached to the vehicle for which it is issued. (c) Failure to secure or attach such license to the vehicle constitutes a misdemeanor. Upon conviction the fine is $25.00 to $500.00 and is to be imposed upon the "Motor Carrier."

Motor carriers may avoid unnecessary expense by using care to have all vehicles properly licensed, the failure of carriers to properly license vehicles frequently results in expensive delays and the loss of profitable business. 

It is not clear as to whether both the carrier and the driver or operator of the vehicle are subjected to fine for operating a vehicle without proper license; however, it does appear that should a driver knowingly operate a vehicle without proper license he would be equally guilty. 

Certain Information to Be Painted on Each Vehicle- 

Law. Section 9 

 That each motor vehicle operated by a motor carrier required to pay the compensation provided for by this Act shall have painted or stenciled on the sides thereof in letters clearly visible, the name of the motor carrier, the location of his place of business and the capacity of the vehicle by which the compensation is measured; and it shall be a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of Ten ($10.00) to Fifty ($50.00) Dollars for each day's operation of a vehicle in violation of this section of this Act. 

The following information must be painted or stenciled on both sides of the vehicle: (a) Name and address of the carrier. (b) Rated carrying capacity of the vehicle. 

Failure to comply with the above requirements constitutes a misdemeanor punishable by fine of $10.00 to $50.00 for each day such vehicle is operated in violation of this section.

Non-Resident Motor Carriers- Law. Section 10 

Be it further enacted, That if any motor carrier shall be a nonresident of the state he shall, prior to operating on the highways of this State any motor vehicle subject to this Act, appoint, and so long as he operates a motor vehicle in this State, maintain an agent upon whom process may be served, the name and resident of such agent to be filed in the office of the Secretary of State and also with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. The operation of such motor vehicle without the appointment of such agent for the service of process shall be and constitute a misdemeanor for each day's operation without the appointment of such

Ch. 14) 973 

MILEAGE TAX 

agent. It is provided, however, that the agent appointed pursuant to this section shall not be liable to or amenable to service of process except in suits which may arise under this Act, and the appointment of such agent shall state that it is done pursuant to this Act. 

The failure of non-resident motor carriers to appoint and maintain a process agent in Tennessee so long as motor vehicles are operated therein, is a misdemeanor. The name and address of process agents must be filed with the Secretary of State and the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation.

Attention is directed to the fact that process can only be served on such agent in suits brought under the provisions of this Act.

This section appears to require the appointment of a process agent in all cases and includes occasional trips made into or through the State of Tennessee. Non-resident carriers may avoid expensive delays in the operation of their vehicles in this regard and such agent should be appointed prior to operation in Tennessee. 

Interstate Commerce- Law. Section 11 

 That this Act and every part thereof shall apply and be construed to apply to interstate commerce, except insofar as the same may be in conflict with the provisions of the Constitution of the United States or the lawful Act of Congress. 

The provisions of this Act apply to interstate commerce. 

A motor carrier operating vehicles from a point in another state to a point in Tennessee is liable for compensation for the use of the highways in Tennessee even though such vehicles transport interstate commerce, the tax being levied upon the carrier and not upon the commerce. 

Records and Monthly Reports- 

Law. Section 12 

Be it further enacted, That in order to ascertain the mileage traveled by motor vehicles subject to this Act, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall prescribe the records to be kept by each operator of such vehicle, and on or before the twentieth (20th) day of each month each operator of a motor vehicle shall file with said Commissioner, in duplicate, a statement verified under oath by the operator or by a person having knowledge of the facts and duly designated therefor by the operator, showing the mileage traveled by each motor vehicle subject to this Act during the preceding calendar month and shall at the time of filing such report, pay to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation the tax revealed to be due by it.

(Ch. 14  

This section authorizes the Commissioner to prescribe the records to be kept by each operator in order to ascertain the miles traveled by each motor vehicle during each month.

Use of Appliances May Be Required- Law. Section 13 

 That the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is empowered to prescribe and require the character of appliances which each operator of a motor vehicle subject to this Act shall use in order to establish the correct mileage traveled by such vehicle and to adopt rules and regulations with respect to the care and inspection of such appliances and reports of the mileage shown by said appliances. 

This section permits the Commissioner to require motor carriers to install upon each motor vehicle, operated

Ch. 14) 977 

MILEAGE TAX 

in Tennessee, mechanical devices or appliances designed to record each mile such truck is operated, and such appliances are subject to inspection under rules and regulations adopted by the Commissioner. The installation of such devices would be rather expensive to carriers and caution should be used, to so conduct the operation and account for each mile accurately, in order to avoid the necessity for the requirement of such appliances. 

Inspection of Books and Records- Law. Section 14 

 That the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may in his discretion require any operator of a motor vehicle subject to this Act operating such vehicle within this state to keep within this state subject to inspection at all times by said Commissioner or his agent such books of accounts or records as may be reasonably necessary to enable said Commissioner to obtain full information at all times regarding the amounts due from such operator under the provisions of this Act. Such records shall at all times be open to inspection by the Commissioner or by any agent appointed by him for such purposes. 

The books and records of all motor carriers operating in Tennessee are subject to inspection, at any time, by the 

Commissioner or his agent.

It is doubtful if the Commissioner could legally inspect the books and records of non-resident carriers at their place of business located outside of Tennessee; however, it appears that it would be unwise to refuse such inspection since this section authorizes the Commissioner to require such carrier to keep all necessary books and records in Tennessee; and, failure to comply with such regulation would be a violation subject to fine. 

Rules and Regulations- Law. Section 15 

Be it further enacted, That every operator of a motor vehicle subject to this Act shall register with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation in accordance with his requirements and shall comply with the rules and regulations adopted by the Commissioner for the purpose of ascertaining the mileage traveled upon the highways of this State by each such motor vehicle. The said Commissioner shall have authority to promulgate uniform rules and regulations as to the time and manner of registration and as to the method of ascertaining the mileage traveled and the compensation due the State on account thereof; and it shall be unlawful and constitute a misdemeanor for any operator of a motor vehicle subject to this Act to operate the same on a public highway without registration and license as herein provided, punishable as aforesaid.

(Ch. 14 

Motor carriers must register with the Commissioner in accordance with requirements and comply with all rules and regulations adopted by him. Section 8 of the Act requires the registration of each motor vehicle and; in addition, the 

Commissioner is authorized to promulgate rules and regulations, which must: (a) Be uniform. (b) Relate to the time and manner of registration. (c) Relate to the method of ascertaining the mileage traveled and compensation due.

The operation of a motor vehicle without license, or the operation of a licensed vehicle by an unregistered motor carrier, is a misdemeanor and punishable accordingly. 

Administration- Law. Section 16 

 That the rights and duties given to and devolve upon the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation under the provisions of this Act shall, in the event of a change hereafter devolve upon the office or department of the state which shall succeed to and perform the duties now performed by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. 

Comment upon this section is deemed unnecessary since it has no practical application to taxpayers. Injunction 

Law. Section 17 

Be it further enacted, That any operator of a motor vehicle subject to this Act, may at the instance of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation or of any person having interest in the subject matter be enjoined by the courts of this state from any violation of the provisions of this Act, or of any order, rule, regulation or requirement of said Commissioner; provided, however, that such injunction or proceedings shall in no respect affect the liability of such operator to conviction for misdemeanor as herein provided.

Motor carriers and their employees may be enjoined from any violation of this Act, order or rule of the Commissioner. Failure to secure such injunction does not affect or prevent a conviction for violations. 

Commissioner to Audit Monthly Reports- 

Law. Section 18 

Be it further enacted, That after the filing of the monthly report by the motor carrier as provided herein, it shall be the duty of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation to audit said report to make such further

Ch. 14) 979 

MILEAGE TAX 

investigation, if any, as may be necessary to ascertain all the facts for the purpose of determining whether said report is correct and whether the full amount due the state has been paid. If, in the opinion of said Commissioner, a further sum is due from said operator, such operator shall be notified in writing, by registered mail or personal service, accordingly, and such operator shall pay said additional amount within ten days thereafter. 

The operator shall have the right to pay such additional amount under protest and to sue for and recover all or a portion thereof upon proper showing that the same was not properly due, but such suit must be brought within thirty (30) days after such payment. 

No operator shall operate any motor vehicle subject to this Act on the public highways of the state after the amount as provided for shall become due and payable to the State, until the same has been paid in full and the operation by such operator of each motor vehicle each day after default in such payment shall constitute a separate misdemeanor punishable as such.

Upon the receipt of the monthly tax reports filed by motor carriers it becomes the duty of the Commissioner to audit such reports and make such investigation as he deems necessary to ascertain whether the correct amount of tax has been paid. If it is found that additional tax is due the carrier is to be notified of such additional amount due and must pay the tax within ten days. Should the taxpayer feel aggrieved, the additional tax must be paid under protest, and suit for recovery brought within thirty days.

Carriers failing to pay any additional tax within the ten day period are prohibited, by this section, from operating any vehicle subject to the provisions of this Act, on the highways of Tennessee until such tax is paid. 

The payment of tax under protest and the bringing of the suit, within thirty days, is the only remedy afforded the taxpayer; and, in all cases involving the payment of additional mileage tax, payment should be made under protest where there is any question as to the legality of such additional tax.

Failure to Make Report or Pay Tax- Law. Section 19 

 That if any such operator subject to the provisions of this Act shall fail for thirty (30) days to make the report required by this Act or to pay the amount due to the state under this Act, then it shall be the duty of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation at once to notify the Attorney General of the State, whereupon the said Attorney General shall have the power and it is hereby made his duty to take appropriate steps to collect said amount, and to enjoin said operator from using the highways of the state until all the amounts past due hereunder, together with interest at the rate of six (6%) per cent per annum and all

(Ch. 14 

cost shall have been paid, provided, however, that such injunction proceedings shall in no respect affect the liability of such operator to conviction for misdemeanor as herein provided. 

The mileage tax is payable not later than 20th of each month and becomes delinquent after that date. Upon failure of motor carriers to pay the tax within thirty days after same is due it is mandatory that the Commissioner immediately notify the Attorney General, and it then becomes his duty to collect the tax and enjoin further operation over the highways of Tennessee by such carrier. 

Delinquent tax is subject to interest at the rate of 6% per annum and carriers are liable for all costs incident to the collection of any delinquency. In addition, delinquent taxpayers are also subject to conviction and fine for violating the provisions of the Act. 

Distress Warrants- Law. Section 20 

 That in order to insure the prompt collection of said compensation in the event the same becomes delinquent, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is authorized from the best information available to ascertain the amount thereof due from any motor carrier and he is authorized to issue a distress warrant against any delinquent motor carrier for the collection of said compensation, which shall be levied as any other distress warrant is authorized to be levied under the law and said compensation so due from any motor carrier that shall constitute a first lien on the motor vehicle or motor vehicles or other property belonging to the motor carrier, and said lien shall be prior to any liens on any such motor vehicle, including mortgages, trust deeds, bills of sale or titles retained by the seller of such vehicle, when the instruments evidencing such liens are executed after the effective date of this Act. 

When any motor vehicle is offered for sale under such distress warrant, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation or his agent is authorized to bid the amount of the compensation due the state plus accrued costs for the motor vehicle upon which the distress warrant is levied, and if the same is sold to him he may sell the same to such purchaser as he may find and pay the proceeds over under this Act. 

This section authorizes the Commissioner to issue distress warrant for the collection of the tax found to be due by any carrier failing to file the monthly truck mileage tax report. The tax may be assessed upon any available information or may be based upon facts determined through inspection and examination of the books and records of such carrier. The Acts contemplate the issuance of the distress warrant immediately the amount of delinquent tax has been ascertained, and may also be issued to collect

Ch. 14) 981

MILEAGE TAX 

delinquent tax in cases where the report is filed, within the time limitation, without payment of the tax due. 

Distress warrants are to be served in accordance with law; and, when so served, constitute a first lien on the motor vehicle and are prior to mortgages, trust deeds, etc. 

Property covered by such lien is to be sold in the manner provided by law and it is the duty of the Commissioner to bid an amount sufficient to cover tax, penalty, interest and costs.

Police Powers-Expense of Administration— Law. Section 21 

 That for the enforcement of this Act, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is authorized and directed to take such steps as he considers necessary, to promulgate proper rules, and to employ necessary assistants to effectively collect said compensation and to enforce the provisions of this Act, payment of the costs of administering the Act to be made out of the funds collected under said Act. Each assistant so employed by the Commissioner shall have full police power for the enforcement of this Act and any other Acts pertaining to the use of the highways of the State and may arrest any motor carrier or the operator of any motor vehicle for violation of the terms of this Act. 

The employes of the Department of Finance and Taxation are vested with police powers for the purpose of administering the provisions of the Act; and, under such power, may arrest any carrier or operator of motor vehicles for violating the terms of this Act. 

The Commissioner does not withhold any portion of the taxes collected for the purpose of defraying the expense of administration. All taxes collected are deposited daily by the Commissioner in State depositories to the credit of the State Treasurer and annual appropriation is made to cover expenses, which are paid by State warrants in accordance with law.

Object of Act-Highway Fund Revenue_ Law. Section 22 

Be it further enacted, That the object of this Act is to require each motor carrier subject to the provisions of the Act and using the highways of the State to pay to the State of Tennessee reasonable compensation for the use of the highways; and the amounts required to be so paid by this 

Act shall be paid into the State Treasury to the credit of the general highway fund for use in the construction maintenance, repair and upkeep of the state highways, after deducting the expense of administration and enforcement of this Act.

(Ch. 14 

This section has no direct application to carriers; is deemed sufficiently clear and comment is unnecessary. 

False Reports— Law. Section 23 

 That the making of a knowingly false report or the wilful failure to file a report when due under the terms and provisions of this Act by any motor carrier shall constitute a misdemeanor and be punishable by law as in cases of misdemeanor. Likewise, all offenses made misdemeanors by this Act shall be punishable as provided by law in cases of misdemeanor except those herein declared punishable by specific punishments in various sections of this Act. 

The failure to file any report required to be filed by this Act or rules and regulations adopted by the Commissioner, within the time specified, constitutes a misdemeanor. 

Motor carriers finding it impossible to file monthly report on or before the 20th of each month, due to sickness, etc., should so inform the Commissioner and apply for extension. of time in which to file such report. 

The filing of false reports knowingly, is likewise defined to be a misdemeanor and is punishable as such. 

Duties of Patrolmen, Judges and Toll Collectors- Law. Section 24 

Be it further enacted, That it shall be the duty of the members of the Tennessee Highway Patrol to see to it that this Act is enforced and that the amounts due the State are paid, and to that end they shall have the right at any time to examine and inspect any motor vehicle, the license therein, and to question the operator thereof for the purpose of determining whether or not such operation is unlawful and if any is found to be unlawful they shall have the right to take such steps as may be found necessary to collect said tax and may make arrest of the operator of the vehicle for violation of this Act. 

It shall be the duty of the Judges of the Criminal and Circuit Courts of the State to give this Act in charge to the grand juries of the State; and to the end that this Act may be enforced, said grand juries are hereby clothed with inquisitorial power to inquire into and ascertain whether or not there has been violation of the provisions of this Act and to return indictments in proper cases. 

It shall be the duty of the various toll collectors on the different toll bridges of the state to inspect various motor vehicles operating across said toll bridges for the purpose of ascertaining whether the operators thereof have complied with the provisions of this Act in regard to a license, payment of tax, etc. and if any toll collector finds that this Act is being violated by any operator, he shall immediately report such fact to any member of the Tennessee Highway Patrol available and within reach, giving detailed information as to violation of the Act. 

This section authorizes members of the Tennessee Highway Patrol to take such action as may be necessary to col-

Ch. 14) 983 

MILEAGE TAX 

lect the tax herein imposed and to make arrest of the operator of the vehicle for violations of this Act. 

Prior to the enactment of Chapter 33, Acts of 1937, (The Reorganization Bill) the supervision of the Highway Patrol was under the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, 

(See Section 11460 et seq. Williams Tennessee Code) how ever, pursuant to the following sections of Chapter 33, Acts of 1937: 

"Section 44. That the Department of administration, through the division of Highway Patrol shall assume and exercise the powers and duties of the Tennessee Highway Patrol under Sections 11460 to 11465 inclusive, of the code, and upon this Act becoming effective said patrol force and all of its records and equipment shall be transferred from the Department of Taxation and Finance to the Division of Highway Patrol.' 

The supervision and administration of the Patrol was transferred to the Department of Administration, Division of Highway Patrol. Section 11462 of the Code of Tennes see as amended by Section 44, Chapter 33, Acts of 1937 is 

"11462. DUTIES—It shall be the duty of the members of the Tennessee Highway Patrol, under the direction of the Department of Administration to patrol the State Highways and to enforce all laws, and all rules and regulations of the Department of Highways and public works regulating traffic on and use of said highways; and under the direction of the 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation to assist him and the county court clerks of the State in the collection of all taxes and revenue going to the State, and in the enforcement of all laws relating to same. 

Therefore, it appears that the enactment of Chapter 33, Acts of 1937 does not alter the duties and powers of the members of Highway Patrol as regards the enforcement of this Act.

This section is mandatory upon criminal and circuit court judges to charge grand juries relative to this Act and such juries may inquire into and ascertain whether the Act has been violated by motor carriers. 

Collectors of tolls at bridges located in Tennessee are authorized to inspect vehicles crossing such bridge and inform Highway Patrolmen of any violations of this Act. 

The provisions of this Section are far reaching and carriers should be very careful to comply with the Act in order to avoid the expensive fines and penalties imposed.

(Ch. 14  

Gates or Barriers- 

Law. Section 25 

 That if the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall find it necessary to properly enforce this Act, he shall have authority to establish gates or barriers on the main highways of the State for the purpose of intercepting persons violating the provisions of this Act and requiring compliance herewith. 

The Commissioner has not established "gates or barriers" on the highways for the purposes mentioned, however, there are a number of Highway Patrol offices erected upon main highways in Tennessee and it is the practice to require all trucks to stop at such points for the purpose of inspection by a mileage tax inspector or highway patrolman.

Non-Resident Carriers; Police Power Affecting- 

Law. Section 26. 

Be it further enacted, That in case a motor carrier comes into the state from points outside the state without first having obtained a license as required by this Act, such motor carrier may be stopped by any member of the Tennessee Highway Patrol or any lawful police or peace officer in the State or by any person named by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation to aid in the enforcements of this Act and may be questioned as to his destination and the route by which he proposes to reach his destination, whereupon the mileage may be ascertained and the compensation due on account of such operation paid by such motor carrier for that particular trip but the person to whom such compensation is paid shall immediately report the fact to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and transmit to the Commissioner the amount of the payment and such motor carrier shall, prior to any subsequent operation into or through the state, obtain a license as required by this Act. 

Provisions of Act Severable- Law. Section 27 

Be it further enacted, That if any clause, sentence, section or part of this Act shall be declared unconstitutional or invalid for any reason, such declaration or holding shall not affect any other section or portion of this Act, it being a legislative intent that this Act would have been passed had such unconstitutional or invalid provisions not been included in this Act. 

Effective Date of Law- Law. Section 28 

Be it further enacted, That all laws and parts of laws in conflict with the provisions of this Act, be, and they are, hereby repealed, and this Act shall take effect thirty (30) days from and after its passage, the public welfare requiring it. 

Sections 26, 27 and 28 are deemed sufficiently clear and comment is unnecessary.
