ARTICLE I Definitions and General Provisions- Section 1. Be it enacted by the general assembly of the state of Tennessee,

That the following definitions and general provisions shall apply in all cases, unless otherwise provided in special cases but the general provision shall not be deemed to control specific provisions to the contrary in any particular taxing item, to-wit: (a) Whenever the word "person" or the word "taxpayer" is used in this Act it shall be construed to include every individual, partnership, firm, corporation or any other association of any kind. The singular pronoun "he,' "him," etc., shall include the plural "they," "them," etc., whenever necessary. 99

(Ch. 15

(b) The word "city" or "cities" when the same may be material in determining the rate of a State or County tax shall include one mile of territory adjoining the corporate limits of any incorporated city, but it is not intended to give any city the right to tax privileges exercised at locations beyond its corporate limits. (c) Whenever the word "collector" is used in this Act it shall mean every officer or employe of the state, county, or city authorized to collect the tax. (d) Whenever the "Federal Census" is referred to in this Act, the Federal Census of 1930 or any subsequent Federal Census is meant, and when taxes are graduated according to "population" the population according to the said Federal Census shall be used in determining the tax. (e) The words "per annum" designate the amount of the tax to be paid for exercising the privilege for twelve months; and such words are to be read into every taxing item where the specific context does not indicate the contrary. 99 Where a privilege tax is referred to as an "annual tax,' such reference is intended to mean a privilege tax obtained for, or renewed for, a period of not more nor less than one year. (f) Every person taxed "per annum" shall have the right to pay the tax quarterly, when the item levying such tax does not expressly require payment for a full year. 

Where quarterly payment is made such person shall receive a license for three months. If still in business at the expiration of such license he shall renew it. Such renewal shall be made in like manner and on the payment of the same fees as on the issuance of the original license. 

Every person having an unexpired license under any prior General Revenue Bill shall, at the date when this Act becomes effective, be required to secure a license under this Act, if this Act increases the rate of taxation upon such privilege. However, such person when applying for license under this Act shall be credited with the ratable proportion of the unexpired license in computing his license tax under this Act.

Ch. 15) 993 

(g) Unless some other collector is expressly designated, the county court clerk shall collect the taxes herein imposed on privileges and shall report to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. (h) The license given by the county court clerk shall be sufficient evidence of a compliance with this law, without the countersignature or certification by the circuit court clerk or any other official. (i) Any person liable for any tax herein imposed doing business in any unincorporated town or in a rural district, shall pay the tax imposed upon the like business done in the city of the smallest population, when such tax is graduated according to the population of cities. (j) Every person conducting business from more than one established place of business in a county shall be liable for the privilege tax on business done at each place and must secure a separate license for each place of business. 

If he conducts business from an established place of business in more than one county he shall pay the State privilege tax in each county and each county in which he maintains an established place established place of business shall be authorized to levy a county tax upon each such establishment in accordance with sub-section (1) hereof. 

If he maintains only one place of business in a county, from that place extending his operations into adjoining counties without establishing a place of business or a branch office in such adjoining counties, he shall be liable for both State and county tax in the county where the place of business is located but only for the county tax in any other county. (k) Any tax imposed by this Act shall not be held to supersede any other privilege tax imposed upon such taxpayer or occupation by any other Act, either special or general, except those imposed exclusively by the terms of

If he claims exemption for any reason, his rights shall be determined as hereinafter provided:

Any disabled ex-soldier, sailor or marine of any war in which the United States has been engaged, or any peacetime soldier, sailor or marine who was disabled while in regular service, owning less than $1,000.00 of property above encumbrances thereon and doing business with a capital stock of not exceeding $600.00, residing within and being a citizen of the State of Tennessee and of the County in which the exemption shall be claimed, being the sole beneficiary of said business shall be exempt from the payment of the privilege tax herein imposed on such business. 

Provided that only one exemption from privilege tax can be claimed by one person under this exemption. Provided further that said business is conducted by the exsoldier, etc., or a member of his immediate family. No ex-service man claiming exemption under this paragraph shall be permitted to operate as a peddler more than one truck.

The county court clerk of the several counties shall require said ex-soldier to make an affidavit setting out his financial condition, and the source of his income before said license shall be issued, and any person making a false affidavit and procuring a free privilege license thereby shall be guilty of perjury and punished under the law. The county court clerk shall receive only a fee of 50 cents for issuing a license to such soldier.

(n) Each person engaged in a single business, which business might fall under two or more items of Section 1 of this bill, shall pay the highest tax imposed by such items, but only one tax. The conducting of the business of a collection, adjusting or forwarding agency without the payment of the privilege tax herein provided for is declared to be a public nuisance subject to abatement under any procedure provided by law and especially to abatement by injunction.

In addition to the above taxes there shall be collected in misdemeanor cases a State and County expense fee as provided in Section 12243 of the Code of Tennessee.

Item 60-Merchants— (a) Permanent Merchants 

Each person engaged in the mercantile business in this State shall pay a privilege tax of fifteen cents (154) per annum on each One Hundred ($100.00) Dollars of the average capital invested. For the purpose of this item “average capital invested" shall mean the average amount of stock as defined by Section 1701 of the Code of Tennessee. The tax hereby imposed shall be based upon a sworn statement of the merchant.

Of the State tax hereby imposed, seven and onehalf (724) cents shall be retained by the county for school purposes. This division of the State privilege tax shall not affect the power of counties and cities to levy the maximum tax of fifteen (15¢) cents on each One 

Hundred ($100.00) Dollars of the average capital invested. 

The State privilege tax hereby imposed shall in no case be less than Five ($5.00) Dollars. Of such minimum tax Two and one-half ($2.50) Dollars shall go to the State for State purposes and Two and one-half ($2.50) Dollars shall be retained in the county for school purposes. 

When the average capital invested by any merchant is not more than Eight Hundred ($800.00) Dollars, such merchant shall pay a tax of Seven and one-half ($7.50) Dollars to the State for State purposes and no ad valorem tax shall be charged.

(Ch. 15  

Merchants starting in business shall pay a privilege tax upon the capital invested and shall thereafter make a sworn statement in accordance with Section 1703 of the Code of Tennessee, upon which statement their privilege tax will be based. 

Merchants maintaining or operating depots or warehouses from which they replenish their stores must report and pay the above privilege tax upon the average capital invested, including the value of the average amount of stock maintained in such depots or warehouses.

Item 65-Oil Depots and Oil Wagons- (a) Oil Depots 

The term "oil depot" as used herein shall be understood to mean a place within this state where petroleum products or substitutes therefor come to rest within this State after movement in interstate commerce and from which such petroleum products or substitutes therefor are not distributed direct to consumer at retail only or where such products are kept for sale after manufacture or processing in this State, in quantities equal to or greater than thirty-one gallons liquid measure. The transfer of such products from a licensed "oil depot" to another location from which wholesale 100.00

Ch. 15) 1045 

sales are made shall make such location a separate and distinct Oil Depot.

If selling, using or otherwise distributing or storing more than 31 gallons of petroleum products, annually

(a) Slot Machines

Ch. 15) 1055 

be irredeemable, shall pay for the same the following tax:

Any person allowing a machine taxable hereunder to be set up in his place of business without the license being attached to such machine shall be liable for the tax notwithstanding the contention that such machine is owned by or is operated by some other person. Any machine to which the license is not attached shall be subject to this tax notwithstanding the contention of the owner or operator thereof that some license in his possession but not attached to the machine was issued for such machine. Slot machines which are not licensed as herein provided for shall be seized by any collector or agent authorized by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and held, together with the contents thereof, until the tax herein provided for shall have been paid. At the time of such seizure the owner or operator of the machine, if known, and otherwise the owner or operator of the establishment in which such machine is found, shall be notified.

At any time within thirty days thereafter any person claiming such machine shall be given a hearing by the Commissioner of Finance and

Taxation with reference to his tax liability. 

Unless hearing is applied for within thirty days, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxa- 40.00 50.00

(Ch. 15  

tion is authorized to dispose of such machine, applying the proceeds of the machine and its contents to the payment of the tax herein. provided for.

Upon application being made to operate any machine under this Item, the county court clerk is authorized to presume that the operation of such machine is lawful. When a license has been issued for the operation thereof the sum paid shall not be refunded notwithstanding that the operation of the machine shall afterwards be prohibited. No county court clerk shall neglect or refuse to collect the tax herein. provided for because of his doubt with reference to the legality of the operation of such machine, but the question of the legality of such operation shall be determined by the proper judicial authorities. (Ch. 15  Item 96-Transfers of Realty and Mortgages- 

(a) Transfers of Realty

On all transfers of realty there shall be paid a tax for State purposes only of One Dollar and 

Fifty-cents per One Thousand Dollars on the consideration which shall in no case be less than the value of the property, to be collected by the Clerk of the County Court of the county in which said transfer is offered for record. 

The County Register is forbidden to record said deed until the Clerk certifies that this tax has been paid, but no Register's fee shall be charged for such certificate of registration and such certificate need not be registered. The

County Court Clerk shall receive as a fee for such certification the sum of 15 cents, to be paid when said transfer is made. This tax shall not be a credit on the tax imposed under

Section 1316, et. seq., of the Code of Tennessee (the Excise Tax Law). 

(b) Mortgages, etc.

Prior to the recording in the Register's Office of any mortgage, deed of trust, or other instrument in the nature of a mortgage or deed of trust, executed as a pledge, mortgage or conveyance in trust of any real or personal property situated in the State, or any interest in any real estate, to secure the payment of any indebtedness, there shall be paid a tax for 

State purposes only of ten cents on each $100.00 or major portion thereof the amount of indebtedness so secured, to be collected by the Clerk of the County Court of the county in which said instrument is offered for record.

The County Register is forbidden to record any such instrument until the Clerk of the County Court of the county in which said instrument is offered for record, certifies on said

Ch. 15) 1061 

instrument that such tax has been paid. The tax herein prescribed shall be paid by the holder or owner of the indebtedness secured by the instrument offered for record; but, this tax shall not apply to an indebtedness of less than $2,000.00. But this Act shall not apply to holders or owners of indebtedness secured by mortgages or deeds of trust when it appears on the face of said instrument that the owner or holder of said indebtedness is the Tennessee 

Valley Authority, Rural Electrification Ad ministration, or any other agency of the United States Government making loans to 

Rural Electric Membership Associations lo- 

Icated within the State of Tennessee. 

Holders or owners of indebtedness secured by mortgages of over $2,000.00 shall pay on the excess above $2,000.00.

This tax shall not be a credit on the tax imposed under Section 1316, et seq., of the Code (the 

Excise Tax Law). 

The County Court Clerk shall receive as a fee for each mortgage so probated the sum of 15 cents to be paid when the mortgage is paid. 

Where part of the property covered by such mortgage or deed of trust is located within and part without this State only such proportion of the amount covered by the deed of trust shall be taxed as the value of the property within the State bears to the whole property.

 Item A-Bottlers and Manufacturers of Soft Drinks, etc.- 

Each person doing business as a bottler or as a manufacturer of beverages known as soft drinks shall for the privilege of doing business pay to the State for State purposes an amount equal to one and one-half (12) per cent of the gross receipts in the State. 

There shall be credited upon the tax hereby imposed any taxes paid under the Franchise Tax Law and under the Excise Law during the calendar year in which the tax hereby levied becomes due.

The tax hereby imposed shall be administered and collected in accordance with Article III, Section 2 of this Act. 

Bottlers and manufacturers of soft drinks paying the tax levied by this item and delivering only the products of their own plant by which this tax is measured shall not be liable for a peddler's tax: and shall not be liable for wholesale jobbers' tax under Item 101.

Item B-Branch or Chain Stores- 

Each person engaged in the business of operating or maintaining in this State branch or chain stores shall for the privilege of operating such stores pay the tax hereinafter set forth. In each such chain or branch store system there shall be exempted from this tax the store in which such system maintains its general offices in Tennessee or if no such general offices are maintained, a store in such system to be designated by the taxpayer in the sworn statement hereinafter referred to. 

Upon each store in such branch or chain in excess of one, there shall be paid a tax of Three ($3.00) Dollars for each one hundred square feet of floor space, or major fraction thereof, in such store.

(Ch. 15  

The term "branch store" or "chain store" as used in this Item shall include retail stores or mercantile establishments operated (or controlled by lease, contract or otherwise) under the same general management, supervision or ownership. The term "chain store" or "branch store," as used herein, shall also include retail stores operated under separate charters of incorporation (if there is a common ownership of a majority of the stock of such separate incorporated companies), or operated under a common ownership of a majority interest in such stores when such separately incorporated companies or stores have the benefit, in whole or in part, of group purchase of merchandise for resale or of common management. 

The term "chain store" or "branch store" shall not be construed to include filling stations or any other store or place in which the principal business carried on therein is the storage, sale or distribution of petroleum products taxed under a separate Item of this Act, but shall include counters, divisions, departments or leased space operated under a chain store system in department stores or other mercantile establishments. 

The term "floor space" as used in this Item shall include the total number of square feet in such store determined by the internal measurements as to width and depth of each floor thereof. "Floor space" shall not include floors, basements or separate rooms used exclusively for storage purposes, to which customers not ordinarily admitted; but counter space, office space, elevator space, etc., shall not be considered storage space and shall be computed as floor space.

The tax hereby imposed shall be paid on or before June 1st of each year for the privilege of op-

Ch. 15) 1069 

erating during the ensuing twelve months period and shall be paid to the Commissioner of 

Finance and Taxation accompanied by a sworn statement of the taxpayer, or his legally authorized agent, setting forth the number of stores operated, the square feet of floor space of each store, and the location of each store, including the exempted store. 

A separate license shall be issued for each store hereunder taxed and such license shall be available for inspection at the store for which issued.

The privilege tax levied by this Item shall be in addition to any other privilege tax required under this Act or under any other Act.

None of the above enumerated Code Sections and no other Code Sections specifying filing fees of particular kinds of corporations, or consolidation of fees and the like, shall be deemed to be altered or repealed by this Act.

Item G-Gas, Water, Electric Power and Light Com panies Each person engaged in the business of furnishing or distributing gas, water, or electric current, whether to dealer, consumer, municipality or other customer, shall, for the privilege of doing such business, pay to the State for State purposes an amount equal to three (3%) per cent of the gross receipts derived from intrastate business in the State. Persons engaged in the business of manufacturing gas or of distributing manufactured gas or natural gas shall, in lieu of the foregoing, pay an amount equal to one and one-half (12) per cent of the gross receipts derived from intrastate business in this State, which payment shall be subject to the same provisions, restrictions and credits hereinafter provided in this Item.

This tax shall not apply to cities or other political subdivisions of the State owning and operating gas companies, water companies or power plants; nor shall it apply to any governmental agency of the United States.

It is the intention of this Item to levy a tax for the privilege of engaging in intrastate com-

Item O-Transportation Companies and Compensation for Use of Public Highways- (a) Transportation Companies 

Each person engaged in the business of operating a transportation company shall, for the privilege of doing such business, pay to the State for State purposes an amount equal to three (3) per cent of the gross receipts derived from intrastate business in this State. 

Within the meaning of this Item, each person operating a railroad, aeroplane, boat or barge, or an express company, or a street railway, or engaged in the business of transporting persons or property or freight for hire by motor vehicle, whether as a common carrier or as a contract hauler, shall be deemed to be a "transportation company. 

This Item shall not apply to transfer companies taxed under Item 9 (f) of this Act, nor to taxicabs taxed under Item 9 (g) of this Act.

When transportation companies are operating partly within and partly without this State, the gross receipts shall be deemed to be all receipts on business beginning and ending within this State, without entering or passing through any other State. It is the intention of this Item to levy a tax for the privilege of engaging in intrastate commerce carried on wholly within

Ch. 15) 1081 

the State and not a part of interstate commerce.

The tax hereby imposed shall be administered and collected in accordance with Article III, Section 

2, of this Act. (b) Compensation for use of Public Highways

Each person engaged in the business of operating automobile busses or motor vehicles, using the roads and highways of this State and carrying passengers for hire, whether doing interstate or intrastate business, shall, in addition to the privilege tax imposed by subsection (a) of this Item, pay as reasonable compensation for the use of the public highways the following fees:

Each bus or motor vehicle with seating or carrying capacity of eleven (11) passengers or less, per mile traveled, 1½¢ for each mile. Each bus or motor vehicle with seating or carrying capacity of more than eleven (11) passengers and not more than twenty-one passengers, per mile traveled, 2¢ for each mile.

Each bus or motor vehicle with seating or carrying capacity of twenty-one (21) passengers and less than twenty-four (24) passengers, per mile traveled, 34¢ for each mile.

Each bus or motor vehicle with seating or carrying capacity of twenty-four (24) passengers or more, per mile traveled, 1¢ for each mile.

The above compensation fees shall be paid whether the seats are occupied or not. 

Each person subject to the fees herein levied shall first obtain a license from the Commissioner of 

Finance and Taxation and shall make monthly

(Ch. 15 

reports showing accurately the number of miles traveled, and such other information as may be required by the Commissioner. Such reports shall be made on or before the 10th of each month for the preceding month. 

If any person herein required to make report shall be delinquent in making such report or in paying such fees or shall make a false or incomplete report, the Commissioner of Finance and

Taxation may apply to the Railroad and Public Utilities Commission for revocation of such person's license from such Commission. 

All penalties and remedies hereinafter set forth with reference to the collection of delinquent privilege taxes shall be applicable to the fees imposed herein provided, this Item shall not apply to street railways operating an urban transportation system with respect to such operations.

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation in the collection of said mileage fees shall keep the amounts paid by intrastate operators separate from the amount paid by interstate operators, a separate account being kept for each class of operators; and at the end of each month the amounts collected from each class of operators shall be turned into the State Treasury. 

The Treasurer shall credit to the general funds of the State such amounts as have been paid by intrastate operators, and the same shall be available for the payment of appropriations made out of said general funds; and the Treasurer shall credit to the Department of Highways and Public Works all amounts received from interstate operators under this Act and the same shall be used exclusively for the maintenance, upkeep and repair of the highways of the State.

 Item P-Workmen's Compensation Self Insurers—

ARTICLE III Administration- Section 1. Be it further enacted: 

The administration of this statute and the collection of the taxes hereby imposed are vested in the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. Any reference hereinafter to the Commissioner shall be deemed a reference to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation.

The Commissioner is hereby authorized to prescribe all rules and regulations necessary for the administration of this Act, and for the collection of the taxes hereby imposed, which rules and regulations shall be binding upon all other authorized collectors of the taxes hereby imposed,

(Ch. 15  

including the County Court Clerks. Rules and regulations not inconsistent with this law when promulgated by the Commissioner, and approved by the Attorney-General, shall have the force and effect of law. A copy of all such rules and regulations shall be furnished every County Court Clerk in printed form, and shall be furnished any taxpayer upon request.

Section 2. Be it further enacted: 

Every person exercising any privilege declared taxable by an Item providing for administration under Article III, Section 2 of this Act shall annually on or before the 1st day of August make and deliver to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, upon such forms and blanks as may be required by the Commissioner, a statement, verified by the oath of the official or agent making such report and statement, containing the following information as of the 1st day of July of the current calendar year: (a) The total gross receipts of the taxpayer for his most recently completed fiscal year from business within and without the State. (b) The total gross receipts of the taxpayer for the same period from such business within the State. (c) Such other and further information as may be deemed necessary by the Commissioner for the assessment of the taxes administered under this Section, and as may be required by the forms and blanks prescribed by the Commissioner.

Provided that the business mentioned in this Section shall be required to pay to the counties and municipalities in this State, all ad valorem taxes of every kind and character, including merchants ad valorem taxes now authorized or that may hereafter be authorized by law, and nothing in this Section shall be construed as a denial to the various counties and municipalities in this State to collect such ad valorem taxes, including merchants ad valorem taxes, from said business.

Gross receipts for the purposes of taxes administered under this Section shall mean total receipts before anything is deducted but shall not include receipts from inci-

D 

Ch. 15) 1085

dental business when such incidental business, if separately carried on, would not be subject to a tax measured by gross receipts under the provisions of this Act. 

Any person failing to file report and pay the tax found to be due in accordance with the provisions of this Section on or before August 1st of any year shall as a penalty for such failure pay an additional amount of ten (10) per cent, together with interest at the rate of six (6) per cent per annum on the total amount of the tax and penalty incurred. 

The Commissioner whenever he deems it necessary to investigate the accuracy of the statement made by any taxpayer shall have the power to send an agent or representative to inspect the books and records of the taxpayer for the purpose of determining the accuracy of the statement and reports made by such taxpayer, to secure any necessary information not disclosed by the sworn statements and to ascertain the correct tax liability. In the event any taxpayer fails or refuses to permit such agent or representative to have access to necessary books and information, then the Commissioner shall have full power and authority to compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of books and papers in the same manner as process may now be issued by the Courts to compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of books and papers. Such process shall run anywhere in the State, and shall be served by the Sheriff, or other lawful officer in any county, city or town, to whom the same may be directed. Disobedience to such process shall be treated in all respects as contempt of court and may be punished as such on the petition of the Commissioner to the Chancery Court of the county where the hearing is had. 

When any taxpayer fails or refuses to file the statement and report hereby required, the Commissioner is authorized to determine the tax liability of such taxpayer from whatever source of information may be available to the Commissioner, which assessment shall be as binding as if made upon the sworn report and statement of the taxpayer. 

Any taxpayer willfully refusing to furnish the required information shall thereafter be estopped to dispute the accuracy of the assessment made by the Commissioner.

(Ch. 15  

All the remedies given by other provisions of this Act for the collection of the various taxes hereby imposed shall be available to the Commissioner for the purposes of collecting taxes administered under this Section. 

The taxes levied by items providing for administration under Article III, Section 2, are hereby declared to be imposed for the privilege of engaging in business for the year beginning on July 1, even though such tax is made payable on the following August 1 and even though such tax is measured by gross receipts for the preceding fiscal or calendar year.

Any person who shall have been engaged in business. for less than a full year on July 1, shall, for the ensuing year, pay as follows:

The measure of the tax shall be ascertained by multiplying such person's gross receipts by the ratio which an entire year bears to the period during which he has engaged in business. 

Any person who first commences business on or after July 1, 1937, shall at the conclusion of each month report to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation his gross receipts for such month and shall pay tax, measured by such monthly gross receipts, at the rate specified in the appropriate taxing item. This tax shall be paid not later than the 10th day of the following month. On August 1 following the date when such person entered business he shall pay annual tax for the year commencing on the next prior July 1, computed according to the preceding paragraph but he shall not thereafter make monthly payments. 

Section 3. Be it further enacted: 

It shall be unlawful for any person to exercise any of the privileges made taxable by this Act before complying with the provisions of this Act. Any one exercising any of said privileges without first paying the tax or without complying with this Act shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and liable for a fine of not less than Five ($5.00) Dollars for each day such privilege is exercised without a license, which fine shall be in addition to any other penalties herein imposed. Any successor by purchase, or otherwise, of any business subject to tax shall be liable for and shall pay the

Ch. 15) 

1087 

tax imposed against such business before such successor can obtain a license to do any of the acts herein declared to be taxable.

Any person acting as agent, trustee, guardian, administrator, executor, assignee or receiver doing any of the acts herein declared to be a privilege is subject to the tax imposed on that privilege. 

Section 4. Be it further enacted: 

(a) That it shall be the duty of every official, agent or deputy charged with collecting, reporting and paying over State and County taxes, or other special revenues and privilege licenses, including fees, fines, forfeitures, costs, interests, or penalties, as now or may be hereafter prescribed by the laws of this State, to keep a complete record of such collections on books and forms prescribed by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation; that they shall report said collections, if it be State revenue, to the proper State official; and if it be county revenue, to the County Judge, or 

Chairman of the County Court, on forms prescribed and approved as herein or shall hereinafter be prescribed by the laws of this State. (b) The reports of the County Court Clerk to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall show the dates of issuance of license, the dates of the payment of the tax, the name of each person paying, the kind of such privilege paid on, the amount of privilege tax paid and the amount of ad valorem tax paid by each, respectively, the dates of the expiration of the license, and any other information called for in the form provided. (c) The collector shall make these reports within fifteen (15) days after the last day of each calendar month to the Commissioner, if it be for State revenue, and to the County Judge or Chairman of the County Court if it be for County revenue, and shall pay the amount shown to be due at the time of making the report. 

If such reports are not filed as required by law, and by this Act, and payments not made as above specified, there shall be added to the amount shown or found to be due from any such collecting official or agency a penalty of fifteen

(Ch. 15 

(15) per cent of the amount so ascertained to be due or of such delinquency.

Said penalty of fifteen (15) per cent, whether the indebtedness be due to the State and County, or State or County, shall be paid over to the State or to the proper officials thereof and for the purposes as are now or may be hereafter provided by law, and any collecting official or agency who has failed to report and pay over as required by this Act or any law of the State shall in addition to the aforesaid penalty, forfeit all commissions on said delinquent amounts. 

For good cause shown the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may relieve such delinquent official or agency of such penalty and restore the forfeited commission. (d) It shall be the duty of the Commissioner to keep permanent records, so as to make available the kind of privilege being paid, and the amount of revenue being produced from each, in every county of the State. 

Section 5. Be it further enacted: 

That for the proper enforcement of this Act the various State and county officials shall perform faithfully and punctually all the duties herein imposed on them, and specifically those hereinafter mentioned (but the enumeration of these duties shall not be construed to relieve them of any other duty imposed under this or any other Act now or hereafter in force), to wit: (a) It shall be the duty of the Commissioner of Highways and Public Works to send to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation the names of every contractor, subcontractor or material man with whom he has made any contract for public work in any county, and the date, if known, on which the work is to begin. (b) It shall be the duty of the County Judge or Chairman of the County Court and the Mayor of the City to give like notice when any such contract is made by either the county or city. (c) It shall be the duty of each agent or employee of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, specifically designated for that purpose, to visit each place of business

Ch. 15) 1089 

in his territory and to call for a production of the license for the doing of that business. The wilful failure or refusal to produce and exhibit such license, whether the tax has been paid, or not, shall constitute a misdemeanor punishable as such. If the license cannot be shown him, such agent or employee of the Commissioner shall report the name of the proprietor, the nature of the business being conducted and its location, to the County Court Clerk of the county in which such business is located, and also to the Commissioner. There upon, the Commissioner shall forthwith issue, or have issued, a distress warrant for the collection of such tax, including interest and penalty due. 

Such distress warrant may be addressed and delivered to the Sheriff or any official authorized to execute process in the county wherein such delinquent taxpayer resides or has his principal office or place of business, or to the Sheriff of any county in which the Commissioner has reason to believe property of such delinquent taxpayer may be found. 

The Sheriff into whose hands such distress warrant may come, or his deputy, may execute same by distraint and sale of personal property belonging to such delinquent taxpayer, and the proceedings in respect thereto shall be the same as are provided by law for proceedings under execution at law from a court of record; and the executing officer shall be entitled to the same fees, commissions and the necessary expense of removing and keeping property distrained as in case of an execution from a court of record. 

If the officer cannot find personal property to satisfy said distress warrant, he may levy same upon any real estate in his county belonging to such delinquent taxpayer; and if levied on land, said distress warrant, together with the officer's return thereon, shall be returned to the Circuit Court of the county, wherein the land lies, and the land shall be condemned and sold under the orders of the said Circuit Court, in the same manner as in case of a levy on land of an execution issued by a Justice of the Peace. Provided, further, that suit or suits may be brought, if necessary. 

The County Court Clerk shall have the same power with reference to the issuance of distress warrants for county revenues that is hereby given the Commissioner for State

(Ch. 15

revenues, and the County Court Clerk may at any time upon request of the Commissioner issue such distress warrants for the collection of State revenues. 

Section 6. Be it further enacted: 

It shall be the duty of each collector promptly to collect all privilege and ad valorem taxes collectible by him when the same become due; and in no case shall any collector or his deputy agree to give, permit or allow any extension of time for the payment of the same or any part thereof. 

Section 7. Be it further enacted: 

The Commissioner or any other authorized collector of the taxes herein imposed shall have the power, and it shall be his duty when he suspects any taxpayer of making a false or incomplete statement necessary for the collection of a privilege tax hereby imposed to proceed in the manner heretofore set forth in Section 2, that is to have an agent or representative investigate the books and records of such taxpayer or, in the alternative, to require the production of such books and records. 

Section 8. Be it further enacted: 

That it shall be the duty of each taxpayer promptly to pay the tax levied under this Act when the same becomes due; and in case any such tax is not paid within fifteen (15) days he shall pay a penalty of ten (10%) per cent on the amount of the delinquent tax for the first month's delinquency, or any fractional part thereof, and thereafter one (1%) per cent for each additional month or fractional part thereof delinquency. Said penalty which shall be on the total amount of tax so delinquent, whether the State and county or State or county, shall be added to the tax collected, and shall be reported and paid over to the State or to the proper officer thereof for the purposes that are now or may be hereafter provided by law. No collector, officer or governmental agency shall be authorized to waive or excuse the penalty herein provided for. 

If any officer, agent, or employe of any person subject to the provisions of this Act shall wilfully fail, refuse, or

Ch. 15) 1091 

neglect to make out, file or deliver any reports or blanks, as required by such law, or to answer any question therein propounded, or to knowingly and wilfully give a false answer to any such question wherein the fact inquired of is within his knowledge, or upon proper demand, to exhibit to the collector or any person duly authorized by him any book, paper, account, record, or memorandum of such person, in his possession or under his control, he shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and fined not less than One Hundred ($100.00) Dollars nor more than One Thousand ($1,000.00) 

Dollars for each offense.

If any person shall aid, abet, direct, cause or procure any of his officers, agents, or employes to violate any of the provisions of this Act he shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and fined not less than One Hundred ($100.00) Dollars nor more than One Thousand ($1,000.00) Dollars for each offense.

Every day during which any person subject to the provisions of this Act, or any officer, agent, or employe thereof shall wilfully fail, refuse or neglect to observe and comply with any order, direction, or mandate of the Commissioner or to perform any duty enjoined by this Act, shall constitute a separated and distinct offense. 

Section 9. Be it further enacted: 

The engaging in any business herein declared to be a taxable privilege without compliance with this law is hereby declared to be a public nuisance. 

In addition to the other remedies herein provided for the collection of the taxes hereby imposed, the Commissioner is authorized to certify to the Attorney-General the failure of any person to make any report or to pay any tax required by this Act. Thereupon, the Attorney-General shall forthwith file a bill in a court of proper jurisdiction to enjoin such person from continuing to exercise said privilege, which injunction shall remain in force so long as such person is in default. Upon the payment of such delinquent privilege tax as may be due with interest and penalty, and upon compliance with this Act the Attorney-General shall

(Ch. 15  

be authorized to dismiss said bill upon the payment of costs by the defendant.

Section 10. Be it further enacted: 

The County Court Clerks with respect to county revenues, and the officers whose duty it is to collect municipal revenues shall have the same powers with reference to the collection of such revenues as are herein vested in the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation for the collection of State revenues. None of the provisions of this Act with reference to the power or duties of the Commissioner regarding the collection of State revenues shall be held to supersede or diminish the powers or duties of the County Court Clerks regarding the collection of the State privilege taxes which are payable to the County Court Clerks. 

The various County Court Clerks charged under this Act with the duty of collecting revenue or taxes shall diligently see to it that the same are collected. It shall be the duty of each County Court Clerk to ascertain the name of every person in his county liable for the payment of any tax or revenue under this bill and it shall be his further duty to use every means at his command to collect said tax as and when due. Each County Court Clerk shall on the first of each month make a sworn report to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, giving the name of each delinquent taxpayer in his county and the amount of taxes due from such taxpayer and his reason for not having collected the same. Any County Court Clerk failing or refusing to collect any taxes or revenue with the collection of which he is charged, and which could have been collected by the exercise of due diligence, shall be liable therefor and his official bondsmen shall likewise be liable therefor. 

Section 11. Be it further enacted: 

When any taxpayer shall tender any uncertified check for payment of the tax due by him and such check shall have been returned to the office of the County Court Clerk unpaid on account of insufficient funds of the drawer of said check in the bank upon which same is drawn, then and in that event an additional tax shall be imposed equal to ten

Ch. 15) 1093 

(10%) per cent of the tax due; and in no case shall the increase of said tax because of such failure be less than One ($1.00) Dollar, and the said additional tax shall not be waived or diminished by the County Court Clerk. 

Section 12. Be it further enacted: 

Any County Court Clerk or other collecting officer who wilfully or negligently fails to carry out the provisions of this Act by making an incorrect assessment, or failing in any way, either in person or by agent, to faithfully enforce this Act shall forfeit in each case the sum of Two-hundred and fifty ($250.00) Dollars to the State of Tennessee, and shall be subject to ouster proceedings. On complaint of the 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, this Section shall be enforced by the Attorney-General in any manner permitted by law. 

Section 13. Be it further enacted: 

If any sheriff of this State shall wilfully fail, refuse or neglect to execute any distress warrant directed to him within the time provided in this Act, the official bond of such sheriff shall be liable for the tax, penalty, interest, and cost due by the taxpayer, and on complaint of any proper officer this penalty shall be enforced by the Attorney-General of the State in any manner permitted by law. 

Section 14. Be it further enacted: 

That no contract heretofore made, or hereafter made, by persons engaged in a business or occupation subject to a license or privilege tax, under this or any other Act, shall be invalid or unenforceable in the Courts because of the failure of such person to have paid such license tax at the time such contract was made or was performed; provided, that such person shall prior to the date of adjudication in the Court of original jurisdiction pay double the tax due at the time the contract was made and in addition thereto the penalty prescribed by law. 

Section 15. Be it further enacted: 

That whenever it shall satisfactorily appear to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation that a license tax, privi-

(Ch. 15 

lege tax, inheritance tax or other tax has been erroneously or illegally collected for the use and benefit of the State, by any county or State official, department, or department head, agent, or attorney, the said Commissioner, with the approval of Attorney-General, is hereby authorized and empowered to adjust, settle and order the refunding of the taxes so collected and to direct the Comptroller to draw his warrant in settlement of the same. 

The Commissioner shall have no power to order any refund unless claim for the same, supported by proper proof, shall have been made within one year from the date of payment.

Section 16. Be it further enacted: 

That it shall be the duty of each Judge of the Courts of the State having a criminal jurisdiction to especially give in charge to and have a Grand Jury of his Court especially investigate all the offenses defined in this Act, and inquisitorial powers are hereby given to Grand Juries in the premises. It shall be the duty of the respective District 

Attorneys of the State, upon the information or at the request of any reputable citizen of the State, to investigate and prosecute ex officio all the offenses defined in this Act. 

Section 17. Be it further enacted: 

That nothing in this Act shall be construed as licensing any character of business that is now or may hereafter become unlawful.

Section 18. Be it further enacted: 

If any part, section, provision or clause of this Act shall be unconstitutional it shall not affect the validity of any other part or provisions hereof. 

Section 19. Be it further enacted: 

That sufficient funds are hereby appropriated to the Department of Finance and Taxation out of funds collected under this Act, for the collection of the taxes herein imposed.

Ch. 15) 1095 

 Section 20. Be it further enacted: 

That all laws and parts of laws in conflict with this Act be and the same are hereby repealed, and this Act shall take effect from and after April 1st, 1937, the public welfare requiring it. 

Passed March 4, 1937.

BEER PRIVILEGE TAX Chapter 115, Acts of 1933 

An Act levying and providing for the collection of a special privilege tax for general State purposes on the sale, storage, manufacture and/or distribution of beer or other beverages of like alcoholic content; and authorizing the various counties and municipalities of the State to levy and collect a like privilege tax. 

Section 1: 

That the engaging in or carrying on by any person, firm, corporation, joint stock company, syndicate and/or association of the sale, storage, manufacture and/or distribution of beer, or other beverages of like alcoholic content as authorized by Chapter 69, Public Acts of 1933, or by any other Acts, as hereby declared to be a privilege and there is levied on each and every such privilege for general State purposes the following taxes, which shall be paid to the County Court Clerk of the county in which such privilege is exercised, in the manner and form provided by law for the collection of such revenue: 

I. 

In Counties or Cities of 100,000 or over: (a) Wherever such beer or other beverage is sold, stored for sale, manufactured and/or distributed for consumption off the premises where sold, and not to be consumed on said premises (b) Wherever such beer or other beverage is sold, stored for sale, manufactured and/or distributed for consumption on the premises where sold, except as provided in (c) and (d) below (c) Wherever such beer or other beverage is sold, stored for sale or distributed in any hotel, boarding house or tourist camp (d) Each brewer on each brewery and/or each agent or distributor at wholesale for any such brewer $ 5.00 10.00 25.00 300.00

(Ch. 15

 II. 

In Counties and Cities of less than 100,000 population: (a) Wherever such beer or other beverage is sold, stored for sale, 5.00 manufactured and/or distributed for consumption off the premises where sold, and not to be consumed on said premises .$ 2.50 (b) Wherever such beer or other beverage is sold, stored for sale, manufactured and/or distributed for consumption on the premises where sold, except as provided in (c) and (d) below (c) Wherever such beer or other beverage is sold, stored for sale or distributed in any hotel, boarding house or tourist camp, each (d) Any brewer on each brewery and/or each agent or distributor at wholesale for any such brewer 12.50 150.00 "Provided, that any agent or distributor of beer at wholesale for a brewer who pays the brewer's tax as above set out the tax imposed by Chapter 69 of the Acts of 1933 shall pay only one-fourth of the tax levied in paragraphs 

(d), Sections I and II hereof." 

Provided, further, that any agent or distributor of beer at wholesale for a brewer who pays the brewer's tax as above set out and the tax imposed by Chapter 69 of the Acts of 1933, when such agent or distributor pays the tax as set out in the proviso next above in the County or City where he has his situs or principal place of business, such agent or distributor shall not be liable for any other State tax in any other County or City in which he does business but shall be liable for a County and municipal tax in such additional County or City for an amount not to exceed $10.00 to any such County and/or City. 

And, provided, further, that a warehouseman having an established place of business who merely stores for the agent distributor or owner paying the taxes provided by this Act shall not be liable for the tax hereunder. 

Section 2: 

That each County and municipality of the State is hereby authorized to levy a like privilege tax on the privileges enumerated in Section 1 of this Act but not to exceed the amounts levied for State purposes in Section 1. 

Section 3: 

That said tax shall be payable annually in advance to the various County Court Clerks of the State in the County

Ch. 15) 1097 

where said privilege is exercised, and the same cannot be paid for a shorter period of time than one year. When the tax on said privilege is levied by any municipality of the State, the same shall be collected by said municipality and paid to the proper tax collecting official thereof. 

When said tax is levied by any County and/or City of the State, the same shall be in lieu of all other taxes that any such County and/or City may levy and collect on the privilege herein defined; but the taxes provided and authorized by this Act shall not be in lieu of those imposed by Chapter 69, Public Acts of 1933; nor shall the privilege taxes herein levied be in lieu of any other privilege taxes payable by any person engaged in any of the businesses declared a privilege and taxed under any general revenue law of the State.

The tax herein levied shall be enforced and collected in the same manner as other privilege taxes under any general revenue law of the State. 

Section 4: 

That this Act take effect from and after its passage, the public welfare requiring it.

MANUFACTURE OF LIQUORS PRIVILEGE TAX 

Chapter 193, Acts of 1937 

An Act to be entitled An Act to permit, authorize and make lawful the manufacture of intoxicating liquors and other intoxicating drinks within the State of Tennessee; and to make lawful the possession, storing and transporting the products thereof, upon certain conditions.

Section 1: 

That the Quarterly County Court of any County within the State of Tennessee shall have the right and power; and, it shall be the duty of said county authorities to call an election, at any time, upon the filing and presentation of a petition bearing the genuine signatures of ten per cent. or more, of the qualified voters of such county, based upon the number of votes cast in the last preceding presidential election in said county. Said petition to be addressed to the Quarterly Court of said County, and to contain such

Ch. 15) 1099 

language as to request, or call upon the said Quarterly County Court, to call an election of the qualified voters of said county upon the question of permitting and legalizing the manufacture of intoxicating liquors and other intoxicating drinks without the boundaries of said county. 

Upon the adoption of a motion, or resolution, by the Quarterly County Court ordering, or calling, an election, as hereinbefore provided, a copy of said motion, or resolution, shall be made and certified to by the County Court Clerk, and filed immediately with the Chairman of the County Election Commission; and, it shall, then, be the duty of the said County Election Commission, in and for said county to order and call an election, to be held in said county; the same to be ordered within 30 days after the filing of the certified copy of the motion, or resolution, as above provided. Said election to be held in accordance with the law as provided for other general elections in the county. The ballots to be used in said election to be provided and distributed by said County Election Commissioners, at the expense of the county, and shall have placed upon the ballots, the words "For Manufacturing Liquors" and the words "Against Manufacturing Liquors," and the voters shall prepare and cast their ballots by placing a "X" mark opposite the "For" or "Against" intoxicating liquors, as he desires to vote.

If a majority of the qualified votes cast in said election, in a county, so holding an election, favor the manufacture of intoxicating liquors or other intoxicating drinks, as herein provided, in that event, it shall be lawful to manufacture intoxicating liquors and/or intoxicating drinks within the boundaries of said county. But, before anyone shall engage in said manufacturing of such intoxicants, within a county, a privilege tax shall be paid, in the sum of 

One Thousand Dollars ($1,000.00) to the State of Tennessee and to the county in which said manufacturing plant is located; and a license shall issue by the Department of 

Finance and Taxation of the State and by the County Court of such county as authorized the operation of said manufacturing business within the boundaries of said county. 

And, if said manufacturing plant is located within the

(Ch. 15 

boundaries of a municipality, likewise a privilege tax of 

One Thousand Dollars ($1,000.00) shall be paid to the municipality, and a license also shall issue by the proper authorities of said municipality, authorizing said manufacturing plant to operate. 

Provided, That nothing in this Act shall be construed as licensing or legalizing the sale of intoxicating liquors and/ or other intoxicating drinks within the State of Tennessee by any distillery or manufacturing plant authorized under this Act.

Provided, further, that nothing in this Act shall be construed so as to repeal, or in any manner abridge or affect the present laws of the State of Tennessee against the sale of intoxicating liquors of every kind. 

Section 2: 

That intoxicating liquors and/or intoxicating drinks, as herein defined, shall be interpreted to mean and include alcohol, spirits, wines, liquors and every liquid or solid, patented or not, containing alcohol, spirits, liquor or wine, and capable of being consumed by human beings; but, nothing herein shall be construed, or defined, as including or relating to the manufacture of any beverage with alcohol content of five per cent (5%) or less.

Section 3: 

That it shall not be unlawful, but shall be legal for the owner and/or operator of said manufacturing plant, as herein provided, to possess, store or transport the products of said manufacturing plant within, over and across the State of Tennessee, provided, that the storing herein provided for shall be within the county authorizing the operation of said manufacture of said intoxicants; and, the possession shall be limited to warehouses of said manufacturers in the counties authorizing the same, and while being transported to points outside of the State. And, it shall be lawful for common carriers to accept for shipment, and to transport the products of said manufacturing plants to points outside of the State of Tennessee, but not to points within said State.

Ch. 15) 1101 

 Section 4: 

That this Act take effect from and after its passage, the public welfare requiring it. 

COLLECTION OF DELINQUENT PRIVILEGE TAXES Chapter 200, Acts of 1937 

An Act to provide for the collection of delinquent privilege taxes by the issuance of distress warrants by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and to prescribe the procedure with reference thereto. 

Section 1: 

That the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation with reference to privilege taxes collected by him is hereby authorized, and it shall be his duty to issue a distress warrant for the collection of the tax, interest and penalty due from each delinquent taxpayer upon delinquency of payment of such tax. Said distress warrant may be addressed and delivered to the sheriff of the county wherein such delinquent taxpayer has his office or principal place of business, or to the sheriff of any county in which the Commissioner has reason to believe property of such delinquent taxpayers may be found.

Section 2: 

That the sheriff into whose hands such warrant may come, or his deputy, may execute same by distraint and sale of personal property belonging to such delinquent taxpayer, and the proceedings in respect thereto shall be the same as are provided by law for proceedings under an execution at law from a court of record; and the executing officer shall be entitled to the same fees, commissions, and necessary expense of removing and keeping property distrained as in case of an execution from a court of record. 

Section 3: 

That if the officer cannot find personal property to satisfy said distress warrant, he may levy same upon any

(Ch. 15  

real estate in his county belonging to such delinquent taxpayers; and if levied on land, said distress warrant, together with the officer's return thereon, shall be returned to the Circuit Court of the county wherein the land lies, and the land shall be condemned and sold under the orders of said Circuit Court in the same manner as in case of the levy on land of an execution issued by a Justice of the Peace. 

Section 4: 

That the remedy or procedure herein prescribed is cumulative to any other remedies or procedures now prescribed with reference to any particular privilege tax or taxes. No other remedy prescribed by any particular taxing statute shall be held to be exclusive or to prevent the Commissioner from proceeding with the collection of the privilege tax under the provisions of this Act. 

Section 5: 

That this Act shall take effect from and after its passage, the public welfare requiring it. 

FERMENTED APPLE JUICE NON-TAXABLE Chapter 250, Acts of 1937 

An Act entitled an Act to make non-taxable the storing, selling, distributing, or manufacturing of pure fermented apple juice, and to repeal all laws and parts of laws in conflict therewith. 

Section 1: 

That hereafter the storing, selling, distributing and manufacturing of pure fermented apple juice shall not be taxable in Tennessee.

Section 2; 

That all laws and parts of laws in conflict therewith, be, and the same are hereby repealed and that this Act take effect from and after its passage, the public welfare requiring the same.

Article 1-Section 1. 

1237 1238 1238 1239 Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of Tennessee, That the following definitions and general provisions shall apply in all cases, unless otherwise provided in special cases but the general provisions shall not be deemed to control specific provisions to the contrary in any particular taxing item, to-wit: (a) Whenever the word "person" or the word "taxpayer'' is used in this Act it shall be construed to include every individual, partnership, firm, corporation or any other association of any kind. The singular pronoun "he," " "him," etc., shall include the plural "they," "them,'' etc., whenever necessary. (b) The word "city" or "cities" when the same may be material in determining the rate of a State or County tax shall include one mile of territory adjoining the corporate limits of any incorporated city, but it is not intended to give any city the right to tax privileges exercised at locations beyond its corporate limits. (c) Whenever the word "collector' is used in this Act it shall mean every officer or employe of the state, county, or city authorized to collect the tax. (d) Whenever the "Federal Census" is referred to in this Act, the Federal Census of 1930 or any subsequent Federal Census is meant, and when taxes are graduated according to "population" the population according to the said Federal Census shall be used in determining the tax. (e) The words "per annum" designate the amount of the tax to be paid for exercising the privilege for twelve months; and such words are to be read into every taxing item where the specific context does not indicate the contrary.

Where a privilege tax is referred to as an "annual tax,'' such reference is intended to mean a privilege tax obtained for, or renewed for, a period of not more nor less than one year. (f) Every person taxed "per annum'' shall have the right to pay the tax quarterly, when the item levying such tax does not expressly require payment for a full year. Where quarterly payment is made such person shall receive a license for three months. If still in business at the expiration of such license he shall renew it. Such renewal shall be made in like manner and on the payment of the same fees as on the issuance of the original license.

Every person having an unexpired license under any prior General Revenue Bill shall, at the date when this Act becomes effective, be required to secure a license under this Act, if this Act increases the rate of taxation upon such privilege. However, such person when applying for license

Ch. 15) 1107 

under this Act shall be credited with the ratable proportion of the unexpired license in computing his license tax under this Act. (g) Unless some other collector is expressly designated, the county court clerk shall collect the taxes herein imposed on privileges and shall report to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. (h) The license given by the county court clerk shall be sufficient evidence of a compliance with this law, without the countersignature or certification by the circuit court clerk or any other official. (i) Any person liable for any tax herein imposed doing business in any unincorporated town or in a rural district, shall pay the tax imposed upon the like business done in the city of the smallest population, when such tax is graduated according to the population of cities. (j) Every person conducting business from more than one established place of business in a county shall be liable for the privilege tax on business done at each place and must secure a separate license for each place of business.

If he conducts business from an established place of business in more than one county he shall pay the State privilege tax in each county and each county in which he maintains an established place of business shall be authorized to levy a county tax upon each such establishment in accordance with sub-section (1) hereof. 

If he maintains only one place of business in a county, from that place extending his operations into adjoining counties without establishing a place of business or a branch office in such adjoining counties, he shall be liable for both State and county tax in the county where the place of business is located but only for the county tax in any other county. (k) Any tax imposed by this Act shall not be held to supersede any other privilege tax imposed upon such taxpayer or occupation by any other Act, either special or general, except those imposed exclusively by the terms of Chapter 13, Acts of the Second Extra Session of 1931 and amendments thereto. (1) Each county and incorporated city is hereby authorized and empowered to levy a privilege tax upon merchants and other such vocations, occupations or businesses declared to be privileges in this Act, to be levied in the same manner and not to exceed in amount the tax levied by the State, except as otherwise stated, in this or any other Act. (m) Any person doing an act herein declared to be a privilege, shall be deemed to be doing business within the meaning of this Act. If he claims exemption for any reason, his rights shall be determined as hereinafter provided:

Any disabled ex-soldier, sailor or marine of any war in which the United States has been engaged, or any peace-time soldier, sailor or marine who was disabled while in regular service, owning less than $1,000.00 of property above encumbrances thereon and doing business with a capital stock of not exceeding $600.00, residing within and being a citizen of the 

State of Tennessee and of the County in which the exemption shall be claimed, being the sole beneficiary of said business shall be exempt from the payment of the privilege tax herein imposed on such business. 

Provided that only one exemption from privilege tax can be claimed by one person under this exemption. Provided further that said business is conducted by the ex-soldier, etc., or a member of his immediate family. 

No ex-service man claiming exemption under this paragraph shall be permitted to operate as a peddler more than one truck. 

The county court clerk of the several counties shall require said exsoldier to make an affidavit setting out his financial condition, and the source of his income before said license shall be issued, and any person making a false affidavit and procuring a free privilege license thereby shall be guilty of perjury and punished under the law. The county court clerk shall receive only a fee of 50 cents for issuing a license to such soldier. 

That all persons being unable to see by reason of total blindness, own-

(Ch. 15  

ing less than $2,500.00 of property above encumbrances thereon and doing business with a capital not exceeding $2,500.00 residing within and being a citizen of Tennessee and of the county in which the exemption shall be claimed, and being the sole beneficiary of said business, shall be exempt from the payment of the privilege tax herein imposed. No person claiming exemption under this paragraph shall be permitted to operate more than one place of business without the payment of privilege taxes. 

The county court clerk of the several counties shall require said applicant who wishes to seek the benefit of the exemptions under this provision, to make an affidavit setting out his disability and his financial condition and the source of his income before said license shall be issued, and any person making a false affidavit and procuring a free privilege license thereby, shall be guilty of perjury and punished under the law. (n) Each person engaged in a single business, which business might fall under two or more items of Section 1 of this bill, shall pay the highest tax imposed by such items, but only one tax. This provision shall not be construed to permit any person to exercise two or more taxable privileges by the payment of only one tax. 

The definitions and general provisions apply in all cases; however, the specific provisions of a taxing item control, even though such provisions may be contrary to the definitions and general provisions. 

PERSON or TAXPAYER includes individuals, part nerships, firms, corporations, associations and all other types of organizations exercising the taxable privilege in Tennessee.

CITY or CITIES includes the territory extending for a distance of one mile from the corporate limits of any incorporated city for the State tax, however, it includes only the territory within the corporate limits for the city tax. "This provision has never been construed to authorize the collection of municipal privilege taxes from businesses located beyond the city limits." (Opinion of Attorney-General to City Clerk, Cleveland, Tennessee, dated 

January 6, 1937.)

COLLECTOR includes any authorized officer or employee of the State, County or City. 

FEDERAL CENSUS means the census taken by the 

United States in 1930.

PER ANNUM means 12 months and is to be read into, or considered as a part, of every taxing item unless otherwise provided in the specific taxing item. 

ANNUAL TAX means that the tax imposed in the specific taxing item must be paid for a full year (12 months) at one time. Where the specific taxing item imposes an annual tax such tax cannot be paid on a quarterly basis.

Ch. 15) 1109 

SPECIFIC TAXING ITEMS imposing a tax per annum may be paid quarterly unless the provisions of the specific taxing item requires payment for a full year (12 months). "When the tax becomes delinquent the County Court Clerk may collect from the taxpayer a quarterly fee plus the penalty for that quarter, but the taxpayer must request such quarterly license, and if he does not, then the penalty for the annual tax should be collected. This is based on the fact that all privilege taxes are levied for one year and the payment of privilege taxes quarterly is an exception to the provisions of the act.”- 

(Opinion of Attorney General to Department of Finance and Taxation dated May 29, 1933.)

This act requires all persons engaged in a taxable vocation or business to secure a license upon the effective date of this act, or April 1st, 1937. Taxpayers who have paid tax under prior General Revenue Acts are to be given credit, for the taxes so paid, against the taxes imposed in this Act (Chapter 108, Acts of 1937 as amended). 

This procedure is necessary for the reason that many of the tax rates in the new Act have been increased. "Furthermore, there is no doubt that if a privilege tax be increased during the licensed period the taxpayer must pay the increased tax. However, in the present case the increased tax represents merely a difference between the sum already paid and the aggregate sum required to be paid for the two privileges."- -(Opinion of Attorney General dated June 25, 1935.)

The privilege taxes imposed for the State of Tennessee are to be paid to the County Court Clerk of the county in which the taxpayer engages in the taxable vocation of business unless otherwise provided in the specific taxing item. The taxes imposed under the provisions of Article 

II, Section 2 of this Act are not to be paid to County Court Clerks, but should be paid direct in accordance with the terms of those specific taxing items and Section 2 of Article II.

The license issued by County Court Clerks is sufficient evidence of compliance with this Act and the countersignature of other State, County or City officials are not required. Taxpayers should be careful to preserve all "licenses" or "tax receipts" issued by the County Court 

Clerk and City Clerk.

Persons engaged in a taxable vocation or business lo-

(Ch. 15  

cated in unincorporated towns or in a rural district must pay privilege tax based upon the population of the smallest incorporated city, provided, the tax is graduated according to population. While this Section does not so state, it is ordinarily understood that the population of the smallest incorporated city within the county is used as the measure of the tax. "Any person liable for any privilege tax doing business in an unincorporated town shall pay the tax imposed on the same business done in the city of the smallest population when the tax is graduated according to the population of cities." (Opinion of Attorney-General dated July 

21, 1937.)

Persons engaged in a taxable vocation or business in more than one established place in the same county are liable for the tax at each such place of business; to illustrate, should a person operate a Beauty Parlor in Nashville, with an established branch located in Old Hickory, the tax would be payable to the State, County and Cities for each established place of business. 

Persons engaged in a taxable vocation or business in more than one county, and having an established place of business in each county, are liable for the tax, on each such place of business, to both the State and the counties. However, if only one established place of business is maintained and operations therefrom extended into other counties without establishing a place of business in such other county or counties, such person would be liable for State and county tax in the county in which the established place of business is located and county tax (but not State) in such other county or counties. "The bill does provide that where a person maintains only one established place of business and pays State and county privilege taxes upon such place of business, then operations can be extended into adjoining counties without incurring any liability for additional State taxes. In this latter case, only additional county taxes must be paid. However, every established place of business, whether in the same county or in different counties, must pay a State privilege tax upon each such establishment where the occupation pursued is a taxable privilege." (Opinion of Attorney-General, dated February 19, 1937.)

The privilege taxes levied in this act do not supersede other privilege taxes imposed by other laws of Tennessee. 

Counties and incorporated cities are authorized to impose

Ch. 15) 1111 

tax on the same privileges; however, such tax cannot exceed the tax imposed upon the same privilege, under the terms of this Act, for the benefit of the State. Counties and cities are prohibited to impose the same or similar taxes as are imposed for the State under the terms of Article II, Section 

2 of this Act.

It appears that the governing bodies of counties and cities must levy the tax by proper resolution or ordinance before such taxes can be lawfully collected; "The various quarterly courts through the State and the cities by proper resolution and city ordinance should levy the tax, if they desire to do so, before the same can be lawfully collected." (Opinion of Attorney- 

General, dated February 11, 1932.)

The doing of an act declared to be a privilege is defined to be "doing business" within the meaning of the Act and subjects such person doing the act to the tax or taxes imposed; however, under certain conditions, disabled exsoldiers and totally blind persons are exempt from the payment of privilege tax imposed by this Act. Before exemption is allowed an "ex-soldier," he must make, and file with the Clerk of the County Court, an affidavit setting forth the following: 

1. That he is a disabled ex-soldier, sailor or marine of a war in which the 

United States was engaged, or that he was disabled while in regular service. 

2. That he owns less than $1,000.00 of property free of debt. 

3. That his "capital stock" does not exceed $600.00. 

4. That he resides in and is a citizen of Tennessee and of the county in which the exemption is sought. 

5. That he is the sole beneficiary of such business. 

The business must be conducted by the ex-soldier or a member of his immediate family and only one exemption from tax can be claimed.

Before exemption is allowed a blind person he must make and file with the Clerk of the County Court an affidavit setting forth the following: 

1. That he is unable to see by reason of total blindness. 

2. That he owns less than $2,500.00 of property free of debt. 

3. That his "capital stock" does not exceed $2,500.00. 

4. That he resides in and is a citizen of Tennessee. 

5. That he is the sole beneficiary of such business.

(Ch. 15  

A person claiming exemption under this Section will not be permitted to operate more than one place of business without payment of tax. "—And must be the sole beneficiary of said business. Under the provisions last referred to it is clear that no person can hire others to engage in taxable businesses and confer upon such others his own tax immunity.' 

(Opinion of Attorney-General, dated June 14, 1935.) 

"You are further advised that no person can claim more than one exemption from privilege tax under the Revenue Act of 1932 as amended. 

If a person engages in more than one taxable privilege the exemption provision has been exhausted when it has been claimed by such person for one of the taxable privileges in which such person engages. "" (Opinion of 

Attorney-General, dated August 3, 1935.)

Persons engaged in a single business or vocation which may fall under two or more taxing items, such person is required to pay the highest tax, however, a person engaged in operating a soda fountain and also selling cigars, cigarettes and tobacco would be taxable for both privileges separately. "The general rule of law is that where a person engages in two or more taxable privileges such person must pay privilege tax for each and every privilege exercised. The exception to this rule is that when a person engages in one taxable privilege, securing license therefor, such person is entitled to do those things which are strictly and genuinely incidental to the taxable privilege without securing another and separate license.' 

(Opinion of Attorney-General, dated October 5, 1935.) 

"One may not engage in two activities, one of which is non-taxable and the other of which is taxable, and claim exemption from the taxable privilege upon the theory that the main activity is the non-taxable one. 

The subterfuge referred to in no way excuses payment of the privilege tax imposed upon peddlers." (Opinion of Attorney-General, dated July 5, 1935.)
