Item 9-Automobiles— 

(a) Dealers 

Dealers are defined to be persons who maintain an office or place of business in Tennessee as an agent or representative of any manufacturer or jobber of automobiles, trucks, or parts. "" -This Motor Company keeps cars upon the premises and has salesmen working the territory. Under these facts it is difficult to say that they have not an established place of business in Jackson, Tennessee, and the conclusion necessarily follows that this Company is liable for the privilege tax.'' (Opinion of Attorney-General, dated September 29, 1934.)

(Ch. 15  

The tax is graduated on the population of the city in which such business is conducted as follows: 

Less than 1,000 

1,000 to 4,999 

5,000 to 24,999 

25,000 to 49,999 

50,000 to 99,999 100,000 and over Agents and salesmen, each $ 15.00 20.00 35.00 60.00 75.00 100.00 10.00

The tax imposed upon agents and salesmen does not apply to the agents or salesmen of dealers who have paid the tax herein imposed upon dealers. "A salesman who confines his business to representing a dealer in a county where the dealer has paid a privilege tax is exempt from both State and County tax, but when he extended his business into another county, he incurs liability for the county privilege tax to such other county. 

He does not incur liability for the State privilege tax because only one State privilege tax is due from him under any circumstance and he is exempt from such tax when representing a dealer who has paid the dealer's privilege tax.'' 

(Opinion of Attorney-General, dated February 26, 1934.) 

Persons buying and selling used or second hand automobiles or parts as their principal, or incidental to their principal, business are taxed under the provisions of this subsection of Item 9. 

"A wholesale secondhand automobile dealer who comes into Tennessee from another state not over twice a year and purchases ten or fifteen automobiles a trip, and ships them immediately out of the State, is subject to a privilege tax. (Opinion of Attorney-General, dated May 24, 1937.) -Automobile dealers selling secondhand cars adjacent to and as an adjunct of their new car business are not liable to an additional tax on the used car business.'' (See B. & B. Chevrolet Company, et al vs. Harvey 

Hall, Clerk, decided November 21, 1936, Tennessee Supreme Court.) -A company which pays a privilege tax as a security dealer is not authorized to engage in the business of selling automobiles even though the only automobiles sold are those which the company takes possession of where there is a default in the payment of a loan secured by such automobile. 

Such a corporation is liable for the privilege tax imposed on automobile dealers.'' 

(Opinion of Attorney-General, dated October 23, 1935.) 

Attention is drawn to the fact that since the decision in the case of B. & B. Chevrolet Company vs. Hall, supra, this item was amended and it now appears a person selling secondhand cars as an adjunct of his new car business would be taxable if such business is conducted at a place other than the principal place of business. 

The tax is imposed upon each place of business, however, if the business is conducted at more than one place of

Ch. 15) 1121 

business within a county, such additional place or places of business is taxable at one-half of the tax set forth in this item. Separate places of business located in different counties would be subject to both State and county tax. "It is my opinion that in the case of the X Company we can reach no other conclusion that they have four principal places of business in Tennessee and that they would be liable for the full tax in each of those principal places of business.'' (Opinion of Attorney-General, dated May 13, 1936.) 

(b) Repair Shops, etc. 

The tax is imposed on persons operating automobile repair and paint shops and battery stations. The tax is graduated on the number of men working in such repair or paint shop as follows: 

2 men or less 

3 to 4 men 

5 to 9 men 

10 to 19 men 

20 and over $ 5.00 10.00 20.00 40.00 60.00 

In counting workmen, the shop owner is to be included if such owner does shop work. 

Filling stations re-charging batteries are subject to a $5.00 tax, provided such station does not deal in batteries. "You are advised that an automobile dealer who has paid the privilege tax required of such dealer is not liable for a separate privilege tax for operating an automobile repair shop as an integral part of his business. 

This was decided by the Supreme Court of Tennessee in the case of Knox ville Motor Company vs. Kennedy, 165 Tennessee 412." (Opinion by At torney-General, dated August 24, 1936.) "The privilege tax on repair shops carries with it the privilege of keeping in stock parts and accessories which are needed to make repairs.'' 

(Opinion of Attorney-General, dated July 23, 1935.) 

Obviously, this item applies exclusively to independent repair and paint shops; i.e. shops not engaged in the sale of automobiles, parts or accessories.

The tax is graduated on the number of automobiles and trucks which such terminal may accommodate as follows:

Less than 10 vehicles 10 to 14 vehicles 15 to 19 vehicles $ 50.00 100.00 150.00 20 or more vehicles 200.00

The tax is measured by the number of automobiles or trucks which the terminal can accommodate at one time; i.e. if the terminal capacity is 15 vehicles the State tax would be $150.00.

Terminal is defined to mean a place where automobiles or trucks meet to take on or discharge passengers or freight. The tax does not apply to a terminal used exclusively by one person; however, if such terminal is used in common by several persons, and at common expense, the tax applies. "The State privilege tax upon a terminal accommodating 15 and not more than 20 automobiles or trucks is $150.00 per annum. Both the county and city are authorized to levy a like tax and no doubt both have done so.' 

(Opinion of Attorney-General, dated January 14, 1937.) 

"-A ticket station where passengers buy tickets and can wait for the arrival of the bus along the line, perhaps in a hotel, drug store, or filling station or some other building is not a terminal within the meaning of sub-section (d) Item 9 of the General Revenue Bill." (Opinion of Attor ney-General, dated February 13, 1932.)

One delivery yard may be maintained separate and apart from the main office or yard without additional tax; however, if more than one such yard is operated, an additional tax of one-tenth of the above tax must be paid for each yard.

Persons selling "sack coal" exclusively are subject to tax of only $10.00. "The file reveals that the X coal company maintains coal yards in each of the four divisions of the city-At each of these yards sales of coal are made. There is only one general office for the various coal yards- 

Under the facts stated you are advised that in my opinion the X coal company is not subject to the privilege tax upon chain stores."' (Opinion of Attorney-General, dated June 21, 1937). "If a person from Virginia brings coal into Tennessee and thereafter sells it by peddling or otherwise, such business is not interstate commerce. The distinction turns upon whether or not the sale and delivery of the coal in Tennessee were pursuant to a contract made prior to its importation into Tennessee. You are advised that if the person about whom you enquire is peddling coal in Tennessee or is selling it after the coal was brought into this State there is liability for privilege tax." 

(Opinion of Attorney-General, dated January 15, 1937). 

"-Obviously, defendant in the prosecution of his business is not excepted from the payment of this privilege tax. It is admitted that his mine is in Campbell County and that he has been selling and delivering coal in Knox County.-Nevertheless he was not entitled to sell coal without a license in any county other than the county in which his mine was located." (See Spurling vs. State, Tennessee Supreme Court, filed May 

2, 1936). "A chemical company doing business in this State cannot sell coal to its employees without incurring liability for the privilege tax of a coal dealer.'' (Opinion of Attorney-General, dated September 13, 1935). 

The revenue derived by the State under this taxing item was approximately $22,000.00 during the fiscal year 193536.

Item 25-Collection, Adjusting, or Forwarding 

Agencies- 

2. Tax must be paid (a) Annually only

The tax is imposed on persons engaged in business as collection, adjusting, or forwarding agents or agencies, and is measured by gross collections with a minimum tax graduated on population of the city in which such business is operated. The rate of tax is one-third of one per cent of the gross collections, while the minimum tax is as follows: 

Less than 50,000 

50,000 and over $100.00 300.00

The minimum tax is payable on or before January 1 of each year and cannot be paid on a quarterly or semi-annual basis. Before a license can be issued the applicant must file a solvent surety bond in the sum of $1,000.00 with the 

County Court Clerk conditioned for the payment of the tax of ½ of 1% of gross collections. At the time the license is issued, he must pay any tax which may be due for the preceding year, based on gross collections. 

The tax applies to justices of the peace, deputy sheriffs, constables, solicitors for accounts, and adjusters of accounts.

Associations of credit men may pay a minimum tax of $100.00 plus the tax of 1/2 of 1% of gross collections, while associations of doctors, dentists, lawyers, architects and

(Ch. 15 

other professional men pay 2 of the gross collection tax and no minimum tax. 

The revenue derived by the State under this taxing item was approximately $1,400.00 during the fiscal year 19351936.

5, 1935). "However, in this connection let me call your attention to the decided distinction between contractors and construction companies. Contractors are defined as being those persons who construct railroads and public roads in this State and they do not fall within the head of construction companies, which latter class of persons must take out a license in each county and for an entire year. On the contrary, since there is no

Ch. 15) 1141 

such provision with reference to the license against contractors, these parties may take out licenses quarterly and are required to have only one State license but a county license in each county in which they do business.' 

(Opinion of Attorney-General, dated May 28, 1935). 

The tax is graduated on the aggregate contract price for construction during any 12 months period as follows: 

Less than $10,000.00 $ 10,000.01 to $49,999.99 

50,000.01 to $99,999.99 

100,000.01 to $249,999.99

The county tax is at the above classified rates but applies only to the aggregate contract price for work done in the particular county.

Persons applying for license as construction companies must pay the minimum amount ($10.00) and enter into a bond, approved by the County Court Clerk, in the sum of $400.00 conditioned for the payment of the additional amount which may be due at the end of 12 months from the date of the issuance of the minimum license. The provisions of the item apply to sub-contractors and no deduction for work re-sub-contracted can be deducted in computing the aggregate contract price. Within 15 days after the end of the 12 months period an accurate statement, made under oath, must be filed with the County Court Clerk showing the aggregate contract price of work performed during the preceding 12 months and the additional tax, if any, must be paid.

The revenue derived by the State under this taxing item was approximately $9,500 during the fiscal year 1935-36.

 Item 29-Cotton Buyers or Cotton Factors or

Merchants paying ad valorem and merchants' privilege tax are not liable for this tax. "" -It has just been called to my attention that I had overlooked the provisions of Chapter 93, Public Acts of 1933, which provides in part that such co-operative associations may also buy, sell and deal in agricultural products of non-members to an amount not greater in value than such as are handled by it for its members.' The above quoted amendment embodied in the Acts of 1933 was evidently intended to meet the situation of the tax covered by my previous opinion. I therefore correct my previous opinion in this regard and hold that a cooperative can lawfully engage in the purchase of products from non-members to an amount not greater in value than such as are handled by it for its members. Since the cooperative association has authority under the amendatory act of 1933 to handle products of non-members, it would not be subject to the tax on cotton buyers or cotton factors-It being provided by Section 3828 of the Code that such association shall pay an annual fee of ten dollars only 'in lieu of all franchise or license or corporation or other privilege taxes.''' 

(Opinion of Attorney-General, dated November 22, 1934). 

The revenue derived by the State under this taxing item was approximately $5,500.00 during the fiscal year 1935-36.

A gas filling station is defined to be any place where petroleum products or substitutes therefor, are sold or

Ch. 15) 1153 

offered for sale and delivered direct to the motor driven vehicle as a fuel for same. "The question is whether item 46, (now 44) providing a tax on the first pump of $10.00 per annum, with a tax of $5.00 per annum on each additional pump, permits the payment of $15.00 as State privilege tax, or requires the payment of $20.00The unit is the particular filling station in question. The tax is $10.00 for each pump at a filling station, with $5.00 for each additional pump at the station. Where two separate places of business are maintained, the first pump at such place of business is taxed $10.00 even though the operator of the filling station has another place of business upon which he is paying privilege tax.", 

(Opinion of Attorney-General, dated Jan. 16, 1937.) 

"Filling stations are not liable for the privilege tax upon oil depots.

"' 

(Opinion of Attorney-General, dated Nov. 2, 1928.) 

"The license tax on oil and gas filling stations can be collected only as to tanks or pumps used for delivering motor vehicle fuels; those used in delivering lubricating oils are exempt.' (See Gulf Refining Company v. Graham, 300 S. W. 564.) 

"A gasoline pump which has not been used during the taxable period cannot be used as a basis for taxation.-since it is not a pump from which products are sold.” 

(Opinion of Attorney-General, dated Oct. 31, 1935.) 

"-Such filling stations are also liable for a merchants' ad valorem tax because such filling stations are merchants. However, such filling stations are not liable for the merchants' privilege tax-" (Opinion of Attorney- 

General, dated June 17, 1935.)

Item 60-Merchants- 

(a) Permanent Merchants 

The tax is imposed on persons engaged in the mercantile business in Tennessee. The tax is 15¢ on each $100.00 of the average capital invested as shown by the sworn statement of the merchant. The minimum tax for the State is $5.00; however; if the average capital invested is $800.00 or less, the merchant is subject to tax of $7.50 and ad valorem tax does not accrue.

The term average capital invested as used in this item is defined to mean average amount of stocks defined by Section 1701, Code of Tennessee, which section is as follows:

Persons engaged in the business of merchandising other than such as are embraced in sections 1702-1703 shall be taxed as herein set out. 

Such persons shall, at the expiration of the period of bond provided for in section 1698, file with the clerk of the county court of the county a statement under oath, showing the amount of capital invested in business to be assessed for taxation; but under no circumstances shall the amount to be assessed be less than the value of the average amount of stock on hand during the preceding year, to be ascertained by adding together the value of the highest amount of stock on hand at any time during said year with the value of the lowest amount of stock on hand at any other time during said year, and dividing the same by two, and adding thereto the actual cash value of all the movable fixtures, safes, desks, office furniture and equipment where same belong to and are the property of said merchant; said statement to be sworn to by such merchant, person, or the head of such firm, company, or corporation, in which he shall state that he has not reduced his stock for the purpose of escaping taxation at any time,

Ch. 15) 1163 

and has fully, truly, and correctly, without evasion or reservation, made return as required by law; and said average amount of stock as sworn to by said merchant shall be deemed the taxable value of the capital of such merchant, upon which he shall pay to the county court clerk the same tax as levied upon real estate and other property for state, county, and municipal purposes. The word "capital" as used in this section shall be construed to mean the average amount of stock on hand during the year in which it is offered for sale; but if the average stock on hand is less than the capital stock employed by said merchant, he shall pay a tax on the capital stock. 

However, it should be observed that the last paragraph of above section states that- "if the average stock on hand is less than the capital stock employed by said merchant, he shall pay a tax on the capital stock.' 

It would appear therefore that a merchant should be assessed under this item on the average stock on hand or the amount of capital stock invested in his business whichever is the highest.

Merchants starting in business are to comply with the provisions of Section 1703, Code of Tennessee, which is as follows: 

All capital employed during the preceding twelve months, in any manner of trading in which there is no stock of goods, wares, and merchandise kept on hand for sale, and the aggregate capital reported shall be deemed the taxable capital of such merchant or factor, upon which he shall pay the same tax as levied upon real estate and other property for state, county, and municipal purposes, and the report herein required shall be sworn to by such merchant or the head of such concern. 

The person engaged in such business shall, at the expiration of the period covered by the said bond, file with the clerk of the county court a statement giving the aggregate amount of capital employed during such period, verified by an oath that said statement, without evasion or reservation, correctly, fully, and truly shows the aggregate amount of capital of every character employed during such period. 

If warehouses are maintained for replenishing stores the tax is to be imposed upon such average stock as is stored in all warehouses or depots. 

Persons selling articles not taxed or exempted from taxation are taxable as merchants. "Where a special privilege tax is imposed upon a business, such business is not liable for the general merchant's privilege tax in addition to the special privilege tax, unless the Revenue Bill clearly imposes both privilege taxes. This means that a business which is liable for the general merchant's privilege tax ceases to be liable for such privilege tax when a specific item is placed in the Revenue Bill imposing special tax upon such business'. (Opinion of Attorney General dated June 17, 1935.)

(Ch. 15  

"This office, in construing the provision referred to, has advised collecting officers that a mere drummer was not subject to the privilege tax of a merchant."' (Opinion of Attorney General dated Jan. 2, 1936.) 

"A Manufacturer who sells left-over stock obtained from rejected orders must pay a merchant's privilege tax."' (Opinion of Attorney 

General dated June 20, 1935.) 

"He does not purchase the farm implements and machinery for resale but carries a stock of such goods belonging to the company and from such stock of goods makes sale. Under the facts, the company is engaged in the sale of merchandise through an agent and is liable for the merchant's privilege tax.' (Opinion of Attorney General, dated Sept. 5, 1935.) 

"A manufacturer is not liable for merchant's privilege tax so long as the manufacturer merely sells his own manufactured articles to jobbers and commission merchants and the only profit taken is from manufacturing." 

(Opinion of Attorney General dated August 12, 1935.) 

"If, however, a manufacturer sells his own manufactured articles as a merchant, adding a dealer's profit to that of the manufacturer then such manufacturer is a merchant and is liable to the privilege tax of a merchant."' 

(Opinion of Attorney-General dated September 23, 1935.) 

"I am of the opinion that twelve months would be the minimum period of time necessary to constitute one a permanent merchant." (Opinion of 

Attorney General Dated April 30, 1931.)

The tax is a special privilege tax imposed on persons having or maintaining an oil depot and is graduated on the number of gallons of petroleum products sold, distributed or stored annually as follows:

The term oil depot is defined to mean, a place where petroleum products or substitutes come to rest in Tennessee, in quantities exceeding 31 gallons, and are not distributed to consumers in retail quantities; or a place where such products are kept for sale after manufacture in Tennessee. "The fact merely of having oil depots, storage tanks and warehouses is not sufficient to make one liable for the tax; but the depots, tanks and warehouses must be kept for the purpose of selling the oil. 

If they are kept as an integral part of a business upon which the tax has been paid, we think the legislature did not mean to tax them." (See 

General Refining & Producing Company vs. Davidson County, 201 S. W. 

736.) -Any person who receives petroleum products after movement in interstate commerce in quantities of more than 31 gallons is liable for the tax.-"} 

Opinion of Attorney-General, dated February 1, 1932. 

-An oil merchant or grocery man selling kerosene or gasoline from his store would not be liable for the tax if he purchased the petroleum products from a licensed oil dealer in Tennessee, but if such merchant purchases oil products in quantities of 31 gallons or more from another state or in interstate commerce, he would be liable for said tax, and this would apply to the operator of a filling station the same as a merchant.' 

Opinion of Attorney-General, dated January 27, 1932. 

"-A company shipping oil from El Dorado, Arkansas, to West Memphis, Arkansas and from there distributing it by truck, to various filling stations operated by it and others in Memphis, Tennessee, in quantities equal to or greater than 31 gallons, is subject to the privilege tax on oil depots."'

Opinion of Attorney-General, dated February 11, 1932. 

66. -A company which only receives and makes deliveries of oil previously sold or holds such oil in storage until called for by the purchasers is not subject to the privilege tax imposed on oil depots.' 

Opinion of Attorney-General, dated February 11, 1932. 

'—Although a gasoline filling station purchased gasoline in quantities equal to or greater than a carload lot and sold the same to its retail trade in quantities greater than required to fill an automobile tank, such filling station is not subject to the tax imposed on oil depots. (See 

Piedmont Oil Company vs. Kennedy, 54 S. W. (2nd) 958.)

Item 96-Transfer of Realty and Mortgages— 

1. Tax may be imposed by (a) State only 

2. Tax may be paid (a) Before such transfer is registered. (a) Transfer of Realty

A tax of $1.50 per $1,000.00 of the consideration received for the transfer of real property. The consideration taxable under this item cannot be less than the value of the property, and is to be collected by the County Court Clerk of the county in which such transfer is offered for record.

(Ch. 15 

In addition to the above tax a fee of 15¢ is imposed for certification of tax payment by the County Court Clerk. "The question is whether or not a real estate transfer tax is imposed on the registration of a certified copy of a will which devises realty. The entire question hinges upon the meaning of the word "transfer." I am of the opinion that the word “transfer'' used in this connection means a conveyance between living parties and does not contemplate a conveyance testamentary in its nature."' (Opinion of Attorney-General dated Sept. 

21, 1928.) "Whenever a corporation is absorbed by another corporation, or the new corporation is re-organized for the purpose of carrying on the business of another corporation and takes a deed to the property of the former corporation, although there is no other consideration than that of facilitating the business of the re-organized company, the transfer tax attaches." 

(Opinion of Attorney-General dated Oct. 12, 1934.) 

-This corporation which was domesticated and authorized to do business in Tennessee owned property in this State. Upon dissolution of the corporation the trustees conveyed the property to the stockholders. Under the statutory provision the privilege tax must be paid for the transfer of realty." (Opinion of Attorney-General dated Sept. 11, 1933.) 

"Where a husband conveyed his property to a third party and such third party reconveyed the property to the husband and wife for the purpose of vesting title in grantees as an estate by the entireties, these were two separate and distinct transfers and a transfer tax must be paid on both transfers."' (Opinion of Attorney-General dated Sept. 11, 1935.) 

"When the grantee is a governmental subdivision of the state, the privilege tax for the conveyance of realty is not due." (Opinion of 

Attorney-General, dated Oct. 29, 1935.) "No transfer tax need be paid when real estate is transferred to the 

University of Tennessee. Opinion of Attorney-General dated Sept. 18, 1933. "A conveyance of land to the Reconstruction Finance Corporation,or to a trustee for same is not subject to the privilege tax.' (Opinion of 

Attorney-General dated May 23, 1935.) "A transfer of realty to a Federal Land Bank is not subject to the privilege tax upon transfer of realty, and since, therefore, it does not require a notation of the County Court Clerk that the tax has been paid, the Federal Land Bank is not required to pay the 15¢ for such certification." 

(Opinion of Attorney-General dated Dec. 4, 1935.) 

"It is asked what transfer tax should be collected in a deed containing love and affection, etc.-It is apparent that the transfer tax must be paid on the amount at least equal to the value of the property. In this particular case the Clerk should collect on the assessed valuations." (Opinion of Attorney-General dated Aug. 22, 1927.) "The State tax should be collected, however, on the basis of the consideration of the original deed since the quitclaim is to take its place and the transfer has never been paid, in accordance with the contention of the County Court Clerk." (Opinion of Attorney-General dated Nov. 27, 1929.)

Attention is drawn to the fact that the tax is imposed on the consideration which shall in no case be less than the value of the property. The word value is not defined and should be given its usual and ordinary meaning; how-

Ch. 15) 1185 

ever, it appears that the value cannot be less than the assessed value of the real estate. (b) Mortgages, etc.

A tax of ten cents on each $100.00 (or major portion thereof) is imposed on the amount of a deed of trust, mortgage, conveyance in trust, or other instrument in the nature of a mortgage of any real or personal property situated in Tennessee. The tax is payable to the county court clerk before registration of such instrument and for certifying payment of tax a fee of 15¢ is payable to the clerk. The tax and fee is payable by the holder or owner of the indebtedness secured by the instrument offered for record. 

The first $2,000.00 of the amount of such mortgage, etc., is exempt from this state tax. Such mortgages, etc. owned by the T.V.A., and other governmental subordinate bodies are not subject to the tax.

It should be noted that the tax applies to mortgages on personal as well as real property and that property partly within and partly without Tennessee is taxable only on the value in Tennessee. "The result is that the tax under the facts stated is not a privilege tax upon the city of Murfreesboro but is a privilege tax upon the person from whom Murfreesboro has borrowed money. "" (Opinion of Attorney 

General dated April 17, 1935.) "The only question you submit is as to whether the special privilege tax-is measured by the $50,000 of bonds secured by this instrument or only by the $30,000 actually issued at the present time This instrument secures the payment of the full $50,000 indebtedness and if the tax measured by the $50,000 is not paid with the registration of the deed, there would be no way to determine the measure of the tax hereafter in the event the remaining $20,000 is issued."' 

(Opinion of Attorney General dated January 26, 1937.) 

"The Mack International Truck Corporation holds a chattel mortgage executed by the Colonial Short Line Company on thirty buses to secure $165,000.00 due to the Truck Corporation:-This tax is levied for the privilege which is afforded by the statutes of Tennessee as protection to the holders of the mortgage against judgment or attaching creditors in this state when it has been determined that the privilege has been exercised, the tax becomes due." (Opinion of Attorney General, dated January

Attorney General dated October 3, 1933.)

GROSS RECEIPTS PRIVILEGE TAX— Law. Article II-Section 2 

 That engaging in the various businesses mentioned in this Section is hereby declared to be a privilege for State purposes and taxable by the State alone, and any person so engaged shall pay to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, unless otherwise provided, the tax herein stated. No county or municipality may impose any tax upon the privileges mentioned in this Section, (except license fees upon motor vehicles which might be imposed in the absence of this section) to wit:

The taxes imposed under the provisions of Section 2, of Article II are "State taxes only" and are payable direct to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation of the State of Tennessee in accordance with Section 2, of Article III 

of this Act (chapter 108, Acts of 1937). Counties and incorporated cities are not authorized to levy taxes similar to those herein levied. 

Item A-Bottlers and Manufacturers of Soft Drinks, etc.- Law: 

Each person doing business as a bottler or as a manufacturer of beverages known as soft drinks shall for the privilege of doing business

(Ch. 15 

pay to the State for State purposes an amount equal to one and one-half (12) per cent of the gross receipts in the State. 

There shall be credited upon the tax hereby imposed any taxes paid under the Franchise Tax Law and under the Excise Law during the calendar year in which the tax hereby levied becomes due. 

The tax hereby imposed shall be administered and collected in accord ance with Article III, Section 2 of this Act. 

Bottlers and manufacturers of soft drinks paying the tax levied by this item and delivering only the products of their own plant by which this tax is measured shall not be liable for a peddler's tax: and shall not be liable for wholesale jobbers' tax under Item 101.

A tax of an amount equal to 12 per cent. of the "gross receipts," in Tennessee, is imposed on persons doing business as a bottler or a manufacturer of beverages known as 

Soft Drinks. 

The term Soft Drinks is not defined in this taxing item, and difficulty may arise in connection with the persons who are engaged in bottling milk, tomato juice, fruit juices, etc.; while these questions do not appear to have arisen, attention is directed to the following excerpts from opinions of the Attorney General dealing with similar questions under former taxing items; "Prior to decision of the Chancery Court of Davidson County, Part II in the case of Anthony Pure Milk Co. v. Cobb, County Court Clerk, this Department had advised the collecting officers that dairies selling bottled chocolate milk must pay the privilege tax imposed by item 14. 

However, in the case referred to the Chancellor held that dairymen who add chocolate syrup to milk, selling the product in ordinary milk bottles, are not liable for the privilege tax imposed by item 14 upon bottlers and manufacturers of soft drinks. No appeal was taken from the decision of the Chancellor. You are advised that in view of the decision of the 

Chancery Court in the case referred to, collecting officers will hereafter be advised by this Department that the privilege tax imposed by item 14 is not to be collected from dairies which add chocolate syrup to milk, selling the product in milk bottles. (Dated Jan. 21, 1936.)

The tax paid on gross receipts is to be credited against the Franchise and Excise tax due by Domestic and Foreign Corporations; however, individuals and partnerships engaged in bottling or manufacturing soft drinks are not liable for the Franchise or Excise tax.

Persons liable for tax under the provisions of this Item who deliver only the products of their own manufacture are not liable for the peddlers tax or the wholesale jobber tax under Item 101.

Item B-Branch or Chain Stores— 

Law;

Each person engaged in the business of operating or maintaining in this State branch or chain stores shall for the privilege of operating such stores pay the tax hereinafter set forth. In each such chain or branch store system there shall be exempted from this tax the store in which such system maintains its general offices in Tennessee or if no such general

(Ch. 15  

offices are maintained, a store in such system to be designated by the taxpayer in the sworn statement hereinafter referred to. 

Upon each store in such branch or chain in excess of one, there shall be paid a tax of Three ($3.00) Dollars for each one hundred square feet of floor space, or major fraction thereof, in such store. 

The term "branch store" or "chain store" as used in this Item shall include retail stores or mercantile establishments operated (or controlled by lease, contract or otherwise) under the same general management, supervision or ownership. The term "chain store" or "branch store, as used herein, shall also include retail stores operated under separate charters of incorporation (if there is a common ownership of a majority of the stock of such separate incorporated companies), or operated under a common ownership of a majority interest in such stores when such separately incorporated companies or stores have the benefit, in whole or in part, of group purchase of merchandise for resale or of common management. 

The term "chain store" or "branch store' shall not be construed to include filling stations or any other store or place in which the principal business carried on therein is the storage, sale or distribution of petroleum products taxed under a separate Item of this Act, but shall include counters, divisions, departments or leased space operated under a chain store system in department stores or other mercantile establishments. The floor space' term 99 as used in this Item shall include the total number of square feet in such store determined by the internal measurements as to width and depth of each floor thereof. "Floor space" shall not include floors, basements or separate rooms used exclusively for storage purposes, to which customers are not ordinarily admitted; but counter space, office space, elevator space, etc., shall not be considered storage space and shall be computed as floor space. 

The tax hereby imposed shall be paid on or before June 1st of each year for the privilege of operating during the ensuing twelve months period and shall be paid to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation accompanied by a sworn statement of the taxpayer, or his legally authorized agent, setting forth the number of stores operated, the square feet of floor space of each store, and the location of each store, including the exempted store.

A separate license shall be issued for each store hereunder taxed and such license shall be available for inspection at the store for which issued. 

The privilege tax levied by this Item shall be in addition to any other privilege tax required under this Act or under any other Act. 

The tax is imposed (in addition to all other taxes) on persons engaged in the business of operating or maintaining Branch or Chain Stores in Tennessee. The store in which such persons or system maintains a general office is exempt from the tax, and if no general office is maintained in Tennessee the taxpayer may designate any store in such chain or system and such designated store is exempt. 

The tax is imposed at the rate of $3.00 per 100 square feet of floor space, or major fraction thereof, of each store in such system in excess of one. 

The item branch store or chain store includes: (a) Retail stores or mercantile establishments operated or controlled by lease, contract or otherwise, under the same general management, supervision or ownership.

Ch. 15) 1195 

3 (b) Retail stores operated under separate charter of incorporation, if there is, 1. Common ownership of a majority of such separate incorporated companies. 

2. Operated under a common ownership of a majority interest in such separately incorporated stores. 

3. When such separately incorporated stores or companies receive a benefit as the result of group purchase of merchandise or common management. "—Item B defines a Chain store, for the purpose of this taxing item as retail stores "operated under a common ownership of a majority interest in such stores," when such stores have the benefit of group purchase of merchandise or of common management. The mere fact that one or more individuals may own an interest in different stores does not constitute these stores a chain. The mere fact that the stores may operate under the same name does not constitute them a chain if there is a common ownership of a majority interest in the store and if the stores have the benefit of group purchase then there is a chain. If Messrs. A & B own less than a majority interest in the store at Tullahoma, it is quite clear that these two stores will constitute a chain. Moreover, if the stores at Tullahoma and Winchester are separately operated and do not have the benefit of group purchase then there is no chain even though Messrs. A & B happen to own a majority interest in such stores.'' (Opinion of Attorney General dated April 30, 1937.) "-X's Inc., of Knoxville, is a separate and distinct corporation from three other corporations having similar names. These other corporations are as follows: 

X's Inc., Greeneville, Tennessee, X's Cash Store, Athens, Tennessee, X's Cash Store, Cleveland, Tennessee. X's Inc., of Knoxville, Tennessee, according to the letter which accompanied your request, is operated independently of the other three stores and does not have the benefit, in whole or in part, of group purchase of merchandise. Three of the stockholders of X's Inc., of Knoxville, Tenn., own stock in the other three corporations referred to above. However, these three stockholders own less than one-third of the outstanding stock of X's Inc., of Knoxville, Tennessee. Under the circumstances stated it is quite clear that X's Inc., of Knoxville, Tennessee is not liable for the tax imposed by item B of the Revenue Act. This tax applies to retail stores operated under the same general management, supervision or ownership. The tax applies if the stores have the benefit of group purchase of merchandise or of common management, when there are separate charters of incorporation providing there is a common ownership of the majority ownership in such stores. In order that the tax shall apply two things are necessary. First, if there be separate charters of incorporation it is necessary that there be a common ownership of a majority interest of the stores. Lacking this requirement, there can be no tax liability even though the stores have the benefit of group purchase of merchandise. In other words, where separately owned stores merely unite for the purpose of group purchase there is not a taxable chain under Item B. Secondly, it is necessary that the stores have the benefit of group purchase or of common management. 

The mere fact that two separate stores operating under different corporate charters, have their stocks owned by the same people would not create tax liability under Item B, if such stores did not have the benefit of group purchase or of common management. The result is that X's, Inc., Knoxville, is not a chain store under the statement of facts made for the purposes of the taxing item." (Opinion of Attorney General dated May 

24, 1937.)

The term Chain Store or Branch Store is further defined to include;

(Ch. 15  

(a) Counters 

(b) Divisions (c) Departments d) Leased space, operated under a Chain Store system in stores and other mercantile establishments; however, the terms do not include filling stations and other places where the principal business is the storage, sale or distribution of petroleum products. "You are advised that Item B of the General Revenue Bill which imposes privilege tax on chain stores is limited in its application to retail stores or mercantile establishments. The result is that this item has no application to a place where petroleum products are sold and distributed wholesale and not retail.'' (Opinion of Attorney General dated March 

24, 1937.) "In the enactment of a tax upon chain stores additional to all other taxes the General Assembly no doubt had in mind the advantages which such stores enjoy over other stores, i.e. the advantage of unified management or of group purchase. The maintenance of coal yards in various portions of the City gives no such advantage. The primary reason for such coal yards is the advantage of mere storage. Indeed, the maintenance of such coal yards is a form of warehousing. The chain store as the term is popularly understood would certainly not include coal yards whatever may be the technical definition of a store-Under the circumstances it is my opinion that a coal yard is not a chain store within the meaning of Item B." (Opinion of Attorney General dated June 21, 1937.) 

"You are advised that in my opinion a restaurant which merely serves prepared food to be consumed on the premises is not a chain store within the meaning of Item B. A store is a place where goods, wares, or merchandise are kept for sale.' (Opinion of Attorney General, dated June 

21, 1937.) 

The term floor space includes the total number of square feet, determined by internal measurements, of each floor in the store, but does not include basements and other rooms used exclusively for storage purposes. However, counter, office, elevator space, etc., is considered floor space.

In other words, floor space is all space in the store exclusive of that used for storage purposes. "You also ask whether the taxing officers were seeking to construe the law as applicable to one or more rooms in a store building which rooms were vacant and not used. It is my opinion that such rooms as were vacant and not used would not be included in the measure of the tax under the terms of the statute and the Department would not undertake to measure the tax by such vacant rooms. (Opinion of Attorney General dated April 8, 1937.) 

The tax is payable on or before June 1st of each year and application for license is to be filed at the same time.

Ch. 15) 1197 

"Each person engaged in business of operating or maintaining in this State branch or chain stores and beginning such operations subsequent to June 1, shall pay tax on a pro rata basis for period beginning with commencement of operations and ending May 31st."' (Commissioner's ruling 

November 2, 1937.)

The license when issued must be displayed, or be available for inspection, at the store for which same was issued.

Syndicates, etc. 

Law: 

Each building and loan association incorporated, organized or doing business under the laws of this State, including Federal Savings and Loan Associations and investors syndicates and the like, shall pay to the Commissioner of Insurance and Banking, direct, a specified privilege tax the equivalent of Twenty-five (25c) Cents on the One Hundred ($100.00) 

Dollars or major portion thereof worth of capital invested in this State. 

The word "capital" shall be construed to include surplus and undivided profits. Each association shall, annually, on or before the first day of 

September, make a sworn return to the Commissioner of Insurance and Banking showing the amount of capital of such association invested in this State, as shown by the books at the close of business on the 30th day of June next preceding and shall at the same time pay the tax as provided above. The amount of capital invested shall be the entire capital of the association actually paid in unless the portion of such capital shall be invested in other states, in which case only that portion of the capital paid in which shall be invested in this State shall be taxed. The tax here provided shall be in lieu of all other taxes of such associations except ad valorem taxes upon real estate and tangible personal property owned by such associations.

Such exemption from other taxes shall include taxes upon or for the use of the franchise, capital, notes, reserves, surplus, loans, accounts, income and profits of such associations, including income tax upon share holders who receive dividends from such associations, and including excise tax.

The tax is imposed on Building and Loan Associations, Federal Savings and Loan Associations; Investors Syndicates, and similar organizations, organized or domesticated under the laws of, and doing business in, Tennessee. 

The rate of tax is 25¢ on each $100.00 or major fraction thereof, of the worth of capital invested in Tennessee.

Ch. 15) 1199 

The word capital is defined to include surplus and undivided profits, however, the word worth is not specifically defined. It would appear that the word worth was intended to mean, that value invested in Tennessee as of June 30, of each year, as shown by the books of the taxpayer. 

The Item requires the filing of a sworn report with the Commissioner of Insurance and Banking, on or before Sept. 

1st of each year and the tax must be paid at the time such report is made.

The tax applies only to capital invested in Tennessee and Associations doing business, both within and without the State, should be careful to maintain records which will accurately reflect the amount invested in Tennessee. 

The tax levied is in lieu of all other taxes except real and personal property taxes. Dividends received from such Associations by residents of Tennessee are not subject to income tax imposed by the State of Tennessee. 

Item D-Corporations, Filing Fees of, etc.— Law: 

The fees for securing charters of incorporation or amendments to such charters or certificates of increase of stock of a corporation, or for receiving and filing other certificates relating to corporations, shall be those fixed by Section 3760 of the Code of Tennessee and enumerated therein. 

Such fees and the said Code Section shall not be deemed to be altered or repealed by this Act.

The fees for the domestication of foreign corporations and for amendments to the charters of domesticated corporations, shall be those fixed by Section 4120 of the Code of Tennessee. 

The fees for filing of annual corporation reports shall be those fixed by Section 4136 of the Code of Tennessee. 

None of the above enumerated Code Sections and no other Code Sections specifying filing fees of particular kinds of corporations, or consolidation of fees and the like, shall be deemed to be altered or repealed by this Act. 

Comment regarding this taxing item is deemed unnecessary.

Item E-Ferries— Law: 

Each person operating a ferry from one point in this State to another point within the State shall pay a privilege tax as follows: 

Each ferry operating in competition with a State owned toll bridge, per annum

Each ferry located within two miles of a State owned toll bridge shall be presumed to be operating in competition with such 25.00

(Ch. 15 

toll bridge and the burden of proving the contrary shall be upon the operator. 

In addition, each such ferry shall pay a privilege tax to the State for State purposes equal to eight (8) per cent of its gross receipts in the State.

This tax shall be paid monthly, not later than the tenth day of the month, to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, measured by gross receipts for the preceding month. Insofar as consistent with the preceding sentence, this tax shall be administered and collected under Article III, Section 2, hereof. 

All other ferries, except those operated by hand or horse power, per annum

It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a ferry without a license from the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and without payment of the above levied privilege tax. Within thirty (30) days after the passage of this Act and thereafter, before engaging in such business, every person operating a ferry must apply for and secure a license from the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, at the same time paying the privilege tax above set forth. Before licensing any ferry, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation shall investigate and determine whether such ferry is operating in competition with a State owned toll bridge. 

Any person operating a ferry must pay the privilege tax demanded by the Commissioner and sue for the recovery thereof under Section 1790 of the Code of Tennessee if he deem such tax to be illegal or to be in excess of that properly payable by him. 

The operation of any ferry without a license or without payment of the privilege tax above set forth is hereby declared to be a public nuisance and such nuisance shall be abated by injunction in the name of the State upon suit of the Attorney General. 25.00 The tax is imposed on persons operating ferries from one point to another point in Tennessee, as follows:

For each ferry operating in competition with a State owned toll bridge $25.00 per year, plus 8 per cent of the gross receipts from the operation of such ferry. 

For each ferry operated with power other than hand or horse power, $25.00 per year.

The tax is imposed by the State only and is to be paid to and administered by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation in accordance with Article III, Section 2, of this Act.

The operation of a ferry without a license is a violation of the law and declared to be a public nuisance which may be enjoined in suit brought by the Attorney-General. 

Before license to operate a ferry is issued the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, or his representative, must investigate and determine whether the ferry is operated in

Ch. 15) 1201 

competition with a State toll bridge. A ferry located within 

2 miles of a State toll bridge is presumed to be operating in competition with such bridge, and the burden of showing that such ferry is not operated in competition is upon the operator of such ferry. 

Taxpayers who deem such tax to be illegal may sue for the recovery thereof in accordance with Section 1790 of the Code of Tennessee.

 Item F-Insurance Companies- Law: 

Each foreign insurance company and each fidelity and surety corporation or company shall, as hereinafter designated, pay direct to the Commissioner of Insurance and Banking, the following taxes, which shall be in lieu of all other taxes except domestication fees and annual filing fees of corporations. 

Fire and all other insurance corporations or companies of other states and foreign countries except life insurance corporations or companies, shall pay two and one-half per cent on gross premiums paid by or for policy holders residing in this State or on property in this State. Life insurance corporations or companies of other states and foreign countries shall pay two and onehalf per cent on gross premium receipts from citizens of and residents of this State, payable semi-annually in January and July, on sworn returns. Life corporations of other states and foreign countries, ceasing to transact new business in this State shall continue to pay the tax herein provided on business in force and until the same is terminated. Companies chartered under the laws of other states, but domiciled in this State, and who maintain their home office in this State, shall be exempt from payment of the two and one-half per cent on gross premiums paid by or for policy holders residing in the State of Tennessee, the same as other domestic companies.

Assessment life corporations ceasing to transact new business in the State shall continue to pay the tax herein provided, or in force until the same be terminated.

Item G-Gas, Water, Electric Power & Light 

Companies- Law.

Each person engaged in the business of furnishing or distributing gas, water, or electric current, whether to dealer, consumer, municipality or other customer, shall, for the privilege of doing such business, pay to the State for State purposes an amount equal to three (3%) per cent of the gross receipts derived from intrastate business in the State. 

Persons engaged in the business of manufacturing gas or of distributing manufactured gas or natural gas shall, in lieu of the foregoing, pay an amount equal to one and one-half (12) per cent of the gross receipts derived from intrastate business in this State, which payment shall be subject to the same provisions, restrictions and credits hereinafter provided in this Item.

This tax shall not apply to cities or other political subdivisions of the State owning and operating gas companies, water companies or power plants; nor shall it apply to any governmental agency of the United States.

It is the intention of this Item to levy a tax for the privilege of engaging in intrastate commerce carried on wholly within this State and not a part of interstate commerce. 

The tax hereby imposed shall be administered and collected in accordance with Article III, Section 2 of this Act. 

Each person engaged in the business of furnishing or distributing electric current shall be exempt from the above tax upon gross receipts up to the amount of Ten Thousand ($10,000.00) Dollars, but shall be liable to the State tax upon all gross receipts in excess of Ten Thousand ($10,000.00) Dollars.

(Ch. 15  

The tax is imposed on persons engaged in the business of furnishing or distributing gas, water, or electric current to dealers, municipalities or other customers. The tax is measured by gross receipts derived from intrastate commerce.

The tax does not apply to the gross receipts derived from the sale of water, gas, or electric current when such sales or distribution is made by companies owned or operated by governmental agencies. 

The tax imposed is to be administered by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation in accordance with Article 

III, Section 2 of this Act.

Item I-Private Car Companies- Law. 

Each person owning or operating stock cars, furniture cars, fruit cars, refrigerator cars, meat cars, oil cars, tank cars, or other similar cars, operating over any of the railroads in this State, shall, in addition to all other taxes levied and assessed in this State, pay annually to the Comptroller a tax for the privilege of engaging in such business within this State. The tax shall be equal to one per cent upon the value of the total property, both tangible and intangible, located in the State, or allocated to the State by the Railroad and Public Utilities Commission. 

The tax is imposed on persons owning or operating furniture, fruit, refrigerator, meat, oil, tanks, or other similar cars over railroads in Tennessee. The rate of tax is:

Ch. 15) 1209 

1 per cent. of the value of the total property. 

Total property means tangible and intangible property located in Tennessee or that property valuation allocated by the Tennessee Railroad and Public Utilities Commission. 

This Item provides that the tax herein imposed is in addition to all other taxes levied and assessed in this State, pay annually to the Comptroller—, and does not specifically provide herein for administration under Article III, Section 2; however, it appears that the tax should be paid to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation on or before August 1st of each year in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 33, Acts of 1937, which transfers the duties of the Comptroller with respect to taxation to the 

Department of Finance and Taxation.

Law.

Merchants selling sewing machines of a company paying tax under (A) above are not subject to the tax imposed on Sewing Machine Companies; however, such merchant would be taxable as an Agent or Dealer.

Item M-Telephone Companies and Telegraph 

Companies- 

Law. 

Each person operating a telephone business for the transmission of messages or conversations within this State or operating the apparatus necessary to communicate by telephone, and each person operating a telegraph company in this State or operating the apparatus neceessary to communicate by telegraph, shall for the privilege of doing such business pay to the State for State purposes an amount equal to three per cent (3%) of the gross receipts derived from intrastate business in this State. 

Such gross receipts shall include all rentals and other similar charges and shall also include all tolls received from business which both originates and terminates in this State. 

When such persons are operating telephone companies or telegraph companies partly within and partly without this State, the gross receipts shall be deemed to be all receipts on business beginning and ending within this State.

It is the intention of this Item to levy a tax for the privilege of engaging in intrastate commerce carried on wholly within the State and not a part of interstate commerce. 

There shall be credited upon the tax hereby imposed any taxes under the Franchise Tax Law and under the Excise Tax Law during the calendar year in which the tax hereby levied becomes due. 

The tax hereby imposed shall be administered and collected in ac cordance with Article III, Section 2, of this Act. 

In addition to the above tax, each municipality is hereby authorized to impose on telephone and telegraph companies, other than mutual home telephone companies not operated for profit, a rental tax of twenty-five (25) cents on each telephone and telegraph pole standing on the streets, or along the streets, of such city. This tax is to be collected and retained by the municipality.

The tax is imposed on persons operating a telephone and telegraph business in Tennessee, or operating the apparatus necessary to communicate by telephone or tele-

(Ch. 15

graph. The rate of tax is 3 per cent. of the Gross Receipts derived from intrastate business in Tennessee, in excess of Ten thousand ($10,000.00) dollars. 

Gross Receipts includes all rentals and other similar charges, and tolls upon business originating and terminating in Tennessee. Persons operating telephone or telegraph service partly within and partly without Tennessee should note that gross receipts includes all receipts derived from business beginning and ending in Tennessee even though such message or conversation may be diverted outside of Tennessee.

This taxing item was not intended to allocate to Tennessee any portion of the gross receipts derived from interstate commerce.

The tax is payable on or before August 1st. of each year, direct to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation in accordance with the provisions of Article III, Section 2 of this Act, and the Franchise and Excise tax payable on July 1 of each year is a credit against this tax. 

In addition to the above tax, municipalities are authorized to impose on telephone and telegraph companies (other than mutual home telephone companies) a tax of 25 cents for each telephone and telegraph pole standing on the streets.

Item 0-Transportation Companies and Compensation for Use of Public Highways- (a) Transportation Companies Law. 

Each person engaged in the business of operating a transportation company shall, for the privilege of doing such business, pay to the State for State purposes an amount to three (3) per cent of the gross receipts derived from intrastate business in this State. 

Within the meaning of this Item, each person operating a railroad,

Ch. 15) 1215 

aeroplane, boat or barge, or an express company, or a street railway, or engaged in the business of transporting persons or property or freight for hire by motor vehicle, whether as a common carrier or as a contract hauler, shall be deemed to be a "transportation company. 

This Item shall not apply to transfer companies taxed under Item 9 (f) of this Act, nor to taxicabs taxed under Item 9 (g) of this Act. 

When transportation companies are operating partly within and partly without this State, the gross receipts shall be deemed to be all receipts on business beginning and ending within this State, without entering or passing through any other State. It is the intention of this Item to levy a tax for the privilege of engaging in intrastate commerce carried on wholly within the State and not a part of interstate commerce. 

The tax hereby imposed shall be administered and collected in ac cordance with Article III, Section 2, of this Act. 

(b) Compensation for use of Public Highways

Each person engaged in the business of operating automobile busses or motor vehicles, using the roads and highways of this State and carrying passengers for hire, whether doing interstate or intrastate business, shall, in addition to the privilege tax imposed by subsection (a) of this Item, pay as reasonable compensation for the use of the public highways the following fees:

Each bus or motor vehicle with a seating or carrying capacity of eleven (11) passengers or less, per mile traveled, 2¢ for each mile. Each bus or motor vehicle with seating or carrying capacity of more than eleven (11) passengers and not more than twenty-one passengers, per mile traveled, 2¢ for each mile.

Each bus or motor vehicle with seating or carrying capacity of twenty-one (21) passengers and less than twenty-four (24) passengers, per mile traveled, 4 for each mile.

Each bus or motor vehicle with seating or carrying capacity of twentyfour (24) passengers or more, per mile traveled, 14 for each mile.

The above compensation fees shall be paid whether the seats are occupied or not.

Each person subject to the fees herein levied shall first obtain a license from the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation and shall make monthly reports showing accurately the number of miles traveled, and such other information as may be required by the Commissioner. Such reports shall be made on or before the 10th of each month for the preceding month. 

If any person herein required to make report shall be delinquent in making such report or in paying such fees or shall make a false or incomplete report, the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may apply to the Railroad and Public Utilities Commission for revocation of such person's license from such Commission. 

All penalties and remedies hereinafter set forth with reference to the collection of delinquent privilege taxes shall be applicable to the fees imposed herein provided, this Item shall not apply to street railways operating an urban transportation system with respect to such operations. 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation in the collection of said mileage fees shall keep the amounts paid by intrastate operators separate from the amount paid by interstate operators, a separate account being kept for each class of operators; and at the end of each month the amounts collected from each class of operators shall be turned into the State Treasury.

The Treasurer shall credit to the general funds of the State such amounts as have been paid by intrastate operators, and the same shall be

(Ch. 15 

available for the payment of appropriations made out of said general funds; and the Treasurer shall credit to the Department of Highways and 

Public Works all amounts received from interstate operators under this Act and the same shall be used exclusively for the maintenance, upkeep and repair of the highways of the State. 

(a) Transportation Companies-Privilege Tax 

The tax is imposed on persons operating a transportation company or service. The rate of tax is 3 per cent. of the gross receipts, derived from intrastate business in Tennessee.

The term Transportation Company includes: 

1. Railroad 

2. Aeroplane 

3. Boat or barge 

4. Express Company 

5. Street Railway 

6. Bus Lines 

7. Motor Vehicle Freight Carrier 8. Motor Vehicle "Contract Hauler'' 

The term does not include Transfer Companies and 

Taxicabs taxed under Item 9 of this Act.

It is not the intention of this Item to tax interstate commerce; however, the gross receipts derived from business beginning and ending within Tennessee, which does not pass through another state, is deemed to be intrastate commerce and is subject to the tax. 

The tax is payable on or before August 1st of each year direct to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation in accordance with the provisions of Article III, Section 2 of this Act; and the Franchise and Excise tax payable on 

July 1 of each year is a credit against this tax.

Item P-Workmen's Compensation-Self Insurers- 

Law.

If an employer covered by provisions of Sections 6851-6901 inclusive, of the Code of Tennessee, known as the Workmen's Compensation Act, or any amendatory Act thereto, shall not execute the bond required by section 6895 of the Code, but shall carry his own insurance as provided by the said Section, such employer shall pay to the Commissioner of Insurance two per cent on the premium which he would be required to pay if he carried the insurance called for with licensed insurance companies.

Exclusive State Privilege Taxes— Law. Section 2. Be It Further Enacted: 

Every person exercising any privilege declared taxable by an Item providing for administration under Article III, Section 2 of this Act shall annually on or before the 1st day of August make and deliver to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, upon such forms and blanks as may be required by the Commissioner, a statement, verified by the oath of the official or agent making such report and statement, containing the following information as of the 1st day of July of the current calendar year: (a) The total gross receipts of the taxpayer for his most recently completed fiscal year from business within and without the State. (b) The total gross receipts of the taxpayer for the same period from such business within the State. (c) Such other and further information as may be deemed necessary by the Commissioner for the assessment of the taxes administered under this Section, and as may be required by the forms and blanks prescribed by the Commissioner.

Provided that the business mentioned in this Section shall be required to pay to the counties and municipalities in this State, all ad valorem taxes of every kind and character, including merchants ad valorem taxes now authorized or that may hereafter be authorized by law, and nothing in this Section shall be construed as a denial to the various counties and municipalities in this State to collect such ad valorem taxes, including merchants ad valorem taxes, from said business. 

Gross receipts for the purposes of taxes administered under this Section shall mean total receipts before anything is deducted but shall not include receipts from incidental business when such incidental business, if separately carried on, would not be subject to a tax measured by gross receipts under the provisions of this Act. Any person failing to file report and pay the tax found to be due in accordance with the provisions of this Section on or before August 1st of any year shall as a penalty for such failure pay an additional amount of ten (10) per cent, together with interest at the rate of six (6) per cent per annum on the total amount of the tax and penalty incurred. 

The Commissioner whenever he deems it necessary to investigate the accuracy of the statement made by any taxpayer shall have the power to send an agent or representative to inspect the books and records of the taxpayer for the purpose of determining the accuracy of the statement and reports made by such taxpayer, to secure any necessary information not disclosed by the sworn statements and to ascertain the correct tax liability. 

In the event any taxpayer fails or refuses to permit such agent or representative to have access to necessary books and information, then the Commissioner shall have full power and authority to compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of books and papers in the same manner as process may now be issued by the Courts to compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of books and papers. Such process shall run anywhere in the State, and shall be served by the Sheriff, or other lawful officer in any county, city or town, to whom the same may be directed. 

Disobedience to such process shall be treated in all respects as contempt of court and may be punished as such on the petition of the Commissioner to the Chancery Court of the county where the hearing is had. 

When any taxpayer fails or refuses to file the statement and report

(Ch. 15 

hereby required, the Commissioner is authorized to determine the tax liability of such taxpayer from whatever source of information may be available to the Commissioner, which assessment shall be as binding as if made upon the sworn report and statement of the taxpayer. Any taxpayer willfully refusing to furnish the required information shall thereafter be estopped to dispute the accuracy of the assessment made by the Commissioner. 

All the remedies given by other provisions of this Act for the collection of the various taxes hereby imposed shall be available to the Commissioner for the purposes of collecting taxes administered under this Section. 

The taxes levied by items providing for administration under Article III, Section 2, are hereby declared to be imposed for the privilege of engaging in business for the year beginning on July 1, even though such tax is made payable on the following August 1 and even though such tax is measured by gross receipts for the preceding fiscal or calendar year. 

Any person who shall have been engaged in business for less than a full year on July 1, shall, for the ensuing year, pay as follows:

The measure of the tax shall be ascertained by multiplying such person's gross receipts by the ratio which an entire year bears to the period during which he has engaged in business. 

Any person who first commences business on or after July 1, 1937, shall at the conclusion of each month report to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation his gross receipts for such month and shall pay tax, measured by such monthly gross receipts, at the rate specified in the appropriate taxing item. This tax shall be paid not later than the 10th day of the following month. On August 1 following the date when such person entered business he shall pay annual tax for the year commencing on the next prior July 1, computed according to the preceding paragraph but he shall not thereafter make monthly payments. 

(a) Reports Required Persons taxable under Section 2, of Article 2 of this Act are required to file annually, on or before August 1st of each year, a report with, and upon forms furnished by, the 

Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. The report must be made under oath and shall contain the following information: 

1. Total gross receipts for the most recently completed fiscal year from business within and without Tennessee. 

2. Total gross receipts for the same period from business within Tennessee. 

3. Such other and further information as may be deemed necessary by the 

Commissioner. 

The provisions of this Section of the law are not to be construed as an exemption for any ad valorem taxes, merchants ad valorem taxes, or other taxes authorized by law to be levied by any county or municipality. (b) "Gross Receipts" Defined

Gross Receipts means total receipts before any deduction, but does not include receipts from incidental business

Ch. 15) 1225 

unless such receipts from such incidental business is subject to the gross receipts tax under the provisions of this Act. 

Therefore, a company taxable on gross receipts would not include receipts from dividends, interest, etc., as a part of the measure of the tax liability. 

(c) Penalties 

Any person liable for the tax imposed by Section 2 of Article 2, must file the report and pay the tax on or before 

August 1st of each year. Failure to file the report and pay the tax subjects such person to a penalty of 10 per cent. of the tax due, plus interest at the rate of 6 per cent. per annum. 

(d) Inspection of Records 

The Commissioner may send his agent or representative to inspect the books and records of taxpayers for the purpose of ascertaining whether the correct tax has been paid, or to secure any information deemed necessary to determine the accuracy of any report or statement. If any taxpayer fails or refuses to permit the Commissioner or his agent to inspect the books and records, power and authority is given the Commissioner to compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of books and papers in the same manner as process may be issued by the Courts. 

The Commissioner is authorized to determine the tax liability from any information available in instances where the taxpayer fails or refuses to file report or reports required under this Act. Should the taxpayer willfully refuse to furnish necessary information, and assessment is made by the Commissioner from information obtained by him, such taxpayer is estopped to dispute the accuracy of the assessment.

All remedies given by other provisions of this Act are available to the Commissioner for the collection of the taxes requiring administration under Article III, Section 2 of this Act. 

(e) Tax Period or Tax Year 

The taxes imposed by items requiring administration under Article III, Section 2, are imposed for the year begin-

(Ch. 15  

ning July 1st and are payable on or before August 1st of each year.

The tax due and payable on or before August 1st of each year is payable for the ensuing tax year and is measured by gross receipts for the preceding period or calendar year. 

Persons who have not been engaged in business for a full year prior to July 1st of each year are to compute gross receipts by the use of the ratio which an entire year bears to the period during which he was engaged in the business. 

To illustrate: 

X enters business on April 1, 1936, thus, on July 1, 1936 he has been engaged in business 3 months or 14 of a year. The gross receipts for the three months amounts to $3,000.00, the computation of gross receipts for the ensuing year will be: 

4 times $3,000.00 ..$12,000.00 and the tax should be assessed at the appropriate rate. 

Persons who commence business on or after July 1, 1937 are required to file report and pay tax on or before the 10th day of each succeeding month up to August 1, and the gross receipts for the ensuing year are to be computed as described above.

Penalty for Doing Business Without License- Law. Section 3. 

It shall be unlawful for any person to exercise any of the privileges made taxable by this Act before complying with the provisions of this Act. 

Any one exercising any of said privileges without first paying the tax or without complying with this Act shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and liable for a fine of not less than Five ($5.00) Dollars for each day such privilege is exercised without a license, which fine shall be in addition to any other penalties herein imposed. Any successor by purchase, or otherwise, of any business subject to tax shall be liable for and shall pay the tax imposed against such business before such successor can obtain a license to do any of the acts herein declared to be taxable. 

Any person acting as agent, trustee, guardian, administrator, executor, assignee or receiver doing any of the acts herein declared to be a privilege is subject to the tax imposed on that privilege. 

It is unlawful for any person to exercise any privilege made taxable by this Act before complying with the Act, and any persons exercising any taxable privilege without a license is guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to a fine of $5.00 for each day such privilege is exercised without the license. This fine is in addition to other penalties imposed. 

Attention is drawn to the fact that any successor or pur-

Ch. 15) 1227 

chaser of any business exercising a taxable privilege is required to pay the tax imposed before such successor or purchaser can do any act declared to be taxable. The license of the former owner does not entitle the purchaser or successor to such business to operate under the unexpired license of the former owner. Agents, trustees, guardians, administrators, assignees, executors or receivers doing or exercising any taxable privilege is subject to the tax imposed.

Collecting Officials to Keep Records- Law. Section 4. Be It Further Enacted: 

(a) That it shall be the duty of every official, agent or deputy charged with collecting, reporting and paying over State and County taxes, or other special revenues and privilege licenses, including fees, fines, forfeitures, costs, interests, or penalties, as now or may be hereafter prescribed by the laws of this State, to keep a complete record of such collections on books and forms prescribed by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation; that they shall report said collections, if it be State revenue, to the proper State official; and if it be county revenue, to the County Judge, or Chairman of the County Court, on forms prescribed and approved as herein or shall hereinafter be prescribed by the laws of this State. 

Officials, agents, and deputies charged with the collecting, reporting, and paying over State and County tax revenues and other special revenues, are required to keep a complete record of such collections on books and forms prescribed by the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, i.e. the Commissioner is charged with prescribing the books and forms necessary to maintain a complete record of such revenue collections and the "paying over" of such revenue to the State of Tennessee and to the several County Courts of Tennessee.

The State Revenue should be reported to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation.

The County Revenue should be reported to the County Court Judge or Chairman of the County Court.
