Reports Due, When-Penalty for Delinquents- Law. Section 4. 

(c) The collector shall make these reports within fifteen (15) days after the last day of each calendar month to the Commissioner, if it be for State revenue, and to the County Judge or Chairman of the County Court if it be for County revenue, and shall pay the amount shown to be due at the time of making the report. 

If such reports are not filed as required by law, and by this Act, and payments not made as above specified, there shall be added to the amount shown or found to be due from any such collecting official or agency a penalty of fifteen (15) per cent of the amount so ascertained to be due or of such delinquency.

Said penalty of fifteen (15) per cent, whether the indebtedness be due to the State and County, or State or County, shall be paid over to the State or to the proper officials thereof and for the purposes as are now or may be hereafter provided by law, and any collecting official or agency who has failed to report and pay over as required by this Act or any law of the State shall in addition to the aforesaid penalty, forfeit all commissions on said delinquent amounts.

For good cause shown the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation may relieve such delinquent official or agency of such penalty and restore the forfeited commission.

It is mandatory upon County Court Clerks and other collectors to make the monthly report to the Commissioner and to the County Judge or Chairman of the County Court, within 15 days after the last day of each month. 

Failure to file the report subjects collecting officials to a penalty of 15 per cent of the amount due. The penalty is

in addition to the forfeiture of the commission allowable to such collecting officials; however, the Commissioner may, for good cause shown, relieve such delinquent official of such penalty and restore the commission.

Inspection of License-Distress Warrant- Law. Section 5. 

(c) It shall be the duty of each agent or employee of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, specifically designated for that purpose, to visit each place of business in his territory and to call for a production of the license for the doing of that business. The wilful failure or refusal to produce and exhibit such license, whether the tax has been paid, or not, shall constitute a misdemeanor punishable as such. If the license cannot be shown him, such agent or employee of the Commissioner shall report the name of the proprietor, the nature of the business being conducted and its location, to the County Court Clerk of the county in which such business is located, and also to the Commissioner. There upon, the Commissioner shall forthwith issue, or have issued, a distress warrant for the collection of such tax, including interest and penalty due. Such distress warrant may be addressed and delivered to the Sheriff or any official authorized to execute process in the county wherein such delinquent taxpayer resides or has his principal office or place of business, or to the Sheriff of any county in which the Commissioner has reason to believe property of such delinquent taxpayer may be found.

The Sheriff into whose hands such distress warrant may come, or his deputy, may execute same by distraint and sale of personal property belonging to such delinquent taxpayer, and the proceedings in respect thereto shall be the same as are provided by law for proceedings under execution at law from a court of record; and the executing officer shall be entitled to the same fees, commissions and the necessary expense of removing and keeping property distrained as in case of an execution from a court of record.

If the officer cannot find personal property to satisfy said distress warrant, he may levy same upon any real estate in his county belonging to such delinquent taxpayer; and if levied on land, said distress warrant, together with the officer's return thereon, shall be returned to the Circuit Court of the county, wherein the land lies, and the land shall be condemned and sold under the orders of the said Circuit Court, in the same manner as in case of a levy on land of an execution issued by a Justice of the Peace. Provided, further, that suit or suits may be brought, if necessary. 

The County Court Clerk shall have the same power with reference to the issuance of distress warrants for county revenues that is hereby given the Commissioner for State revenues, and the County Court Clerk may at any time upon request of the Commissioner issue such distress warrants for the collection of State revenues. 

It is mandatory upon the Commissioner, through his agents and employees, to visit each place of business for the purpose of inspecting licenses. The wilful refusal or failure of persons, required to have a license, or licenses, to produce and exhibit such license, even though the tax has been paid, constitutes a misdemeanor, and the inspector or employee must report such refusal to the County Court

Clerk; and at the same time it is made mandatory upon the 

Commissioner to issue distress warrant for the collection of the tax penalty and interest due. 

The distress warrant is to be addressed to the sheriff, or other official authorized to execute process, in the particular county. The authorized official into whose hands such warrant may come for execution may execute same by distraint and sale of personal or real property. 

County Court Clerks are given the same right and power to issue distress warrants for the collection of the privilege taxes imposed by this Act as are given to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, and such clerks may upon request of the Commissioner, issue warrant for the Collector of State taxes or revenues. Extension of Fine for Payment of Tax Not Allowed- Law. Section 6. 

It shall be the duty of each collector promptly to collect all privilege and ad valorem taxes collectible by him when the same become due; and in no case shall any collector or his deputy agree to give, permit or allow any extension of time for the payment of the same or any part thereof. 

Attention is drawn to the fact that under the provisions of this Section of the law, collecting officials are prohibited from extending time for the payment of tax, or any part of same. This provision is mandatory; and taxpayers may avoid penalty by complying with the Act and promptly paying privilege taxes.

Examination of Books and Records— Law. Section 7. 

The Commissioner or any other authorized collector of the taxes herein imposed shall have the power, and it shall be his duty when he suspects any taxpayer of making a false or incomplete statement necessary for the collection of a privilege tax hereby imposed to proceed in the manner heretofore set forth in Section II, that is to have an agent or representative investigate the books and records of such taxpayer or, in the alternative, to require the production of such books and records. 

Comment has heretofore been made upon the subject matter contained in this Section, and further comment is deemed unnecessary.

(Ch. 15 

 Penalties, Fines, etc.- Law. Section 8. 

That it shall be the duty of each taxpayer promptly to pay the tax levied under this Act when the same becomes due; and in case any such tax is not paid within fifteen (15) days he shall pay a penalty of ten (10%) per cent on the amount of the delinquent tax for the first month's delinquency, or any fractional part thereof, and thereafter one (1%) per cent for each additional month or fractional part thereof delinquency. Said penalty which shall be on the total amount of tax so delinquent, whether State and county or State or county, shall be added to the tax collected, and shall be reported and paid over to the State or to the proper officer thereof for the purposes that are now or may be hereafter provided by law. No collector, officer or governmental agency shall be authorized to waive or excuse the penalty herein provided for. 

If any officer, agent, or employee of any person subject to the provisions of this Act shall wilfully fail, refuse, or neglect to make out, file or deliver any reports or blanks, as required by such law, or to answer any question therein propounded, or to knowingly and wilfully give a false answer to any such question wherein the fact inquired of is within his knowledge, or upon proper demand, to exhibit to the collector or any person duly authorized by him any book, paper, account, record, or memorandum of such person, in his possession or under his control, he shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and fined not less than One Hundred ($100.00) Dollars nor more than One Thousand ($1,000.00) Dollars for each offense.

If any person shall aid, abet, direct, cause or procure any of his officers, agents, or employes to violate any of the provisions of this Act he shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and fined not less than One Hundred ($100.00) Dollars nor more than One Thousand ($1,000.00) Dollars for each offense.

Every day during which any person subject to the provisions of this Act, or any officer, agent, or employe thereof shall wilfully fail, refuse or neglect to observe and comply with any order, direction, or mandate of the Commissioner or to perform any duty enjoined by this Act, shall constitute a separated and distinct offense.

The Act places the burden upon the taxpayer to pay the privilege taxes imposed, and makes it the duty of collecting officials to collect the tax, when the same becomes due. 

If the tax or taxes are not paid within 15 days after becoming due, such taxpayer is subject to penalty of; 

10% of the delinquent tax, for the first month or part thereof, and 1% additional penalty for each additional month or part thereof. 

The penalty applies to the total delinquent tax whether such tax be due the State or County, and to the total tax payable to both State and County. The entire amount of penalty collected is to be reported to and paid over to the State.

Attention is drawn to the fact that no one is authorized to waive or excuse the penalty imposed under the Act. 

Taxpayers who fail or refuse to make and file any re-

Ch. 15) 1233 

port or statement required to be filed under the terms of this Act are guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to fine of from $100.00 to $1,000.00 for each offense. Persons who aid or abet taxpayers to violate the provisions of this Act are subject to the same penalties and fines. 

Attention is drawn to the fact that each day the taxpayer wilfully fails, refuses or neglects to observe or comply with the Act constitutes a separate offense. 

Doing Business Without License-Public Nuisance- 

Suit to Enjoin- 

Law. Section 9. 

The engaging in any business herein declared to be a taxable privilege without compliance with this law is hereby declared to be a public nuisance. 

In addition to the other remedies herein provided for the collection of the taxes hereby imposed, the Commissioner is authorized to certify to the Attorney-General the failure of any person to make any report or to pay any tax required by this Act. Thereupon, the Attorney-General shall forthwith file a bill in a court of proper jurisdiction to enjoin such person from continuing to exercise said privilege, which injunction shall remain in force so long as such person is in default. Upon the payment of such delinquent privilege tax as may be due with interest and penalty, and upon compliance with this Act the Attorney-General shall be authorized to dismiss said bill upon the payment of costs by the defendant. 

To engage in, do business or exercise a privilege subject to tax under the provisions of this Act without first paying the tax and obtaining a license therefor, is expressly declared to be a public nuisance; and, in addition to the penalties and fines imposed, the Commissioner may certify the name of such person failing to make report and pay tax to the Attorney General. It is mandatory upon the 

Attorney-General to immediately file a bill in any proper court to enjoin such person from continuing to exercise such privilege. 

If such suit is filed the taxpayer may have same dismissed upon payment of tax, penalty, interest and court costs.

County Court Clerks to Report Delinquents— Law. Section 10. 

The County Court Clerks with respect to county revenues, and the officers whose duty it is to collect municipal revenues shall have the same powers with reference to the collection of such revenues as are herein vested in the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation for the collection of State None of the provisions of this Act with reference to the power revenues.

(Ch. 15  

or duties of the Commissioner regarding the collection of State revenues shall be held to supersede or diminish the powers or duties of the County Court Clerks regarding the collection of the State privilege taxes which are payable to the County Court Clerks. 

The various County Court Clerks charged under this Act with the duty of collecting revenue or taxes shall diligently see to it that the same are collected. It shall be the duty of each County Court Clerk to ascertain the name of every person in his county liable for the payment of any tax or revenue under this bill and it shall be his further duty to use every means at his command to collect said tax as and when due. Each County Court Clerk shall on the first of each month make a sworn report to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, giving the name of each delinquent taxpayer in his county and the amount of taxes due from such taxpayer and his reason for not having collected the same. Any County Court Clerk failing or refusing to collect any taxes or revenue with the collection of which he is charged, and which could have been collected by the exercise of due diligence, shall be liable therefor and his official bondsmen shall likewise be liable therefor. 

County collecting officials and City or Municipal collecting officials are vested with the same powers relative to the collection of county and city privilege taxes as are vested in Commissioner of Finance and Taxation.

County Court Clerks are required to report delinquent taxpayer to the Commissioner each month, after such clerk has used every means at his command to collect said taxes and when due. The monthly report to be made under oath and must contain: 

1. Name of delinquent taxpayer 

2. Amount of tax due 

3. Reason for not having collected the tax 

County Court Clerks who refuse or fail to collect any tax or revenue which could have been collected by the exercise of reasonable diligence are liable for the tax due and the official bond of such clerk is also liable. 

Bad Checks-Penalty- Law. Section 11. 

When any taxpayer shall tender any uncertified check for payment of the tax due by him and such check shall have been returned to the office of the County Court Clerk unpaid on account of insufficient funds of the drawer of said check in the bank upon which same is drawn, then and in that event an additional tax shall be imposed equal to ten (10%) of the tax due; and in no case shall the increase of said tax because of such failure be less than One ($1.00) Dollar, and the said additional tax shall not be waived or diminished by the County Court Clerk.

Incorrect Assessment of Tax-Penalty- Law. Section 12. 

Any County Court Clerk or other collecting officer who wilfully or negligently fails to carry out the provisions of this Act by making an incorrect assessment, or failing in any way, either in person or by agent, to faithfully enforce this Act shall forfeit in each case the sum of Two-hundred and fifty ($250.00) Dollars to the State of Tennessee, and shall be subject to ouster proceedings. On complaint of the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation, this Section shall be enforced by the Attorney-General in any manner permitted by law. 

County Court Clerks and other collecting officials, their agents and employees, who wilfully or negligently fail to carry out the provisions of the Act by making an incorrect assessment of privilege tax or to enforce this Act must forfeit the sum of $250.00 and are also subject to ouster proceedings. It is mandatory upon the Attorney-General to enforce the provisions of this Section upon complaint of the Commissioner.

Failure of Sheriff to Execute Warrant-Penalty— Law. Section 13. 

If any sheriff of this State shall wilfully fail, refuse or neglect to execute any distress warrant directed to him within the time provided in this Act, the official bond of such sheriff shall be liable for the tax, penalty, interest, and cost due by the taxpayer, and on complaint of any proper officer this penalty shall be enforced by the Attorney-General of the State in any manner permitted by law. 

The bond of the sheriff is liable for the tax, penalty, interest and cost due by the taxpayer if the sheriff fails, refuses, or neglects to execute any lawful distress warrant directed to him in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

Double Tax Liability, When- Law. Section 14. 

That no contract heretofore made, or hereafter made, by persons engaged in a business or occupation subject to a license or privilege tax, under this or any other Act, shall be invalid or unenforceable in the Courts because of the failure of such person to have paid such license tax at the

(Ch. 15 

time such contract was made or was performed; provided, that such person shall prior to the date of adjudication in the Court of original jurisdiction pay double the tax due at the time the contract was made and in addition thereto the penalty prescribed by law. 

States cannot abridge the obligation of contracts; however, if suit is brought upon contract in the courts of Tennessee by a person who has not paid the privilege tax for which he is liable under this Act, such person is liable for double tax and such tax, penalty, interest and costs must be paid before the date of adjudication by the Court. Refunds- 

Law. Section 15. 

That whenever it shall satisfactorily appear to the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation that a license tax, privilege tax, inheritance tax or other tax has been erroneously or illegally collected for the use and benefit of the State, by any county or State official, department, or department head, agent, or attorney, the said Commissioner, with the approval of Attorney-General, is hereby authorized and empowered to adjust, settle and order the refunding of the taxes so collected and to direct the Comptroller to draw his warrant in settlement of the same. 

The Commissioner shall have no power to order any refund unless claim for the same, supported by proper proof, shall have been made within one year from the date of payment.

Claims for refund of privilege taxes erroneously paid to or illegally collected by the State, either direct or through the County Court Clerks, are to be filed with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation. This section authorizes the refund of taxes erroneously or illegally collected by the State, after approval by the Commissioner and the Attorney-General, upon State warrant drawn according to law.

Attention is drawn to the fact that such claims for refund must be supported by proper proof and must be filed within one year from the date of the payment of such tax. 

If said claim is not filed within one year the same is barred.

Domestic Street Railway Companies (Chapter 157, Acts of 1937)- 

The tax is imposed on domestic street railway companies engaged solely in the operation of transportation systems.

The law is in lieu of all other State, County and City privilege taxes imposed in special or general revenue bills; however, incorporated cities may impose this tax. 

The State tax is payable to the County Court Clerk, and it appears that the tax may be paid annually or quarterly; it is graduated on the population of the County in which such business is conducted and is measured by each mile of street roadway over which equipment is operated, as follows: 

Less than 20,000 

20,000 to 49,999 

50,000 and over $5.00 per mile 

10.00 per mile 

20.00 per mile

It appears that the tax becomes due and payable May 

13, 1937 and annually thereafter.

Manufacture of Liquors-Chapter 193, Acts of 1937This Chapter provides for the calling of an election in any County for the purpose of determining whether the manufacture of Liquor for export will be permitted. In the event such election is held and the manufacture of liquor is made legal a tax of $1,000.00 is imposed. 

The tax may be imposed by the State, County and incorporated city in which liquor is manufactured, and is payable direct to the State, the County and the City.

 Collection of Delinquent Privilege Taxes-—(Chapter 

200, Acts of 1937)

This chapter authorizes the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation; and makes it mandatory, that he issue “distress warrants" for the collection of any delinquent privilege tax authorized by any statute to be collected by him. 

The remedy or procedure herein prescribed is cumulative to any remedy or procedure heretofore prescribed in any particular tax statute of Tennessee.

Automobile Dealers- 1. Statute imposing privilege tax on automobile repair shops, except those operated by automobile dealers giving free services, held applicable to dealers charging for repairs. (Knoxville Motor Co. et al v. Kennedy, 55 S.W. (2nd) 265, 1932.)

Automobile Tire Dealers- 

1. Merchant, dealing chiefly in automobile tires, though selling some other articles incidentally, held liable for privilege tax imposed by Pub. Acts 1927, since tax is not limited to automobile tire dealers operating service stations, when tires were sold or renovated. (Frank v. Lindsey, 2 S.W. (2nd) 412, 1928.) 1240

Ch. 15) 1241 

 Billiard Tables- 

1. Municipal charter authorizing council "to exclusively license and regulate" billiard tables conferred power on council to exclusion of other officials, but did not authorize town to tax billiard tables in contravention of subsequent statutes. (White et al v. Callis et al, 51 S.W. (2nd) 485, 1932.)

Brokers-Cotton Futures— 

1. Statutes imposing tax must be strictly construed against taxing power, and right to collect tax must not be extended by implication beyond clear import of statute. 

2. Where plaintiff engaged in business of soliciting orders from cotton dealers for purchase and sales of cotton for future delivery to be executed by firm in another State terminated connection with order when transmitted to nonresident firm, and deposit of margin was not required on soliciting order, but only when non-resident firm determined margin was necessary to protect it against loss, contract was one on margin, and subjected plaintiff to privilege tax under Revenue Act 1927, on soliciting of order on which margin was required, regardless whether plaintiff had any personal connection with demand for margin paid to non-resident firm. (Boggs v. Crenshaw, 7 

S.W. (2nd) 994, 1928.)

Coal Dealers- 

1. Contracts made within the State for the sale of coal, which were breached by the omission of the seller to load at its mines in Kentucky cars of coal to be shipped to States other than Kentucky, related strictly to interstate commerce. 

2. The State cannot impose a privilege tax on the negotiations within the State of contracts between corporations conducting their entire business within the State, for the sale and delivery of goods in interstate commerce. 

(Federal Coal Co. v. U. S. Fuel Corporation, 147 Tennessee 

212, 1922.)

Collecting and Adjusting Agencies- 

1. Privilege tax on "Collecting and/or adjusting agencies or companies" held aimed at those engaged in collecting, adjusting, and remitting proceeds of claims sent them. 

2. Company paid by debtors, engaged in budgeting debtors' incomes, and arranging with creditors for payments of debtors' obligations, held exempt from privilege tax on "collecting and/or adjusting agencies or companies. (Tennessee Credit Clearing Co. v. Lindsey, 35 

S.W. (2nd) 393, 1931.)

Electrical Appliances- 

1. Legislature has wide range of discretion in selecting objects of legislation, and classification in legislation is not reviewable unless palpably arbitrary. 

2. Statute imposing privilege tax on sellers of electrical appliances, which exempted merchants whose stocks was not more than $5,000, of which electrical appliances constituted not more than 10 per cent, held not unconstitutional as based on arbitrary and unreasonable classification. (Sterchi Bros. Stores Inc. v. Wallace, et al, 77 S.W. (2nd) 

807, 1935.)

Employment Agencies- 1. It was competent for the legislature to provide a regulatory license for and also an occupation tax on employment agencies, the two not being inconsistent or impinging on each other; and hence Public Acts 1917 Chapter 

78, providing for the regulation and supervision of "employment agencies," and requiring one engaging in such business to pay a fee and obtain a license, did not repeal Pub. Acts 1917, Chapter 70, taxing the business of emigrant agents. 

2. A licensee is bound to know that his license or permit, issued on payment of a tax primarily for revenue, is held subject to modification or repeal of the law under which it was issued, from the making of which charge if the public welfare required it, no incidental inconvenience to him

Ch. 15) 1243 

would stay the law. (McMillan v. City of Knoxville, 139 

Tennessee 319, 1917.)

Florist- 1. Horticulturist operating greenhouse and nursery on his own land held not "florist" within statute imposing privilege tax. 

2. Tax statutes will not be extended by implication beyond clear import of language used, and their operation cannot be enlarged so as to embrace matters not specifically pointed out, although standing upon close analogy. (Doran v. Crenshaw, 61 S.W. (2nd) 469, 1933.)

Gasoline Filling Stations— 

1. Tax provided for by Revenue Act 1927, on pumps operated by oil and gas filling stations, held limited to pumps or tanks used for delivery of petroleum products sold as a fuel for motor driven vehicles, and not to apply to pumps used to deliver lubricating oils incidentally required in operation of such machines. (Gulf Refining Co. v. 

Graham, 300 S.W. 564, 1927.)

Insurance Agents- 

1. One who solicited for foreign fraternal benefit association held an "insurance agent" under statute which requires each insurance agent or solicitor to pay a privilege tax, since fraternal benefit associations are included in descriptive term "insurance companies." 

2. Privilege tax levied on solicitors for fraternal benefit association held not violative of statute which exempts all funds of fraternal benefit societies from taxation except real estate and office equipment, since tax was on solicitor and not on the organization. (Tobin v. Estes, 79 S.W. (2nd) 550, 1935.)

Mineral Water Dealers- 

1. Revenue Act of 1925, fixing privilege taxes and imposing tax upon one engaged in business of selling either distilled water or water from springs or well or mineral water, includes business of selling water from spring on

(Ch. 15  

farm, containing no mineral or medicinal properties or value. (Seven Springs Water Co. v. Kennedy, 299 S.W. 

792, 1927.)

Oil Depots- 

1. Operator of filling stations, selling and delivering gasoline and oil at retail directly to customers, though large customers received delivery by tank truck at their place of business for convenience, held not operating "oil depot" within privilege tax statute. (Piedmont Oil Co., Inc., v. Kennedy, 54 S.W. (2nd) 958, 1932.) 

1. Gasoline, on being unloaded and stored, ceases to be subject of transportation in interstate commerce, and loses its immunity as such from state taxation. 

2. Exaction of privilege tax from oil depot operator selling at retail products coming to rest after interstate transportation held not unlawful discrimination in administration of tax on ground other retail filling stations were not required to pay such tax. (Spur Distributing Co. v. Lindsey, 62 S.W. (2nd) 53, 1933.)

Peddlers- 

1. Distinctive feature of "peddling" is concurrence of selling and delivering. 

2. Distributor selling and concurrently delivering meat to retailers held subject to privilege tax as "wholesale peddler," notwithstanding only regular customers were visited, sales were not petty, and orders for future delivery were taken. (Swift & Co. v. State et al, 55 S.W. (2nd) 

267, 1932.) 

1. Company which manufactured and marketed own goods and paid ad valorem and other state and county taxes held exempt from payment of municipal peddlers privilege tax notwithstanding company did not pay taxes in municipality into which company sent its truck for distribution of merchandise. (Murfreesboro Bread & Ice Cream 

Co. v. McMinnville, 68 S.W. (2nd) 935, 1934.)

Ch. 15) 1245 

1. Wholesale produce merchant sending out salesman on regular trip to take orders for delivery on next regular trip held not engaged in business of concurrently delivering and selling its produce, and so not a "peddler' subject to statutory tax on peddlers. (Davidson Estate v. Weeks, 71 

S.W. (2nd) 689, 1934.)

Photographers— 

1. The Act of 1870, C. 71, Sec. 1, taxing photographers as exercising a privilege, is constitutional. The fact that the privilege is discriminated according to the size of the town where the establishment is situated, does not affect the constitutionality of the law. 

2. The exercise of an occupation or business which requires a license from some proper authority, designated by a general law, and not open to all or any one without such license, is a privilege within the meaning of the constitution. (State v. Sehlier, 50 Tennessee 281.) 

1. Operator of drug stores who sold kodak films to customers who brought them back after exposing them and operator had them developed by photographer held not photographer's agent who was liable for privilege tax under act imposing such tax on agents engaged in business of developing films exposed by others. (Rogers Pharmacy, Inc. v. Crenshaw, 80 S.W. (2nd) 88.)

Public Accountants- 

1. Statute placing privilege tax on public accountants, not employing more than five persons, held applicable to public accountant conducting business personally without assistants. (Johnson et al v. Crenshaw et al, 47 S.W. (2nd) 

557, 1932.) 

Realty Transfers— 1. Statutes creating privileges will be construed so as not to impose double taxation, unless such construction is expressly or impliedly required. 

2. In a suit to collect a real estate transfer tax imposed by Revenue Act 1915, Section 8, the value of the property

(Ch. 15  

stated in the deed is only prima-facie evidence of its true value. 

3. When a railroad pays the transfer real estate tax imposed by Revenue Act 1915, Section 8, upon property extending through several counties, the tax need be paid only to the clerk of the county court of the county in which the deed to the land involved is first registered. (State ex Rel Stewart v. L. & N. R. Co., 139 Tennessee 406, 1917.)

(Ch. 16  CODE OF TENNESSEE-1932 as amended. 

Section 99: 

Ceded Property Exempt- 

The property over which jurisdiction is ceded shall be held exonerated and free from any taxation or assessment, under the authority of this state or of any county or municipality therein, until the jurisdiction shall have reverted. 

Section 270: 

Refund of Taxes; Power of Commissioner- 

The Commissioner of Finance and Taxation is empowered and directed to settle and adjust with taxpayers all errors and double assessments of taxes erroneously or illegally collected and turned over to the comptroller by the county trustees or state official, and to direct the refunding of the same.

Section 270.1: 

Refund of Taxes; Limitation 

Any claim for refund by the state of taxes or revenue alleged to have been erroneously or illegally paid shall be filed with the Commissioner of Finance and Taxation supported by proper proof within one year from the date of payment, otherwise the taxpayer shall not be entitled to refund and said claim for refund shall be barred. 

Section 1035: 

County Revenue; Sources of- 

County revenue is derived from taxes on polls, property, privileges, litigation, merchants, peddlers; from strays, fines and forfeitures, as below, and from money remaining unclaimed more than two years in clerks' offices.

Ch. 16) 1255 

PROPERTY TAX Section 1036: 

County Taxables Same as State- 

The polls, property, and privileges that are taxable or exempt from taxation, for county purposes, are the same that are taxable or exempt from taxation for state revenue. 

Section 1045.1: 

Tax for County Purposes; Limitations on Rate- 

For the year 1932 and subsequent years the various counties of this state be and they are hereby authorized to levy, for general county purposes, upon all taxable property within said county which is subject to ad valorem taxation, a tax not to exceed forty cents (404) upon the one hundred dollars' ($100.00) worth of taxable property and such tax shall be in addition to special taxes for other purposes now permitted by law; provided, however, that in all counties where, by special act, particular counties of this state are not authorized to levy for general county purposes a greater tax than herein authorized, this act shall not be construed as repealing such private or special acts. 

Provided, however, that in counties of this state having by the last federal census or any subsequent federal census a population of more than three hundred thousand (300,- 000) persons and operating under what is known as the commission form of government or having a board of county commissioners, through whose office part of the county taxes are disbursed, the limit of twenty cents (204) on the one hundred dollars' ($100.00) worth of property herein provided for shall apply separately to taxes levied for general county purposes to be disbursed through the office of the board of county commissioners and to taxes levied for general county purposes to be disbursed through the office of the chairman of the county court; that is to say, the quarterly county courts of such counties may levy an annual county tax for general county purposes not exceeding twenty cents (204) on the one hundred dollars' worth of property to be disbursed through the office of the board of county commissioners of such counties and may also levy an annual tax for general county purposes not exceeding

(Ch. 16

twenty cents (204) on the one hundred dollars' ($100.00) worth of property to be disbursed through the office of the chairman of the county court of such counties. 

Section 1048: 

County Court Imposes Taxes; When- 

The county court may impose taxes for county purposes, and fix the rate thereof, at its first session every year; and if the court omit said duty, at said first session, it shall perform it at any subsequent quarterly session. 

Section 1049: 

Tax on Value of Property; Same as State- 

Taxes on property for county purposes shall be imposed on the value thereof, as the same is ascertained by the assessment for state taxation. 

Section 1051: 

Principle of Equality and Uniformity Must Be Ob served- The county courts shall not levy any higher pro rata of taxes on any species of property, privilege, or poll, than that fixed for the state, but the percentage of such levy, as compared with the state tax, shall be equal and uniform. 

Section 1081: 

Sources of Revenue; State- 

The revenue of the state is derived from taxes on polls, property, incomes, sales of land, the exercise of privileges, litigation, from fines, forfeitures and escheats, from merchants, from peddlers, and from inheritance taxes, jail fees and interest.

Section 1082: 

Poll Tax for School Purposes; Payable by Whom 

Every inhabitant between the ages of twenty-one and fifty years, except persons who are deaf, dumb, blind or incapable of labor and of earning a livelihood, shall pay an annual poll tax of one dollar for school purposes, which shall be collected by the trustee of the county and retained

Ch. 16) 1257 

PROPERTY TAX 

in the county where collected and apportioned to the schools of said county in the manner prescribed by law. Liability for poll tax and the exemption therefrom is determined and fixed according to the age of the inhabitant, on the tenth day of January of each year.

Section 1083: 

Exemption from Poll Tax; When- 

Any person incapable of labor, wishing to have himself declared exempt from the poll tax, shall apply to the quarterly county court by petition, stating the ground of his claim thereto; and if the court, upon hearing the petition and the testimony produced before them, be of opinion that the petitioner is incapable of labor, they shall declare him to be so, of record; and the production of a copy of the same, duly authenticated, to the collector, shall be his authority for omitting to collect the poll tax from such person.

Section 1084: 

Property Subject to Taxation- 

All property-real, personal and mixed-shall be assessed for taxation for state, county and municipal purposes, except such as is declared exempt in the next article, or unless otherwise provided.

Section 1085: 

Property Exempt from Taxation- 

The property herein enumerated shall be exempt from taxation: (1) All property of the United States, all property of the State of Tennessee, or any county, or of any incorporated city, town, or taxing district in the state that is used exclusively for public, county or municipal purposes. (2) The real estate owned by any religious, charitable, scientific or educational institution and occupied by such institution or its officers exclusively for carrying out thereupon one or more of the purposes for which said institution was created or exists, and the personal property of any such

(Ch. 16  

institution used exclusively for one or more of the purposes for which such institution was created or exists. 

But the property of such institution shall not be exempt if the owner, or any stockholder, officer, member or employee of such institution shall receive or may be lawfully entitled to receive any pecuniary profit from the operation of that property in competition with like property owned by others which is not exempt, except reasonable compensation for services in effecting one or more of such purposes, or as proper beneficiaries of its strictly religious, charitable, scientific or educational purposes; or if the organization thereof for any such avowed purpose be a guise or pretense for directly or indirectly making any other pecuniary profit for such institution, or for any of its members or employees, or if it be not in good faith organized or conducted exclusively for one or more of said purposes. The real property of any such institution not so used exclusively for carrying out thereupon one or more of such purposes, but leased or otherwise used for other purposes whether the income received therefrom be used for one or more of such purposes or not, shall not be exempt; but if a portion only of any lot or building of any such institution is used exclusively for carrying out thereupon one or more of such purposes of such institution, then such lot or building shall be so exempt only to the extent of the value of the portion so used, and the remaining or other portion, to the extent of the value of such remaining or other portion, shall be subject to taxation. 

Provided further that any real property hereafter bought in by any such institution under foreclosure sales made to satisfy or protect bonds, mortgages, lien notes or other obligations in which endowment funds are invested, shall be exempt for a period of one year from the effective date of this act or from the date of such subsequent purchase.

That this Act shall apply to exemptions from taxation of the property of religious, charitable, scientific and educational institutions for the year 1936 and every subsequent year thereafter: provided, however, that all property of any educational institution owned, operated, or controlled

Ch. 16) 1259 

PROPERTY TAX 

by the State of Tennessee as Trustee, or otherwise, shall be exempt from taxation. (3) All cemeteries, places of burial used as such, and monuments of the dead. (4) All roads, streets, alleys, and promenades where condemned, dedicated, or thrown open for public travel or use free of charge. (5) All growing crops of whatever kind, the direct product of the soil of this state, in the hands of the producer or his immediate vendee, and articles manufactured from the produce of this state in the hands of the manufacturer. (6) Personal property, not including that by way of income, of the value of one thousand dollars in the hands of each resident taxpayer; provided, that any conveyance of personal property, including money, bank stock, notes, choses in action, accounts, or other evidence of indebtedness, in trust or otherwise, to any minor by the parent or parents thereof shall be presumed to have been made for the purpose of avoiding the payment of taxes thereon, if it appear that such conveyance affects enough personal property which, added to the amount of personal property remaining in the hands of such parent or parents, will exceed in the aggregate, the amount heretofore set out as exempt from taxation, and it shall be the duty of the assessor to list all such property as the property of the person making such conveyance or creating such trust; provided, that the maker or makers of the trust instrument or conveyance or delivery of such property may appear before the county board of equalizers and by proof establish the bona fides of such trust or conveyance. (7) All property protected by valid charter or contract exemption. (8) Leasehold estates and improvements thereon, in the hands of the lessee, holding under incorporated institutions of learning in this state, when the rents therefor are used by said institutions purely for educational purposes, where the fee in the same is exempt from taxation to said institutions of learning by charter granted by the State of Tennessee.

(Ch. 16  Section 1086: 

State Bonds Exempt- 

Whenever the State of Tennessee shall issue any bonds upon her faith and credit for any public purpose, neither the principal nor the interest of said bonds shall be taxed by this state or by any county or municipality of this state, and it shall be so stated on the face of said bonds when issued.

Section 1087: 

County Bonds Are Exempt- 

Whenever any county shall issue any bonds upon the faith and credit of the said county for any public purpose, without regard to when authorized, neither the principal nor the interest of said bonds shall be taxed by the state or by any county or municipality in this state, and it shall be so stated on the face of said bonds when issued. 

Section 1088: 

Municipal Bonds Are Exempt- 

Whenever any incorporated town or city shall issue any bonds, without regard to when authorized, upon the faith and credit of such town or city for any public purpose, neither the principal nor the interest of said bonds shall be taxed by this state or by any county or municipality of this state, and it shall be so stated on the face of said bonds when issued.

Section 1329: 

Lien for Taxes, Damages and Costs- 

The assessed taxes on all real estate, personalty, railroad, telegraph, and telephone, and other public service companies, and all damages and costs accruing thereon, shall be and remain a first lien upon such property, from the tenth of January of each and every year, for the taxes of that year.

Ch. 16) 1261 

PROPERTY TAX Section 1330: 

Extent of Lien- 

19 This lien shall extend to each and every part of all tracts or lots of land, and to every species of taxable property, notwithstanding any division or alienation thereof, or the assessing or advertising of the same in the name of persons not actually owners thereof at the time of the sale, or though the owner be unknown. 

Section 1331: 

Lien upon Fee in Property and All Interests- 

Said taxes shall be a lien upon the fee in said property, and not merely upon the interest of the person to whom said property is or ought to be assessed, but to any and all other interests in said property, whether in reversion or remainder, or of lienors, or of any nature whatever. 

Section 1332: 

Tax Is on Property not Person— 

The whole proceeding for collection of taxes from the assessment to sale for delinquency shall be proceeding in rem, and shall not be invalid on account of such land having been listed or assessed for taxation to any one as owner or owners or to any person or persons not the owner or owners or to unknown owner or owners. 

Section 1333: 

Tax Lien is Confined to Leasehold; When— 

Where there is assessable under the law a leasehold interest in real estate or any improvements on real estate, which said real estate is exempt from taxation in the hands of and to the owner thereof, the taxes assessed against such leasehold interest or interest in improvements on such exempt real estate shall be a lien only upon such leasehold interest or interest in improvements, and not upon the interest of the owner of the fee or the remainder or the reversion of the fee.

(Ch. 16  Section 1348: 

Assessments of Personal Property Annually: Real 

Estate Biennially- In order to provide revenue for state, county, and municipal purposes, personal property, privileges, and polls shall be assessed annually, and real estate shall be assessed every two years, in the odd years. 

Section 1349: 

Assessments at Actual Cash Value- 

All property of every kind shall be assessed at its actual cash value. The term "actual cash value," is defined to mean the amount of money the property would sell for, if sold at a fair, voluntary sale.

Section 1350: 

Municipal Taxes Collectible by County Trustee;

When Due and Delinquent- 

All municipal taxes collectible by the county trustee shall become due and delinquent at the same time as state and county taxes.

Section 1351: 

Basis of Assessments- 

The basis of all assessments shall be as follows, to wit: (1) To assess the property to the person or persons owning or claiming to own the same on the tenth day of January of the year for which the assessment is made, if known; if not, to unknown owners. (2) To assess the property held by executors and administrators in the county, district, or ward in which the decedent resided at the time of death until such shall have been distributed; but if the deceased lived in another state, then the property shall be assessed where the personal representative resides. (3) To assess personal property held by trustees and guardians of minors, married women, and lunatics to each guardian or trustee in the county, ward, or district where such minor, married woman, or lunatic resides, if a resident

Section 1352: 

Assessment of Real Estate Must Show What- 

In assessing real estate, the following shall be shown: (1) The description of the property; (2) The name of the true owner or owners, if known;

(Ch. 16  

(3) The actual cash value of the land or lot, including the improvements, and also all interest in real estate or improvements thereon assessable as under the preceding section, sub-section 5; and, (4) The actual cash value of mills, gins, manufactories, distilleries, breweries, foundries, and other buildings, for similar purposes. 

Section 1353: 

Describing Real Estate In describing real estate, the following rules shall be observed: The number of town lots (and blocks) of the property as a whole or a part shall be given; the name of the street, avenue, alley, or road on which it fronts, and the front feet thereof shall be given, unless the size, dimensions, and property can be more conveniently given in acres, then to be given in acres. If the property is a part of any known sub-division, its size, dimensions, quantity, and front feet or acres shall be given. In describing tracts of land, when it can be done, the surveyor's district, range, township, section, and sectional sub-division shall be designated and the number of acres. The lands by which the described tract is bounded shall also be given in the assessment when part of a known tract, sub-division, lot, or block of land is assessed by a description which identifies it, any other part of it which is assessed but not so identified, shall be held to embrace all of such tract, sub-division, lot, or block not included in the part identified; but a failure to assess according to this law shall not in any wise vitiate the assessment or sale of lands under the same, and parol testimony shall always be admissible to supply a description of land on the assessment roll or in conveyance for taxes, where such testimony will show what land was assessed and sold, and there is enough in the description on the roll or conveyance to be applied to a particular tract or parcel of land by aid of such testimony. 

Section 1354: 

Method of Assessment in Special Taxing Districts- 

All tax assessors in assessing for public taxes any tract of land lying partly within the limits of a drainage district, or drainage and levee district, and partly outside the limits of such district, shall assess that part of such tract lying

Ch. 16) 1265 

PROPERTY TAX 

within the limits of such district as one independent tract, and that part of any such tract lying outside of the limits of such district as an independent tract, to the end that it may be definitely known what is the amount of the state and county taxes, and any special school district taxes, assessed against the part of the land within the limits of such district.

Section 1355: 

Classification of Personal Property- 

All personal property shall be assessed under the following classification:

Class 1. Household and kitchen furniture, tableware, libraries, jewelry, sewing machine, guns, more than one gun, musical instruments, and all other personal property of a similar character. 

Class 2. Farming implements, machinery, wheeled vehicles, automobiles, tools of all kinds, and all other personal property of a like character. 

Class 3. All kinds of livestock, including dogs. 

Class 4. Steamboats, ferry boats, and all other kind of water craft.

Class 5. Money on hand or on deposit in this state or elsewhere not otherwise assessed in this state. 

Class 6. All other tangible personal property not herein above designated.

Class 7. All personal property which is a part of a capital invested in the business of a merchant, commission, or auction merchant, factors or manufacturers shall not be assessed separately as personalty, but shall be assessed as part of the capital as provided in section 26 of this act. 

Class 8. In assessing steamboats and ferry boats, boats navigating within streams within or bordering on this state, the same shall only be assessed to the extent of the interest therein of any person, company, corporation or firm residing or doing business in this state. The fact that any personal property hereby assessed may be deposited, encumbered, or transferred or pledged as collateral or loaned or out of the possession of the owner, whether the same be in or out of the State, shall not in any wise excuse the same

(Ch. 16  

from being listed and reported for taxation. In assessing personal property, the taxpayer shall, in making out his tax schedule, state how much insurance he carries on his personal property.

Section 1356: 

Gross Income to Be Used in Assessing Certain Properties- In estimating the value of saw, grist and other mills, distilleries, breweries, foundries, establishments for mining and quarrying, working marble, making gins or carriages, and other manufacturing establishments, bridges, and ferries and wharves, the annual gross income of the same, their location, and other sources of value shall be taken into consideration; and the same shall be considered together with the real estate to which it adds value. 

Section 1358: 

Falsely Swearing to Schedule; Guilty of Perjury- 

Any person swearing falsely or corruptly or knowingly in any material statement in such schedule or to any statement made as a witness to such assessor or deputy assessor shall be guilty of perjury and indicted for the same. 

Section 1359: 

Refusing to Take Oath; Misdemeanor 

Any witness refusing to take such oath or make such answers when called upon by the assessor to do so shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction, shall be fined not less than ten dollars. 

Section 1361: 

Return to Be Made by Taxpayer- 

It shall be the duty of the taxpayer, his agent, or attorney, to fill out, or have the assessor or deputy to fill out for him, the schedule hereafter provided for, and the assessor or deputy assessor shall require an oath to be made to the same, personally before him or before some justice of the peace, by said taxpayer or the agent or attorney of such taxpayer, to the correctness of the items and the

Ch. 16) 1267 

PROPERTY TAX 

questions therein, and that said schedule, fully and truly and without evasion, reservation, or concealment, sets out all properties of every kind and character of the taxpayer or property holder therein named, and for said purpose each assessor and deputy assessor is invested with the power to administer such oath. 

Section 1362: 

Failure to File Return; Assessor Makes Assessment- 

If any taxpayer shall fail, neglect, or refuse to fill out said schedule and answer each question fully and according to law, sign, and swear or affirm to the same and return it to the assessor not later than the 20th day of April of each year, then the assessor shall make the assessment against such taxpayer.

Section 1363: 

Notice to Taxpayer of Assessor's Action- 

The assessor shall note upon his books opposite the names of taxpayers who have refused, neglected, or failed to fill out and return said schedule, and whom the assessor has assessed for such failure, neglect, or refusal. Such taxpayers shall be notified thereof by said assessor or his deputies at least five days before the county board of equalization commences its annual session, and said taxpayers must show good cause why said assessment should not be made. An entry of the notice shall be made, together with the date thereof, on the assessor's books opposite the taxpayer's name.

Section 1364: 

Failure to Protest Against Assessment; Conclusive— 

If the taxpayer fails, neglects, or refuses to appear before the assessor or the board of equalization prior to its final adjournment, then the amount thus assessed by the assessor shall be conclusive against the taxpayer, and said taxpayer shall be required to pay the taxes on said amount; provided, however, nothing herein shall be taken as conclusive against the state, county, or municipality.

(Ch. 16  Section 1365: 

Oath Required of Taxpayer- 

Said oath shall be entered on such schedule beneath the same and subscribed and sworn to by the party listing, but nothing in this chapter shall be construed as requiring the person listing the property to make oath to the value of the property, but it shall be the duty of such assessor to examine into and compute the actual cash value for taxation of the property contained in the list made out by himself or the taxpayer or the agent or attorney of the taxpayer. 

Section 1366: 

Failure to File Return; Penalties- 

It shall be a misdemeanor for any taxpayer or the attorney or agent of any taxpayer to fail, neglect, or refuse to fill out or have filled out the schedule or list hereafter provided for, or fail, refuse, or neglect to take and subscribe to the oath or affirmation required to such tax schedules, or to fail to return the same to the assessor as prescribed by law, which misdemeanor shall, upon conviction, be punishable by a fine of not less than ten dollars nor more than fifty dollars.

Section 1371: 

Returns of Trust Estates; Fiduciaries- 

Persons acting as executors, administrators, guardians, agents, attorneys, clerks of any court, or in any fiduciary capacity whatever, shall make a return of the property, moneys, and effects held or controlled by them in any of said capacities, separate from their individual returns, showing the names of the person or persons for whose use and benefit such is held, and the same shall be listed separately for taxation; provided, that every such trust estate shall be entitled to the same exemption as if owned by a single taxpayer.

Section 1372:

In all cases where any person acting in a fiduciary capacity, company, firm, corporation, agent, or attorney

Section 1385: 

Reassessments; Where Improvements Are De stroyed- If any improvement to the value of two hundred dollars or more on real estate shall be destroyed by fire or flood or other casualty, then the owner thereof may, on his application to the county court clerk, have the real estate so damaged reassessed by the assessor, and such reassessed valuation shall be substituted on the assessment roll in place of the original assessment. 

Section 1386: 

Improvements to Real Property; Assessments— 

It shall be the duty of the assessor in making his annual assessment of personal property to ascertain whether or not any permanent improvements have been placed upon any real estate previously assessed, so as to increase the value thereof to the amount of two hundred dollars or more, and in such case he shall reassess such real estate, taking into consideration the value thereof resulting from permanent improvements, which assessments shall in all cases be made as of the tenth day of January of the year of which the assessment is made.

(Ch. 16 

 Section 1389: 

Reassessments When Property Subdivided- 

If a part of the real estate in any case has changed ownership or has different owners than that shown in the former assessment, then the assessor shall fix the value of each owner in such real estate, the aggregate of all of which shall be the same as the assessment to the original owner, unless said real estate or some portion thereof has been enhanced by permanent improvements or its value decreased by the destruction of permanent improvements, in which case a reassessment shall be made, so as to fix the value as of the tenth day of January of the year for which the assessment is.made, and all changes in ownership of real estate, together with the description of the real estate after the change of ownership, shall be noted by the clerk of the county court on the assessment roll, and also upon the trustee's tax books. 

Section 1391: 

Shares of Stock in Financial and Certain Other Cor porations; How Assessed 

The shares of stock of stockholders of any bank or banking association, savings bank or loan company, or insurance company, or investment company, or cemetery company, or company or incorporation doing business in this state, other than such as are defined and assessable under sections 1404-15 inclusive, whether domestic or foreign shall be assessed and taxed for state, county and municipal purposes as the personal property of the stockholders, whether they reside within or without the state; provided, however, the assessment of such shares of stock as the property of the stockholders shall be in lieu of any assessment or taxation of the capital stock or corporate property of such corporation, or association. Shares of stock assessable under this section shall be assessed at not less than the actual cash value of the same, less the assessed value of the realty and value of personal property otherwise assessed or returned for taxation, which actual cash value of shares of stock shall be computed by looking to

Section 1392: 

Realty and Personalty; How Assessed 

Real estate and personal property of any corporation, company or association defined in this section shall be assessed in the same manner, and where situate, as other real estate and personal property; but in computing the assessable value of such shares of stock the assessed value of the realty and the value of personal property otherwise assessed or returned for taxation shall be deducted from the value of the shares of stock and the remaining value constitute the value upon which the assessment shall be made.

Section 1393: 

Assessment Made Where Corporation Located- 

Assessments of shares of stock under this article shall be made at the place, ward or district of the town or county in which the corporation, association or company is located. 

Section 1394: 

Return Required- The president or business manager of any corporation, association or company governed by this article is required to fill out and furnish upon oath to the assessor an assessment schedule in writing (to be filed with the county clerk for preservation) which schedule shall contain the following questions: (1) The amount of capital invested in the business. (2) The shares of stock outstanding, with the name and residence of the shareholder. (3) The market value; and if no market value, the actual value of the shares of stock, and what the shares of stock can be sold for on the market. (4) The amount of dividends for the last two years, and amount of surplus and undivided profits, if any. (5) A certified copy of the assessed value of the real estate and tangible personalty and where situate. (6) Such other facts pertaining to the value of the shares of stock as may be demanded or deemed material by the assessor.

(Ch. 16  Section 1395: 

Assessor May Summon Witnesses; Inspect Books etc- The assessor shall have full power to summon witnesses, to inspect or require the production of books and papers, and obtain and consider any evidence other than said statement which he may deem proper or necessary. 

Section 1396: 

Shares of One Hundred Dollars Each Assessable- For the purpose of this article and for taxation, when the capital is not divided into shares of stock, each one hundred dollars of the capital invested shall be held as one individual share, and shares are defined and declared to be the personal property assessable at the actual cash value of same.

Section 1397: 

Shares of Partners to Be Reported- If the president or business manager has a partner or partners, he shall, upon his oath, furnish to the assessor in writing the number of shares, ascertained as above provided, held or owned by such partner or partners in the business, which shares so held shall be assessed where the business is located as hereinbefore indicated. 

Section 1398: 

President or Manager to Pay Tax The president or manager shall pay the tax so levied and make the amount so paid a charge against such partner or partners; he shall be held to be the sole owner of all the shares in the business, the same to be assessed at the place heretofore designated.

(Ch. 16  Section 1401:

Resident Stockholders- 

When the owner of stock in any bank or banking association or other corporation included in the provisions of this article, organized under the laws of this state or the United States, shall not reside in the same county where the bank or corporation or association is located, or is a non-resident of this state, the revenue collector for the state or county or municipality shall, respectively, have the power to collect the tax assessed by this article by instituting attachment proceedings, and said tax shall be and remain a prior lien on the stock until the payment of the same. 

Section 1402: 

Tax Is a Lien on Stock; Paid by Corporation- 

For the purpose of collecting such taxes, and in addition to any other laws of this state relative to the imposition and collection of taxes, it shall be the duty of such corporation to pay the taxes due upon such stock, regardless of any dividend or earnings belonging to such stockholder, a prior lien being declared on all such stock, on and after the tenth day of January of each year, and the said corporation being subrogated to such prior lien for the purpose of enforcing repayment of any taxes that may be so paid for the account of any such stockholder. 

Section 1403: 

Attachment by State, County or City- If the taxes on such shares shall not be paid by such corporation, then the state, county, or municipality may, after such tax may have become delinquent, proceed to collect the same by attachment on said shares of stock in any court of competent jurisdiction, through counsel to be employed for that purpose.

Assessment of Quasi Public and All Other Corpora tions- Every quasi public corporation doing business and being operated in this state, such as gas works, waterworks, and electric light companies and all other corporations quasi public in their character and which possess rights, franchises, and privileges, shall pay an ad valorem tax upon the actual cash value of its corporate property, including its franchises, easements, incorporated rights, and privileges, and all other corporate property, which value shall not be assessed at less than the aggregate actual cash value of both its shares of stock and bonded debt, and which value shall be computed by looking to and considering the market value; and if no market value, the actual value of such stock and bonds to the corporation; and provided, also, that the assessed value of the corporate realty and tangible personalty otherwise assessed shall be deducted in making the assessment from the value of the corporate property or capital stock. The term value of the capital stock or corporate property, as used in this section, shall be construed as including all tangible and franchise value. 

All corporations, foreign and domestic, other than those designated in this section and in the proviso in this clause, shall be assessed in the same mode and manner as quasi public corporations set out in this section; provided, however, this section shall not be construed as including railroad, street, and interurban railway, motor bus and truck, telegraph, telephone, building and loan, insurance, manufacturing, and banking companies or corporations, the

Section 1407: "Manufacturers" to Pay On Property; Exemptions—

All persons, copartners, and joint stock companies engaged in the manufacture of any goods, wares, merchandise, or other articles of value shall pay an ad valorem tax upon the actual cash value of the property-real, personal, or mixed-which is used and held for the purpose of manufacturing, preparing, completing, and finishing goods, wares, and merchandise, and the article in the manufacture of which the parties aforesaid shall be engaged; provided, the value of articles manufactured from the produce of the state in the hands of the manufacturer shall be deducted in assessing the property.

 Section 1408: 

Manufacturing Corporations; Corporate Property 

Including Franchise, Taxable Each manufacturing corporation, either foreign or domestic; shall pay an ad valorem upon the actual cash value of its capital stock or corporate property, including its franchises, easements, incorporeal rights, and privileges, and all other corporate property, which said value shall not be less than the actual cash value of both its shares of stock and its bonded debt, and which said value shall be computed by looking to and considering the market value; and if no market value, the actual value of such stocks and bonds; provided, that the assessed value of the corporate realty and tangible personal property otherwise assessed, and in the case of manufacturers, the value of the articles manufactured from the produce of the state in the hands of the manufacturers shall, in making the assessment, be deducted from the value of the capital stock or corporate property.
